Only 2 pizza choose basically which is perfect. I got lucky and on Sunday morning around 10:45 I enterrés without any queue! Which was top

reviews.author: Cosmin P
reviews.text: I had a great experience at Starita in Naples. I ordered two pizzas, both of which were absolutely delicious—full of flavor and cooked perfectly. The service was also excellent; the pizzas arrived at the table extremely quickly, and the waitstaff were attentive, friendly, and professional throughout the meal. The prices were quite reasonable for the quality offered. Overall, I was very satisfied and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic Neapolitan pizza.

reviews.author: Crystal King
reviews.text: I don’t normally eat pizza — it’s just not my cup of tea. But I ate three slices here. The pizza was juicy and rich in tomato flavor. The crust had that chewy texture I like, with a crunchy edge. I also appreciated that there was no added sugar to make it sweet. It tasted very natural, and even after eating, you don’t feel greasy.

reviews.author: Jamez Ali
reviews.text: Brilliant pizza place! One of the best in the city away from any tourist spots. Very busy and usually put your name on waiting list then they call you in! The pizza had beautiful tangy sauce with creamy smooth cheese along with fluffy base! Brilliant service considering how busy it is but they keep up the standard of being attentive throughout.

reviews.author: Ueda Etona
reviews.text: A pizzeria always crowded with local people rather than tourists. Located a bit north of city center, where you can reach around 15 min. by either metro or bus. They are open for dinner at 19:00 sharp, but many guests had made a line at the opening time, which means you would not have seats if you come later than opening time. Since your pizza comes promptly after your order, most guests stay roughly 30 min. only, huge queue is not always long time. Your table will be assigned with table number at the entrance. English menu is available. You can choose from wide range of classical and their original Pizza, which is fan, but you cannot enjoy many types because the size is large! Their original tomato sauce is tasty and bread part of the pizza is smooth to eat (a bit salty). The famous fried pizza has a unique shape and good taste but inside cheese may knock out you if you don’t share it with other members. The staff is friendly and will recommend you a suitable wine as well. Must visit. Small caution. Staff may say “Service fee is not included” but you can consider that table charge is actually charged!

reviews.author: Michael Alexandre Campos
reviews.text: Best pizza I had in Napoli. It was really amazing. The place is a bit out of the touristy area but it’s near the metro and easy to find. I went on a Sunday evening and there was no waiting to get a table.

reviews.author: Nia Hudson
reviews.text: A real taste of Napoli! Traditional wood-fired pizza which tasted as good as it looked. Speedy service and accommodating staff! The best gluten free pizza base I’ve had so far! It didn’t fall apart like others do and it was light and fluffy! 10/10 recommend for gluten-free and traditional pizzas.

reviews.author: Thomas Vav
reviews.text: An amazing Italian restaurant with fantastic pizza made in wooden oven. The place is not big, has few tables outside -but it's always loud because of the passing by people - and around 7 tables inside. We tried 2 different pizzas and they were delicious, with lot's of mozzarella and with very tasty crust. Everything was delivered super fast and the staff was always very attentive and with good English .

reviews.author: Rasťo Kiavčin
reviews.text: Freakin’ fresh pizza! 🍕🔥 One of the best I’ve had - super light dough, top-quality ingredients, and that perfect Neapolitan char. Fast service, great vibes. 📸 I’ve added a photo of empty plates because… it was so good, we didn’t even take a photo before devouring it 😅 5/5, no notes.

reviews.author: Dwayne Wilkinson
reviews.text: Another fabulous restaurant with outstanding food. We were able to get in without waiting at around 6:15 PM the menu is huge and the choice is a difficult one to make. Wasn't touristy and had quite a number of locals (always a good sign). I settled on the Carolina with the full burrata cheese ball in the middle of the pizza was an absolute taste sensation.

reviews.author: Maneera Chopra
reviews.text: Hands down the best neopolitan pizza in Naples! We went on a quest for pizza and this out performed all the other locations by far. Our favorites were the pesto and margarita, all the ingredients were fresh and the dough light and fluffy. The chocolate hazelnut pizza was also surprisingly crispy and delicious. You can’t miss this spot in Naples

reviews.author: Cinzia Del Monaco
reviews.text: Light dough. Good products. Reasonable prices given the area. Staff helpful and very nice. I will happily return.

reviews.author: Alessandro Cascino
reviews.text: You can't make fun of people like this, especially a Neapolitan who knows how to eat and knows the places. A classic fry for 9 euros (complete with fake photos on the menu) is outrageous. One expects to at least taste all the pieces but, in addition to being miniature, they were actually missing. The paper underneath to fill the basket was truly bordering on ridiculous. Pizza not bad, but 50 euros for two simple margheritas and a sparkling water are really too much, the place is worth it, but not like that, the place isn't a palace after all.

reviews.author: El To
reviews.text: Maximum 2 stars not beyond due to quality of service. The pizzas were burnt on the edges and especially underneath. The one with tomato was very thin and stuck to the plate. The cashier neither looked at you nor said hello when paying the bill, completely indisposed towards customers. Add to this the high prices compared to other pizzerias in Naples

reviews.author: Diego Grasso
reviews.text: Excellent pizza dough, light and tasty, artfully leavened. Excellent raw materials. The flaw is the service, we saw the pizzas arriving at occupied tables afterwards and, despite requests to check the order, we waited almost an hour for three pizzas. Service surprise at 12% included in the bill. A tip: for a pizza costing €10.00, two slices of ham are a bit low.

reviews.author: Marcello Riunno (Sbam)
reviews.text: The Service is Fantastic and the pizzas exceptional. The dough from this pizzeria is one of the few recently tested which they have allowed to rise properly, which is essential so as not to leave the pizza on your stomach. Very light and superbly seasoned with quality ingredients, there is the possibility of finding excellent pizzas outside the seasonal menu. I recommend the pistachio you won't regret it. I don't give 5 stars just because of the prices on the menu, they could be more friendly. In-depth analysis. Awareness and Intelligence, most of the people who wrote negative reviews of this pizzeria don't have a glimmer of both. The gourmet pizzeria on the seafront is not the classic Neapolitan pizzeria, I have never sat down thinking about ordering a margherita, clearly by reading their menu you understand immediately that having a margherita is like ordering fried potatoes and schnitzel in a restaurant where they serve fresh oysters and spaghetti with seafood, if I wanted a margherita I go to the historic center for around €3 and there are the best margheritas in Naples Neapolitan, Obviously being on the seafront it is to be avoided during full events such as holidays or Friday/Saturday dinner or Sunday lunch, given the crowd the service will be much less efficient and the quality at the table will be lower than what you would get on a Wednesday lunch. There is no place I know that doesn't offer worse service when the place is extremely crowded (perhaps only Nennela is saved.) If you order fried food, my brother, but haven't you learned yet that in the restaurants where tourists go they don't order starters or mixed drinks? they make a hole in your chest and you need 4 little shits but even those who live in caves know this...

name: Street Stall - Piazza Dante
address: Street Stall - Piazza Dante, Naples, Italy

name: Street Stall - Quartieri Spagnoli
address: Street Stall - Quartieri Spagnoli, Naples, Italy

name: Street Stall - Via dei Tribunali
address: Street Stall - Via dei Tribunali, Naples, Italy

reviews.author: BaDaR Al Alawi
reviews.text: Must visit street with many shops, restaurants and gift shops. Some noisy motorcycles but good place to walk.

reviews.author: Tony Ultra
reviews.text: One of the must walk and see Main Street of Napoli…shops cafes bakeries restaurants etc

reviews.author: Negar Javan
reviews.text: Great street to walk in the morning and experience Napoli life.

reviews.author: Lee Cloke
reviews.text: Busy street lots of buildings to see

reviews.author: Daniel W.
reviews.text: Via dei Tribunali, the heart of Naples. One of them.

name: Street Stall - Via Toledo
address: Street Stall - Via Toledo, Naples, Italy

reviews.author: Edison Pan
reviews.text: Beautiful metro station, it was funny to go up and down without taking the exit !

reviews.author: Josh Birman
reviews.text: Just okay. Some shops but seemed more clothing, etc. if you're into that type of thing, you might enjoy it

reviews.author: Darius Karkalas
reviews.text: If you've ever been to Oxford Street in London, it's something like that. Lots of people, really crowded, lots of shops (dominated by sports shoes), if to be honest, there's a lack of variety. I really expected more.

reviews.author: Floww
reviews.text: I went into a metro station and accidentally found myself in an underwater space cathedral designed by Poseidon himself. No joke—Toledo Station isn’t just a metro stop, it’s what happens when an architect says, “What if we turned public transportation into an emotional journey?” The whole place looks like you’ve been swallowed by the ocean in the most glamorous way possible. Blue mosaic tiles everywhere. Light tunnel thing that makes you feel like you’re ascending to metro heaven. I half expected a dolphin to guide me to my platform. Escalators? Long enough for a full existential crisis. But who cares—you’ll be too busy staring at the glowing abyss above you like you’re in a sci-fi movie and Beyoncé is about to descend from the ceiling. Honestly, I’ve never felt so spiritual in a metro. Missed three trains because I was busy taking selfies and contemplating the meaning of life in tile form. Final verdict: Come for the train. Stay for the accidental enlightenment. Toledo Station is the Sistine Chapel of metro stops—with less Michelangelo, more LEDs.

reviews.author: Sunlit.27
reviews.text: Amezing for shopping, eating something, walking , everything is so perfect and beautiful a good place for go outside, best place in Naples impressive

reviews.author: Mahsa Moayedi
reviews.text: Food is very mediocre. However, a bottle of wine was $6. The atmosphere is super fun. After the meals are served, the staff starts singing and dancing and you get to party along. Over all, go for a good time and definitely not the food.

reviews.author: Marc Dominguez
reviews.text: Wonderful Dining Experience! We had our son’s birthday lunch here and it was good! Theres a long line outside so be prepared to wait, you know its good just if there’s a line outside! Best to come around 11am when the lines are just starting to build up. The food was very good, truly authentic Napolitan food , simple but very tasty and well cooked. Seafood, meat, salad are good quality! A musician entertained us as we dined, but you need to tip him. We got the outdoor Alfresco table, its less stuffy and cramped compared to the inside seating. Must try when in Naples

reviews.author: Cynthia G
reviews.text: This is a Neapolitan institution that I believe shouldn't be missed when you're in town. We arrived 15 minutes before opening and there was already a long queue. The restaurant spans three floors, so it seats a good number of diners, and to our surprise, most of them were locals. If you're seeking something quiet or intimate, this might not be the spot for you. Service was efficient and friendly enough, even though we didn’t speak Italian. The place runs like a well-oiled machine, with orders arriving within minutes. We tried the famous potato pasta, which was decent, but a bit heavy and not as enjoyable since it wasn’t served warm enough. The seafood pasta, on the other hand, was piping hot and packed with flavor. The pesto salad was really refreshing. For mains, the grilled codfish was good, though the schnitzel was a bit dry. We didn’t particularly enjoy the sides. That said, a two-course meal at 16€ is hard to beat!

reviews.author: kaan Bilgili
reviews.text: I like the restaurant overall , it also has a great location. Waiters made our day with their unusual tradition lol . The dancing part was shocking for us . We had fun , ate italian dishes and danced . We got the menu completo which has primi , secondi and contorni . We finished them all and they were delicious but we cant say that we were completely full afterwards.

reviews.author: Samanta M
reviews.text: We had few recommendations for this place and seemed like a unique spot so decided to give it a try. The queue was ridiculous and we spent over an hour and they were late to open. The service was rushed and not super sweet too. Food was ok but not the top food. Had better meals in Napoli! But it was fun to get up ans dance although again it was over very quickly and just seemed very rushed. If it wasnt so rushed would have been great.

reviews.author: Mahsa Moayedi
reviews.text: Food is very mediocre. However, a bottle of wine was $6. The atmosphere is super fun. After the meals are served, the staff starts singing and dancing and you get to party along. Over all, go for a good time and definitely not the food.

reviews.author: Jonathan Berkowitz
reviews.text: Amazing food. Amazing wine selection. Amazing service. This family owned and operated restaurant is a true gem. You must get a reservation at least a month before your visit. It is worth it! Everything is freshly prepared and locally sourced. Cannot wait to return. The staff is knowledgeable and friendly and attentive and enthusiastic about their food and that you are happy. I always feel welcomed as soon as we walk through the doors.

reviews.author: Arnout Mostert
reviews.text: Managed to get a reservation by making sure I was awake at midnight 30 days before the date I wanted to have lunch. Well worth it. Fantastic food and fantastic staff on hand. Great wines by the glass. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Tri Chiem
reviews.text: One of our favourite restaurants in Rome. The rigatoni all’amatriciana was was incredible. We ordered for family style but I could have easily eaten that dish all by myself it was so good. The good food was matched by friendly service. Reservations are recommended otherwise you’ll be eating late like us.

reviews.author: Dylan H
reviews.text: Certainly lived up to the hype! Everything was perfect. The artichoke and mozzarella were incredible (we actually ordered a second serving of those in lieu of dessert!)

reviews.author: IMtrigirl
reviews.text: First things first, make a reservation. Seats are coveted here and you must reserve far in advance. Or, wait at the door for a no show. Next, it is worth it worth it worth it. The food is incredible, perfectly done. The Roman artichoke was amazing with mozzarella. The pasta was almost too al dente but fantastic flavors. The meat was tender and so flavorful. Great wine choices and a few delicious desserts as well. Staff was super friendly and attentive. Priced fair for the experience and delicious food but also, prepare to pay. We highly recommend and we will definitely be back. And we appreciate the amazing flavors that came out of the kitchen.

reviews.author: Ajit Kalra
reviews.text: Here’s what you need to know: outstanding meal and worthy of the 3 stars. Ambiance is unparalleled with the rooftop looking over all of Rome The most memorable and jaw droppingly brilliant dishes were the red shrimp, the veal, and the zucchini flower with saffron and caviar. No mediocre courses - no mistakes in execution. Incredible service by Simone. Chef Heinz took the time to come out to each table and warmly Greet them - such dedication after decades of success. Core Food memory for us now, after 15 3X Michelin star meals and dozens of other Michelin starred meals. The elegance place settings are another lovely contribution to the meal. Our meal was $1200 for 2 guests.

reviews.author: Thomas Chopper Russo
reviews.text: My wife and I were incredibly fortunate to secure a reservation at La Pergola after days immersed in the breathtaking works of Da Vinci, Raphael, and other masters. What awaited us at dinner was nothing short of a masterpiece of its own—crafted by the brilliant Heinz Beck. Every aspect—the food, the atmosphere, the service—beautifully affirmed the honor of the restaurant’s Three Michelin Stars. Each dish was a revelation, not just in taste but in meaning, as we were lucky enough to learn the inspiration behind several of them. The layers of flavor, the precision, the harmony of textures—it was all deeply moving. This was more than a meal; it was an experience that stirred the soul. We would return to Rome just to dine at La Pergola again.

reviews.author: Elisa Gatti
reviews.text: wow. a real michelin stars restaurant, the service was great. atmosphere was private and romantic, i couldn’t have asked for more. the food just kept coming! so fresh, so lovely.

reviews.author: Kevin Lu
reviews.text: My 3rd 3-star Michelin restaurant and now multiple try of Michelin starred locations, just giving context of expectations, but hopefully not saying it in a pretentious way. Decent was the pasta carbonara-esque dish. Definitely far from the best pasta I had in Italy. Almost everything else lacked flavor and umami. There was a focus on healthiness of dishes but one of the most flavorless meals of my life. Bread was mediocre, and the dessert was so lacking it taste, it was slightly nauseating. Leaving hungry at a 3 star place is beyond insane. 750+ euro for two to kinda want McDonald’s at midnight after bc everything is closed at that point when you do a 4 hour dinner… Water and 20 euro olive oil on Amazon was good though. In all seriousness, don’t waste your money.

reviews.author: Fah VK
reviews.text: I’m so fortunate to get the table at La Pergola. The dining room is elegant and festive. The amuse-bouche dishes were prepared by the chef in front of our table. All of the dishes were full of flavors with authentic taste and modern presentation. The water and coffee menu are extraordinary, something I never seen before. Overall, a wonderful experience in Rome.

reviews.author: Darrin Taylor
reviews.text: Had a great meal here. We made reservations and good thing we did, it's very small and was full when we got there. Wife had lasagna which was very rich and pretty truffle-heavy, a surprise for her. I had spaghetti and Meatballs which was great. Desserts were tasty too.

reviews.author: Steven Ong
reviews.text: Booked a table 2 days in advance as hear truffle very famous in this restaurant. Ordered truffle fettucini & tenderloin beef steak. I am not the steak eater due to don't like the smell but surprisingly I can eat this and no smell at all! Highly recommended their steak. Truffle fettucini taste great as well, just the texture a bit soft, if can make it a bit hard will be perfect.

reviews.author: עדי זיטלני
reviews.text: The food arrived fast and hot, the portion was fine, but the truffle felt not-original for some reason (too much truffle for the price..) The ravioli was better than the risotto. With 2 cocktails (disrecommadendation for the cocktails also) we paid 66€.

reviews.author: Catalin Vaitis
reviews.text: I am super frustrated with this restaurant. Back in Rome after many years, my wife reserved this place for the first night, totally destroyed my good vibe. The place looks very modest (this is a polite understatement), with scratched walls, plastic plants, cheap furniture. I’ve been to cheap / bad looking osterias, but then food was good or decent. This was not the case. First I had a Battuta di Fassona. Hands down this was the worst I ever had. The truffles were tasteless, felt like eating paper. A sign for low quality truffles is when they bring the truffles in the plate already…they do not shave them in front of you. The plate was seasoned with super market quality mustard. Not even a sauce, it was plain super market cheap mustard. Typically the plate comes with grissini or at least 2-3 types of bread. This came with some very basic bread, looking someone went to the nearest super market to buy some cheap bread. I am sorry I did not take some photos. Second course was pasta with truffles. Same paper tasteless truffles (not shaved in front of the client) and some super boiled pasta (should put to shame anyone pretending to cook in Italy) and swimming in some white tasteless sauce. The wine list is very short and the Brunello I ordered was quite bad. The room where we stayed was only with tourists, literally no one was speaking Italian. Probably another warning sign that it’s literally a tourist trap. I am really surprised by the high ratings this place has.

reviews.author: Gisela Holmgren
reviews.text: Wonderful real Rome cuisine. Really to recommend. We had pasta med meatballs and as a dessert creme brulee. Personal very respectful and the restaurant clean and fresh.

name: Osteria da Zi Umberto
address: Osteria da Zi Umberto, Rome, Italy

reviews.author: Camilo Arango
reviews.text: Authentic and delicious. This place is very popular, so be prepared. There is a line before they even open. But if you get in, you are in for a treat! We tried three different pastas and they were all outstanding! The staff was very friendly and attentive. I can't wait to come back next time I'm in Rome.

reviews.author: Sam Costa
reviews.text: We LOVED this spot! My cousin recommended it and it was our first time in the neighborhood. Such a wonderful experience. We got a seasonal salad which was a mixture of veggies. I believe it had escarole, artichokes, flava beans, and more… so good! We also split the zucchini flowers and carbonara pasta.

reviews.author: Phil
reviews.text: Excellent meal here today. Carbonara for me and gnocchi for the Mrs. Bread was great and service was very good. Strongly recommend reservations as the place filled up very quickly.

reviews.author: Joon Park
reviews.text: Osteria da Zi Umberto, nestled in the heart of Trastevere, offers an authentic Roman dining experience that captures the essence of traditional Italian cuisine. The restaurant's warm and inviting atmosphere, complemented by its rustic decor, creates a cozy setting for both locals and visitors alike. We started with a delightful mix of grilled vegetables. The red peppers stood out with their natural sweetness, enhancing the overall flavor profile of the dish. For the main course, we indulged in two classic Roman pasta dishes. The bucatini all'amatriciana featured perfectly cooked pasta enveloped in a rich tomato sauce, accented by the savory depth of guanciale. Equally impressive was the spaghetti alla carbonara, which boasted a creamy texture and a harmonious blend of eggs, guanciale, and pecorino cheese. Complementing our meal was the house wine, which paired seamlessly with the flavors of our dishes. The restaurant's charming ambiance made for a memorable dining experience. Whether you're dining with family, friends, or a loved one, Osteria da Zi Umberto provides a genuine taste of Rome's culinary heritage in a setting that feels both intimate and welcoming.

reviews.author: Robert Allan
reviews.text: Osteria da Zi Umberto is the kind of place where your taste buds throw a party and your waistband begs for mercy — and honestly, both are worth it. Tucked into the buzzing heart of Trastevere, it serves up Roman classics with so much flavor and heart, you'd swear a nonna was hiding in the kitchen wielding a wooden spoon like a magic wand. The cacio e pepe is creamy, peppery perfection, the amatriciana is a bold, beautiful mess of tomato and guanciale glory, and the fried artichokes? Crispy gold. The wine is cheap, the vibe is chaotic in the best way, and the whole experience feels like you stumbled into a family dinner where you're the guest of honor — just don't expect peace and quiet. Come hungry, leave stuffed, and dream of returning every night thereafter.

reviews.author: anita
reviews.text: Absolutely wonderful experience! It’s our second time in Pasta e Vino, this time we had truffle carbonara, lasagna, and gnocchi with cherry tomatoes – every single dish was bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection. The atmosphere was warm and truly felt like a family-run place, full of charm and heart. The staff were incredibly kind and welcoming, making us feel right at home. We will surely get back to Pasta e Vino when we’re again in Italy. One of the best meals we had in Rome – highly recommended!

reviews.author: Sara Govero
reviews.text: Tucked into the charming, cobblestone streets of Trastevere, Come Na Votra delivered one of the most memorable dinners of my trip. I ordered the seafood pasta and, wow. #stlouispescatarianapproved The noodles were perfectly al dente, and every bite of seafood tasted fresh and expertly cooked. Not overdone, not chewy but just right. The dish struck that dreamy balance of richness and lightness. And this pasta isn’t poison like the US’s pasta. Combine that with a brisk Roman evening and the restaurant’s cozy ambiance, and you’ve got a beautiful dinner that lingers in your mind long after the plate’s clean. A must if you’re in the area.

reviews.author: Dominick
reviews.text: I remember when this was a tiny restaurant in Trastevere. It’s amazing to see the growth they’ve experienced, and it’s well deserved! Simple but delicious Roman cuisine, great selection of wine and cocktails, friendly service and the prices are reasonable. Also it’s open during the afternoons when most Italian shops close for riposino. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Jaquez Thomas
reviews.text: Words can’t explain how good this food is. This is quite literally THE BEST food I’ve had since being in Italy. The ravioli was made with butter and cheese and I’d eat it all over again if I could. The in house cheese cake was absolutely delicious and light. You didn’t feel too heavy after eating it. This spot gets an 11/10 for me. I would 100% return to this place

reviews.author: Timo Hebecker
reviews.text: ☆Foccacia aglio e olio 4/5 ☆Gnocchi in Truffle-Sauce 5/5 ☆Ravioli Burro e Parmiggiano 5/5 ☆Tiramisu 4.5/5 ☆Service 5/5 ☆Restaurant Atmosphere 4/5 ☆Price-Performance 4/5 We came here on our first day in Rome. The Servers were very friendly. We had the Gnocchi in truffle-Parmesan sauce an the spinach-ricotta Ravioli in Parmesan-sauce. Both dishes tasted delicious. Therefore we came again on our last day. The Tiramisu tastes very good as well and would have been the best I ever tasted, if it wasn't topped with chocolate-chunks. Anyways we would definitely recommend everybody to come here and have some great food!

reviews.author: Mattie
reviews.text: Everything about our experience at Piperno was perfect. We sat outside in the courtyard and the atmosphere was wonderful. The food was delicious and the service was impeccable. We were there for a special occasion and the hosts made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived and we were well looked after until the moment we left several hours later! When we return to Rome, we will be back. Thank you!

reviews.author: Francesc Mercadé
reviews.text: Incredibile. If you visit Rome it's absolutely necessary also to visit the restaurant Piperno! Fantastic the carxofi a la giudia, and you can combine with other delicious proposals. Fantastic experience. Great.

reviews.author: Maximilian Raynor
reviews.text: A rare gem and a true 10/10. We visited during a busy sunny lunch but chose to sit inside because the interiors are nothing short of cinematic. Everything is authentic and original which results in a time-travelling experience un-like many restaurants in the world. Because everyone else was outside there was nothing to indicate the modern resulting in the true fantasy of 1950s glamorous Rome. Please never change the interiors or add ugly modern features- it’s perfect just how it is ❤️ the owner was friendly and cool and all the waiters look sharp, elegant and professional in their white tuxedos and bow ties. My wine was one of the nicest I’ve had in years. Starter was tasty and unique and served on great plates. I’d love to see a few more vegetarian/ vegan options, fresh Italian salads or vegetable pasta sauces, otherwise I cannot fault this restaurant. Thank you!

reviews.author: Anna N
reviews.text: Outstanding. Wonderful food, great service.

reviews.author: Matthew Coats
reviews.text: Fabulous established restaurant serving simple dishes beautifully. I first came here 15 years ago and remember how delicious the food was and even today, when so much time has gone by, it’s just as good as it was. Impeccable service and fabulous house wine.

reviews.author: Jimmy Le
reviews.text: 3/5 Food - Pizza was average at best. Zucchini flowers were actually good. Don't get the Suppli (rice balls) there were really dry. 2/5 Service - Our waiter was kind of rude. He was short tempered with us and was trying to rush us. We ordered a couple of pizzas and he said, “ Thats it!” Who says that? 5/5 Ambiance - Very nice and big inside. I wasn’t expecting it to be that open and nice.

reviews.author: Joshua Drew
reviews.text: I have made it a point to come to Emma's when I am in Rome. Excellent menu and everything is a good choice. I have sat outside and inside. Both are great experience. I have come with a large group (10) and small (4) all can be accommodated.

reviews.author: Chris Hutchens
reviews.text: An absolutely fantastic restaurant. They made a real effort to get our large group a table. Service was brilliant from the start with attentive waiters/waitresses. Food was superb with fresh and flavoursome dishes. The pizzas had the perfect level of crust and topping. Wine was well recommended. Puddings were lush! Thank you for a lovely final lunch before we departed.

reviews.author: Angela Rubertino Woody
reviews.text: Birthday dinner for my husband 2 weeks ago - great service, and delicious food. Artichoke salad was excellent, burrata was super fresh, pizza and pastas were all great. To make sure they could accommodate our group size (party of 8), we made reservations the day before.

reviews.author: Marina Verkhotina
reviews.text: Emma is a place I’ve known for ages, yet it never fails to amaze me. This time, the experience was made even better by the waiter’s exceptional knowledge of both the wine list and the menu—his recommendations were spot-on for our group of six. The pizza here is undoubtedly one of the best in Rome, and once you see the photos, no further explanation is needed! High-quality ingredients, perfect dough, and great attention to detail make it a must-try. Absolutely recommended, but be sure to book in advance!

reviews.author: Petra Labura
reviews.text: Authentic Roman cuisine in a warm and lively setting, just steps from the Spanish Steps! Alla Rampa is a real gem—friendly service, generous portions, and delicious traditional dishes. The antipasti buffet is a must-try, with a wide variety of fresh and flavorful options. I had the pasta with basil pesto and it was one of the best I’ve had in Rome! Also had that when I was first time there, I just love it! It was busy, but the atmosphere felt relaxed and welcoming. Perfect for a cozy Italian lunch or dinner with charm and character. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: aaron paz
reviews.text: Been to Rome a few times and hands down the best Pasta I had. Not a typical tourist scam. This is a Pasta place. Servers are also very professional and speak English. Nice cozy place. Try it!

reviews.author: Diana Musaeva
reviews.text: Great food. (I mean your artichokes…..so delicious….). Great service. (We were served by Franco and the other guy. Franco was amazing. The other guy should know that he can’t be calling everyone „baby“.) Great atmosphere. We loved it from the inside and outside. Looking forward to visit you again when I’m next in Rome.

reviews.author: Sherri Gerhardt
reviews.text: Delicious food, ambiance and great service by Michelangelo! We had multiple servers and us being Americans knowing zero italian was a challenge for us. At the end, we had a server which we could communicate with. So, no fault of theirs. Their bread at the beginning of the meal, was dry and hard crusted. Nothing great, no olive oil or butter with it. That's the only downside. I had the spaghetti seafood that was fantastic!

reviews.author: Ryan Rosenthal
reviews.text: Great Lunch! I have been eating virtually the same food every day, but the Lobster tank made me deter from the norm and I was not disappointed. The salmon was good as well as the clams. If you are in the area, this place is a must try.

reviews.author: Z tobe
reviews.text: During our trip to Rome, we had dinner at Roscioli Salumeria. We also ate at the sister restaurant, Rimessa Roscioli. The experience between the two restaurants could not have been more different. At Roscioli, it took 15 minutes before we could flag down a waiter to order bottles of water and another 15 minutes before we could order our food. We were at the restaurant for 45 minutes before our appetizers arrived. The waiter seemed stressed out and overwhelmed; other patrons were getting frustrated by the lack of service, too. I felt bad for him, but I felt worse for us. The food was fine, but not exceptional. My appetizer - suckling pig - was quite good. But my pasta Carbonara was forgettable. The lovely delicate flavor of my wife's burrata was totally overwhelmed by sundried tomatoes, and her eggplant parmesan came to us soggy. In contrast, at Rimessa Roscioli, the service was unhurried and attentive; we ordered the tasting menu, and everything was cooked perfectly, each dish was well-balanced and mixed classic Italian cuisine with a few creative twists. Summary: Roscioli Salumeria doesn't live up to the hype. If you really want the "Roscioli" experience you've been reading about and don't mind the price tag, you'll have better luck at the sister restaurant, Rimessa Roscioli.

reviews.author: Meriel Kim

reviews.author: Z tobe
reviews.text: During our trip to Rome, we had dinner at Roscioli Salumeria. We also ate at the sister restaurant, Rimessa Roscioli. The experience between the two restaurants could not have been more different. At Roscioli, it took 15 minutes before we could flag down a waiter to order bottles of water and another 15 minutes before we could order our food. We were at the restaurant for 45 minutes before our appetizers arrived. The waiter seemed stressed out and overwhelmed; other patrons were getting frustrated by the lack of service, too. I felt bad for him, but I felt worse for us. The food was fine, but not exceptional. My appetizer - suckling pig - was quite good. But my pasta Carbonara was forgettable. The lovely delicate flavor of my wife's burrata was totally overwhelmed by sundried tomatoes, and her eggplant parmesan came to us soggy. In contrast, at Rimessa Roscioli, the service was unhurried and attentive; we ordered the tasting menu, and everything was cooked perfectly, each dish was well-balanced and mixed classic Italian cuisine with a few creative twists. Summary: Roscioli Salumeria doesn't live up to the hype. If you really want the "Roscioli" experience you've been reading about and don't mind the price tag, you'll have better luck at the sister restaurant, Rimessa Roscioli.

name: Street Stall - Piazza Navona
address: Street Stall - Piazza Navona, Rome, Italy

reviews.author: Robert Chmielak
reviews.text: Piazza Navona is the perfect spot to unwind after a long day of exploring Rome! This stunning Renaissance-era square is surrounded by beautiful buildings, features breathtaking fountains, and offers a wide range of restaurants and pubs. Despite the crowds, the piazza's spacious design makes it easy to find a spot to relax. You'll also find talented street artists sketching portraits and live music adding to the lively atmosphere. A truly special place to soak up the Roman charm and unwind.

reviews.author: Larry H.
reviews.text: Very large square not far from the Pantheon. Beautiful art and architecture is all around. Quickly became one of my favorite places to relax, grab some lunch and take in the sites. Lots of food options all around. Great for people watching.

reviews.author: Michael Combs
reviews.text: This is a really cool place to go and have dinner relax hang out. Listen to music. It’s very fun. Take your pic of any restaurant in the area. They’re all good. Have a drink, relax, romantic.

reviews.author: Denis
reviews.text: A cozy and very atmospheric square. A quiet spot for a short break or a walk — like a little corner of peace in the heart of the city. Beautiful architecture all around, neat buildings, and a pleasant vibe. Highly recommend visiting if you want to experience a less touristy side of Rome.

reviews.author: Patricia Gench
reviews.text: A lovely place to visit and see the fountains to take photos. Many restaurants and places to eat or stop for coffee. It was lively without being too crowded. There were two churches to go in to look around and light candles..both beautiful inside.

name: Street Stall - Ponte Milvio
address: Street Stall - Ponte Milvio, Rome, Italy

reviews.author: Pauline Yoong
reviews.text: Huge station with many retail shops, bars and cafes. Toilets are relatively clean. There’s a new toilet on second floor too. You got to pay 1.50 euro to enter the toilet and only pay by exact cash.

reviews.author: Misha Smiley
reviews.text: Well-connected and spacious train station in the heart of Rome. Plenty of shops, restaurants, and transportation options available. Can get very crowded, especially during peak hours. Security presence is noticeable, but keep an eye on your belongings. A practical and central hub for travelers exploring the city or heading elsewhere in Italy.

reviews.author: Sujay Sreekumar
reviews.text: Pretty huge station, lot of shops in and around the terminus. The platforms were ok, not an entirely seamless process. But as a large busy terminus railway station, it is good enough.

reviews.author: Rags Srinivasan
reviews.text: Roma Termini station is a bustling hub that offers more than just trains. The station boasts an impressive array of designer stores, making it a convenient spot for some high-end shopping. Coffee lovers will appreciate the excellent coffee options available, ensuring you can get a quality cup of espresso while you wait. The lounges provide a comfortable space to relax, and the easy-to-read display boards make navigating the station straightforward. However, one downside is the difficulty in finding toilets, which can be a bit frustrating. Despite this, the overall experience at Roma Termini is quite positive. Four stars for the amenities and convenience!

reviews.author: Craig Hill
reviews.text: Taxi stand is a bloody free for all. No one's running it and your cab drivers are not serving people in the order of the line. And they're is record heat with people suffering heart strike it here!

reviews.author: Carolina Salazar
reviews.text: What an amazing spot! Authentic Italian food with a homemade touch and zero fuss. It’s super close to the Colosseum you can even see it in the background while you eat. The food is delicious, very affordable, and service is quick. I had the best Diavola pizza of my entire trip to Rome. Definitely a place I’d go back to!

reviews.author: Oldouz Shirinzadeh
reviews.text: Absolutely incredible experience! We walked in to this restaurant by chance on the first day of our vacation in Rome —and ended up coming back for every meal after that. We tried nearly the entire menu, and not a single dish let us down. Everything was consistently delicious, and full of flavor. The red wine deserves a special mention—it became a highlight of our visits. The tiramisu was the best I’ve ever had—perfectly balanced and melt-in-your-mouth good. Prices were reasonable for the quality, especially considering the location. Some of the outdoor seating even had a view of the Colosseum, which made the experience feel even more special. The staff were warm, friendly, and genuinely welcoming. Despite a queue every time we went, they managed to seat people quickly and efficiently. This place became the unexpected highlight of our trip, and we’re already missing it. Can’t recommend it enough!

reviews.author: Galyna Tymchyk
reviews.text: Although there are many small restaurants near the Coliseum, we read numerous positive reviews about this place and decided to give it a try. It’s a small but busy café, yet we were promptly seated by the host. Be aware that the tables are quite close to each other, so if you value privacy, this may not be the best choice for you. I imagine that during peak season, finding a table could be challenging, but we were lucky. We were initially seated outside, but when it started raining, the host quickly found us a spot inside, ensuring we stayed dry—such thoughtful service! As for the food, it was great—flavorful and well-prepared. I would have appreciated a bit more prosciutto on my pizza, but considering the very affordable prices, I understand the portioning. Overall, this charming little spot offers a true local atmosphere rather than a fancy, upscale dining experience. Definitely planning to visit again!

reviews.author: Mohammad “Adrian” Khalatbari
reviews.text: This was a charming local Italian restaurant. The prices were incredibly affordable, and the taste of the pizzas was absolutely amazing. We also ordered a lasagna, which I’d say was above average in flavor. One thing worth mentioning is the house white wine I ordered – a large carafe was only €6, and the quality was surprisingly high. Definitely a great experience overall!

reviews.author: Seaside Girl
reviews.text: Just off the beaten track by the coloseum..but what a find. Lots of people eating which is a good sign. We dined outside cared for by Sabrina. She was amazing..controlling all the tables outside and took every single order. Fantastic employee. Food was good..beer was cold..sun was plentiful.

reviews.author: Krzysztof Janosz
reviews.text: Excellent experience. The staff is very attentive and well organized. Food is gorgeous. From the pasta dish, through the main course till desert everything was perfect. We can personally recommend most the horse steak (juicy & tender!) and ravioli with leeks and saffron, but everything we tried was really good. Heavily recommended place! If you do not make a reservation, better come at the opening time.

reviews.author: Isa Salomo
reviews.text: Cozy street restaurant with a very friendly service. Without any doubt, the best culurgiones in town, so far. We tried both options and they were both amazing. The courgette appetizer was a delight and the grilled pecorina awesome. Tiramisu and cheesecake were delicious.

reviews.author: Ivonne Grasser
reviews.text: We started with the meatballs as an appetizer, followed by two different types of pasta. Everything was very tasty. The service was quick and friendly. Unfortunately, the outdoor seating was completely full when we arrived around 9 PM, but we were able to get a table inside after a short wait.

reviews.author: Mahsan Heydari
reviews.text: We had a good dinner and experience there, found the restaurant searching on google maps and glad we did :) food was delicious. We didn’t reserve and we had to wait around 10 mins but everything went fast. 2 appetizers and two mains and great local wine! Kind staff and good service!

reviews.author: David Berze
reviews.text: Excellent food and wine. The meatballs in tomato sauce were a highlight, just the the donkey stew. The pastas were also very good. Very professional and kind service as well. Make sure to have a reservation as it gets busy.

reviews.author: Sevil Coskun
reviews.text: Definitely must try place in Taormina! Taste of the food is amazing especially we loved shrimps so fresh and tasty. The waiters are super nice and professional.. prices are a bit higher than average but it is normal for this michelin guided restaurant, definitely worth it! If we will be in Taormina later, it is in our number one place to go for a dinner.. Thank you for everything, it was a tasteful experience :)

reviews.author: Nina Patel
reviews.text: We visited this restaurant on 3rd September 2023 following recommendations from guide books. The restaurant is located near the Duomo near the upscale Four Seasons White Lotus hotel. The place was quite quiet it could be due to its location. We were given a nice table on the terrace. The service from start to finish was great. The menu was large and there were many choices. All the food we ate was delicious and very large portions. One dish each and one to share is enough for two people. Highly recommend this place!

reviews.author: Aseem Handa
reviews.text: TL;DR: Beautiful restauraunt with great Sicilian food and service at a slightly higher price range. Definitely worth a visit for a romantic dinner or a treat! First and foremost, these are Sicilian portions!! Bring your appetite and order with this in mind! We enjoyed beautiful Sicilian fare and service, all the waters were fluent in English (bonus) and their hospitality and recommendations were top notch. Highly recommend the peppered mussels and clams to start, but be aware it's a Big portion (easily 1.5-2kgs). We also really enjoyed the fish fillet gratin, a preparation we hadn't seen in Sicily yet - they nailed it! After dinner we sought a recommendation for digestives and were provided some amazing Sicilian Amaro options to choose from. We had the Segesto and sugar free (natural) one. Both were delicious although the latter is not for the faint hearted! Whilst it's a bit more expensive here, it's definitely worth at least one visit. For awareness, the smaller things you might not have elsewhere add up here. Cover (€3 pp), Water, the wine by the glass was a bit more expensive here - go for a bottle if you like wine! Would definitely return to try the other deliciousness on offer.

reviews.author: Daniel
reviews.text: Great food and general experience. The tuna was so fresh and rich, and the raw red prawns was also amazing. One of the best tiramisu we've tried in sicily - for those who like it with extra coffee and a pinch of chocolate 🙏 It took a little too long for the food to arrive, though. But when it did everything was great.

reviews.author: John Weavers
reviews.text: A culinary treat, just off the main strip of Taormina. A tightly controlled menu still offers a wide array of tastes and flavours, complimented by some full bodied, local wines. The red tuna with onions in particular was a succulent delight from first mouthful to last. Although not the cheapest, and sadly finished with a slightly dry dessert, this remained comfortably the best meal we had in town over our stay.

reviews.author: Max
reviews.text: Very nice dinner in Toarmina. Of note was the parmigiana and the artichoke pasta. The fennel balls also very good. I found the tuna a bit disappointing hence the 4 stars. All in all a very good evening on the terrace of this small and tasty restaurant.

reviews.author: Andrea Olivato
reviews.text: Very good restaurant in the center of Taormina. Even though it’s right off the main road, it’s tucked into a small alley, so you’re not bothered by noise or heavy foot traffic. The polpette al finocchietto were the highlight. I had never tried this dish before, but it was incredibly fresh and flavorful—truly excellent. The pasta al carrubo was also a pleasant surprise and really enjoyable. A great spot for something a bit different in a peaceful setting.

reviews.author: T M
reviews.text: Really lovely and knowledgeable staff, and delicious pasta. They have certain specialties made in-store, including the fennel balls.

reviews.author: T- Lam
reviews.text: A lovely trattoria serving more home style Sicilian meals. Lovely setting but if you want an outside table best to book. The orange & fennel salad seems so simple but was delicious. Glad they had gluten free pasta which allowed my wife to enjoy Italian pasta dish. My ravioli was simple but tasty. We decided to try the snails, interesting but a bit chewy. Enjoyed our suggested glass of wine to pair with our meal. Very decently priced.

reviews.author: PABLO DE LA TORRE VARGAS
reviews.text: Tischi Toschi is a true gem in Taormina. My husband and I enjoyed a romantic dinner in a cozy atmosphere, reminiscent of a local reliquia. The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive. The dishes were outstanding, especially the fennel balls and the homemade pasta con sardina, which were delicious. In summary, it's a lovely spot that combines local charm, excellent service, and exquisite food. We can’t wait to return!

reviews.author: pamela austria
reviews.text: The store has a wide assortment of items. I love their pizza with capers and anchovies. Their staff at the dining area were nice and helpful.

reviews.author: Andy Siegel
reviews.text: great place to go shoppring and have a nice dinner. many great food options, to take home. the restaurant was very nice and the service perfect. we git there and where seated directly.

reviews.author: K Reviews
reviews.text: Eataly serves amazing Italian food with truly authentic flavors. The pizzas we tried were exceptional—delicious, fresh, and perfectly crafted. The service was excellent, with friendly staff ensuring a smooth dining experience. However, the ambiance falls short since the restaurant is located in a supermarket, which takes away from the charm. Despite this, the quality of the food and service makes it worth a visit for Italian cuisine lovers.

reviews.author: Vanessa Rose Castro
reviews.text: We didn't know what to expect. They served good pasta and pizza. The place was busy and had many things to offer including seafood!

reviews.author: Josh “Focus”
reviews.text: Great to visit the inspiration of the other Eataly’s around the world. The wine cellar is outstanding and diverse.

reviews.author: David Goldsmith
reviews.text: Fantastic! Just a perfect meal, so Turinese - elegant cooking in a quasi-rustic setting. Just full of Italian families enjoying a night out. Free from whining Americans or surly Germans, or braying Brits. Stunning cuisine. The offal dishes were fabulous. Faultless. And, so inexpensive for what it is - a great Nebbiolo for 22 Euros. A real meal deal steal.

reviews.author: Natasha Pittet
reviews.text: Lovely authentic meal, at a very decent price. Pea flan, artichokes and salsiccia taglierini, and agreti, perfectly sauted. Great ambiance with almost only Italians. My one disappointment was the dessert, which had a slight taint of "fridge", maybe the zabaglione accompanying the tasty hazelnut cake

reviews.author: Marina Peshovska
reviews.text: Incredible place if you wish to experience a traditional Italian lunch. Hosts were very helpful and friendly, food was beyond delicious! Enter the restaurant to see incredible lifeline of photos of the owners and their family through the years the restaurant has been running but also some famous names who have been at the local too. Keep in mind though that there is a midday siesta so make sure to finish lunch by 1pm or have yourself some dinner after 5.

reviews.author: Carmen Seghete
reviews.text: Someone highly reccommended us this restaurant for its vieux towards the beautiful piazza and church Gran Madre and for its food. We arrived at 7:15 PM and had to wait until 7:30 PM when they open. Some other groups of people also waited; meanwhile waiters were not busy. Very impolite keeping all of us standing for 15 minutes or longer. The menu did not have anything special and taste was not great, however prices were higher than for other restaurants with similar menu. We understood that we have to pay for the view :) Don’t go, the experience does not worth the effort!

reviews.author: Brilliant Fate
reviews.text: The deep flavor of the pasta was good.. And desserts were so delicious.

reviews.author: Levani Qoqiashvili
reviews.text: First of all, I want to say that Piedmont is, for me, one of the most delicious regions on Earth — everything comes together here: nature, people, produce, wine, aesthetics, culture, and art! I always feel joy returning to this region, but one thing has consistently puzzled me — why was it so hard to eat well in Turin? How could the capital of such an incredibly rich region lack a place where flavor, atmosphere, and service all come together in harmony? Tomorrow is the World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2025 awards, and it brought me back once again to this beautiful city. I asked all my Italian and Georgian friends who are familiar with Turin for recommendations, but most of them, unfortunately, shared the same impression — finding truly great food here is not that easy… But this time, I was lucky! My friends recommended this incredible place, where the philosophy of Slow Food truly comes to life. You can feel the focus on quality ingredients from the very first bite. The design is cozy, the music is just right, the service is warm and unintrusive — which is rare. The wine list is outstanding. And most importantly — the food is absolutely delicious! I’m impressed and inspired. You’ve gained another loyal guest in me. I come from a small country — Georgia, the birthplace of wine — where we not only appreciate places like this, but carry them in our hearts. Wishing you great success!

reviews.author: David Goldsmith
reviews.text: Well this place deserves its reputation, and Michelin star. I really enjoyed my 2 hours there, and had some fascinating and interesting dishes. As did the mem-sahib. Offally good food, yes, of course, but that is the nature of the beast. If you don't like it, try McDonalds (delighted if all Yankees chose that). The overall meal was superb, and about 200 Euros for the two of us. We did not stint ourselves.

reviews.author: Gabriella Flandina
reviews.text: The food was good really different and special dishes, in my opinion the portion was very small, it is a different concept and I like the environment but also not so much for me because almoast all dishes used brains, hearts, tongues, xD so interesting but not for me.

reviews.author: Malcolm Vernon
reviews.text: Exceptional quality ingrédients carefully put together to produce a fantastic meal. Wines on the board generally sourced locally, including a brillant cinsault rosé. The cod and bone marrow combination was amazing, the pasta dishes deeply flavoured, and my lamb tripe main really came together. They seem to put the foreigners together out the front which is a bit odd.

reviews.author: P K
reviews.text: Great local cuisine with some creative twists. Some of the best bread we’ve had over the last 3 weeks in Italy. Pasta was perfectly cooked. Lively atmosphere and great wines by list. It definitely deserves the shoutout from Michelin.

reviews.author: Badger
reviews.text: This is an exceptional restaurant, and we were delighted to have chosen to come here, expecting one star Michelin dining in a historic beautiful dining room, but ending up being blown away by the quality of the food. The food was innovative and delightful, with creative interpretations of Piedmontese cuisine, in which flavours popped with every dish. Cooking was technically excellent. The eight course degustation was preceded by two amuses bouche and punctuated by four "bread services" of various savory items and an optional cheese course. Staff were all warm, professional and skilled. Paired wines complemented dishes perfectly. Prices, while expensive for Turin, were completely fair relative to comparable places in Europe. I'd recommend without hesitation.

reviews.author: Pierre Swaelus
reviews.text: One of the best restaurants in Turin - by far! Incredible setting, sensationally tasty food, and caring staff will accompany you throughout your evening. Can only recommend. Pro tip: make sure to check their kitchen staff in action prior to your dinner at the neighbouring Farmacia 😉 Enjoy!

reviews.author: Fabrizio SCOTTO di SANTOLO
reviews.text: Actually a tourist attraction, it was an icon in Turin, they showcase an excellent execution in the kitchen. Service is extremely provincial with a number of wrong manouvres to accomodate the turists that are the mainl customers. The kitchen is still the reason to come. Extremely expensive for what it delivers. There are better restaurants in the area at a fraction of the price. Unfortunately. Not worth a visit unless someone is paying for you.

reviews.author: Jacob N
reviews.text: Incredible meal here at Del Cambio! Matteo Baronetto has truly delivered a unique and interesting experience here for diners. I went with the 9 course surprise tasting menu and not a single dish disappointed. They were plated in new and different ways than what I'm normally accustomed to at fine dining restaurants like this. Often times presented on multiple plates that you can take bites of individually or combine at your own will. Compared to normally everything on one plate, with a sauce poured over at the table or on a large plate apart from each other. The visuals were stunning, the flavors were intense, subtle, and simply delicious. Very happy with my experience here.

reviews.author: Kevin Van Bogaert
reviews.text: Del Cambio is, unfortunately, a major disappointment, especially given its reputation and exorbitant prices. The dishes, while visually appealing, fall far short in terms of flavor and originality. It feels like more effort is put into presentation than the actual quality of the food. For what’s on offer, the prices are absolutely outrageous. The service is nothing short of abysmal. Wait times are long, and when staff finally make their appearance, they come across as uninterested and inattentive. For a restaurant that claims to offer fine dining, this is completely unacceptable. Del Cambio seems to rely heavily on its historical significance and location, but misses the essence of what a true gastronomic experience should be. In short, this restaurant is not worth the money and offers far too little value for the price.

reviews.author: Karen Smith
reviews.text: If you have one tasting menu in Torino this should be your choice . We were absolutely delighted surprised , entertained and most of all blown away by the quality of the ingredients the exciting and unexpected flavour combinations .the meal was a feast not just for the mouth but also for the eyes Everything is made in house from the amazing breads , the fermented products including their incredible kombuchas . Situated looking out onto the iconic Fiat race track on the roof of the old Fiat factory . If you go during the day you have the added advantage of great views over the track. Service is professional, friendly and impeccable . Prices dare I say it still too good value for the level of cuisine served

reviews.author: Karla Jovanovic
reviews.text: Great experince. Food was 10 out of 10, very professional and friendly service, excellent choice of local wine and also this is located in the former Fiat factory. The interior is a combination of a modern and industrial with good music behind. Very good value for the money.

reviews.author: Eddie
reviews.text: I tried their seasonal tasting menu (meat) and everything was great. The servers were very professional and recommended a great red wine to pair with today’s dishes. The location is also very unique (located above the Fiat race track, which is above a mall). All in all, a great experience and I would recommend this place for a great date night (walk around the pista, watch the sunset with a great view, food and service).

reviews.author: Jenny Zu
reviews.text: We were a huge group and had the restaurant for us. Very good food, nice atmosphere, friendly waiters. Thanks for having us! If you go to the restaurant, take a walk at La Pista first, it takes about 10 to 15 minutes with stunning views.

reviews.author: Constantinos Kandiliotis
reviews.text: WOOOW just WOOW! I visited Torino on the 08.09. for just a day and since I had very limited time I chose to have lunch at the Lingotto complex rather than searching for a restaurant in the city. To be honest, I chose the La Pista initially for its proximity and for being on the top of the building and literally next to the legendary Fiat test track. I had no idea of its concept, decoration and menu. But what a surprise!!! I was greeted like royalty, despite being very.. casualy dressed and for sure not according to the restaurant's image and atmosphere. Nevertheless the staffs behaviour made me very comfortable, being extremely polite, responsive and always by my side for anything that I might needed. Since I do not drink alcohol, I asked the maitre for an non alcoholic apperitif, which he made for me in zero time. I can easily say it is one of the best I have ever had, being super flavourful and fresh. As for the dishes... Ohh dear...That first dish, with the black rice, the tuna the dressing, so tasteful, so fresh and so interesting as a concept .. Then the calamari and shrimp plate followed by a very flavourful sauce and accompanied by potato chips, handmade to be exact, all and all a tasteful plate and a wise choice. Interestingly it blended very well with the apperitif. And finally the desert.. I am a chocolate addict, yes and it fulfilled my expectations 1.000%, being fresh and full of flavour. With the check, a small plate with sweet bites came along and with that my experience at the La Pista had a very satisfying end. I also liked the modern decoration of the restaurant but I have a feeling that at night it's looks even better. I am SO VERY PLEASED with the restaurant and I promise I will be back. Cudos to the super attendive staff, my sincere BRAVO for their professionalism. As for the prices, I expected to be far more expensive than they actually were and that was another pleasant surprise. So if you visit Torino, THIS IS THE PLACE for your lunch,dinner, business lunch, you will be rewarded with the restaurant's general environment.

reviews.author: Cvetelina Vasileva
reviews.text: Great atmosphere, wonderful interior, incredibly friendly staff, the food is good, but it is at a lower level than the service, I expected a slightly higher level.

reviews.author: Lydia Aydon
reviews.text: Great place for lunch, good spot for people watching from outside tables in pedestrian street. Food was good - my sea bass was delicious though I felt the asparagus pasta was a little overcooked and not very hot.

reviews.author: Elena (Butterfly)
reviews.text: 4.5. Very tasty and good served food. Good selection of wines. Friendly staff. Unfortunately not all wines which was mentioned in menu by glass were available ( the bill for one person 40-50 euros minimum)

reviews.author: James Mayall
reviews.text: A lovely restaurant with great service, wonderful atmosphere and brilliant food. Well worth a visit

reviews.author: Kate Brennan
reviews.text: A lovely lunch experience! I was a little intimidated at first when I walked in as I felt a bit underdressed as this is definitely a fancier kind of restaurant! However, the staff treated me very kindly and I felt very welcome here. The Plin with sage & butter was just divine. I loved that when they offer the Parmesan it is left on the table so you can add as much as you like throughout the meal. The wine was also excellent and I appreciated the generous serving! Despite being a fancy restaurant, I felt that the pasta dish I had was very generous in portion size and really reasonably priced considering the quality of the dish and the surroundings you are in. I didn’t have room for something sweet but the dessert trolley is a sight to behold. This was my last supper in Turin and it was great to finish on a high note. Grazie!

reviews.author: kitty nason
reviews.text: What a lovely and unexpected meal to have in the heart of Turin. I tried the matcha ravioli… and oh my!! Who would have thought matcha and ravioli is such a delicious combination. The food is presented so beautifully. The garden we sat in is very lush and calming on a hot evening. The staff were incredibly friendly, and one of the managers came over and gave us some great recommendations for our time in Turin. I’d come back here just to have the ravioli again.

reviews.author: Edison Y
reviews.text: HOW DARE THEY. It was a fabulous night. The service was quick. Staff was kind and patient with us clueless visitors. And the food was INCREDIBLE. Our favourite was the pasta with pomodoro sauce, but the one with ragu sauce was equally delightful. It was our first meal in Torino after a 5-hour drive and we had such a wondrous sleep after. Would absolutely return!

reviews.author: Dara Mirovaia
reviews.text: It was a wonderful dinner at a wonderful restaurant. Thank you so much! Everything was delicious and well thought out. A great combination of flavors. Special thanks to the waiter Dario and all the staff for their courtesy and hospitality!😍

reviews.author: Sude Yilmaz
reviews.text: We were caught with slim options for lunch as most restaurants and cafes in Torino are shut midday however, after some browsing we saw Solferino Restaurant still open and gave it a try. We had the grilled vegetables to share, the Agnolotti di Magro and the Brucio pasta options. Everything tasted amazing and the service was impeccable. Even though we were obvious tourists who didn’t speak any Italian, we were treated with the utmost respect as if we were locals. Our jackets were taken, the staff spoke so kindly and the interiors reflected the same calm demeanour of the restaurant. With absolutely no expectation, we were even offered some sweat treats on the house after our meal which topped everything off. If I happen to be in Torino once more, I will most definitely be making the effort to visit this branch again.

reviews.author: Luca
reviews.text: Nice and elegant restaurant offering good dishes based on the local tradition, well prepared and with good and seasonal ingredients. Very polite staff. I was really disappointed to see plastic flowers on the table! This is a no go, from style and sustainability point of view and it is the main reason I gave an overall 3 stars as rating.

reviews.author: Diana
reviews.text: I went for dinner with my family and was very pleased with the choice, we had the authentic Torinese food and hospitality experience. The service is friendly and impeccable, the menu offers traditional dishes well executed and generous in quantity. We had the agnolotti, bollito and guancia cooked in Red wine and everything was so yummy and high quality. Great selection of Piemontese wines too.

reviews.author: Jeanne Neylon Decker (Traveltawk)
reviews.text: Tre Galline is classic Piemontese cuisine at its best. There's a reason this restaurant has been here forever! The service, ambiance and food are all top notch. Everything on the menu sounded so good we had trouble choosing, but were delighted with all of our choices. The agnolotti was amazing-- perfect pasta with just the right amount of sauce. The beef was also incredible-- cooked to perfection. My husband had the rabbit and was very happy. We were too full for dessert but Marina brought us a little sweet treat anyway. I will be back on my next visit to Torino for sure. Be sure to book a table --it's essential! You need to ring the bell to enter. Leonardo will welcome you in.

reviews.author: Mathilda Dembele
reviews.text: I recommend this restaurant for the food that was amazing and the atmosphere in a very animated street of the city centre. I tried the crema di piselli con verdure di stagione e formaggio di mandorle (green beans cream with mushrooms, asparagus, potatoes, almond cheese), a 10 out of 10, would go there only to try that dish again. They also have a great and rich selection of wine and nice deserts !

reviews.author: Sankari Reddy
reviews.text: Unassuming restaurant but exceptional quality. The first truly wholesome meal I have had in Turin. Real pietmontese food. Diverse wine selection - from very expensive to more affordable. Wine recommendations are excellent. Many local selections to choose from.Staff are warm and friendly and speak English. Management went out of their way - we received a complementary appetizer and zabaione - which were both excellent with complex flavours. We ordered three main dishes, one dessert, one bottle of wine and one large sparkling water which totaled €110. The veal and puréed potato with Nebbiolo red wine sauce was exquisite, the meat literally disintegrated in your mouth. The veal sausage gnocchi was cooked to perfection and the flavours were complex and satisfying. The boiled meat plate (typical pietmontese) was above expectations and I will order this next time I attend at this restaurant. It came with a selection of sauces (abundant servings) and candied fruit. For a restaurant of this quality and reputation, we left very satisfied and not hungry as with other fine dining establishments. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Carlos Ferreira
reviews.text: Excellent restaurant in old town Torino, near to the central market. IF you happen to be in daytime near the place, you will never believe how nice and pleasure it becomes by night. I recommend the agnoloti and the panacota as desert

reviews.author: Wisanu Tuntawiroon
reviews.text: I recently visited Porta Palazzo in Torino, and it was a vibrant and memorable experience. Known as one of the largest open-air markets in Europe, Porta Palazzo is a bustling hub of activity and culture. The highlights of my visit included the fascinating stone structure in the underground, which was historically used to store food. This architectural gem added a touch of ancient charm to the modern hustle and bustle of the market. The market itself is a feast for the senses, with colorful displays of fresh produce, artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and handcrafted goods. The atmosphere is lively, with vendors eagerly engaging with visitors and sharing the stories behind their products. Despite the lively atmosphere, the market can get overwhelmingly crowded, especially during peak hours. However, this is a minor criticism compared to the overall vibrant and authentic experience that Porta Palazzo offers.

reviews.author: Enzo Lopez
reviews.text: I love this market, Porta Palazzo is the heart of Turin the greater place ever the temple of food for Italians and foreigners. You can find anything in there is a marvelous place to enjoy your time in the city center and get the best most beautiful produce ever.

reviews.author: Udit Tamrakar
reviews.text: Porta Palazzo is a vibrant and expansive market that truly captures the essence of Turin's multicultural spirit. As Europe's largest open-air market, it offers an impressive array of goods—from fresh produce and meats to clothing and household items—making it a one-stop destination for both locals and tourists. The atmosphere is lively, with vendors enthusiastically engaging customers, creating an authentic and energetic shopping experience. One of the standout features is the market's diversity. Strolling through the stalls, you're treated to a mosaic of cultures, with products and foods representing various international traditions. This multicultural blend not only enriches the shopping experience but also reflects Turin's inclusive community. However, the market's bustling nature can be overwhelming, especially during peak hours. Navigating through the crowded aisles requires patience, and it's advisable to be mindful of personal belongings. Additionally, while the variety is vast, the quality of goods can vary, so discerning shoppers should take their time to select the best offerings. In summary, Porta Palazzo is a must-visit for those seeking an immersive and culturally rich market experience in Turin. Its vast selection and vibrant atmosphere make it a unique destination, though visitors should be prepared for its energetic pace.

reviews.author: Avihay Froochzad
reviews.text: Fresh fruits and vegetable market, with multicultural sellers. Keep your belonging close to you.

reviews.author: Eric Prive
reviews.text: Varied outdoor and indoor market with many fruit, veg, meat, fish and various produce stalls. Worth a visit to browse and enjoy. Big food hall with various types of cuisine is adjacent aswell for brunch or lunch or just coffee.
