name: Street Stall - St. George
address: Street Stall - St. George, Madaba, Jordan

reviews.author: Steiner Mark
reviews.text: Majestic Hilltop Church with Hidden Caves & Tower Viewpoint Discover a stunning church perched above the town, known not only for its grand architecture but also for the mysterious caves lying beneath its foundation. Climb the ancient tower for panoramic views across the entire town and surrounding landscape, a truly breathtaking experience that combines history, faith, and natural wonder. Better to visit when winter is about to begin.

reviews.author: Marina S
reviews.text: Home to the world-famous Madaba Map, St. George’s Church is a living mosaic of faith and history. Built in the late 19th century over the ruins of a Byzantine church, it houses the oldest known map of the Holy Land—crafted from millions of tiny colored stones. Known locally as كنيسة القديس جورج, this active Greek Orthodox sanctuary draws pilgrims and historians alike, standing as a bridge between ancient cartography and living worship. Its humble exterior hides a treasure that continues to shape how we see the sacred geography of the past.

reviews.author: Adrian Rodrigues
reviews.text: A lovely Church with the oldest mosaic map in the world. Unfortunately the church was under renovation when we went so most of the artworks were not in place. The main one we got to see was the Map on the floor.

reviews.author: Abdullah Widyan
reviews.text: The Church of the Map in Madaba, located in blessed Jordan. The Church of the Map is a Greek Orthodox church, famous for its mosaic map of the Holy Land—covering Palestine, Jordan, and Sinai—and dating back to the year 560 AD. The map is composed of over two million mosaic pieces and provides a vivid depiction of the natural landscape, as well as the topographical layout of cities and villages—up to 150 locations. It includes incredibly detailed elements, even down to streets and roads within cities. This mosaic map is considered one of the oldest discovered mosaic floors and the oldest original map of the Holy Land. The map stretches south to the Nile Delta, north to Sarafand in Lebanon, west to the Mediterranean Sea, and east to the city of Karak. Among the sites featured on the map are: 1. Jerusalem 2. Bethlehem 3. Hebron 4. Jericho 5. Karak 6. Mount Sinai 7. The Jordan River 8. The Nile River 9. The Mediterranean Sea 10. The Dead Sea

reviews.author: Bo
reviews.text: A nice Orthodox Church with a beautiful mosaic map on the floor. It’s open but part of it is under restoration work as well May 2025.

reviews.author: Paul Biehl
reviews.text: At Al Arabi you can get really tasty falafel and even more tasty hummus. One of the best hummus I’ve had so far. The people are very friendly, the food is fresh, and the place itself definitely has a vibe!

reviews.author: Gilbert Sagalla
reviews.text: Recommended to eat here by a local Airbnb host, very satisfied with our food. The customer service was excellent with complimentary tea and hummus, we all ordered the Arabic shawarma as was recommended by the waiter and also tried the mixed grill, delicious, quick and convenient, highly recommend the falafels too! We were all enticed with the fresh mango juice which did not disappoint,

reviews.author: Adil R
reviews.text: I came here as I was recommended highly to eat here by a local taxi driver, very satisfied with our food and place. It was all very clean. The customer service was excellent with complimentary tea and hummus was given at breakfast. I ordered the authentic local breakfast with some omlettes. They were all very nice, delicious, quick and convenient, highly recommend the falafels too!

reviews.author: D kim
reviews.text: We ordered take away Arabic schawerma meal. My some loved it. The French fried not crunch like you have in the States. Schawerma was very good.

reviews.author: Glen R
reviews.text: Quick edit: Just recovered after 48+ hrs of food poisoning, damn so not try the traditional "upside-down chicken" dish this will literally turn your insides upside-down. I had a £115 taxi ride to 3 stops to the dead Sea the morning after here and I can tell you the only dead thing my girlfriend saw was my well to live. All the attractions were ruined as I chundered my way though all of them, once I arrived my insides started to turn and I can tell you the amount of wind I had would make wind turbines jelous and gas mining crew cry. Beware this place will take a good 2-3 days off of your holiday. Good restaurant with quite a few choices! Food was a decent portion, perhaps not the baklava though... Friendly staff with quick service, not too expensive either!

reviews.author: Luiza Vieira
reviews.text: The restaurant is super cozy, the decoration is beautiful, the food is amazing and the staff is friendly. I went there with my family after a long day of walking through Petra and it was exactly what we needed. The price is fare, considering it’s all you can eat and they also offer a variety of desserts.

reviews.author: Josh Ester
reviews.text: Recommended for your meal time during your journey to the 7 wonders of the world - Petra. The ambience is unique. The food is tasty. The sweet desert is also good to try.

reviews.author: k m
reviews.text: You can eat valuable Middle East dishes by 12JD. Soft drinks need extra fee.

reviews.author: OM
reviews.text: The best place to eat in Petra! They serve lunch buffet and the food is traditional, very good and worth it! Ambience is great as well, everyone is so friendly. This place was recommended by our taxi driver that drove us from the Dead Sea and it is one not to miss

reviews.author: Florentina Badea
reviews.text: Best food experience in town! We had an absolute blast, the food was exceptional, extremely tasty, fresh and more than enough. The staff was very attentive to our needs and bringing the food at the right moment. Completely unexpected and such a great time we had. The place is lovely decorated as well with a rustic vibe, also cultural. We went there for dinner and the menu was fixed, but we really enjoyed it. Definitely recommending it!

reviews.author: Mritunjay Kumar
reviews.text: I visited Al Wadi because it’s one of the highest-rated restaurants in the Petra area, but unfortunately, my experience didn’t live up to the hype. While the location is convenient, especially for tourists visiting Petra, I felt the food and service were underwhelming. The dishes lacked the freshness and flavor I expected, especially given the strong reviews. Service was rushed but attentive. It seems like the high ratings might be more about the location and limited local options rather than the overall quality. If you’re looking for an exceptional dining experience, you might want to explore other spots or manage your expectations.

reviews.author: Sruthi Madabushi
reviews.text: This restaurant was rated as one of the best in Petra, hence we were curious to try this place. The food was really good and authentic. The atmosphere was also good, and while the town and nearby area was busy it added to the vibe of the restaurant. It’s very centrally located to the Wadi Musa town and was closely located to Petra.

reviews.author: Fahd Batayneh فهد بطاينة
reviews.text: An excellent restaurant in Petra in the downtown area with a decent menu of soups, salads, starters, local traditional and international dishes, drinks, and desserts. The restaurant is an old building that is very well designed with paintings and antiques, making it look and feel nostalgic. Food portions are enough for one person, and dishes are very tasty. The bake traditional Jordanian bread. Staff are very friendly, and can speak several main languages. They accept cash and card payment. Parking can be slightly challenging though one can park almost anywhere.

reviews.author: Anca Enache
reviews.text: Great food and atmosphere! Jeff was an amazing server that made sure that everything is perfect. The food was delicious and quick to arrive. He also show us the traditional making of tannur(local bread) as seen in the video.

reviews.author: HECTOR RAMIREZ
reviews.text: Fantastic service! Jeff took great care of us—super friendly, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect. The food was delicious and came out quickly. Highly recommend this place, especially if you get Jeff as your server!

reviews.author: Rachel Fritz
reviews.text: Convenient Stop in Petra with Great Views After walking so far into Petra, I really needed a place to eat, and this turned out to be a good option. While I don’t usually like buffets, they had some solid choices—my favorite was the pasta. I also enjoyed the chicken, though it did upset my stomach a bit (which seems to be a common buffet issue). What stood out the most was the stunning view and the super friendly service. It’s definitely more expensive than it should be, but given the remote location, I can understand the pricing. The cats added a funny and unique twist—they’re everywhere and not shy about coming up to you (or even sitting on your lap). If you’re not a fan of cats, this might not be the place for you. I also had some tea, which was nice, though I agree with others that the drinks are overpriced. That said, I enjoyed my meal and appreciated the convenience after a long day of exploring Petra.

reviews.author: Paul Ciprian
reviews.text: A decent restaurant, located in the middle of the archaeological site. It has a pleasant, shady terrace. The menu is buffet style. For me, it was important that they serve alcohol, both beer and spirits, which is not very common for a Jordanian restaurant. I stopped twice at them, as a rehydration break :) halfway through the route, both on the way to the Monastery and on the way back.

reviews.author: ahmad amarat
reviews.text: the staff were very helpful. the allowed us to have drink inside the restaurant without asking us to have lunch. it was nice overall service and atmosphere

reviews.author: Sebastian Attila Baróthy V. Baróth
reviews.text: A pleasant experience. If you are staying in the Petra Guest House then you get 20% off. Worth the visit

reviews.author: Cashflow RE Diana Lovetravel
reviews.text: We brought our own food so only order pomegranate drink.

reviews.author: mohammed Irshaed (The king of taste)
reviews.text: As a tourist guide , I always recommend my tourists to go there as it is a hidden gem of Petra . The service is amazing there , lots of options with affordable prices. It has such a unique atmosphere which makes you feel cozy and comfy especially after a long hiking day in Petra. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED .

reviews.author: Rtexal Tan
reviews.text: Pit stop at the Tomb Bar on a hot afternoon is a highlight. I call it Tomb Bar because it's really converted from an ancient Nabatean tomb. I think the official name Cave Bar sounds better though 😁 Petra beer on tap, their local Jordanian dish (different daily) is also well prepared too. 20% off between 2-4PM seems to be the current promo!

reviews.author: Eric Stander
reviews.text: Must do in Petra. Amazing beautiful cave bar. Amazing setting inside a real cave. Great drinks and cocktails. Great food. Friendly and efficient service. Nice staff. Welcoming and an amazing escape from the outside temperature.

reviews.author: Shin-Ei Taku
reviews.text: After spending 8 hours climbing up and down around the Petra site, drenched in sweat with my legs aching, I found this bar near the exit that serves locally brewed beer. It was incredibly refreshing! The place perfectly matches its name—it’s inside a cave, and the temperature difference from the outside is huge. It was such a comfortable and relaxing spot!

reviews.author: Jack M
reviews.text: Amazing place! We came twice, sitting once outside and once inside. The food was very good (burger), and the drinks were great as well (cosmo and the petra special.) Prices were fair, and the ambiance was very nice as well. Take the left side entrance to avoid the vendors!

reviews.author: Nadiya Khan
reviews.text: What a beautiful restaurant to visit! The interiors are so stunning. You just can’t keep your camera in your pocket. The food was great too — we ordered the mixed grill and a mansaf, and both were amazing. I actually found this place on Google while searching for the best restaurants in Petra, and it definitely didn’t disappoint. I'm so glad I visited — it looked even better than the pictures!

reviews.author: Alis C.
reviews.text: There are many menus here. The foods taste and presentation were good. The shop is spacious, wide and warm. I think the atmosphere must be very good if you come in the evening. The bread and dip served are very delicious. I like it very much. The shop is on the 3rd floor.

reviews.author: Dimitrije Stankovic
reviews.text: Very nice restaurant in Petra, 2 min away from the entrance of Petra. Lovely big terrace. Delicious food: my wife and I went there twice during our stay in Petra and food was great on both occasions. We took a mix of cold starters and soup + main meal (first night non-veg, another night veg moussaka) - all this was delicious. Excellent staff, great atmosphere, decent prices. We really enjoyed!

reviews.author: Bo
reviews.text: This restaurant is an absolute treasure near Petra—home-cooked Jordanian food at its finest! We had the Musakhn, lemon with mint juice, and chicken sagieh, and every bite was packed with flavor and care. The Musakhn was beautifully spiced with tender chicken and perfectly caramelized onions on warm, fresh bread. The chicken sagieh was comforting, and the lemon mint drink was so refreshing after a day of exploring. The hospitality was warm and genuine, making us feel like we were dining in a family home. If you’re anywhere near Petra, don’t miss this unforgettable experience. We arrived around 6pm and were seated immediately.

reviews.author: Jesse Lee
reviews.text: Fun facts the restaurant is actually on the third floor when we first went to the second floor. The place was empty and we thought the restaurant was close. It’s only when a busboy came down with a dirty dishes that we realized the restaurant is on the third floor nobody was there to greet us. The food was OK I was expecting more based on all the good reviews.

reviews.author: Mariam Ossama
reviews.text: Super cool place. One of the new 7 wonders of the world. Wear comfortable shoes because you will walk a lot. There are some means of transportation there like donkeys, camels and buggies. All of course with extra charge. Buying tickets is easy. Inside you can buy food, water etc and buy souvenirs.

reviews.author: Nikola Yanakiev
reviews.text: This place is absolutely stunning! A must visit wonder of the world. Definitely go to the top and appreciate the treasury from above.

reviews.author: Niraj Kaji
reviews.text: Amazing and massive, much bigger than I thought. Spread over several miles. We walked the back way from Little Petra (took the 4x4 option part of the way) which was stunning and allowed us to avoid the 800 steps to the Monestary. Wear hiking boots and I found hiking poles helpful to take strain off the knees. Note there is a tea and beverage shop at the top near the Monestary and also a full service restaurant midway, past the Treasury. We got lucky with good weather but I could see this being VERY hot during the summer. Bring lots of water. As far as timing, I would recommend a full day for the sights. We also saw Petra by night. I'm glad we did it but the show is simple. The show only lasts 30 minutes and there is time for pictures at the end.

reviews.author: Naveen B Mathew
reviews.text: We visited in the first week of April, and the weather was perfect—not too hot or too cold. The entry fee for tourists was 50 JOD. The atmosphere felt warm and welcoming, making it an enjoyable experience. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Sothy Uch
reviews.text: Amazing and breathtaking, this place is a wonderful destination for those seeking a journey through time. It's expansive, so be sure to bring appropriate hiking gear.

reviews.author: Shishira Thomas
reviews.text: Overpriced, but to be expected in the middle of the Nabatean lands in the middle of nowhere. Good service and great location. Chicken Shawarma was more fries than chicken. Water was 5 times more than a general store. If you walk ahead a little bit, you'll find water for half the price.

reviews.author: Isinsu Dogan
reviews.text: This is place is the perfect stop for a lunch after a long walk in Petra. Considering it being in a world heritage site it was surprisingly affordable and their kebab made me come back the next day, it was delicious. Staff was friendly and the setting was nice under the trees.

reviews.author: Ihar Beliauski
reviews.text: Nabatean Restaurant in Petra pleasantly surprised us, especially considering some negative reviews. The shawarma was not only delicious but also prepared swiftly, addressing any concerns about service time. While the prices leaned towards the higher side, the limited restaurant options in the area made it a convenient and satisfying choice, especially when exhaustion set in. The beautiful surrounding views added to the overall dining experience, making Nabatean Restaurant a worthwhile stop for those exploring Petra.

reviews.author: Barbara Hass
reviews.text: I had a tea on the terrace of the restaurant and was invited by the owner to a quick breakfast snack - hummus, falafel and pita bread. I really enjoyed the food, the hospitality, the conversation. I'd definitely go there again. By the way the toilets are very good in this place. The best experience I had in Jordan so far. Super clean with soap and toilet paper.

reviews.author: Ahmad Abd-Allah
reviews.text: They enforce you to make orders Bad behaviour I didn't order anything, so I didn't rate the food Prices are very high The atmosphere is great though

reviews.author: Dominica Martin
reviews.text: Lovely hotel. Staff very helpful, friendly and efficient. Very comfortable and in a great location at the entrance to Petra. So nice after a lot of walking in Petra not to have to walk far to hotel. Lovely breakfast with great choice . Cave bar atmospheric and lovely for a drink at end of day

reviews.author: Felipe Pimenta
reviews.text: We had a wonderful experience at Petra Guest House Hotel from the moment we arrived until our departure. The room was clean and cozy, providing a perfect retreat. The breakfast was impeccable, with a variety of delicious options that we thoroughly enjoyed. A highlight of our stay was the thoughtful gesture from the receptionist during our early checkout at around 6:30 AM. She prepared a breakfast box for us since we wouldn't have time to sit down for a meal, and it truly made our day. We were so grateful for her kindness. We highly recommend Petra Guest House Hotel to our friends and family. It's a place where you feel valued and well-cared for.

reviews.author: Mike Belgue
reviews.text: Petra Guest House was a wonderful stay. It is immediately next door to the Petra Visitor Centre and entrance into the park. It is very convenient and nothing was better than an ice cold (overpriced) Petra draft lager on their Cave Bar patio immediately after a long day of exploring! Staff were very friendly and helpful. Breakfast buffet was a great spread and delicious. Our room was nothing special but it was clean and the bed was comfy.

reviews.author: Badia Ab
reviews.text: The perfect place to say to visit Petra and to get around . Mohamed is amazing, really helpful with the best advices and very welcoming. Thank you so much for your help. Rooms are spacious and excellent breakfast. The French Moroccan girls 🤗

reviews.author: Christian Borggio
reviews.text: I had a great stay at this hotel. The place was comfortable, clean, and well-located for visiting Petra. Mohamed, the host, was incredibly helpful, providing great tips on how to explore Petra in one day. His hospitality made my stay even more enjoyable. Highly recommend this hotel for anyone visiting Petra!

reviews.author: Tade (Ltee)
reviews.text: Amazing cooking class dinner—fun, hands-on experience with friendly hosts, tasty food, great vibes, unforgettable night!

reviews.author: steve toghill
reviews.text: Absolutely fabulous evening spent cooking authentic Jordanian food with the best chef and teacher and then eating the scrumptious meal we cooked. And he shares his recipes so you can try it out at home. A must do thing to try in Petra!

reviews.author: Tina Keeble
reviews.text: We had a brilliant fun evening at Petra Kitchen under the wise guidance of Chef Reda and his team. We were greeted with a fresh juice - perfect after a day hiking in Petra. Dressed in aprons and chef hats, we got chopping. Chef Reda and his team prepped some items in advance so we could make, between us, a fantastic menu - soup, hot and cold mezze dishes and delicious Magluba for main course. The team were fun, professional and we had a great evening cooking and chatting with like minded folk. Doesn’t matter if you can cook or not, you can learn. After prep we all sat down on a long table to enjoy the results. Thoroughly recommend it. Jordanian food is delicious and we loved this meal. And you get the recipes all printed to take home. My favourite was probably the baba ganouj and fatteh. If you’re in Petra do this one evening, it’s great.

reviews.author: Campbell Wolford
reviews.text: We had an amazing cooking class with just the two of us and the head chef. The food was fantastic and very fun to make. The best part however was getting to learn about Jordanian culture and life. This is a must do activity in Petra!

reviews.author: Damian Borges
reviews.text: We had a wonderful time at Petra Kitchen tonight. Chef Reda guided us expertly through the preparation of various Jordanian delicacies including a spectacular mansaf. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Tade (Ltee)
reviews.text: Amazing cooking class dinner—fun, hands-on experience with friendly hosts, tasty food, great vibes, unforgettable night!

reviews.author: Seaf Raja
reviews.text: A very nice hotel located very close to the Petra Gate. The rooms are new and clean. It is one of the most beautiful hotels in the city. There are swimming pools, a Turkish bath, a bar, and a wonderful restaurant.

reviews.author: Mohamed Albargothi
reviews.text: This place is such a fantastic spot to visit! The mountain views are absolutely gorgeous, and I had a wonderful time soaking it all in. The services were amazing too—everyone was so friendly and helpful, which made my experience even better. I definitely recommend checking it out!💯

reviews.author: Zaid Modhi Mansour
reviews.text: Great hotel, walking distance to the main site. Rooms were clean and spacious, staff were very friendly. Highly recommended! Would definitely visit again

reviews.author: Farouk Mufti
reviews.text: Renovated in 2025, this hotel is all you need for your stay in Petra.. Clean, Hospitable, and great location

reviews.author: Rana Qadi
reviews.text: The hotel was a great experience especially that it is renovated .. the location the colors the brightness the freshness like no other ..

reviews.author: Denny Hamonangan Chan
reviews.text: This resto is just a few meters from the Petra Visitor Center. The food was great, and the price was affordable. The server was friendly, and he even served me a kind of herbal tea while my food was being prepared. It is highly recommended if you are nearby and looking for authentic Beduin cuisine.

reviews.author: Γαλνανατ Πυχομχιτ
reviews.text: When you walk out of Petra Just one minute You will find this restaurant. I'd like to recommend you to try it. That is, everything that is served tastes not bad, is delicious, and is worth the price paid. As for the rice menu, it is soft and delicious. You will feel very sorry. If you just walk by, highly recommend.

reviews.author: Elisa Renda
reviews.text: Excellent food at convenient price in a typical.bedouine setting. Service was speedy and very accurate and we enjoyed genuine local dishes with the freshest ingredients. Coming back is a good option since we coul only try a few dishes of the wide menu! Good for a snack or a complete meal.

reviews.author: Samuel Ribeiro
reviews.text: Terrible experience — not recommended. We had a very disappointing experience at Red Cave Restaurant in Petra. The portions were extremely small and poorly served. The prices on the bill were rounded up from the ones on the menu, and we were charged extra items we didn’t order. After we paid, the staff insisted we pay an additional 10% “government fee”, which does not exist, plus 5% for paying by card, also completely made up. This kind of behavior feels dishonest and left us with a very bad impression. Sadly, we cannot recommend this place. There are many better and more honest options around Petra.

reviews.author: Natalia Shirin David-Vaz
reviews.text: One of the worst food experiences of our lives. The shawarma chicken was cold and hard. Dry as the Jordanian desert. The burgers came out of the supermarket freezer section and the one dessert we ordered was quite soggy. The fries smelled and tasted of stale oil as well. I informed the owner of it while paying the bill and he didn’t even ask what the issues were. He just said that I was the first one to complain. It was overall the worst. I left hungry and the others just ate because we were so exhausted and hungry after the trek in Petra earlier that day.

reviews.author: Denny Hamonangan Chan

reviews.author: Ethu Crorie
reviews.text: We received great service from Yasser from Egypt. He could not be any friendlier. Tried the mansaf and the mixed grill.

reviews.author: Dhrubo Mistry
reviews.text: "Stopped by for lunch and was blown away by the quality! I had the grilled chicken sandwich with a lemon mint drink—super fresh and full of flavor. The bread was warm, the filling generous, and the drink was incredibly refreshing. Great spot for a wholesome meal."

reviews.author: kullan at
reviews.text: Delicious food, excellent hospitality. I do not understand why they have 3.6 point. They deserve better

reviews.author: Rachel Fritz
reviews.text: Unexpected Gem with Delicious Kebabs I stumbled upon this restaurant accidentally while looking for another spot, but the owner’s warm invitation convinced me to give it a try. I ordered the chicken kebab, and it did not disappoint—absolutely delicious! Sitting outside on the tourism street was a nice touch, though there were quite a few flies and some very persistent cats. Thankfully, I like cats, and the owner made an effort to shoo them away. I also tried the lime and lemon juice, which was incredibly fresh and tasty. I only wish there was more of it and that the mint had been strained better. Despite reading reviews about overcharging, I didn’t feel that way. While there was a service fee, it seems to be the norm while traveling. Overall, I recommend this spot, especially for the kebabs—they were fantastic!

reviews.author: Shrabon Biswas
reviews.text: Every time I visit, I make sure to order the soup of the day. You can tell it’s homemade with care—thick, aromatic, and served piping hot. The combination of their grilled veggie salad and a bowl of soup makes for a satisfying and healthy lunch.

name: Street Stall - Little Petra
address: Street Stall - Little Petra, Petra, Jordan

reviews.author: Ali Steele
reviews.text: A must do when in Jordan. Prepare for large crowds, camels and horses racing by and for some locals selling their wares.

reviews.author: Sharaf Harb
reviews.text: It needs more care from ministry of tourism and to watch carefully from the police to avoid treating tourists wrongfully way!!!

reviews.author: Sachin Chugh
reviews.text: Kind of a let down for a 7 wonders of the world needs better management and regulations control of various activities especially pricing of standard products of not controlled it might lose its place on tourist maps

reviews.author: Mohammad Naeem
reviews.text: Magic area in petra

reviews.author: Loveleen Chahal
reviews.text: Petra ...

reviews.author: Gary Rogers
reviews.text: A beautiful slot-canyon that reveals something new around every turn. There are ancient carvings along the way, remains of Roman road, and water drainage work. The Treasury is the prime objective but it is made far more impressive by the dramatic approach.

reviews.author: Paul Ciprian
reviews.text: The first interesting part of the archaeological site. From the Visitor center to the entrance to this impressive canyon, you have to walk about 2.5 km (there are a lot of locals who offer mules for rent). The canyon is slightly more than 1000 m long and ends at the foot of the impressive Treasury. The vertical walls of red stone are impressive. The road is flat and easy to travel. Very crowded, there are hundreds of tourists, some coming, others leaving.

reviews.author: Shahtaj Noor
reviews.text: Walking through the 1.2 km narrow Siq(Arabic of canyon) is like stepping back in time, surrounded by history and the impressive natural beauty of the rock formations. The walk through this magical corridor, as it snakes its way towards the hidden city, is one full of anticipation for the wonders ahead. I will recommend to take the walk instead of buggy as it’s truly a unique and unforgettable experience of visiting Petra. Every turn will make you excited if it’s the turn when treasury can be seen. It’s around 35/40 minutes while you go but may take longer time during return as the it’s bit steeper in some places. Take water bottles with you. And please please take a good guide because every spot, stone or curve has some significance and good guide can give you better information.

reviews.author: Ahmad Abd-Allah
reviews.text: 1.25 Kilometres between colorful canyon rocks 2100 years ago Nabataeans used this trail to go to Petra their hidden city

reviews.author: Francis Alba
reviews.text: Probably the most breath taking hike I have ever done with a beautiful end after :) This is also the only shaded part of Petra. Bring a wide brimmed hat, sunscreen and maybe even a parasol if going in the summer months

reviews.author: Jesse Lee
reviews.text: We were so lucky to come during the low season. It was not crowded and we got to spend time to enjoy the site and take lots of good pictures without people getting in the way. Best time to come is after tour groups in the morning so early afternoon and late afternoon is much better than first thing in the morning. If you can handle it, take the bus to the back entrance and walk to the front. Be aware there are over 1000+ steps up and down for the hike. Take the challenge.

reviews.author: Caroline Crutchley
reviews.text: Loved the view from balcony area it's 10 dinar to climb up. Go in morning for the best light.

reviews.author: Shishira Thomas
reviews.text: Magical! The route through the Siq to get here is amazing! And what an incredible feat of the Nabateans! You have to see it to believe it. I also recommend "Petra by Night." It's the best light show I've seen in the world. It's a separate ticket but worth every penny. Also recommend "Why Not" Cafe (pictures included) just after the treasury for their fantastic orange juice! I've never been a fan of orange juice, but after this, I think I've been converted.

reviews.author: Gary Rogers
reviews.text: Talk about a bucket-list experience! This is monumental in size and the entire setting at the end of the Siq slot-canyon makes the entire experience so dramatic. Everyone wants their video of the approach from the slot-canyon, here is mine.

reviews.author: Joon Alino
reviews.text: Absolutely breathtaking! Visiting The Treasury in Petra was an unforgettable experience. From the moment we walked through the Siq and saw the stunning façade emerge, it felt like stepping into another world. The carvings are incredibly detailed, and the sheer size of the structure is mind-blowing. The site is well-organized, and there are plenty of guides available if you want to learn more about the history. We opted for a guided tour, which added so much depth to our visit. The early morning light made the sandstone glow beautifully, and the crowds were manageable. A few tips: Wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and be prepared for a lot of walking. Also, beware of the vendors and camel ride offers—they can be persistent but are generally friendly. If you can, experience Petra by Night—the candlelit Treasury is absolutely magical! Overall, this is a must-visit destination and worth every bit of the journey. Highly recommended!

name: Street Stall - Wadi Musa
address: Street Stall - Wadi Musa, Petra, Jordan

reviews.author: Mariam Ossama
reviews.text: Super cool place. One of the new 7 wonders of the world. Wear comfortable shoes because you will walk a lot. There are some means of transportation there like donkeys, camels and buggies. All of course with extra charge. Buying tickets is easy. Inside you can buy food, water etc and buy souvenirs.

reviews.author: Nikola Yanakiev
reviews.text: This place is absolutely stunning! A must visit wonder of the world. Definitely go to the top and appreciate the treasury from above.

reviews.author: Niraj Kaji
reviews.text: Amazing and massive, much bigger than I thought. Spread over several miles. We walked the back way from Little Petra (took the 4x4 option part of the way) which was stunning and allowed us to avoid the 800 steps to the Monestary. Wear hiking boots and I found hiking poles helpful to take strain off the knees. Note there is a tea and beverage shop at the top near the Monestary and also a full service restaurant midway, past the Treasury. We got lucky with good weather but I could see this being VERY hot during the summer. Bring lots of water. As far as timing, I would recommend a full day for the sights. We also saw Petra by night. I'm glad we did it but the show is simple. The show only lasts 30 minutes and there is time for pictures at the end.

reviews.author: Naveen B Mathew
reviews.text: We visited in the first week of April, and the weather was perfect—not too hot or too cold. The entry fee for tourists was 50 JOD. The atmosphere felt warm and welcoming, making it an enjoyable experience. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Sothy Uch
reviews.text: Amazing and breathtaking, this place is a wonderful destination for those seeking a journey through time. It's expansive, so be sure to bring appropriate hiking gear.

name: Al Qattar Camp
address: Al Qattar Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

name: Bait Ali Camp
address: Bait Ali Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Ilona Jankowska
reviews.text: Beautiful lodge located in the middle of a desert. Stunning views, including sunset viewpoint on a hill above pool. Very friendly, welcoming staff.

reviews.author: Fahd Batayneh فهد بطاينة
reviews.text: While this is one of many many lodges and camps in the Wadi Rum area, it is one of the finest in the place. The lodge is located very close to the main road, thus you can drive your vehicle right to the entrance of the lodge. The road is a few 100 meters long, and is a muddy road. They have a reception that is well-staffed, and has a decent books library. They have many rooms of different sizes. While being simple rooms, they are spacious and well-maintained. They have an on-site restaurant and a cafeteria. The food here is very tasty and well-cooked. Compared to some other camps tried out, their food stands high. This camp offers tours and boogies, and they can advise you on the different locations one can visit. The food area is outdoor during the warm season, and indoor during the cold season. They have a decent swimming pool. They also have a short hiking trail that takes you to the mountain adjacent to the camp with lovely views to Wadi Rum. Try to have a conversation with the locals inside the camp; mainly Osama. The locals are extremely smart and very kind.

reviews.author: Guzel
reviews.text: The place is absolutely amazing!! The stuff, the food, the atmosphere. They also organized us the trip to desert, and let ua check out later. We also had a stunning stargazing activity in the hotel. Be sure to swim in the pool, it’s clean and nice to refresh after the time in the desert. Definitely will come back again!

reviews.author: alaa dahabreh
reviews.text: I’ve visited several times before, but this time the experience truly stood out. Everything felt elevated — from the cleanliness and the quality of the food to the warm, welcoming atmosphere. I absolutely loved it and will definitely be coming back again soon. The power of desert and mountains are phenomenal.

reviews.author: Mais Sider
reviews.text: - Bad service, rusted furniture, facilities need maintenance and very unprofessional staff. - Only hands towels are offered. - Jeep safari and buggies cost 2 or 3 times higher than what they are meant to be. - Good food and spacious rooms.

name: Bedouin Camp Dinner
address: Bedouin Camp Dinner, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Tamara Neiroukh
reviews.text: We recently went on a trip to Wadi Rum in Jordan and stayed at the Wadi Rum Bedouin Camp in these amazing bubble-like tents. The experience was absolutely incredible! The place was spotless, and the hospitality from the hosts was outstanding. Everyone we met was so respectful, and the food was delicious. They really go above and beyond to make sure you have everything you need. We had such a wonderful time, and the sleep was incredibly comfortable with a very clean room. Watching the sunset and sunrise was absolutely breathtaking. You can also ride camels and discover many things we’d never heard of before. Everything was so beautiful and unique. If you’re looking for a fantastic getaway, I highly recommend visiting this place.

reviews.author: Sherif Ashraf
reviews.text: I don't know how the stars system for hotels are decided but this is a 5 star hotel. Very clean rooms, very high quality, AC, nice shower, very comfortable bed. You can see amazing views of stars and sunset and mountains from the comfort of your bed. The food in dinner and breakfast was delicious. The staff are extremely friendly and polite. We did the 6 hour jeep tour, it was a ton of fun and super nice places, the tour guide was amazing and Wadi Rum by itself is very special. Overall such an awesome experience. I will come back again somehow.

reviews.author: Tara Bennett
reviews.text: Stayed with friends and was beyond impressed with Wadi Rum Bedouin Camp. Dinner and breakfast were offered and both were excellent. We spent time before dinner sitting around the fire with the camp owners after getting chilly on our 3 hour jeep tour of the Wadi Rum sights. Our tour guide was knowledgeable and friendly. We had the front row tents vs. the back row domes, and were impressed by the size, by the bathrooms and showers, and by the location. We enjoyed the sunset from our covered porch on the tent. The beds were comfortable, and the view from bed over the Wadi Rum desert was beautiful. Got up early to watch the sun rise over our camp and watch the light hit the rocks turning them deep red.

reviews.author: Adrienne Crozat
reviews.text: This is a wonderful smaller camp in Wadi Rum in a gorgeous location. We stayed in one of the tent-style rooms, and it was clean and very comfortable, with sufficient outlets to charge phones. The view from the large windows was amazing, and we really appreciated having a nice deck to sit on and read and enjoy the beautiful view. The bathroom was large and clean with a very good shower and even a hair dryer. The common areas were also very comfortable and well decorated. The night we stayed was chilly, so we especially appreciated the fire places and hot tea. The food was very good and fresh as well. Finally, the staff was incredibly kind, and we felt that we were being welcomed into their home. Mohammed patiently answered all our questions and made sure we were well taken care of, and we received a great jeep tour from Hassan. I highly recommend this camp and will absolutely stay here again.

reviews.author: Gin Greg
reviews.text: Amazing camp! Mohammad, Hasan and Ahmad are really incredible people! If you wanna feel real bedouin vibes but in comfortable conditions and see beautiful clear night stars, stars gazing and meet nice local people you should do this camp.

name: Bedouin Lifestyle Camp
address: Bedouin Lifestyle Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Promise Land Glass
reviews.text: What an awesome experience! I was a last minute addition and I was accommodated no problem. I was able to join up with a tour that had just started and fell in with them seamlessly. The locations they took us to were beautiful and away from crowds. Lunch and the teas throughout were great. We had a gorgeous view for sunset, then returned to our camp out in the desert where a delicious zarb dinner was prepared for us. Afterwards music was played around the fire and of course, more tea. After the group broke for the night I spent time on my balcony stargazing and enjoying the beautiful night sky out in the remote desert. This is a great crew and you'd make a great decision to spend your Wadi Rum adventure with them!

reviews.author: Daniel Benjamin
reviews.text: Staying at Bedouin Lifestyle Camp was the highlight of our trip to Jordan! From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with warm hospitality and felt like part of the Bedouin family. The camp is beautifully set in the heart of Wadi Rum, offering stunning desert views and a peaceful escape from the world. The accommodations were comfortable and authentic, giving us a real taste of Bedouin culture while still providing modern comforts. The food was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and made with love. The activities were incredible! The jeep tour took us through breathtaking landscapes, hidden canyons, and famous rock formations, while the camel ride at sunrise was an unforgettable experience. Evenings around the fire with traditional music and stories under a sky full of stars made this stay truly magical. If you’re looking for an authentic, well-organized, and welcoming desert adventure, Bedouin Lifestyle Camp is the perfect place. We can’t wait to return!

reviews.author: Anthony Malandin
reviews.text: We chose a 2 day tour it was great ! Beautiful views, great camp and very helpful and friendly staff. Also show us the authentic lifestyle of the Bedouins. Definitely will recommend !

reviews.author: Samet Sahin
reviews.text: What a time! I stayed at Bedouin Lifestyle Camp for 3 nights. Due to conflicts in Middle East, there were almost no tourists. I had the whole camp for myself. In my first night, I stayed alone with the local Bedouine guy Rijal. He made us amazing food, he doesn’t speak English but we had no problems. I also did a 2 hours jeep tour with Aekrem and his children. It was very fun. I recommend it. 4 hours could be too much though. There are electricity in the tents. But no connection. There are men/women bathrooms in a seperate building. You can also take shower. It is more than enough given that it is in the middle of the desert. Tents are not windproof. And trust me, it gets TOO cold and TOO windy. I had to sleep with my hoodie, two blankets and still woke up in the middle of the night because of the cold and wind. Beware. There are few camps in the sight, but they are far away that you feel totally alone. You can see all the stars in the night and it was fascinating! Wow. The owner is friendly and speaks English fluently. So you can always get some help from him. They provide free camp-village-visitor center trips, unless you ask for some optional trips that are paid. So overall, that was a very good experience. I’m very glad to make it. Pro tip: Get a book and climb upon a cave and read it there.

reviews.author: Jan Hron
reviews.text: A very wonderful experience. Everthing was great, a very kind driver to tasty food, nice clean tents amd of course a magnificent desert itself. I strongly recommend.

reviews.author: SONICK THUKKANI
reviews.text: Wadi Rum may be a desert, but it's far from ordinary. This incredible landscape carries centuries of history — once a vital trade route linking Iran, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia. With its dramatic red sands, towering rock formations, and wide-open silence, it's a place that leaves a lasting impression. Entry is free with the Jordan Pass, and once inside, a Jeep tour is a must. I highly recommend the 4-hour tour — it hits all the major highlights, gives you time to sip herbal tea in a local Bedouin village, and includes some adrenaline-pumping rides through the sand dunes. Our driver made the dune drifting part a blast — we couldn’t stop smiling! If you're planning to stay overnight (and you should!), book a tent inside the protected area. Watching the sunset fade into a night full of stars is a surreal experience. Don’t miss the stargazing tour — the desert sky here is unbelievably clear. Dinner is another highlight — a traditional meal slow-cooked underground in the sand for over three hours. The flavor and the experience both are unforgettable. Wadi Rum is more than just a desert — it’s an experience of nature, history, and Bedouin hospitality all in one. Absolutely worth the visit!

reviews.author: Vijay Kumar
reviews.text: Wadi Rum, also known as the Valley of the Moon, offers an awe-inspiring desert experience. The vast expanse of red sand dunes, towering sandstone mountains, and unique rock formations create a surreal and captivating environment. The area’s natural beauty has made it a popular filming location for movies like Lawrence of Arabia and The Martian. ￼ The protected area is rich in history, with petroglyphs and inscriptions dating back thousands of years, showcasing the region’s cultural significance. Visitors can explore the desert through various activities such as jeep tours, camel rides, and hiking, often guided by local Bedouins who share their knowledge and traditions. While the landscape is undeniably stunning, it’s important to choose reputable tour operators to ensure a respectful and environmentally conscious experience. Facilities are basic, so come prepared for the desert conditions. Overall, Wadi Rum is a must-visit destination for those seeking natural beauty and a glimpse into Jordan’s rich heritage.

reviews.author: Dip
reviews.text: Best desert experience ever. Amazing natural beauty. If you need to make a choice between Petra and Wadi Run. Best to do Wadi rum safari. Sleeping in a tent is ok. The tent we stayed in was a deluxe tent, more like 1 star. Dinner was good. Breakfast was a total dispointment. It's better to stay somewhere else

reviews.author: Alex Bezrukov
reviews.text: I love Wadi Rum. I often come here with my family on weekends to spend a night at one of the camps and a day riding in a 4x4 to visit the amazing sites Wadi Rum has to offer. From cupcake-shaped mountains to beautiful sandy landscapes and ancient sites with rock carvings and inscriptions, there are so many things to see and do. It is a must-visit destination, along with Petra and the Dead Sea.

reviews.author: Sammy Rodrigo
reviews.text: Loved Wadi Rum! Beautiful desert with lots of locals that take you on tours. We did a 3-hour afternoon jeep tour and loved it. We saw camels walking around the area and lots of little tents for people to stay over night

name: Captain’s Desert Camp
address: Captain’s Desert Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Kordonkar Tamka
reviews.text: The rooms were not clean, which was disappointing. Additionally, this camp is not located in the heart of Wadi Rum — it’s more of a starting point. In the actual Wadi Rum desert, there is no cell signal, whereas here there is, which indicates the location is still on the outskirts. Unfortunately, the stars are not clearly visible from the camp, which takes away from the full desert experience. While the food was decent, the presence of numerous mosquitoes made the stay uncomfortable. Overall, I would not recommend this place.

reviews.author: Hebah Obaid
reviews.text: Great place. The food was amazing, call them when you make reservations for a better price. If you want a cool room go for the cave room they tend to be cooler on hot days we tried both the panorama and the cave. It was a great experience, the employees made it even better

reviews.author: Fadi Naim
reviews.text: I loved Captain's Desert Camp for several reasons: - the room was very neat, cozy and decent, beyond what I was expecting - the place itself is very lovely and cozy - the staff is friendly and helpful - the accomocation prices are very reasonable, knowing that the rooms are in pretty good conditions My only negative comment is that the shower glass panel is not that wide, so the floor gets wet easily. This can be improved. It was a very memorable stay and I totally recommend it to anyone going to Wadi Rum.

reviews.author: Dana Abdullah
reviews.text: A very bad and very disappointing experience at this camp. From the moment we arrived, the staff were extremely unwelcoming and disrespectful. Even something as simple as parking became an issue due to their rude and unhelpful attitude. Instead of hospitality, we were met with hostility, which made the entire visit unpleasant. I do not recommend this place to anyone looking for a positive and enjoyable experience. The management should seriously reconsider how they treat guests if they want to improve their reputation.

reviews.author: bayan abunijem
reviews.text: Captain Desert Camp is absolutely amazing!! The camp is sooo beautiful and everything was great! The camp is a little more on the calm side. Everyone was amazing and customer service was super friendly. The room we stayed in was great!! Spacious with AC. the food was the best part!! It was so so soooo good!!!

name: Desert Horizon Camp
address: Desert Horizon Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

name: Desert Moon Camp
address: Desert Moon Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Ryan Smith
reviews.text: Our first time in Wadi Rum and Rum Magic Nights made the experience so much better. The location and tent were already outstanding, we had the tents with AC and private showers which was a plus. The activities were amazing, we did half day (4 hours) exploring the desert then finished the day with a camel ride under the sunset. And lastly the food, this was some of the best I had whilst in Jordan, better than some 5 Star Hotels we stayed in, especially the Bedouin style dinner. Overall it was a Very peaceful place and the staff were the best. I would recommend a minimum of 2x nights here to be able to absorb everything in and make the most of it!

reviews.author: Holly Dixon
reviews.text: This desert camp in Wadi Rum has everything you need, including really nice service from the staff and a generous buffet dinner demonstrating traditional Bedouin cooking! But we especially enjoyed the sunset desert 4x4 tour with our driver Aziz! His friendly conversation, really enjoyable driving and local knowledge of Wadi Rum was a highlight of our stay in the desert! If you’re staying at Rum Magic Nights make sure to book a 4x4 tour through them!

reviews.author: Colbert PhotoStudio
reviews.text: Absolutely magical experience at Rum Magic Nights! The Zarb dinner was out of this world—perfectly seasoned, slow-cooked underground, and bursting with flavor. And don’t miss the freshly baked pita bread at breakfast—warm, fluffy, and straight from the fire. Truly the best way to start your day in the desert! The camp itself is stunning, with clean, comfortable tents and surprisingly strong internet—a real luxury in the middle of Wadi Rum. We were able to relax under the stars, upload photos, and stay connected with no issues. If you’re curious what the experience looks like, I filmed a video during our stay—just go to YouTube and search “Magical Adventure at Rum Magic Nights” to see the magic for yourself! Highly recommend this camp for anyone visiting Wadi Rum. We’ll definitely be back!

reviews.author: Haru Ish
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our one night stay here. Very nice location in the middle of Wadi Rum desert. Room is cozy, nice food, and service. You can enjoy spectacular view and sunset. There is a friendly cat which is huge bonus for me.

reviews.author: Lauren Zwicker
reviews.text: Our stay at Rum Magic Nights was magic. They were so friendly and welcoming, the trucks were waiting for us in the village to drive us to the camp, the Zarb meal was ready for us on our arrival and was so delicious- tender slow cooked Smokey lamb and chicken, potatoes and rice, hummus, shrak. For those that were interested, they taught us a line dance after dinner which was very wholesome and fun. We then sipped tea and told stories around the fire under the amazing dessert stars. The room was clean and comfortable, with working heat pumps and a full bathroom. Wifi was strong and worked everywhere. Will definitely plan to return!

reviews.author: Tinkara Lečnik
reviews.text: Very good falafel, the best in the village. The man fried them fresh. We payed 5.5 jd for falafel, pita, hummus and 2 teas. Definetly would recommend.

reviews.author: Paweł Klempka
reviews.text: Amazing place! Staff is very friendly and welcoming. Falafel was delicious. Best prices in the whole village and the atmosphere is much better than at the main street. Loved it :)

reviews.author: Bryce Clothier
reviews.text: Delicious falafels and a friendly host. Great spot for food in the village.

reviews.author: Alessandra Falcone
reviews.text: Why this place sponsoring the videos above with cruelty on animals is still open? YOJ HAVE TO CLOSE NOW!

reviews.author: Brooks Matthew Benefiel
reviews.text: Really Good Falafel

reviews.author: تجربة عزت
reviews.text: One of the most impressive and inclusive desert camps I’ve ever visited! I had an unforgettable experience at Rahayeb Camp. The place is not only incredibly well-organized and clean, but what truly sets it apart is their exceptional accessibility. As someone who uses a wheelchair, I was amazed to see how thoughtfully they’ve designed the camp — every detail is wheelchair-friendly. What blew my mind is that they are the only camp in the world (yes, the world!) with a custom-built ramp that allows wheelchair users to board a pickup truck for a desert tour. It’s something I never imagined possible, and they made it happen with so much care and professionalism. The team was beyond kind, respectful, and genuinely passionate about creating a comfortable experience for everyone. I felt 100% welcome, safe, and relaxed the entire time. This is more than just a camp — it’s a symbol of true inclusion. If you or someone you know is looking for a magical desert escape that doesn’t compromise on accessibility, Al Hay B Camp is the place to go. Thank you to the amazing team for making this dream a reality! I’ll definitely be back

reviews.author: K8 Strickland
reviews.text: Newly updated brighter dining areas, sitting areas, front office. The camp location is protected within mountains. Comfortable beds in large tents. We noticed a slight plumbing problem and the staff instantly switched us to another room. Very accommodating and friendly staff. We took the stargazing tour with Atallah who obviously loves Wadi Rum. It was an outstanding, peaceful, quiet experience. While we saw a few shooting stars and identified constellations, Atallah built a small fire from brush, and served us hot herbal tea. Grandson loved it and drank 3 servings. Highly recommended. The next day, we took a camel ride with our young children. The guide was a mature 14 year old who explained desert formation and gave us the names and ages of our 4 camels. Wonderful experience. Overall, the accommodations and the staff were fantastic! A top experience in our repeat visit to Jordan! Suggestion - park close to the main road and the staff will come take you the short distance to the camp. City cars aren’t made for desert sand.

reviews.author: A L
reviews.text: Can't say it was an awful stay, but it wasn't the best either. Problems: - 2 of the 3 nights we stayed, there was a large party (around 150 people). These are parties for the locals not guests. Loud music went from 6pm to 11pm (and crowd only quiets down after 12am). Dinner was nice but chaotic due to the crowd. - Tours were disappointing and we were charged more than their website stated. For the jeep tours, they essentially just drive you around with very minimal explanation of the place. They also ended up cutting a couple of tours short (we paid for the full time). - Staff were nice, but were unhelpful at times. In the evening, they put off any requests until after dinner. Even when we ran out of toilet paper, we had to wait. They were also not too helpful when it comes to giving information about the tour options , it was really hard to understand what you would get out of each tour when booking. (Probably partly due to language barrier) Pros: - We stayed at the mini suite, which was very spacious, and has an aircon. - They were flexible, whether that is booking tours or providing lunch. - Decent price for room including breakfast and dinner

reviews.author: Issa Na
reviews.text: The camp is a beautiful and peaceful place with amazing scenery and a great atmosphere. However, the hygiene and cleanliness could be improved to make the stay even better.

reviews.author: Rocco Costa
reviews.text: We spent three days at this wonderful camp. The staff worked really hard to make the stay enjoyable and regularly served delicious meals. It is really impressive what they were able to offer and the quality of the camp, especially with its remote location. The tents are especially nice and cozy. I was amazed they could provide air-conditioning and hot water using their solar grid. The wadi outside the camp looks like another planet. Would definitely stay here again.

name: Rum Gate Camp
address: Rum Gate Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: SONICK THUKKANI
reviews.text: Wadi Rum may be a desert, but it's far from ordinary. This incredible landscape carries centuries of history — once a vital trade route linking Iran, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia. With its dramatic red sands, towering rock formations, and wide-open silence, it's a place that leaves a lasting impression. Entry is free with the Jordan Pass, and once inside, a Jeep tour is a must. I highly recommend the 4-hour tour — it hits all the major highlights, gives you time to sip herbal tea in a local Bedouin village, and includes some adrenaline-pumping rides through the sand dunes. Our driver made the dune drifting part a blast — we couldn’t stop smiling! If you're planning to stay overnight (and you should!), book a tent inside the protected area. Watching the sunset fade into a night full of stars is a surreal experience. Don’t miss the stargazing tour — the desert sky here is unbelievably clear. Dinner is another highlight — a traditional meal slow-cooked underground in the sand for over three hours. The flavor and the experience both are unforgettable. Wadi Rum is more than just a desert — it’s an experience of nature, history, and Bedouin hospitality all in one. Absolutely worth the visit!

reviews.author: Vijay Kumar
reviews.text: Wadi Rum, also known as the Valley of the Moon, offers an awe-inspiring desert experience. The vast expanse of red sand dunes, towering sandstone mountains, and unique rock formations create a surreal and captivating environment. The area’s natural beauty has made it a popular filming location for movies like Lawrence of Arabia and The Martian. ￼ The protected area is rich in history, with petroglyphs and inscriptions dating back thousands of years, showcasing the region’s cultural significance. Visitors can explore the desert through various activities such as jeep tours, camel rides, and hiking, often guided by local Bedouins who share their knowledge and traditions. While the landscape is undeniably stunning, it’s important to choose reputable tour operators to ensure a respectful and environmentally conscious experience. Facilities are basic, so come prepared for the desert conditions. Overall, Wadi Rum is a must-visit destination for those seeking natural beauty and a glimpse into Jordan’s rich heritage.

reviews.author: Dip
reviews.text: Best desert experience ever. Amazing natural beauty. If you need to make a choice between Petra and Wadi Run. Best to do Wadi rum safari. Sleeping in a tent is ok. The tent we stayed in was a deluxe tent, more like 1 star. Dinner was good. Breakfast was a total dispointment. It's better to stay somewhere else

reviews.author: Alex Bezrukov
reviews.text: I love Wadi Rum. I often come here with my family on weekends to spend a night at one of the camps and a day riding in a 4x4 to visit the amazing sites Wadi Rum has to offer. From cupcake-shaped mountains to beautiful sandy landscapes and ancient sites with rock carvings and inscriptions, there are so many things to see and do. It is a must-visit destination, along with Petra and the Dead Sea.

reviews.author: Sammy Rodrigo
reviews.text: Loved Wadi Rum! Beautiful desert with lots of locals that take you on tours. We did a 3-hour afternoon jeep tour and loved it. We saw camels walking around the area and lots of little tents for people to stay over night

name: Rum Stars Camp
address: Rum Stars Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Ric Cook
reviews.text: Rum Stars provided the perfect experience when visiting the Wadi Rum. First, taken to their office for some beautiful tea. All our bags were taken to the camp while our driver and guide, the fantastic Mohammed, took us to visit the Fig tree of Lawrence of Arabia. Throughout the day we were taken to various sites around the Wadi Rum until we were told to go through a canyon and Mohammed would meet us on the other side. Once we went through, Mohammed had prepared us a full lunch spread: galayet, feta and corn, endless bread, we couldn't have asked for more. Mohammed never rushed us, completing the trip at our pace. We rested until we were ready to move on. Continuing with the sites, we eventually had the opportunity to do sandboarding! Such a cool experience. Finally on day 1 we were driven to a perfect view of the sunset in Wadi Rum. Once we were done, Mohammed drove us back to the camp, where all our bags were ready for us. We were given some more tea and saw the bedouins make Zarb, cooking under the ground. It was such an amazing experience. After dinner, we spent the evening watching the stars, while hanging out with the bedouins, having conversations about bedouin life and enjoying tea around the fire. During the day, I asked Mohammed about his traditional dress and where best to purchase this. He told me about how to purchase high quality material for his dress, which I appreciated. However, on day 2 Mohammed surprised me and had purchased me a high quality emirati style dress. I genuinely couldn't believe the level of hospitality the people at Rum Stars offer! On day 2, Mohammed took us to the highest mountain in the Wadi Rum and climbed with us to the top. We got an amazing view of the entire Wadi Rum and the Saudi Arabia border. Once we reached the bottom, we were taken to a beautiful shaded area, where Mohammed cooked us another fantastic lunch. You really would not expect the quality he provided while in the desert. We then went on a two hour camel ride from our camp to the sunset spot, enjoyed another dinner with the bedouins, and had a lovely sleep in our fantastic home in the Rum Stars camp. Overall, I couldn't have asked for more. It was my favourite part of visiting Jordan, only improved by the incredible staff at Rum Stars. I would recommend this company to anybody.

reviews.author: Lorraine White
reviews.text: Rum Stars Camp is amazing. My husband and I had the pleasure of staying there and we could not have asked for more. We did the Classic Bedouin Tour which I also highly recommend. We had the such a lovely day. All the food was delicious, from the lunch prepared and cooked in the dessert, dinner cooked the traditional way underground and breakfast, and, as a vegetarian, I had plenty of options. Our guide was Zay (I'm not sure I spelled it correctly) and he was fantastic, very knowledgeable. He had great stories for us as we drank Bedouin tea by the fire after dinner. There was plenty of drinking water available too. We stayed in the luxury accommodation and if your budget allows you to, I recommend it. We had and ensuite, a balcony looking out over the dessert and a very comfortable bed. We had sockets for charging phones or using other devices. Electricity does go off at midnight but this was not an issue as we're already asleep. They also provided us with a flask of hot water, coffee, tea, chocolate and water. I cannot recommend Rum Stars Camp enough. Thank you for a fantastic day and night.

reviews.author: Mike Beavington
reviews.text: What great hosts. We enjoyed the bittersweet pleasure of having the camp to ourselves because of the current sad situation. We felt important to not cancel and to enjoy the Jordanian hospitality. The basic tents were good but there was a bit of a strong incense smell initially. That’s the only downside. The food was great. The hosts also helped us out so much when I came down with a nasty cough (not covid) I missed a lot of the activities but my wife as treated amazingly. The bathrooms were fine. Our friends had the deluxe place and really enjoyed the sunrise.

reviews.author: Aline Menezes
reviews.text: Rum Star Camp was all you could ask for. The location is nestled between a dune and a rock face which is stunning. Dinner and activities are on a tent on the dune and the view is stunning, especially at night. The food was incredible, with options for vegetarians. Everything is included in the price and it's really good value for the money. I wish I could remember all the team names, but they all were so nice, I went on a Jeep tour, Our guide has a perfect English, he was a really great guide! He takes great photos too. The tents are clean and there are plenty of blankets so you don't get cold. The bathroom were very clean and had a very hot shower. I Would definitely recommend! I wish I had booked two nights, one night is enough time to enjoy the camp and the desert but you will want more. Thank you all♥️

reviews.author: WS
reviews.text: Joined 2 days 2 nights tour and stayed in the regular tent. I am satisfied and happy with the tour as well as the tour guide. The first day we spent time with other group mates to walk the canyon, do sand boarding, crazy climbing at Lawrence’s spring. We did the simple but delicious lunch, and some relaxing time after the lunch (which Im also expected because the local said they will take nap after lunch to avoid activities at the hottest time of the day). The dinner is also great with variety of food. After dinner we spent some time dancing with the group and listened to the local singing. The regular tent is very basic, literally a bed and a small table and trash bin. The shared bathroom is clean and there is hot water for a quick shower. I have nothing to complain. On the second day we drove to the southern part of Wadi Rum and we hiked at the highest mountain in Jordan. A very tiring but yet rewarding hike! We also spend a long time having lunch with our tour guide afterwards and had a nice chat exchanging our culture. This is what travelling is about, we know more about others’ culture, we respect each other, I treasured this moment with our tour guide a lot. What I think is you cannot expect luxury food and accommodation in the desert, and the camp is what I am expecting to experience. If you are not prepared to walk a lot and experiencing the desert, maybe you should stay in a hotel instead. I highly recommended this tour, if you are a hiker, you should also challenge to hike the highest mountain in Jordan as well! I am glad I chose a 2 days 2 nights tour here.

reviews.author: Noah Ge
reviews.text: Great place to stay in Wadi Rum! Also do the full-day keep your. Raad was an amazing guide and fun driver. The food is of high quality! (Also vegan and veggy option)

reviews.author: Tom Mousa
reviews.text: Very bad experience I have been to rum too many times this was the worst experience ever even though we have paid 180JD 3 of us for 1 night and we ended up checking out Thursday night and leavig the place non of the comment was met plus a very bad attitude from the crew I will make sure everyone know how bad this place is

reviews.author: Solo Rabe
reviews.text: Very welcoming, available, friendly staff. We had a magical stay in the desert accompanied by our great guide.

reviews.author: Veli Keser

address: Sun City Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Randy Folliard
reviews.text: Sun City Camp in Wadi Rum exceeded all expectations—an absolutely magical experience from start to finish! The staff were incredibly welcoming and attentive, making us feel right at home in the heart of the desert. Our lodging was the perfect blend of comfort and adventure: spacious, air-conditioned, with a private bathroom—a true luxury in such a remote setting. The food was delicious and thoughtfully prepared, adding to the authentic experience. The three-hour jeep tour through the stunning desert landscape was thrilling, and the sunset camel ride was simply unforgettable—peaceful, breathtaking, and surreal. If you're visiting Wadi Rum, this is the place to stay. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: filippo mancinelli
reviews.text: had an unforgettable stay at this camp in Wadi Rum. The room was absolutely beautiful, blending comfort with a stunning panoramic view of the desert—sunrises and sunsets were magical. The food was exceptional—every meal was fresh, flavorful, and authentically Jordanian. What truly made the experience stand out, though, were the hosts. They were phenomenally friendly, welcoming us with warmth and making us feel right at home from the moment we arrived. Their hospitality and attention to detail turned an already amazing location into a truly special experience. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Anas Ibrahim
reviews.text: The weather in Wadi Rum was quite windy, but the strong desert sun made it feel warm and vibrant. The jeep rides through the vast, rugged landscape were especially fun—fast, bumpy, and full of excitement. Racing over sand dunes and weaving through dramatic rock formations added a real sense of adventure to the experience. At night, we enjoyed a delicious Zarb dinner cooked underground and listened to Bedouin music under the stars. It was a magical, peaceful, and adventurous experience all in one.

reviews.author: Telmo Martins
reviews.text: Best camp you can stay at. Service from the start at reception is very personal, the domes are complete with clean toilet shower and a stunning and calm view of the desert. Activities are plenty with a team of locals who can give you an overview on everything. Dinner was one the best meals I had in Jordan with fresh meat and vegetables. Mahmoud made the experience quite nice with dancing after dinner involving everyone. Great place for adventures or just chilling outside with a book.

reviews.author: Rose Canon
reviews.text: Amazing Experience at Sun City Camp, Wadi Rum! Sun City Camp was nothing short of amazing! The staff was incredibly accommodating and friendly, making sure we had everything we needed. The food was delicious, with a great selection that truly added to the experience. Special thanks to Haytham and the chef Mohamad. A special shoutout to our tour guide who drove us all the way from Amman - Mohammad Madi. He is the best! And to our jeep driver too - Qusai, for an unforgettable Wadi Rum safari! He was not only informative but also made the entire ride fun and exciting. His knowledge and enthusiasm truly enhanced our adventure through the stunning desert landscape. Highly recommend Sun City Camp for anyone visiting Wadi Rum—it’s an experience you won’t forget!

name: Wadi Rum Night Camp
address: Wadi Rum Night Camp, Wadi Rum, Jordan

reviews.author: Ercan Teksoylu
reviews.text: Frankly, renting a place in a country we don't know at all in a geography we don't know scared us a little, but when we arrived at the place we rented, we saw that it was a really perfect place. The balloon houses have air conditioning, a private bathroom, a small area where you can prepare and eat something, plus a refrigerator, air conditioning, an electric teapot, and a great environment where you can watch the sunset or prepare and drink something while watching the sunrise, which will increase your comfort when you sit in the evening. The breakfast, lunch and dinner meals are sufficiently satisfying and varied, especially the dinner, with its three-story specially prepared Bedouin-style menu extracted from underground, offers both a visual and delicious feast to its guests. After dinner in the evening, you can sit and smoke hookah, sip your brewed tea under the stars and enjoy the taste of Bedouin melodies sung around the fire played with a single-string instrument. There is an organization in the camp for you, Safari Tours, camel tours, balloon tour, in short, that can meet all your expectations.

reviews.text: J’ai passé une nuit extraordinaire dans une bubble room au Wadi Rum Night Luxury Camp lors de mon solo road trip en 2022. Dormir sous les étoiles, dans une bulle transparente avec vue sur les montagnes de Wadi Rum, est une expérience inoubliable ! La tente était confortable, propre, et offrait une sensation de luxe tout en restant proche de la nature. Le personnel était chaleureux et accueillant, et le dîner au camp était délicieux. C’est l’endroit parfait pour se déconnecter et admirer la beauté du désert. Je recommande vivement pour une expérience unique et magique !

reviews.text: Socotra island has all of the spectacular and wonderful things that they are rarely to be seen in the other places over the world - beautiful caves, white sand beaches, sand dunes, cliff and oceanfront, bottle tree and desert roses, dragon blood trees, Egyptian vultures, to name a few.

reviews.author: Rugile Gile
reviews.text: Incredibly versatile landscape across a small area. Gorgeous trees and even more fascinating sea life 🤩 You will have a time of your life. I definitely had!

reviews.author: A J Bashha
reviews.text: The Dragon's Blood Tree (Dracaena cinnabari) is a remarkable species endemic to Socotra Island, Yemen, where it grows in large densities of woodland. Its distinctive umbrella-like mushroom shape is entirely natural. These trees can live up to 600 years and reach a height of 10 meters. The tree's deep red resin, resembling blood, has been highly valued since the Roman era for its uses in dye, violin varnish, medicine, makeup, and rituals. Socotra, located in the Indian Ocean near the coasts of Yemen and Somalia, is politically part of Yemen, though it has historical and cultural connections to Somalia. The island features spectacular scenery and is home to numerous endemic species of plants, birds, and other fauna, such as the Dragon's Blood Tree. Its unique landscape includes rugged mountains, canyons, wadis, caves, and picturesque beaches. The calm, shallow sea and the warm climate make it an attractive destination for nature lovers, scientists, and adventurers. Tourists often engage in snorkeling, fishing, hiking, and sightseeing, making the most of the island's natural beauty. However, Socotra lacks proper tourist infrastructure, such as hotels or guesthouses, and camping remains the only accommodation option. Transportation and facilities are underdeveloped, which preserves its untouched appeal. The island's population is relatively low and includes indigenous Socotri people, along with residents from other parts of Asia and Africa. The Socotri are known for their generosity and hospitality toward visitors. Despite its natural wonders, Socotra faces challenges, including illegal flights from the UAE that are not approved by Yemen’s government. These activities, tied to the UAE's broader role in Yemen, raise concerns about the island’s sovereignty. Nonetheless, Socotra remains a remote and captivating destination for those willing to embrace its rustic charm and unspoiled environment.

reviews.author: Muhammed Ashik
reviews.text: Al Kout Mall is one of the most vibrant and popular shopping destinations in Kuwait. It’s always lively with visitors, especially during weekends and holidays, creating a bustling yet energetic atmosphere that adds to the shopping experience. The mall is spacious and well-designed, offering a clean, neat, and modern environment for shoppers. One of the major highlights is the wide variety of branded shops available—almost all major international and local brands have outlets here. During promotional seasons, there are attractive discount sales, making it a great place for budget-conscious shoppers to grab quality items at affordable prices. Families with kids will find the children’s play area very convenient and enjoyable. It’s a safe and fun space where children can be entertained while parents shop or relax. The food court is another strong point of Al Kout Mall, with plenty of food and beverage options available—from fast food to fine dining, catering to all tastes and preferences. Overall, Al Kout Mall combines entertainment, dining, and shopping in one location, making it a perfect spot for families, friends, and even solo visitors. It’s a must-visit place if you're in Kuwait and looking for a great mall experience.

reviews.text: I’ve been to Fareej Swaileh (فريج صويلح) twice now in Kuwait, and both times the experience has been consistently great which says a lot. The food is tasty and hits the spot, but what really stood out was how fast everything came out; I honestly don’t think we waited more than five minutes. It’s perfect when you’re hungry and don’t feel like waiting forever. Another thing I love is the لقيمات (sweet dumplings) they serve for free before and after the meal. It’s such a thoughtful touch that makes the whole experience feel warm and welcoming. Definitely a spot I’ll keep coming back to.

Despite the crowd, the service was excellent and English-friendly. Highly recommended for anyone wanting to try authentic Kuwaiti cuisine!

reviews.text: I went to them many times in different timing and occupations. Their set of menu is good to go and the test is amazing. The breakfast, launch and dinner each have unique flavors. Usually they serve the soup in a bread but you can ask them to be served in a regular bowel. I recommend the chicken soup. For the breakfast they have separate dishes or as a packages ( Freej Swaileh BK and Emirati BK - as I attached) For lunch and dinner, they have variety from rice to stew, I prefers beef stew (Saloonat Latham) with whit rice. For salads try Chefs special which is Arabic slaw with cheese served in a nice crispy bread and sour sauce. For dessert you can try different types, but I recommend LUQAIMAT with cheese (fried dough with cheese) and Karak tea (TEA with MILK). They have inside sitting and in the winter they do a lovey decoration outside, so you can have great time with your family and enjoying the nice weather too.
