reviews.author: Shake Kandy (Shake)
reviews.text: Great place to chill out in a group or alone. Food is amazing, and the servers are always watching to get rid of used plates/cups or help to order anything new. Easy access to the beach and a good clean pool. The only issue I found is that there are many bees for a city that was telling their bee's are being extinct. Food we had were salmon starter, meat mix plater, kebab plate and seafood mix plate.

reviews.author: Isaac Huether
reviews.text: The atmosphere and service was amazing! My steak was not cooked how I asked or even close to it, and the steak was not tender at all. However the tapas dessert and my girlfriend’s meal were great! I would highly recommend the truffle potatoes. The sauce was divine on those, and the chicken gyoza had a fun twist on it that made it delicious! The prices were so good too.

reviews.author: Na Tasha
reviews.text: The guacamole was really good! Everything else was … okay. Nothing to rave about. Restaurant is beautiful - 2 floors. Worth it if you can get a table against the window for ocean views!

reviews.author: Alexander
reviews.text: We went there for lunch and also drinks one night. Hip place at night, lots of young people partying… but during the day this beautiful spot offers great views onto the ocean. The food is delicious, and people are very kind. Smoking is allowed as in most places in Morocco but at this place and for our lunch it was bothering us as the air was pretty thick with smoke. That’s the only reason I am taking away two stars for atmosphere.

reviews.author: Hassan
reviews.text: This place is truly in a league of its own honestly, it might be the only restaurant in the world where you’d go just to check out the bathroom, it’s that impressive! Since it opened, it has completely raised the bar for fine dining in Casablanca. The view is stunning, the service is always spot-on, and the menu keeps evolving while staying solid. It’s one of my favorite by sea destinations. The food is consistently good yes, it’s a bit pricey, but totally worth it. I had the white fish carpaccio which was delicate and flavorful, and the Caesar salad was surprisingly one of the best I’ve had. If you’re in Casablanca, Cabestan is a must-go spot.

name: Le Casablanca Hotel Dining
address: Le Casablanca Hotel Dining, Casablanca, Morocco

reviews.author: Oussama Imariren
reviews.text: Everything was nice from the staff's attention to the property's charming facilities and vibe. The only downside was the bed. it was too soft, no lumbar or back support, you wake up with a very sore back.

reviews.author: Richard Lee
reviews.text: Le Casablanca Hotel was a lovely place to start our trip to Morocco. The building is elegant and traditional but very comfortable. It's situated in an upscale neighbourhood which feels very safe for walking. Our room was large and comfortable - lots of room for the two of us and our luggage - and it was quiet, even though the hotel is on busy street. Wifi was strong and reliable throughout our stay. We ate breakfast and dinner at the hotel. The breakfast buffet is extensive and not crowded when we were there. Dinner was very good - great selection of traditional international dishes. We had nothing but good service from the friendly, helpful staff.

reviews.author: Alex N
reviews.text: Le Casablanca is located in a quiet neighborhood, 10 minutes by taxi from most of the known landmarks in town. My room was spacious, although a bit noisy because of the traffic (the hotel directly faces a busy, 4-lane road). The cleanliness isn’t top notch, although adequate for local standards. Unfortunately some members of the personnel lack in competence, or training, or passion for their work - or of all of them. The outcome is well exemplified by the breakfast buffet, of which I attach a few photos taken at 9:36am on a Saturday morning.

reviews.author: zineb doumi
reviews.text: I had a disappointing experience at Le Casablanca Hotel yesterday. We were stopped at the entrance by a security guard who refused to let us in because of my friend's dress, claiming it was too short. What made the situation even more frustrating was seeing another guest walk out at the same time wearing an equally short dress without any issue. This felt discriminatory and inconsistent, and it's not the kind of treatment you expect from a 5-star establishment. We left feeling uncomfortable and unwelcome. I hope the management addresses this kind of behavior and ensures all guests are treated with respect and fairness.

reviews.author: Sahar Ou
reviews.text: Convenient location, beautiful hotel, spacious rooms and good service overall. The food at la pergola is amazing. The tea time in the lobby is nice. The room service is quick and pretty decent. The spa is small but the therapist was very good. Highly recommend

reviews.author: Nitka Mittal
reviews.text: We had such a wonderful experience at Le Cuistot Traditionnel! From the moment we walked in, we were warmly welcomed by the kind owner, who made us feel right at home. The restaurant itself is absolutely beautiful — the traditional interiors are full of charm and authentic touches that create a cozy, inviting atmosphere. And the food… truly outstanding. We tried a few different tajines, and every single one was packed with flavor and cooked to perfection. You can really taste the love and tradition in every bite. If you’re looking for a place that combines genuine hospitality with delicious, authentic dishes, this is it. We can’t wait to come back!

reviews.author: Malak Jaafar
reviews.text: I am so happy my friend recommended Le Cuistot Traditionnel because I think if you are in Casablanca and don’t pass by this gem, you are missing out. The decor and ambiance are just spectacular and you feel like you’re in a different world once you step in. But nothing matches the food - everything is homemade and tastes like it was made just for you by our collective Moroccan mom or grandma. Even the dessert is baked in-house. The staff are lovely and go out of their way to help. 10/10 in every way. Thank you for having us.

reviews.author: er nest
reviews.text: Le Cuistot in Casablanca - the best Moroccan cuisine I’ve had so far! The food was absolutely excellent, rich in flavor and perfectly prepared. The staff was incredibly attentive, ensuring a flawless dining experience. The atmosphere was warm, welcoming, and relaxed, making it the perfect spot to enjoy an authentic meal. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Iryna Atmar
reviews.text: Authentic place in Casablanca to try real tasty Moroccan cuisine. Cozy atmosphere, friendly personnel and chef welcoming you personally 😌 good portions, plenty of options to choose! Definitely recommend 👍🏻

reviews.author: Yavuz Selim Elmas
reviews.text: Chicken Pastilla is a great choice whether you have it as antipasti or dessert after the meal. It’s Friday later afternoon and the place was so calm. I definitely would like to try here again next time. I guess its a family establishment which makes it more special.

reviews.author: Alexander
reviews.text: Absolutely loved it. The art deco style, spacious rooms and bathrooms, the boutique hotel character, and how nice everyone is. The rooms don’t have numbers but names of artists of the creative art deco period, and attention to detail in the decoration is impeccable. Antique furniture from the 1930s, stained glass windows, and pieces evoking decorative Moroccan art. A real gem and within walking distance of the old city and wall. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Lailee Taghdisi
reviews.text: The hotel is cool and has a great rooftop however our room should not be a room that the hotel rents out. The restaurant is above and any time a fork was dropped the whole room shook. There was noise nonstop- this was the Josephine Baker room. We told the front desk lady and she asked if we told anyone and we told her we did- she didn’t apologized and then followed up by trying to swindle us by booking a car that was 5x that was market rate- these cars are not nicer by any means and on top of it she has a mocking tone the whole time. She should not be working at this hotel- super shady and disrespectful. I work in the industry and one should always find a way to help the guest especially in a foreign country and she was just trying to “be right”.

reviews.author: Ahmad
reviews.text: This boutique hotel in Casablanca offers a unique and delightful experience. The standout feature is the creatively themed rooms, each decorated in homage to famous actors. Our room came with a small balcony, which was a lovely spot to relax and take in the Casablanca atmosphere. The attention to detail in the room decor was nice A pleasant surprise was the on-site restaurant. It offers an intriguing fusion of authentic Moroccan and Chinese cuisines, providing guests with a unique dining experience without leaving the hotel. The hotel's size gives it an intimate feel, perfect for those who prefer a more personalized atmosphere over large chain hotels. Its location in Casablanca makes it a great base for exploring the city. Overall, this boutique hotel offers a blend of comfort, creativity, and convenience that makes for an enjoyable stay in Casablanca.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

reviews.author: Matt Aliberti
reviews.text: Great one night stay, I wish we had stayed longer. The hotel has great style and really responsive service. We stayed on the fifth floor in a large room with a balcony. Nice tub, clean bathroom, comfy bed. You can take the cool curved stairs all the way up from the lobby to the roof. On the roof is a mediterranean restaurant and bar - we had lunch, dinner, and drinks up there, its a great space. And the service is great. The front desk helped us get checked in, have lunch, and get in a cab in time to make the final tour of the day at the Hassan II mosque. They gave us walking maps, coordinated rides, and cared about our comfort and safety. It is a highly professional hotel and I highly recommend.

reviews.author: Kelly Peak
reviews.text: Amazing hotel and staff. Zach at the front desk went above and beyond to ensure our trip was the most enjoyable (great food recommendations, including the hotel restaurant), made dinner reservations, and he really helped me with my delayed baggage.

reviews.author: Alexander
reviews.text: This the more tradition restaurant of the hotel Le Doge. Great food, not many tables so I recommend making a reservation. We enjoyed eating there the day we arrived after a long trip and didn’t want to leave the hotel. Excellent food, had the lamb and kebab dishes, paired with Moroccan wines. Very friendly wait staff in a quiet and traditional atmosphere. Simply wonderful.

reviews.author: Marietta C
reviews.text: Awesome Moroccan food with a few Lebanese and Mediterranean elements. Delicious place for a cozy night and romantic atmosphere in an elegant restaurant with amazing staff. Great vegetarian options and don’t skip dessert!

reviews.author: Katerina Smoldyreva
reviews.text: I cannot say enough to recommend this beautiful restaurant. It hits you an all the senses- set in a beautifully colourful Moroccan Art deco rooms, it offers aromatic and very tasty indeed Moroccan dishes. Quiet Arabic music on the background does not hamper, but enhances conversation and the service was amazing too! We were cordially welcomed and immediately felt at home, cracking jokes with the lady of the house. Even the dishes were authentic Fez porcelain from around 1960’s! Everything was perfect!

reviews.author: Sabrina Lian
reviews.text: We were staying at the affiliated hotel and ended up dining here out of convinience, turned out to be the best culinary decision of the trip. The decor and ambience are just perfect, opulent and cozy at the same time, food was absolutely delicious and very generously portioned, service was seamless and welcoming, overall a true undiscovered gem. A must try for Casablanca!

reviews.author: Jiaying Guo
reviews.text: Great food and great service. The security also made sure I got in the taxi safely. But the restaurant decoration makes me feel like I’m eating at a library

reviews.author: toni rikardo
reviews.text: best place in casablanca great view great service, food is delicious and fresh. we need to encourage people like these to invest in casablanca. good luck

reviews.author: DREDD POWER
reviews.text: 7.6/10 - Great Monk fish in mushroom sauce, served with rice. 7.8/10 - Service was good, people speak English. Great Ocean View, very close to crashing waves. Also The light house to the right still operates.

reviews.author: Boris Hardi
reviews.text: Great food and setting at the Le Pilotis restaurant. French beach club atmosphere and really exceptional food. We had steaks and fish and wine. All was really tasty and on point.

reviews.author: Riccardo Villa
reviews.text: Pilotis have an unique food choice making a fusion between japanese and spanish classics. This place have an awesome view on the sea during the day and have also a charming atmosphere for dinner. It deserves a visit even if it may result quite expensive.

reviews.author: Yi
reviews.text: It is a nice restaurant with perfect sea view, food is good with reasonable price

name: Le Relais de Paris
address: Le Relais de Paris, Casablanca, Morocco

reviews.author: Brandon Melnychuk
reviews.text: Multiple dinners were excellent. The tartar appetizers are very very good. The pastas and fish were excellent. Staff are very attentive and pleasant. Definitely worth trying!

reviews.author: Harold Overman
reviews.text: On Tuesday evening April 16th we ended up in this famous restaurant on the Corniche in Casablanca (after we tried to book other restaurants which were all fully booked). Over the last 10+ years I have been here many times for lunch and dinners. It’s a nice restaurant where you cannot book in advance. It’s based on first come, first served. We always loved the foie gras poêlé aux pommes caramélisées, but unfortunately this starter was removed from the menu. Instead we tried the Goat Cheese salad, the Avocat-Gambas salad and 6 snails (escargots). Nice starters. As main course we tried again our favorite menu for two: the Chateaubriand which is the restaurants’ signature dish at 485 MAD. It was not as good (and much) as before. The waiter mixed up the two orders (one was well done and one saignant), the ognions and garlic were not well cooked enough. As desert we tried the fondant and crème brûlée. Overall we enjoyed our dinner, but felt it was not as good as before.

reviews.author: Marwa
reviews.text: i’ve been to relais de paris many many times, and it never disappoints, the steak is always cooked exactly how i ask, the sauce is absolutely insane , truly the best in town! the fries are crispy and delicious, and the side salad is fresh and healthy, i genuinely love this place, if you’re looking for the best steak and sauce combo in the city, this is it.

reviews.author: Sissy SN
reviews.text: Good variety of Mediterranean food in this restaurant situated in an upmarket neighbourhood of Casablanca. This brasserie does not take reservations and gets extremely busy. The staff speak various languages which is a plus! We decided to visit late afternoon as the wait for a table can be disappointing.. The service was very pleasant especially from our waiter and Mounir ( the Maitre D).. We were disappointed that we could not order Oysters and the beef fillet steaks as they had ran out after a busy Sunday lunch. The Caesar salad was authentic although it should have been served without cherry tomatoes. The entrecôte was good but not my first choice.. French fries recommended. Parking is available as well as valet parking right outside the main entrance This brasserie is part of a hotel ‘Villa Blanca’ and is quite the vibe for the trendy crowd in town. The crème brûlée was good but could have had a bit less sugar in it and was quite big ( one is enough to share). Overall, I would highly recommend this brasserie but I must stress, they get very busy at lunchtime ( especially weekends)so if you are prepared to wait, go for it. Weekdays ( evenings) are totally a different vibe. Keep up the good work and get more Oysters and Beef fillets in stock… Attentive staff from the moment one enters…

reviews.author: abril arbuis
reviews.text: A resto nearby the sea... feel the fresh air and enjoy your food. The menu list is quite expensive. Choose a table indoor or outdoor... I will recommend outdoor ☺️

reviews.author: sheydreams76
reviews.text: Don't think about it, just do it! Beautiful food, you will not be disappointed!

reviews.author: Mouhcine RANIB
reviews.text: The decor is a real success. The place is pleasant and a change from the ordinary. The dining menu is a bit limited, but what they offer is truly delicious. For the wine list, you'll need a sommelier; you'll be spoiled for choice

reviews.author: Raul Sánchez-Moncayo
reviews.text: Surreal We ordered different dishes and they brought us all the same, including the one who ordered fish, we couldn't distinguish the meat we ate, luckily the light was very dim since it was impossible to distinguish the color of the floor from the dirt it had, the attention left a lot to be desired, if you like adventure this is your place if you want to eat medium well better look for another

reviews.author: Massimo Priasca
reviews.text: Excellent cuisine, interesting wine list

reviews.author: simo vital
reviews.text: Ideal place for a quiet drink....

reviews.author: Pia Justinek
reviews.text: Soukaina served us professionally and was very friendly. We had a 7-month-old baby with us, and she was very accommodating. Everything she recommended regarding the food was excellent. All praises go to her; because of her, our experience and the food were perfect. Thank you, and I highly recommend her to everyone! 🫶🏻

reviews.author: Tim Müller
reviews.text: Thank you for that wonderful last evening in Morocco!! Yes, the food itself is more pricey BUT thats totally justified because: fantastic interiors and lighting like in a fairytale out of 1001 nights, tasty, juicy Tajin(350 MAD)with fruits in it after many fastfood disappointnents this vacation, a show with life Orchester and a sexy belly dancer. Last but not least, the staff is very attentive and sweet, trying to make your stay as nice as possible. Got traditional cookies and snacks and in the end a waitress even helped me to get a taxi. A must see in a rather dreary city.

reviews.author: Jim Tompkins
reviews.text: Wonderful evening of great food and amazing entertainment! We wanted to experience Casablanca and Dar Beida fulfilled our wishes to the max!

reviews.author: Rebe Arce
reviews.text: Loved the experience. Amazing live music. Friendly and great service & staff. Each platters were delicious. Thank you Khalid for the best service in the town.

reviews.author: Ahmad Alshehhi
reviews.text: Very nice authentic Moroccan restaurant with live music. The food was very delicious and the staff are very friendly.

reviews.author: Georgie Boost
reviews.text: Admittedly, I was a bit undecided if we were going to book for an evening at this nostalgic Casablanca cinephile's haunt, however, I am super delighted we did. The decor was tasteful and not overdone, the service was courteous and attentive and entertained us with their comical humor. We enjoyed delicious starters and entrées with hearty portions, so much so, that we didn't have room for dessert. We enjoyed the Moroccan Volubulis red wine along with the piano renditions of old and modern songs. A very enjoyable evening. Make sure you get a quick look at the upstairs lounge with it's nostalgic photos of Casablanca and sit at the bar after your meal for the full experience. We had the later time-slot, so it was lovely to not have to shift off our table for the second sitting.

reviews.author: Amy Leese
reviews.text: Food was 😋 delicious. Staff were very attentive and friendly. Plus looked very smart. Entertainment at 8pm was all the best most memorable songs. A real treat. 😊 Booking....an absolute must as it is always fully booked!! Simple to do ...email them and do email confirmation 24 hrs before you go. You don't want to miss out!

reviews.author: Kristian Peter
reviews.text: Iconic restaurant in Casablanca… you should stop in for a cocktail and the live Jazz. We didn’t eat, but the cocktails were good and the service was on point for a Monday evening. Watch the movie prior to stopping by so you can see the details, overall a fun experience!

reviews.author: Puja Sweet
reviews.text: This is definitely a to - go place if you’re a movie buff and wanna get an experience of the classics. The vibe was amazing. But the staff was quite rude. Despite having a bookings, were allotted a corner table with zero view. We were 3 of us and they said the table in the ground floor was for 4 people but later we saw that the same table was allotted to 3. They also went out of their way to create spaces and tables at some corners withgood view for few people out of nowhere. I felt there was a some sort of discrimination based on how you dress up . We just went after Hamam and it was our last day of the trip , so we were quite exhausted and weren’t quite dressed up as went post Hamam , but didn’t want to miss out on the experience , hence went. But the staff was quite judgmental it seems. Then we ordered 3 drinks, a main course and desert worth 800 MAD but the waiter told us it is not sufficient order and we need to order more if we want to sit on that table It was quite disappointing and rude as we already had evening snack and weren’t very hungry but we still ordered 3 drinks, a main course and a desert all worth 800 MAD . Despite that, he was quite rude and at the same time was treating other table people quite differently. Went there for experience but Didn’t have a good experience in general. The food and drinks no doubt were good. We ordered risotto, mimosa , whiskey sour and gin and with that rice pudding . Everything was good in taste. It was just the behavior of the staff which was unexpectedly rude and unwelcoming.

reviews.author: John Eakins
reviews.text: I know the idea is totally kitschy but it’s actually good food and a great ambiance. I was shocked there’s no gambling though. It’s worth going. Do agree some people need to dress it up a bit!

reviews.author: Silver Decor
reviews.text: The Central Market one of the most famous urban markets in Morocco with historical and cultural significance. It is located on Muhammad V Boulevard, among the colonial architecture of the 20th century. Crammed with locals, the daily market is a fascinating place for tourists to get a taste of local culture, while picking up bargains on everything from food to flowers and traditional clothing.

reviews.author: Kevin Costello
reviews.text: This is somewhat like a bit of the medina souk, enclosed in its own walls, offering well liked fish grill restaurants, fruit and vegetables as well as flowers and other such market goods. Nothing is priced?. The cafes were busy and the fish market had some high end fish and shellfish, much sought after.

reviews.author: Anna V Travelling
reviews.text: You will find Central Marketplace in all big cities in Morocco including CasabIanca. I went there to eat fresh seafood. Fish restaurants are very clean, they offer fresh seafood only, good service, affordable prices. Fresh oysters 8-10 MAD, it is about 08-1 USD I ordered sardines for 30 MAD (about 3 USD). Sardines served with bread basket, salad, lentil porridge and lemon.

reviews.author: HISTRO zhang
reviews.text: Recommend! There are lots of local guy came here as well. I came twice, the first time order in the restaurant, the second time bought the sea food myself and the restaurant responsible for cooking. The second option is better. I bought a whole crab with less than 100 mad. And the way they cook keeps the original flavor quite well.

reviews.author: Manami Toshirozawa
reviews.text: Fresh seafood from the market is served! This is the best place to eat seafood in Casablanca with affordable price. Open 10 am, close 20 pm.

reviews.text: All kind of electric goods available here

reviews.author: Annabelle
reviews.text: 10/10. Honestly so nice. As soon as you walk in the restaurant is beautiful. The food was delicious! The service was incredible & the staff were all very helpful/kind. Would definitely recommend! The terrace is also very beautiful. Thanks for letting us try some Moroccan sweets!

reviews.author: Alaa Nassimi
reviews.text: I recently visited this restaurant, and unfortunately, I was disappointed. The prices were much higher compared to other places in the area, which made the experience feel less worth it. To make matters worse, I found a fly on my flan, which was really off-putting. Overall, I wouldn’t recommend it due to the high prices and hygiene issue.

reviews.author: Daniel Dalsgaard
reviews.text: The views were magical, the food was amazing, and just overall great experience!! Probably the most touristy place in town, and on the pricier end (still less than Marakech), but well worth it!

reviews.author: Darren Parker
reviews.text: Beautiful Moroccan restaurant with fantastic and attentive service. Food was excellent value for great quality and very good flavours. Great feel with interesting decor and lovely roof terrace.

reviews.author: Vala Ntino
reviews.text: Hello Everyone ❤️ In our world today, where attention to health and nutrition has become a priority, the search for healthy foods that combine benefits and delicious taste is increasing. Health is not just the absence of disease, but rather a state of physical and mental balance, and proper nutrition is the basis of this balance. But this does not necessarily mean sacrificing taste or pleasure in eating Food. Today we can enjoy nutritious meals full of essential nutrients for our body, while still being delicious and inspiring to taste. Smart food choices allow us to enjoy both health and pleasure at the same time. If you are looking for an exceptional dining experience that combines delicious flavors with a comfortable atmosphere, we at our restaurant offer you everything you wish for and more. We have a diverse menu of dishes that combine delicious taste with health benefits, as we use the best fresh and local ingredients to prepare each meal. Whether you are a fan of international cuisine Or you prefer traditional dishes with an innovative touch, we have something that will satisfy your taste. The restaurant's warm atmosphere and friendly service make every visit an unforgettable experience. Come enjoy delicious food in a place that makes you feel at home! Happy Life ❤️🌹

reviews.author: Hassnae moukham
reviews.text: The hotel is cheap, calm with great localisation Not that clean but good overall.

reviews.author: Halcyon Lily
reviews.text: This restaurant serves the best food in Chefchaoen that’s super fresh and delicious. Tried many places and love this the most so kept going back. Meals are served with proper spiced olives and bread. Staff are very friendly and welcoming too.

reviews.author: Veronika Bon Jour
reviews.text: The blue city in Morocco is one of the most beautiful places to visit without a doubt, beautiful landscapes, its inhabitants very friendly, I felt very lucky and welcome in this place. Thanks to #Alkasabah Riad for their attention and care 🙌🏽🙏🏽 #HotelRestaurantAlKasbah I am convinced that a place is always made more beautiful by the warmth of its inhabitants.

reviews.author: Said Belowahed
reviews.text: So clean and cozy, the stuffs are nice they give us everything we needs like plates to eat our takeout in the room, there a beautiful terrace with a beautiful view on the center of old Medina. The rooms are a bit small and the bathroom is shared "there two bathrooms". Amd that's it have a nave vacation in the most beautiful city in the world.

reviews.author: SkyWalker vs. Tiger
reviews.text: Great central location. Very nice outside areas but the terrace upstairs wasn't at it's best. Good food quality and portions. Depending on fellow clients, it can get noisy. Very helpful staff but some of them lacking total customer service.

reviews.text: The food tastes incredibly delicious — just like homemade. Even the bread tastes like the kind we used to bake at home, not the usual bakery bread. It has the same flavor as the bread my grandmother used to make long ago. The place is very clean, and the service is polite and courteous.

reviews.author: Imad Hinda
reviews.text: I loved this restaurant located in the heart of the old city, which allows you to travel through Chefchaouen cuisine and enjoy the distinctive and delicious local dishes. The staff was professional and helpful, which made the experience even more enjoyable. I highly recommend it to all visitors to the blue city.

reviews.author: Iman Ben mesaoud
reviews.text: Moroccan restaurant 100%. It serves Moroccan cuisine, salads, tagines, couscous, natural juices, and the dessert . The service from the staff is excellent and the prices are very reasonable. I recommend visiting the place.

reviews.author: Megan Pappan
reviews.text: Excellent service, food, drinks, and atmosphere! We had the vegetable couscous and lemon/ginger/mint juice. Everything was phenomenal! Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Yahia Hindoun
reviews.text: A magical dinner experience in the heart of Chefchaouen 💙 Warm atmosphere, authentic Moroccan hospitality, and delicious traditional food. The tagine was unforgettable, and the vibe of the blue streets made everything even more special. Highly recommended for anyone wanting to feel the true spirit of Morocco! ✨🍽️🇲🇦.

reviews.author: Oussama Souadka
reviews.text: Amazing fresh fish! The mixed seafood plate is something special - you can tell everything is perfectly cooked and really fresh. The chef knows what they're doing. Plus, the view from their terrace is absolutely beautiful. Will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Nitka Mittal
reviews.text: A peasant meal and evening at Bab Ssour While exploring the distinctive blue streets of Chefchaouen, finding Bab Ssour was a pleasant discovery. From the moment we entered, the atmosphere felt warm and inviting. The staff were notably friendly. Their welcome felt sincere, contributing to a comfortable sense of hospitality that set a positive tone for the meal. Simple things like the menu in multiple languages added to the experience. Choosing from the menu was made easier by the helpful staff at Bab Ssour. When I mentioned I was unsure what to order, they took the time to discuss the options and offered good recommendations based on my preferences. It was clear they knew their menu well and aimed to ensure guests had a rich experience. The food itself was very good. Following their suggestions, we enjoyed Moroccan flavours. The dishes tasted fresh and seemed carefully prepared. We thoroughly enjoyed Baisara, Lentil soup and the Moroccan mint tea. The goat tagine was tender and well-spiced. We capped the meal with their delicious yoghurt as dessert (caveat: it was very sweet, but we decided are on a holiday). For those seeking good, authentic Moroccan food served by welcoming staff who make you feel comfortable, Bab Ssour is a solid choice. It's certainly a great choice if you're in the area.

reviews.author: Slawek Gawronski
reviews.text: Couldn't find the main door, had to ask for the directions. Seem to be a family run restaurant. Nice view from rooftop terrace. Had to wait for a while to place the order, but the food was delicious.

reviews.author: George Olivier
reviews.text: This place was super popular w/ tourists as we had to wait in a short line before being seated. Upon entering, the place is hectic. It's very large w multiple levels for seating and extremely noisy. We shared a large table w/ another couple. In addition, the waiter was initially rude, inattentive and the kitchen was out of several dishes. Furthermore, the dishes came out @ random times w my appetizer being served before my entree and our drinks not being served until after we finished our meal. The food was solid and extremely cheap. We paid the equivalent of $14 for 2 starters, 2 entrees, and 2 desserts. 1 fast food meal in the U.S. costs more than that so that's definitely a good thing. I'd recommend this place as other patrons seemed to have a better go of it.

reviews.author: Donatas L
reviews.text: Enjoyed our lunch here! The food was tasty and prepared fairly quickly. I wouldn’t recommend the shrimp tajine—it was a bit too oily for my taste—but the other tajines were excellent! The view from the terrace wasn’t great, as it’s enclosed by windows.

reviews.author: Marius Dijokas
reviews.text: It's a bit hidden diamond in narrow Chefchouen streets. But it worth to be find. I am always happy when entering the restaurant you can feel that You're very welcome here. This feeling came with this traditional one. The woman who meets me at the entrance and the man who was always with the smile on his face. The terrace was stunning. Go there when the sun goes down. And last but not least- the food, simply good Moroccian kitchen, with quality products made me so happy! شكرًا لك

reviews.author: AskMiyoko Miyoko
reviews.text: We were thrilled to find this gem, tucked away in a less touristy area of the city. The warm welcome we received and delicious tea and tagine were almost as impressive as the views from the rooftop. You will not be disappointed, and yes…. Definitely order the lemon tart. 😋

reviews.author: Luz Nahir
reviews.text: Chefchaouen is a very special place, but this spot really won us over. It’s a beautiful traditional Andalusian home, with several charming floors and a beautiful rooftop terrace for sunny days, as well as an antique shop in the lower level. We were surprised to be the only ones there, and given the warm and kind attention we received from Mohammed and the people working there, we felt moved to leave them this review. The food is wonderful and feels fresh and home made; special mention to the Gambas Tajine, when we first tasted them and felt azahar notes, we were sold. Meat tajine w/ plums + almonds, the soups, carrot + orange salad…. All was great. Simple and warm, nutritious food. Oh and PLEASE order the lemon tart. Tangy and sharp, with just the right amount of sweetness. The menu (may ‘23) is a 3 course meal (entree, main and dessert) and for 110dh it is 🔥. Please go and give our warmest regards to Mohamed and team 🤍

reviews.author: H Begum
reviews.text: The lemon and olive tagine was one of the best I’ve had.

reviews.author: Célia Ghidini (Soramine3009)
reviews.text: An amazing experience in Chefchaouen ! The food was incredible, good quality, nice view, the kindest waiter and cheap !

reviews.author: Brahim El ouardighi
reviews.text: Best home made food

reviews.author: Oussama Ben khajou
reviews.text: The best service 💯✨💪

reviews.author: callista
reviews.text: Charming cafe where you can have a delicious, typical breakfast at a good price. The lady is very friendly!

reviews.author: Hai Long NGUYEN
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Karl Price
reviews.text: We’ve had a month touring Morocco and are tired of taglines and couscous, this restaurant was a breath of fresh air. The dips with our bread were varied and best of all they were spiced. For main we had chicken skewers which were nicely spiced with some lovely vegetables and rice. So much of our food here has lacked spice it was a pleasure to have our taste buds tingled again. Wholly recommend it, 125 Dhms per person for our food and drink.

reviews.author: Ellie Taylor
reviews.text: We had a great dinner at Lalla Messaouda. It wasn’t very busy, but the food was delicious. We really enjoyed the Lamb and Goat Tagine, as well as the chicken cous cous. The veggie tagine was a little bit plain though. We also were given complimentary bread and dips included which was lovely.

reviews.author: jihane fetouaki
reviews.text: Had couscous there in friday it was good but it was missing salt , little bit expensive compared to the portion but the atmosphere and service worth it . Especially the decoration of the place is unique

reviews.author: Scott
reviews.text: Sizzling! All the nibbles were satisfying, too. Sitting on a wooden throne was also pretty special. I'd say it was delicious. The chef is Chefchaouen but you've probably heard that one before.

reviews.author: Rose A
reviews.text: If you like something light and refreshing, and healthy, this is the place to dine. Their salads are so good and fresh, and they would offer menu of the day. Homecooked Moroccan food for sure. No wonder this top 5 on most blogs in the Internet. Ambiance is cozy, love the table setup and the friendly staff. It's a shame I didn't ask for the name, but he was so friendly and accommodating. Thumbs up to this place! Again, if you want something fresh, healthy, and home cooked authentic dishes, this is a must try.

reviews.author: Rach L Robinson
reviews.text: Great local spot. We had grilled vegetable sandwiches, Moroccan salad, fresh orange juice and a fresh mint lemonade. Food was flavourful and portions were generous. Simple delicious options and a nice quiet atmosphere.

reviews.author: Salaheddine L
reviews.text: Very nice local restaurant, it feels like it represents the area too with the food options. Price is good as well, for two people 10€ would be more than enough for a meal with drinks!

reviews.author: Cindy Latte
reviews.text: The harira soup was rich and flavorful, with a perfect balance of spices. The couscous was cooked to perfection and paired well with the tender chicken in the lemon tajin. Overall, the meal was delicious and highly recommended!! Thank you

reviews.author: Mayuri
reviews.text: We came here after reading many positive reviews on Google, but unfortunately, we had a very disappointing experience. We ordered the Chicken Tagine and Couscous with Chicken — both dishes were completely flavorless, just plain steamed chicken and vegetables. We could barely eat anything for dinner. If you want to save your money and avoid leaving hungry, do **not** visit this place.

reviews.author: Kasia Jaworska
reviews.text: A very nice little restaurant a bit off the beaten track. The service was quick and efficient and the food was delicious! We had chicken lemon tajine and vegetable couscous. Both dishes were very good!

reviews.author: Marius Dijokas
reviews.text: Really good local food with the accent of modern kitchen! And they know the main rule - every restaurant starts from the bread! They gave two types of breads and both feel's restaurant made and are very delicious. I dare to say I didn't tried better bread throughout all my 2 weeks journey in Morocco! The cold starter was already good as the main dish. Feeling that made from quality and love! The restaurant interior is very impressive too!

reviews.author: G Lim
reviews.text: Came here by accident and glad we did!! I had the seafood tagine and it is probably one of my favourite meals in Morocco! The service is great too! Staff is welcoming, polite and conversant in English. The ambience is amazing - very cozy, tastefully decorated and i love the orange blossom scent in the restaurant. If i have another day in chefchaouen, i’d definitely be back again!

reviews.author: Micah Polston
reviews.text: This place was recommended to us by our local host. The beef skewers were the single best bite I had while in Chefchaouen. The pasta side dish, which came with several entrees, could have been a main dish as our entire family liked it. Another bite to note was the chicken that came in the ceasar salad, we all said "wow." The Moroccan soup is memorable as well. Only Dirham [cash] is accepted here (no credit card, no euro); exchange locally for a better rate, not at ports of entry. If you are able to have multiple meals while in Chefchaouen, this would be my #3 recommendation; if lunch on the roof, during the day and it's not raining, #2.

reviews.author: Mahir Shadman
reviews.text: Excellent food and very affordable price. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Najam Munawar
reviews.text: Tissemlal is an absolute gem in Chefchaouen and a must-visit for anyone exploring this beautiful town. This restaurant offers an authentic Moroccan dining experience that’s hard to match, blending amazing flavors with a stunning atmosphere that leaves a lasting impression on anyone who visits. Their tagine and couscous are hands-down some of the best you’ll find in the region. Each dish is rich in flavor, perfectly cooked, and carries the comforting spices that make Moroccan cuisine so special and memorable. Their fresh and refreshing fruit juice is an ideal pairing, balancing the meal with a burst of natural sweetness that adds to the overall experience. And let’s not forget the local olives they serve—so fresh and flavorful that they instantly elevate the entire dining experience, making it even more authentic. What truly sets Tissemlal apart, however, is its rooftop sitting area. The view from the top is absolutely breathtaking—you get an unparalleled perspective of Chefchaouen’s lively main square, surrounded by charming greenery and the majestic mountains in the backdrop. It’s the perfect spot to relax, savor your meal, and soak in the beauty of the Blue City. The tranquil yet vibrant atmosphere makes it ideal for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Tissemlal is not just a restaurant—it’s a complete experience. A visit here is a memory you’ll treasure long after leaving Chefchaouen. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Joseph Gay
reviews.text: PLEASE READ BEFORE BOOKING I’ve been travelling for years and stayed in countless hostels, hotels, and Airbnbs — this was by far the worst experience I’ve ever had. There is no reception, no staff, and no information upon arrival. Room keys were left out randomly with no indication of which belonged to whom. We had booked a private two-bed room with a bathroom, but instead were split into separate dorm beds — with no notice, no refund, and no way to speak to anyone about it. About an hour later, the owner appeared from one of the two shared bathrooms (which he had locked for his personal use), and began aggressively confronting us about the booking — even though we showed him proof of what we paid for. Rather than offering any solution, he threatened to kick us out and stormed off. The conditions of the place are also awful. It’s unbearably hot — the bathrooms are essentially saunas, and our rooms had no AC or proper ventilation, just a tiny fan (barely the size of a hand) for two people in separate rooms. One of the room doors even fell off its hinges and shattered, nearly injuring a friend. Despite this, the owner demanded over €60 in damages. When questioned, he smashed more glass, seemingly to intimidate us, and brought in his brother, who tried to physically fight another guest while yelling slurs. I cannot recommend strongly enough that you stay somewhere else. This place is not safe, not clean, and not what is advertised. If you think this sounds exaggerated, read other recent reviews — our experience was not unique.

reviews.author: Travis Guy
reviews.text: This was the cleanest hostel we stayed at during our Morocco trip. Our room was comfortable with nice duvets. A good amount of bathrooms and showers. The breakfast was nice (something different than the normal breakfast...good oatmeal with fruit). When we arrived, the proprietor wasn't there (office hours were listed as 9-3), but it wasn't an issue as he had the paperwork laid out with the key (we were in a private room) and info as well as towels. The proprietor was very nice when we chatted with him, and he gave good suggestions on how to get to the waterfall and Tangier. It appeared as though some people when they arrived, didn't have the info quite as well-laid out as when we arrived, but they seemed to figure it out. The terrace had great views! Unfortunately it was a bit rainy and drizzly while we were there, so it was not good weather for having breakfast or hanging out up there. Looking at some other reviews people have left (having issues with the owner not being there/responsive during check-in), I wonder if he's a bit short staffed right now. He mentioned how hard hit the lodging and hostel business was hit due to covid travel restrictions and they they're still recovering, so he might not be able to hire the full staff he wants right now. Unsure...just conjecturing. We had booked 2 nights at Riad Baraka and then 1 night at Riad Sakura as we hadn't known how many nights would stay in Chefchaouen, so we booked a 100% refundable night at Sakura. When we went to Sakura they said they didn't have room for us, even though we had booked a night (through hostelworld). Luckily Riad Baraka had our room still available, and he said it was no problem and was very nice about it. I think the only problem we had was that the toilet paper would run out in the female bathroom, but that's easily solved by always traveling with a spare roll...

reviews.author: Lachlan Marshall
reviews.text: DO NOT STAY HERE! I’ve stayed at many hostels, some being worse rated advertised than this but this is the worst by far! So much misadvertisement. From the start the host wasn’t there when we arrived and gave us no check in instructions. We had to figure it out for ourselves. Finally we found the “owner who doesn’t work there just lives there” who got angry at us as we were impeding on his only free time at 4pm. We were given incorrect rooms to what we booked and paid for and were told to deal with it. He then got angry for not giving him the money we owed as he wasn’t there on arrival to give it to. We got the cash and gave it to him and he told us he would give the change later which we never received. He was rarely on site and was rude and ignorant with small things such as asking for toilet paper he said he’d get around to it later and never do it. He also has a brother or friend who lives or stays there. We had a confrontation with the owner over an incident which we aimed to handle peacefully but we were met with swearing and yelling and the brother got involved getting in our faces and getting hands on even picking up glass and threatening us. The breakfast is a plate of croissants and cake nothing else so no buffet or variety. He was also seems sleeping on the floor of the rooftop one night. Most unpleasant workers and hosts ever and most unpleasant experience. Don’t get fooled by the pictures and description because the host runs it so poorly

reviews.author: oscar
reviews.text: It’s hard to know where to begin. We arrived in the mid-afternoon with no instructions for check-in and no one to greet us. After waiting around for nearly an hour, a man finally appeared—only to immediately tell us we had “interrupted his one hour of peace” and that we had already ruined his day. Unfortunately, this was just the beginning of a pattern: he continued to mention throughout our stay how we were “ruining his day,” making us feel unwelcome and uncomfortable. We were checked into rooms we hadn’t booked, yet somehow made to feel like we were at fault. Whenever we asked for basic necessities like toilet paper, he would say “yes” but then leave and not return to the hostel for long stretches, making it hard to rely on him for anything. His defensive and unfriendly demeanor made it nearly impossible to ask questions or raise concerns. Although , the hostel has great rooftop that offers a peaceful spot to relax. But all of that was overshadowed by the tense and, at times, threatening atmosphere created by the host and his brother. A serious issue occurred when one of the hostel doors—already compromised by a loose hinge—fell and broke when used. We immediately said we would cover the cost, but instead of accepting this, the owner's brother became aggressive. He got in my friend’s face (someone who wasn’t even involved in the incident), called him a “midget,” and behaved in a way that suggested he wanted to physically fight him. This wasn’t a misunderstanding—this was a grown man, likely in his 50s, threatening a guest over a broken door we had offered to pay for. It was deeply uncomfortable and left us feeling unsafe. At one point, we also saw the owner lying in the main staircase—not sleeping there all night, but in a way that only added to the sense of disorder and discomfort. It’s a shame. The hostel has potential, and the city is incredible, but none of that can make up for the unprofessional, hostile, and threatening behavior we experienced. I would strongly caution others considering this place

reviews.author: ben m
reviews.text: Hey everyone, I don’t normally leave reviews on any place but I thought I would come on here to save anyone the trouble we went through. This place was hands down by far the worst place I have ever stayed at in my entire life. We first arrived and there was nobody seen to check in, and scattered papers we where supposedly meant to fill out after searching the whole building the owner comes out of the shower angry at us saying this is his “ shower time” during check in times. The worst was yet to come, during our stay in our room we closed one to the barthroom doors and it fell off its hinge as they must have been loose, smashing glass. The next day we were out and he went through all of our rooms when we were not there. He then confronted us about it and stared getting extremely angry and smashed a glass during it “by mistake”. Then during all of this his brother ( skinny, tattooed, 2 teeth ) from next door stormed up the stairs and started yelling to me and my friends, coming up into our faces wanted to fight us. He was very aggressive and seemed like he was going to punch one of us until the owner his brother had the calm him down and leave the hotel, overall this is not an exaggeration I’m a 21 year old guy with 5 mates and we did not feel safe staying at this hostel. I have no reason to lie and this is only here to help others not make the same mistake we did that turned the most stunning place in morrocco a very average stay.

reviews.author: divya hegde
reviews.text: Whoever designed this riad must possess an extraordinary artistic sensibility. Every corner of the space reflects a deep understanding of beauty, balance, and emotion. The color palette is chosen with such finesse — soothing yet vibrant, traditional yet fresh — creating an atmosphere that feels both timeless and alive. The placement of the furniture seems effortless, yet it’s undeniably intentional, creating cozy nooks and inviting spaces that naturally draw you in. What’s truly remarkable is the presence of greenery throughout the riad. The plants aren’t merely decorative; they breathe life into the space. There’s no strict rule to their arrangement — and yet, everywhere they are placed feels like exactly where they belong. Whether trailing from a windowsill or nestled beside a sunlit doorway, they feel like living brushstrokes in a grand painting. This place isn’t just designed; it’s curated with love- It’s drenched in artistry — not the kind that shouts, but the kind that whispers to your senses and quietly stirs your heart. The terraces of this riad are simply stunning — each one offering its own little slice of serenity. The swimming pool isn’t large, but it’s just the right size, surrounded by cozy sitting areas that invite you to linger and relax. I haven’t even had breakfast here yet, but I’m already soaking in the warmth and charm that fills every corner of this place. What I love is how every detail seems thoughtfully considered. The rooms may not be large, but they’re beautifully designed — intimate, elegant, and full of character. Even the bathrooms are lovely, maintaining that same understated style and attention to detail. And perhaps for the first time in a riad, I’ve noticed the little conveniences that make such a difference — proper space for bags and suitcases, well-placed shelves, and most importantly, a full-length mirror. It’s those small, thoughtful touches that really elevate the experience. I genuinely love every bit of it — this place is a quiet masterpiece of comfort and design. We are here only for 1 night, i wish we could stay for a little longer.

reviews.author: Happy Now
reviews.text: A stunningly beautiful place to stay overnight. Well maintained. Great view. You can tell the attention the host has put into making this place feel so warm and welcoming. Stairs are narrow and lots of climbing, so try bring light luggages. Be ware if you do not like community living. Can be noisy living together, but we love it. Electricity get short circuited a few times overnight, no big deal, easily fixed.

reviews.author: Janosch Graffenberger
reviews.text: I was there for the Hammam and it was a great experience. I can highly recommend it. It's a very beautiful Riad, the service is excellent. I've got tee and cookies while I wait and evrryone here is very friendly and reputable. The Hammam treatment was one hour, in that time I had the whole hammam room for myself while the staff member treated me with several tradional cleaning steps. Definitely worth the money :) Thank you!

reviews.author: Kate Irani
reviews.text: Very quaint stay at a beautiful home from a long time ago. Some of the rooms are grand and others a little bit tight if you’re carrying luggage. However the interiors and the terraces leave you wanting to stay longer. Service was with a smile no matter time of day. Please remember to take small bags or the Riad can organise their small van to meet your bus to bring your luggage up. There’s a bit of a walk and it’s uphill so be prepared.

reviews.author: karan dhawan
reviews.text: My experience with Riad Cherifa, located in the picturesque town of Chefchaouen, Morocco, was one of unparalleled hospitality and integrity, and although I couldn't make it to the property, the owner’s exceptional business ethics left a lasting impression. Due to unforeseen circumstances, I had to cancel my trip, and my booking was non-refundable. Despite the policy, the owner of Riad Cherifa demonstrated an incredible act of kindness and professionalism by refunding the entire amount without hesitation. It’s rare to find such genuine understanding and a customer-first approach in the hospitality industry. This is a clear testament to their ethical standards and commitment to treating their guests with fairness and compassion. Even though I didn't have the pleasure of experiencing the riad’s comfort firsthand, this gesture alone speaks volumes about the caliber of service and trustworthiness that Riad Cherifa offers. Any business that prioritizes integrity over profits deserves to be celebrated and supported. If you are planning a visit to Chefchaouen, I wholeheartedly recommend Riad Cherifa, not only for its reputed beauty and charm but also for the exceptional character of its owner. It’s businesses like these that renew your faith in hospitality and set the gold standard for others to follow.

reviews.author: Stephanie Moulton
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel! Our room felt like a movie set. The room and bathroom were clean and comfortable. There were extra blankets in the room, heat, and AC. Breakfast was scrambled omelet, pastries, yogurt, coffee, tea, juice, spreads, and breads. Great location! Very close to the central square, Kasbah, restaurants, and shops. It was pretty quiet for how central the location was. Staff are very friendly and helpful. Absolutely would recommend!

reviews.author: Jaclyn Lindabury
reviews.text: Great views from the rooftop. Staff were great; they helped us navigate taxis to and from the bus station and were with us every step of the way. The location was perfect and nearby the markets and restaurants. A small, buffet style breakfast was downstairs in the restaurant space.

reviews.author: Carla Benavides
reviews.text: good location. the single room I got was quite small. nice welcome with tea and cookies. service was good too, folks were nice and attentive.

reviews.author: A D
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, the staff are unbelievably polite (Rashid is AWESOME!), and it's located a few feet away from the center of the Medina. The rooms are enchanting and clean. Water pressure is good on the 2nd floor. The breakfast meets expectation: pastries, bread and jams, scrambled eggs, yogurt, coffee, tea, orange juice. It fuels us to start the day and it is much appreciated. The Kasbah is a 2-3 min walk, there are so many restaurants around it and many have rooftop seating. Note: when asking for taxi ride to the hotel, make sure they drop you off on top of the Medina so you roll your luggage down. If they drop you off at the bottom you will have to pull your luggage up a much longer way through all the small businesses. The beds were a little too hard for me. I also think a small shelf next to the shower or a shower rack would be helpful. I have a hanging toiletry bag that allowed me access to my stuff, and the water did pool about an inch.

reviews.author: Harold Soans
reviews.text: Beautiful part of town. Easy access to minouret which overlooks the best sunset and the evening calls for prayers.. Specially in Fridays. Don't miss it. Nice clean rooms with terrace breakfasts overlooking the blue city.

reviews.author: Darren Parker
reviews.text: Set in the back streets of the Medina, a very authentic Moroccan feel. Beautiful reception from the team. Big spacious room and comfortable bed. Nice spa area, just unfortunate not to have A masseuse available. Had a Hamman treatment which was great though. Nice feel to the hotel throughout. Great breakfast.

reviews.author: Anju Patwardhan
reviews.text: Loved the property. The rooms are beautifully done up and the service is exceptional. Staff are very friendly and super helpful. Enjoyed their Moroccan hamam, the indoor heated pool (they book it for 1 person only for an hour to provide privacy) and the spa (massage). Food is excellent and freshly prepared. So you need to order 1 hour in advance. Great location inside the Medina, with a nice view.

reviews.author: Shirley Vallance
reviews.text: A wonderful Ryad. English speaking staff who were extremely helpful and friendly. I had a traditional Hamman in the spa and it was great. Absolutely wonderful breakfast and enjoyed the evening meal as well. Highly recommend this place.

reviews.author: Joann Zwagerman
reviews.text: Everything was perfect. The first day we walked to the Spanish Mosque for the sunset when the view from our patio was just as good! We had an issue with our train service and they took the time to sort it out for us. They are very pleasant and kind. The Riad is in a great location, and the pool was a hit!

reviews.author: Marion Hanh
reviews.text: Hammam was great. We did a massage too and it was not that great as the lady I had was on her phone for some time, and the lady my partner had were just stroking him lightly most of the time.

name: Street Stall - Bab Ssour
address: Street Stall - Bab Ssour, Chefchaouen, Morocco

reviews.author: Oussama Souadka
reviews.text: Amazing fresh fish! The mixed seafood plate is something special - you can tell everything is perfectly cooked and really fresh. The chef knows what they're doing. Plus, the view from their terrace is absolutely beautiful. Will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Nitka Mittal
reviews.text: A peasant meal and evening at Bab Ssour While exploring the distinctive blue streets of Chefchaouen, finding Bab Ssour was a pleasant discovery. From the moment we entered, the atmosphere felt warm and inviting. The staff were notably friendly. Their welcome felt sincere, contributing to a comfortable sense of hospitality that set a positive tone for the meal. Simple things like the menu in multiple languages added to the experience. Choosing from the menu was made easier by the helpful staff at Bab Ssour. When I mentioned I was unsure what to order, they took the time to discuss the options and offered good recommendations based on my preferences. It was clear they knew their menu well and aimed to ensure guests had a rich experience. The food itself was very good. Following their suggestions, we enjoyed Moroccan flavours. The dishes tasted fresh and seemed carefully prepared. We thoroughly enjoyed Baisara, Lentil soup and the Moroccan mint tea. The goat tagine was tender and well-spiced. We capped the meal with their delicious yoghurt as dessert (caveat: it was very sweet, but we decided are on a holiday). For those seeking good, authentic Moroccan food served by welcoming staff who make you feel comfortable, Bab Ssour is a solid choice. It's certainly a great choice if you're in the area.

reviews.author: Slawek Gawronski
reviews.text: Couldn't find the main door, had to ask for the directions. Seem to be a family run restaurant. Nice view from rooftop terrace. Had to wait for a while to place the order, but the food was delicious.

reviews.author: George Olivier
reviews.text: This place was super popular w/ tourists as we had to wait in a short line before being seated. Upon entering, the place is hectic. It's very large w multiple levels for seating and extremely noisy. We shared a large table w/ another couple. In addition, the waiter was initially rude, inattentive and the kitchen was out of several dishes. Furthermore, the dishes came out @ random times w my appetizer being served before my entree and our drinks not being served until after we finished our meal. The food was solid and extremely cheap. We paid the equivalent of $14 for 2 starters, 2 entrees, and 2 desserts. 1 fast food meal in the U.S. costs more than that so that's definitely a good thing. I'd recommend this place as other patrons seemed to have a better go of it.

reviews.author: Donatas L
reviews.text: Enjoyed our lunch here! The food was tasty and prepared fairly quickly. I wouldn’t recommend the shrimp tajine—it was a bit too oily for my taste—but the other tajines were excellent! The view from the terrace wasn’t great, as it’s enclosed by windows.

reviews.author: kaira kaplinsky
reviews.text: The most magical Blue City in the world! Bucket list for all! The best time to explore without crowds is early morning right after sunrise. greeting sunsets at the Spanish mosque is a must, although be prepared for bugs😩😁

reviews.author: Nazim Lala
reviews.text: This is a beautiful town with very hospitable people. There aren't many sellers / hawkers constantly pestering you too but their wares, so you can really enjoy your stroll through town. We went later in the day when it cooled down a bit and there were fewer people in the streets.

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. Chefchaouen is a must-visit for photographers, art lovers, and anyone looking to experience Morocco’s laid-back and artistic side. Whether you’re exploring the picturesque alleys, enjoying a mint tea in a cozy café, or watching the sunset from a hilltop, every moment here feels magical.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: Beautiful city! I love the colors, the people, the food and most importantly the shops on the street😍 If you want to get away to the mountains for some peaceful time away from the city, I highly recommend spending two or three days in Chefchaouen!

reviews.author: Mourad Chafik
reviews.text: Chefchaouen’s medina is truly one of the most beautiful and peaceful places I’ve ever visited. The blue-washed walls, narrow alleys, and stunning doors create a dreamlike atmosphere that feels both relaxing and inspiring. Locals are friendly, the shops offer authentic handmade crafts, and there are plenty of cozy cafes to enjoy traditional Moroccan tea. It's the perfect place to wander without a map, discover hidden gems, and take amazing photos at every corner. Whether you're there for the colors, the culture, or just the peaceful vibe—Chefchaouen is unforgettable

reviews.author: Said Belowahed
reviews.text: Rabat is an amazing city to visit, There is a lot of places to see and enjoy, Hassan tower is an amazing place with the Shrine next to it, and view to river. The Mausoleum of Mohammed V is a mausoleum located on the opposite side of the Hassan Tower, on the Yacoub al-Mansour esplanade in Rabat, Morocco. It contains the tombs of the Moroccan king and his two sons, late King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah. The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah in Rabat, Morocco. It is located at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river opposite Salé. The Chellah or Shalla, is a medieval fortified Muslim necropolis located in the metro area of Rabat, Morocco, on the south side of the Bou Regreg estuary. The Phoenicians established a trading emporium at the site.

reviews.author: Jose Tavares
reviews.text: I really liked this medina, very little touristy and essentially frequented by the inhabitants of Rabat. while walking its streets I learned a lot about local habits. Inside the medina are some good restaurants, so you have to ask them why they are difficult to find. Medina very safe

reviews.author: Monsignore Catweasel
reviews.text: big old medina where you can buy a lot of different things. Mobile phones from all brands. Alot of different brands clothes shoes . Also in the have a nice food to get many meals and spices fom fastfood to cousine . There also many free shops where you buy anything handmade .

reviews.author: Errol Clement Dsouza
reviews.text: Nice place but street food charged me more because I was from a different country

reviews.text: Beautiful city , even though it is some times overcrowded but in most of the year it's a pleasant place to visit
