name: Street Stall - Ras El Ma
address: Street Stall - Ras El Ma, Chefchaouen, Morocco

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: Nice hike/ walk to "Ras el Maa" It makes you see the beauty of nature and admire God's creations. When in Chefchaouen, it is a must visit!

reviews.author: F K
reviews.text: Ras el Ma offers a delightful walking experience, particularly on a sunny day when the weather is just right. The trail meanders through beautiful landscapes, providing a peaceful atmosphere that enhances the enjoyment of the hike. Along the way, you’ll find several juice stations, perfect for quenching your thirst and refreshing yourself with local flavors as you navigate the path. At the start of the trail, you'll notice a lively presence of dogs, adding a charming and playful element to the journey. As you continue, these furry companions gradually become less frequent, allowing you to immerse yourself in the serene environment. As you ascend, the anticipation builds, culminating in a breathtaking view from the top. The sight of the entire blue city sprawled out below is nothing short of mesmerizing, with its iconic blue-painted buildings contrasting beautifully against the surrounding landscape. This panoramic vista captures the essence of the region, making the trek well worth it. Whether you’re seeking solitude or a moment to connect with nature, Ras el Ma provides a rewarding experience that combines the thrill of exploration with stunning visual rewards.

reviews.author: Tom Groves
reviews.text: Busy part of town with small waterfall and river running. Lots of people with stalls selling and kids swimming in the river. Cool atmosphere

reviews.author: Rasheed TK
reviews.text: I had the pleasure of staying at Ras El Ma for three days, and it was a truly unique experience. The area is defined by a cold stream water fall that flows through, creating a refreshing, forest-like atmosphere, especially at night. This stream is not just beautiful but also practical—local traders use the cold water to chill their freshly squeezed orange juices, which are a must-try. Ras El Ma serves as a gateway to both the Medina and Bouzafar Mosque, making it an ideal spot for exploring the historical and cultural highlights of Chefchaouen. The combination of natural beauty, vibrant local life, and historical significance makes Ras El Ma a perfect place to stay and soak in the charm of this enchanting blue city.

reviews.author: Fatima Mahmood (Fatima Pixi)
reviews.text: Not the best or more extravagant waterfall/spring I’ve ever seen, but it’s something nice to add to your itinerary! You can get fresh orange juice and chill by the water, it’s such a vibe 🍊🧡

reviews.author: Mark Tissot
reviews.text: The location changed due to development of the harbour area. Call them to check the new location. Now serve delicious fresh fish in an upmarket setting. Strongly recommended!

reviews.author: Ady Jurd
reviews.text: Food poisoning to two people, glad it's closed down it needed to be!

reviews.author: HG KRAUSE
reviews.text: It was nothing at all. The fish soup was watery, the avocado salad was undressed and tasteless. Main course ok, but the cleanliness is not good, plates are not clean and the floor is really greasy. There are so many good restaurants in Essaouira, this is not one of them.

reviews.author: Vigneul Motte
reviews.text: It's wise to book, especially in the evening! Restricted lunchtime hours Evenings from 8 p.m. are reasonably priced until 9:30 p.m. if booked in advance!

reviews.author: Julien Sarat
reviews.text: Good, but focus on simple fish dishes on the grill and avoid cooked dishes.

reviews.author: Annette Cerulli-Harms
reviews.text: Three of us went for the hammam “pack detente” experience - two as a couple and a single woman. We all had a fantastic experience. The place is clean, thoughtfully decorated, staff is well trained, respectful and skilful in providing a relaxing hammam and massage experience. Would go again and recommend it.

reviews.author: Andrea D.
reviews.text: Wonderful place. Worst cocktails ever. Took 30 minutes even though we were the only guests in the rooftop bar. Also very expensive. After complaining nothing has changed. We only got the information, owner and staff are new. What a bad service! We also had a massage with untrained workers, 400 dirhams. After complaining 3 times to do a massage and no strokes it got better. But there are much better locations in Essaouira for spa. High class massage and perfect cocktails. The best part of the stay is the riad and the decor, with great attention to detail. On the picture you see Gin and Jam, 110 dirhams. 😁

reviews.author: Michelle Kent
reviews.text: I had one of the best relaxing massages I have ever had. Hafida was professional and courteous and I left feeling and smelling amazing!!

reviews.author: Bart Devos
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel and infrastructure. Kind and helpful staff. Delicious breakfast. Amazing rooftop bar and restaurant. Absolutely recommended.

reviews.author: deborah dewolff
reviews.text: We went there for a massage, and it was an amazing experience!! The masseuse was very nice and the overall staff lovely!

reviews.author: Marie Laboucarie
reviews.text: By far the best furniture store in all Essaouira! The curation is made with incredible taste and the place is extremely well designed. Congrats again on putting together such a precious jewel, can’t wait to come back

reviews.author: Hannah Braithwaite
reviews.text: You must check this place out! Huge collection of so many amazing things! The owner is such a nice guy and I think they can ship to your home too.

reviews.author: Yuna Rapoport
reviews.text: Incredible collection and very insightful and friendly owner who speaks perfect English (in addition to French).

reviews.author: Fawzia Radman
reviews.text: Five flors of amazing stuff! Incredible finds! One needs an entire day just to search.

reviews.author: Philip Chua
reviews.text: This place is amazing - ambience takes you back in time, food is superlative, service is excellent, music is astounding!!!

reviews.author: Hicham Hnini
reviews.text: La Fromagerie isn’t just a restaurant — it’s an experience. Tucked away in the countryside outside Essaouira, it feels like a hidden sanctuary where everything slows down. From the moment you arrive, you’re welcomed like family. There’s no formal menu — just a generous table filled with house-made cheeses, fresh bread, olives, and warm, comforting dishes made with local ingredients. The cheeses are the stars — each one with its own story, texture, and character. The owner takes time to explain them all with pride and passion, which makes you appreciate every bite even more. The setting is rustic and peaceful, surrounded by olive trees, goats, and sunshine — you completely forget the noise of the city. If you’re looking for a quiet, soulful food experience that’s different from the usual tourist spots, this is it. Come with an open mind, a good appetite, and some time to relax. This place stays with you — not just for the food, but for how it makes you feel.

reviews.author: Julian Rolfe
reviews.text: La Fromagerie was included as part of a bespoke food and culture trip to Morocco. We had a quick visit to the cheese production room, it was the end of Eid al-Adha so many of the staff were away enjoying the festivities. To be honest, some of the reviews are naive, no wine, what do you expect! The food was beautifully simple. The fried cheese In bread with the sprouting seeds was delicious, all of the cheeses were delicious, the lamb mechoui was outstanding. The visit to see the goats and chickens was great fun too, learning about the process and especially not using lemon to kick start the cheese process, which really had an impact on the delicious flavour.!

reviews.author: Jonas Jacobs
reviews.text: A true hidden gem just a few minutes outside of Essaouira. Every dish is bursting with flavor, and the use of local ingredients—especially the recurring presence of goat cheese—adds a beautiful depth and consistency to the menu. The mechoui, a slow-cooked goat dish, was absolutely outstanding: tender, rich, and full of character. One small suggestion for improvement would be to include a drink menu, ideally with wine pairings to complement the cheese. Highly recommended for food lovers seeking something authentic and refined.

reviews.author: Emma Bachmann
reviews.text: We had high expectations for this restaurant based on its glowing reviews, but unfortunately, our experience fell short. The setting itself is beautiful—secluded, with an oasis-like atmosphere and authentic decor that should make for a truly memorable visit. The promise of cheese and wine to round off the meal was especially enticing. However, the reality didn’t quite match up. When we arrived, the restaurant was completely empty. While this might be due to visiting during the off-season, it did make us wonder about its usual appeal. The menu structure was another letdown—you couldn’t simply choose a dish but had to commit to a full four-course menu. Unfortunately, the food was bland and uninspiring, making the wait for the cheese feel longer than it should have. And even when we finally got to the much-anticipated cheese, it turned out to be a selection of the same type at different aging stages, and found both a hair and a fly squashed into the pieces—not quite what we had hoped for. Another disappointment was the lack of drink options. With only water available and no wine or even soda to accompany the meal, the experience felt incomplete. This restaurant has everything it needs to be an incredible dining destination—the ambiance, the concept, and the potential for a great culinary experience. But based on our visit, it fell flat. Hopefully, with some adjustments, it can live up to its potential.

reviews.author: Hassib Marouf
reviews.text: A very beautiful place. The owner and the staff were extremely kind and the ambiente was very cozy and quiet We had a Menu with a lot of different food (salade, tajine, ...) and finally a cheese plate with the home made goat cheeses.

reviews.author: Toby Savage
reviews.text: What a lovely restaurant! We thoroughly enjoyed our meal here tonight and look forward to another visit. Great food and delightful hosts. Thank you

reviews.author: Neil Richardson
reviews.text: Wonderful restaurant with rich dark wood theme. The room was peaceful and well decorated. Staff very attentive and polite. Food was well prepared and full of flavour. I had lamb tajine and was not disappointed. Waitress gave good wine recommendations and kept an eye for when to top up glasses. I would recommend this lovely place and come back again

reviews.author: Stanislaw Mackowiak
reviews.text: Beautiful restaurant with great atmosphere. The food was lovely, the farmers salad was fresh and the tagine was piping hot. Service was super friendly - would highly recommend!

reviews.author: Jill Lowe
reviews.text: This restaurant is lovely inside. Dark wood, candles and original artwork set the scene. We had delicious chicken, lemon and olive tagine. This does not come with any carbs, so we asked for extra bread. This was not a problem. Please ask for Apple and honey pastilla with whisky ice cream for your dessert. You will not be disappointed!

reviews.author: Kristine Hartman
reviews.text: Great restaurant just inside the old Medina walls and next to the ocean. Amazing quality and quantity of food for the prices. Especially set in the upscale atmosphere. Service was perfect. Food was wonderful. We had the chickpea & apple salad, veggie couscous and a dill tagliatelle fish plate. Also a large bottle of sparkling water and a half bottle of red Moroccan wine for only 70 MAD. Our ENTIRE tab...340 MAD Note: they do not accept credit cards.

name: La Table by Madada
address: La Table by Madada, Essaouira, Morocco

reviews.author: runningdogyankee
reviews.text: Excellent food and ambiance. Fresh seafood with the chef’s touch. Just the right flavorings to the sauce in the clam pasta. Not overwhelming with tomatoes. Seafood soup infused with fresh local spices. Wonderful ambiance and packed with diners. You need a reservation to get a table.

reviews.author: Rafael Kacinari
reviews.text: The best restaurant in Essaouira! The atmosphere is reminiscent of a posh French restaurant. The service is impeccable, and there's a great wine list to accompany the refined menu. We had a seasonal salad to start, fresh and full of flavour, followed by a top-quality John Dory fillet and a delicious millefeuille of vegetables. Don’t miss this restaurant when in town. Greetings to the charming restaurant manager from a Croatian couple!

reviews.author: Marco Kramer
reviews.text: Very nice and fancy restaurant. Definitely one of the best in Essaouira. Seating however is horrible (benches and seats are low..) food and atmosphere is nontheless perfect!

reviews.author: Ruth Reynolds
reviews.text: Everything about this place was great. We walked in and the vibes were excellent. There was a man playing acoustic guitar & a dancer who performed intermittently throughout the meal. The decor was lovely, fine dining chic. The food was great, steak was cooked to perfection and the sauce was delicious. The bill came to just over 1100dh between 3, which is on the pricier side for restaurants in Essaouira but more than worth it for La Table.

reviews.author: Enya Yau
reviews.text: Nice environment, nice food, nice service and nice music. We enjoyed our night here very much.

reviews.text: Nice environment, nice food, nice service and nice music. We enjoyed our night here very much.

name: Le Chalet de la Plage
address: Le Chalet de la Plage, Essaouira, Morocco

reviews.author: Zhanna Leonteva
reviews.text: Went there only for drinks. The service was quite slow, although it was nice to be seated with the view overlooking the beach.

reviews.author: MarLies Hofstede
reviews.text: The location by the beach is nice. It was recommended by our hotel but later they said only to go there daytime. We had dinner. Both ordered small sole. My husband did not eat his since it had a bad smell. The waiter said it was fine!! 😳 the worst reaction to give. Then I did not trust my fish either. The waiter said the other soles were all the same 😂 so we ordered tajine with sardine balls. Mwoah, a lot of garlic but we ate some. So not to be recommended.

reviews.author: MARK MATTHEWS
reviews.text: One of those places living on a past reputation over price and with owners and staff that actually believe their doing you the favour of serving you staff attitude fine if you don’t mention any problem like under cooked fish or hair in the food. Lovely setting to eat my father food was lovely well cooked and tasty mine looked amazing but one piece of fish was well under cooked it was busy so did not mention it. I did how ever after virtually completing my meal find the longest black hair I asked the waiter to look 👀 he just said not there problem its blown in from the beach may be but it must have landed under the chips was a clever hair. I did not photograph it as I felt sick at the thought of what I had just eaten and the attitude so just stood up went to the owner and asked for the bill. The conversation in Arabic was as follows between lady owner and waiter manager whats wrong with them waiter they say he had a hair in his food manager did they finish the food waiter yes all of it manage well thats ok then. Such a shame I bet it could be amazing if they work on customer service.Also like to add do you know what a fish knife is you need some 🤣

reviews.author: Bogdan Tasnadi
reviews.text: Good seafood and agreable service. Very nie setting, specially on the terrave, next to the beach. Good choice of dishes and drinks. Prices above average, notably for the drinks. They have a private parking ot nearby.

reviews.author: Morocco First
reviews.text: As a tour operator in the US I brought a group of American tourists to this filty restaurant. The owner is thinking he is important by hanging a pictures of himself with some french actors. We had a reservation for 14 pax. Unfortunately, three of the group didn't eat, so I lost the menu price for 3 pax which I tought it wasn't the restaurant's fault, but two of customers from the group asked if they can switch from having fish to Shrimps. The owner said this is impossible, it can't happen like this way. In the meantime my group still waiting for just a salad to be served over 30 minutes while I can see French customers walking from outside getting served quicker than us. I went to the waiter to ask what's going on. He said its not my Problem, I told them already about it We spent over 2 hours to have a lunch for a small. I took a pick inside the kitchen very dirty and smelly. I am not sure but I felt ike this Restaurant doesn’t like American tourists. I will never ever bring any groups there. Terrible service and a scammer owner. The food was below average. Stay away from it. Don't be impressed by the hanging pictures.

reviews.author: Mike Hobday
reviews.text: Very poor service

reviews.author: carlo abriani
reviews.text: Visited 11.13.14. Nice place with veranda overlooking the beach, clean facilities, efficient and polite waiter. Good and plentiful shrimp appetizer, the sea bass of the day was unfortunately decidedly undercooked and inside, near the plug, decidedly raw and with traces of blood (serious). €52. in 4 only with water.

reviews.author: Kastanienhof Gästehaus
reviews.text: Our visit on February 27, 2013, to "Le Coquillage" in the free port of Essaouria, Morocco, was very disappointing. The food was tasteless (vegetables cooked mushy, sea bream unseasoned), three of the nine sea urchins seemed bad. Overpriced and bad by Moroccan standards. By the way, we were the only guests that evening and, after declining a dessert order, were escorted out without being asked to provide the bill. Very bad, the seafood was not fresh, the fish and vegetables were unseasoned and absolutely overcooked. An expensive and bad location.

reviews.author: younes ASRI
reviews.text: Decent food, nothing more, and a superb view of the Essaouira corniche and the beach. But that might change with the construction of a seawall right in front.

reviews.author: francois-georges Pradel
reviews.text: With such a location, we expect to find the pearl of Essaouira's fish restaurants.....and the disappointment is heavy...the table on the terrace with a view of the sea fails to do so. forget the depressing amateurism of the cuisine and the service.....the products are not what we have the right to expect, and.......recount your change carefully before going out... ....lol I only spent one day in Essaouira and that is my only disappointment, the rest of the city and the people who live there are wonderful....... I will come back, but I will go eat my lobster elsewhere...... lol

reviews.author: Scarlett Pyemont
reviews.text: Had a delicious dinner here yesterday with my family. As soon as we went in we were amazed by how beautiful the restaurant is! The atmosphere was so nice and the servers were attentive and really friendly. We ordered starters and a main course each, all were very fancy and very scrum. There were lit candles everywhere, even in the bathroom! This restaurant is so nice and i highly recommend :)

reviews.author: David Hastead
reviews.text: Fantastic. After a week in morroco the highlight of culinary delight. French Morrocon, live music, enjoyable but not overwhelming.

reviews.author: Michael G
reviews.text: Nice Seafood, Grumpy Service. Beautiful room with candles and live music. The fresh fish was nicely prepared, but not special. The service was poor, once served I never saw the server again. The server brought me the wrong wine and then became very grumpy when I asked to be charge for the one I ordered. They say they take credit cards but when you go to pay the claim the machine is not working, so cash only. There are heaps of restaurants here, most with happy service.

reviews.author: Karaev Ishan
reviews.text: After a long car trip you arrive in an old port area with a chilling wind and a strong smell of the ocean. You choose a riad to stay and get there a recomendation to dinner at Le Patio. When you get there, you take a bottle of white local wine and the fish of the day. Here your perfect evening begins.

reviews.author: vittorio vedove
reviews.text: I think the bad review of this place are not right.. his intimacy is unknown in the city, the dishes were really good with uncommon flavours. The goat cheese and veggies was awesome 10/10 the shirmp cigars good 8/10 main dishes we tried: Lamb shoulder was very tender and the gravy sauce had the right flavours 10/10 , fish tajin with pears a 10/10

reviews.author: Aymen TOUHENT
reviews.text: Live band singing for fun! Not at all happy with the quality of the performance. The music that started was 100 times better.

reviews.author: Emna Masmoudi
reviews.text: Friendly atmosphere Friendly environment Top service

reviews.author: Foued Daly
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Grech Anis
reviews.text: nan

name: Mille et Une Nuits
address: Mille et Une Nuits, Essaouira, Morocco

reviews.author: steve sharratt
reviews.text: You simply have to make the effort to visit here if you are in Essaouira, do walk or take a local taxi and pay what you think the taxi is worth to you, we paud 50 dhirums n driver was well happy (that’s £4). Drinks and food are great as is the food, you’ll see all the sights from this bar,watersports,camels and horses too.

reviews.author: Bradley Miller
reviews.text: A must go to for an Essaouira visit. Best sunset spot. Drinks are reasonably priced and pizza is a super delicious flat crust style. Definitely recommend the Kefta one. Service is phenomenal but the best part is the ocean side camels and horses right outside the window. Live music. Great atmosphere. This place has everything I’ve ever wanted!

reviews.author: Mariana Ortiz
reviews.text: Beautiful views, delicious food, and relaxing vibes. Try their pizza and shrimp 🍤, we also had the croquettes. I highly recommend this place - it also has live music to add to the ambience. Easy street parking.

reviews.author: V B (Pixie)
reviews.text: Lovely scenic restaurant to relax and eat after a long walk along the coast. I decided to stop here at Ocean Vagabond. I had the 4 fromages pizza and Aperol Spritz, what can I say the pizza was delicious 😋 and the waiting staff were friendly and the service was very good.

reviews.author: Laura van den Boogert
reviews.text: I can highly recommend this cool and hip place! I went here twice. The food is excellent and the atmosphere is nice. The first good rose/wine I've had in Morocco. I also like the cats walking around sniffing for food ;). (I let them, if you don't want the cats that's no problem)

reviews.author: PHIL V
reviews.text: My wife and I had dinner here last night based on all the positive reviews. We found the reviews to be spot on. The food was delicious, the service very friendly and efficient, atmosphere very pleasing and cost, very affordable. Excellent choice for lunch or dinner. Cash only but don’t let that deter you from one of the best restaurants in Essaouira.

reviews.author: Nahim&Sabreen AR
reviews.text: Kind and welcoming service in a clean, homey setting. The food was very tasty, and the portions were very generous. The decor was also fun to observe as we ate, with all the historic artefacts on the walls.

reviews.author: Chris Campbell
reviews.text: The food was great, reasonably priced, and the staff were all super friendly. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Bulubulu
reviews.text: Sweet nice mint tea and malty beer. Food are very tasty. Environment is relaxing. It was recommended by our bnb host for traditional Moroccan food that is not very touristy although they do have english menu. Staff are super friendly, one helps to entertain a kid in the other table. 3 course set menu is 139 dirham, you can order just a main course with 95 dirham.

reviews.author: Victor Eshkeri
reviews.text: This is a little gem. A beautiful and relaxed restaurant, and the best meal I had in Morocco expertly balanced with the recommended wine. The owner is a character, kind and full of life, and the staff all attentive and delightful. Just don’t forget to take cash (no card machine); I promise it is worth it.

reviews.author: Willy Janssens
reviews.text: Great location with ocean view. Porter picked up luggage from the car outside the walls of the Medina and brought them back. Good restaurant in which you can bring in wine from outside as they don’t serve alcohol.

reviews.author: Peter Walpole
reviews.text: It is seldom I have been ushered out of a Hotel bang on the dot of 12.00 …because the porter had to return to take other baggage to awaiting cars ….i was making a last minute email before I lost the internet….when I say ushered …I should say told to leave !! The Riad has old world charm and amazing views of the sea…..the Old World Charm extends to loose bathroom taps , a bath shower tap you couldn’t regulate , waste bins not emptied , curtains that didn’t draw and a picturesque window that was dirty and only opened with the strength of a strong man ! Breakfast was very ordinary compared to the high cost of room , cold boiled eggs , packet baked croissants and odd selection of bits and pieces …rounded off with almost fresh bread … If you like this kind of Old World Charm …then this is the place for you …..

reviews.author: Lukas Fuhs
reviews.text: Our stay at Hotel Mimuna in Essaouira was very enjoyable. The hotel is beautiful, and our room had a perfect sea view. The breakfast was excellent, with fresh and tasty options. The staff was friendly and helpful, and the luggage service was well organized. Overall, a great place to stay if you’re looking for a comfortable and scenic hotel in Essaouira.

reviews.author: Rasmus Bredvig
reviews.text: Had a really calm visit here. The way the rooms are setup facing the ocean makes for wonderful views! Staff was very friendly and the atmosphere of the hotel was in general very relaxed

reviews.author: Jan Naszewski
reviews.text: Great location, we had a room with a sea view. Staff was very friendly but overall the hotel is average and definitely not worth the price, you can get a hotel in the area with same or better quality for half the price. The room was not 100% clean on arrival, which was fixed after we complained.

reviews.author: Telah Morrison
reviews.text: Decent Riad in the Medina. Rooms are clean. There was a faint smell in our room and a fellow traveller had to change rooms as their room really smelled of sewage. Locations is very convenient. Hot water runs out, and there is no heat or AC in the rooms

reviews.author: Maciej Baginski
reviews.text: Cheap Hotel with Riad decorations, good for 1 night stay, but not comfortable for longer. Poor breakfast. Positives: exclent location in the medina close to restaurants, shops and town. Nice reception guy. Negatives: No heating in the room in January (cold in night), smells strange, breakfast with almost none vegetables.

reviews.author: Tony Clark
reviews.text: An acceptable guest house, good location. Rooms adequate, very clean. It's rare that I post any management issues, with many years of travel behind me. The main Front house manager FARAH, has a rude arrogant dismissive attitude. small requirements for the room were ignored, as if it was myself was the problem. I can't recommend this guest house with this poor behaviour and service from management

reviews.author: grizzly Canada
reviews.text: not sure how the hotel gets 4 stars, rooms are very small, breakfast is limited. staying here two nights, one night didn't have hot water, the reception came, and just let water run for a few minutes, and said "let water running after 5 minutes", not recommend.

reviews.author: Angela Mastandrea
reviews.text: When we arrived, there were no towels in our room and we quickly found out that there was no hot water either. Manager came to fix it and when i showered the next day it was better. Breakfast was nice, varied. Located right in the medina and a short walk to the beach.

name: Street Stall - Bab Doukkala
address: Street Stall - Bab Doukkala, Essaouira, Morocco

name: Street Stall - Essaouira Beach
address: Street Stall - Essaouira Beach, Essaouira, Morocco

reviews.author: Noura EL ALLAM (Flare)
reviews.text: Amazing beach especially during the sunset time, you can ride, quads, camels and horses also learn to surf as there are many people who provide these services. Get healthy juice on the way and there are good restaurants nearby. The only inconvenience there are the dogs, some of them aren’t friendly and the province should do something about it.

reviews.author: walid abbadi
reviews.text: Strong Winds and Ideal Water Sports: Essaouira Beach is known for its strong and steady trade winds, making it an ideal destination for windsurfing and kitesurfing. * Stunning Natural Beauty: The beach boasts soft golden sand and clear blue waters, overlooking the historic island of Mogador. * A Calm and Relaxing Atmosphere: Unlike some other Moroccan beaches, Essaouira Beach has a more relaxed and peaceful atmosphere, making it ideal for families and individuals seeking relaxation. * Proximity to the Enchanting Old Town: The beach is located close to Essaouira's old medina (walled city), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, allowing visitors to easily explore the history and culture of the region. * Diverse Activities: In addition to water sports and relaxation, visitors can enjoy horse or camel rides along the beach, long walks along the promenade, and fresh seafood at seaside restaurants.

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: Wow! You can’t visit Morocco without stopping by Essaouira and its beautiful beach. The calm waves, the fresh ocean breeze… just perfect. And the sunset? Absolutely breathtaking. The weather was amazing, warm but refreshing. Walking through the souk felt like something out of a music video—colorful stalls, the smell of spices, and such a relaxed vibe. Everything about this place is just so special. Whether you’re wandering the medina, chilling by the water, or grabbing fresh seafood, you’ll fall in love with it. Can’t wait to go back!

reviews.author: Alexandru Ioan
reviews.text: Large, beautiful beach with few people on it. You have to walk inside the sea a lot to swim as the slop is very gentle. Be careful of the tide. It can come fast and wet your belongings if you're not careful.

reviews.author: Petr Weiss
reviews.text: A wide sandy beach with pebbles, occasional umbrellas and loungers. Fairly large waves for swimming or surfing. You might want to try windsurfing or kitesurfing instead. There are a public toilets nearby (for 2 or 3MAD).

name: Street Stall - Fish Market
address: Street Stall - Fish Market, Essaouira, Morocco

reviews.author: Kevin Costello
reviews.text: The fish markets of Essaouria are amazingly busy places. Very slippery and smelly but a fantastic insight into the local industry and how it supports tourism. Lots to see

reviews.author: Ioana Costea
reviews.text: Tourist trap if you choose to have the fish cooked on site. We did this and ended up paying twice as much as in the port area where you will get the same experience, but in a much more pleasant setting.

reviews.author: Mike Gmt
reviews.text: Learn a bit of Arabic. Be patient and pick what you want to eat. Buy. Get it cleaned. Find the place where to eat. They will BBQ it. Wonderful. Just remember that you are going there for the experience.

reviews.author: Lisa2023
reviews.text: Fresh catches of the day, you can buy the seafood and the restaurant there cook it for you. Delicious

reviews.author: Dan Murphy
reviews.text: Decide on a purchase with the vendors and make the exchange with them if you intend to take some fish to a restaurant and have them cook it. Beware the touts. You will almost certainly be approached by touts looking to help you with the fish and grill it for you. They WILL take a big premium for this. I recommend that you do not engage with them. MAKE THE PURCHASE YOURSELF WITH THE FISHMONGER AND TAKE IT TO A RESTAURANT OF YOUR CHOOSING FOR THE BEST EXPERIENCE.

reviews.author: kaira kaplinsky
reviews.text: The most magical Blue City in the world! Bucket list for all! The best time to explore without crowds is early morning right after sunrise. greeting sunsets at the Spanish mosque is a must, although be prepared for bugs😩😁

reviews.author: Nazim Lala
reviews.text: This is a beautiful town with very hospitable people. There aren't many sellers / hawkers constantly pestering you too but their wares, so you can really enjoy your stroll through town. We went later in the day when it cooled down a bit and there were fewer people in the streets.

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. Chefchaouen is a must-visit for photographers, art lovers, and anyone looking to experience Morocco’s laid-back and artistic side. Whether you’re exploring the picturesque alleys, enjoying a mint tea in a cozy café, or watching the sunset from a hilltop, every moment here feels magical.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: Beautiful city! I love the colors, the people, the food and most importantly the shops on the street😍 If you want to get away to the mountains for some peaceful time away from the city, I highly recommend spending two or three days in Chefchaouen!

reviews.author: Mourad Chafik
reviews.text: Chefchaouen’s medina is truly one of the most beautiful and peaceful places I’ve ever visited. The blue-washed walls, narrow alleys, and stunning doors create a dreamlike atmosphere that feels both relaxing and inspiring. Locals are friendly, the shops offer authentic handmade crafts, and there are plenty of cozy cafes to enjoy traditional Moroccan tea. It's the perfect place to wander without a map, discover hidden gems, and take amazing photos at every corner. Whether you're there for the colors, the culture, or just the peaceful vibe—Chefchaouen is unforgettable

reviews.author: Said Belowahed
reviews.text: Rabat is an amazing city to visit, There is a lot of places to see and enjoy, Hassan tower is an amazing place with the Shrine next to it, and view to river. The Mausoleum of Mohammed V is a mausoleum located on the opposite side of the Hassan Tower, on the Yacoub al-Mansour esplanade in Rabat, Morocco. It contains the tombs of the Moroccan king and his two sons, late King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah. The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah in Rabat, Morocco. It is located at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river opposite Salé. The Chellah or Shalla, is a medieval fortified Muslim necropolis located in the metro area of Rabat, Morocco, on the south side of the Bou Regreg estuary. The Phoenicians established a trading emporium at the site.

reviews.author: Jose Tavares
reviews.text: I really liked this medina, very little touristy and essentially frequented by the inhabitants of Rabat. while walking its streets I learned a lot about local habits. Inside the medina are some good restaurants, so you have to ask them why they are difficult to find. Medina very safe

reviews.author: Monsignore Catweasel
reviews.text: big old medina where you can buy a lot of different things. Mobile phones from all brands. Alot of different brands clothes shoes . Also in the have a nice food to get many meals and spices fom fastfood to cousine . There also many free shops where you buy anything handmade .

reviews.author: Errol Clement Dsouza
reviews.text: Nice place but street food charged me more because I was from a different country

reviews.author: Mohammed Ezzine HADDADY (‫محمد الزين الحدادي‬‎)
reviews.text: Beautiful city , even though it is some times overcrowded but in most of the year it's a pleasant place to visit

name: Street Stall - Place Moulay Hassan
address: Street Stall - Place Moulay Hassan, Essaouira, Morocco

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: Walking through the vibrant streets of Essaouira's Medina was like stepping back in time. The whitewashed walls, blue-painted doors, and narrow alleyways create a captivating atmosphere that blends history with artistic flair. Local artisans display their handmade crafts and paintings, giving the area a unique bohemian vibe. The bustling markets are full of life, with vendors selling colorful textiles, intricate pottery, and fresh produce. The coastal breeze and the scent of spices make wandering through the maze-like alleys a sensory delight. Don't miss the chance to visit the iconic ramparts, which offer stunning views of the Atlantic Ocean. Essaouira is a perfect blend of culture, history, and creativity – a must-visit for those seeking an authentic Moroccan experience.

reviews.author: Rob “BOBY” K
reviews.text: This is the true heart of Essaouira, a place that never sleeps. There's always something happening here; it's full of people, music, and scents. This isn't a monument you just look at – it's a place that you truly experience. From one side of the square, you enter the narrow streets of the medina, and from the other, you can smell the ocean and see the port. You can sit in one of the many cafés, order a mint tea, and just watch the scene for hours. You'll see vendors, fishermen returning from their catch, and tourists from all over the world wandering about. It has a great, lively atmosphere. It's the essence of the city in one spot. You absolutely have to sit there for a while and soak in the vibe.

reviews.author: Abdelkabir BOUDRARI
reviews.text: In the evening, Essaouira's medina transforms into a lively tapestry of sights and sounds. The whitewashed walls and blue shutters glow under the setting sun, casting a serene ambiance. Street performers fill the air with music, while the scent of grilled seafood from the bustling port mingles with the salty breeze. Locals and visitors alike stroll along the ramparts, enjoying panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean as the sky transitions from golden to twilight hues. The city's vibrant nightlife emerges, offering cozy cafés, rooftop bars, and intimate music venues, making Essaouira a captivating destination after dark.

reviews.author: Ana Hi
reviews.text: A breezy coastal gem, Essaouira offers relaxed vibes, fresh seafood, and a charming medina. Windsurfers love it, and the old port city is full of artistic flair and colorful scenes.

reviews.author: Kevin Costello
reviews.text: Great open space next to the port and medina with multiple uses depending on the time of day and season. A centre for arts and crafts and recreation, and to just sit on the wall and watch the world go by.

reviews.author: Ben_glt 34
reviews.text: Many shops without salespeople harassing you to buy

reviews.author: Hanna M
reviews.text: A souk as you'd imagine it. A lot of chatter and little substance. But despite everything, the people are very nice and friendly!

reviews.author: TheYvanbreizh
reviews.text: Souk not interesting.

reviews.author: Gratien pub (gpnam)
reviews.text: Just one place, tourist bus stopped, everything else being closed.

reviews.author: Ross Daniels
reviews.text: This is an absolutely fantastic place a bit of a labyrinth but so enjoyable with winding streets and multiple marketplaces and plenty of cafes and eating spots. Great atmosphere and one of the streets will take you down to the beach. We spent hours just wandering around and it’s up there with any marketplace in Morocco.

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: This has got to be the best souk in Morocco! I’ve been to many, but Essaouira’s felt so special. I spent about five hours there and still didn’t want to leave. Each shop has its own unique vibe, and the shopkeepers were incredibly kind and helpful. Every time I asked where to find something, they wouldn’t just point me in the direction—they’d actually walk me there and leave without the other shopkeepers noticing. It was such a genuine experience. You’ll find everything from handmade Moroccan teapots and beautiful tea glasses to breathtaking paintings and handmade rugs, linen clothing, genuine leather goods, and the most fragrant spices. If you’re looking for authentic treasures, this is the place!

reviews.author: Mohammed nurul Islam
reviews.text: Best place to shop in all city

reviews.author: Federica Preda
reviews.text: Beautiful and quaint! The shops are full of local souvenirs and for all budgets! Exceptional fish and real Argan oil! We will definitely return. A quiet city where you can reach everything on foot.

reviews.author: World Trip
reviews.text: A favorite ❤️ A truly delightful souk in the port city of Essaouira ✅ The climate is pleasant and the people are truly friendly!

reviews.author: Khedira Ghazi
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: ida russo
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Emma Emily
reviews.text: Stopped here after walking round the port. Although drinks are not mentioned on the menu board outside, there is a side entrance that leads to a rooftop bar. We had a couple of beers and some pretty good chicken skewers. They also had pizza and a variety of other meals. There is a view over the water from some tables, and a good place to relax.

reviews.author: joe van der meulen
reviews.text: Very cool rooftop bar and THE PLACE TO GO if you want to drink alcohol. Fun party vibe with excellent live band with proper stage and PA. It’s a great place for a night out and they often play gnaoua music although they didn’t when we were there. Music was still great. Not cheap but well worth the money for a free gig and great atmosphere xoxo PS. We didn’t try the food But the staff were dancing which was fun to watch

reviews.author: Christopher Penny
reviews.text: Great place with a fab view and good food. My tip would be to make sure you wear a jacket or hoodie because the terrace gets windy and cool. booze.

reviews.author: Peter Lambrose
reviews.text: Although you do have to pay an entrance fee, you get 2 drinks with it. In some ways it balances it out. I didn’t even bother trying the food, the drinks were fine. I was told to go there for a very specific reason. That is watching the sunset at their roof bar. You can see the beach on one side, where the sun sets. You can also see the fort thing Essaouria has as well as the barren rocks. All these tied in with the sunset is a great view, and I highly recommend checking it out. The ambiance is fine, the staff are fine, the drinks are fine, but the view in unbeatable.

reviews.author: Bradley Miller
reviews.text: Awesome bar/restaurant! Have great live music, decent drink prices, and the pizza is pretty solid too! Great vibes and super great ambiance, totally worth the climb up the stairs!

reviews.author: Emma Emily
reviews.text: Stopped here after walking round the port. Although drinks are not mentioned on the menu board outside, there is a side entrance that leads to a rooftop bar. We had a couple of beers and some pretty good chicken skewers. They also had pizza and a variety of other meals. There is a view over the water from some tables, and a good place to relax.

reviews.author: Jeff Zander
reviews.text: The personnel were some of the most pleasant people you can find, loved the atmosphere and the cafe was located within the Medina near the blue gate. Got the camel burger, excellent and got the carrot cake, also excellent. Highly recommended

reviews.author: Stephen Anyan
reviews.text: Had an amazing experience at Café Clock and I can’t recommend it enough! The ambiance is warm and inviting, with a unique blend of cozy corners and an artistic vibe that makes you feel right at home. The facilities are good (by North African standards) The food? Brilliant. The menu is diverse, with plenty of options to suit all tastes, and everything I tried was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. But what really made my visit stand out was the exceptional service. Not only was the staff attentive and friendly, but I also had a small incident where I dropped my wallet in the bathroom. I wasn’t aware it was gone until I was about to leave, but a man who had been playing guitar noticed it and kindly returned it to me. That kind of thoughtful gesture really added a personal touch to the experience. 4.5 stars for me. Not giving 5 stars because it’s not a wheelchair accessible area.

reviews.author: Y S
reviews.text: They have many cozy rooms and beautiful terraces. The food was great as well! We tried their recommendation, the camel burger—it was our first time eating camel meat, and it had a unique and delicious taste. Unfortunately, we couldn’t finish our lemonade and ginger drink because it was a bit too strong for us! 😅

reviews.author: Amy Leese
reviews.text: Gorgeous setting and friendly attentive staff. I was guided to rooftop area with plenty of seating. Super chilled vibe. Relaxing. Attracts tourists. Mostly young singles or young families. I tried the famous camel burger!! 🍔 Well cooked and presented. Never tried camel before!!!

reviews.author: Brendan DS
reviews.text: Legendary Fez cafe which now has branches across Morocco. Housed in a Riad the cafe is spread over four levels with an impressive roof terrace. The service is top notch with waiters friendly and knowledgeable

reviews.author: Guy Manchester
reviews.text: We loved this place. The atmosphere was wonderful with lots of different levels and spaces to sit and the food was great. Especially recommend the (vegan) vegetable pastilla - the coriander dressing was especially inspiring! To cap it off there was some great local musicians playing live upstairs.

reviews.author: James Gomm
reviews.text: Really nice chilled cafe in the south part of the old city, which has a nice friendly atmosphere and colourful artwork on the walls (we ended up visiting twice). They have a roof terrace as well as some indoor seating. They do a few different moroccon dishes - the lamb tagine was particually good (sadly didnt get a photo) and went very well with the mint lemonade. The coffee was pretty decent as well. They also offer cooking classes (we didn't do pne, but saw some people having a lession when we ate upstairs).

reviews.author: Aishah B
reviews.text: Great breakfast, had the Berber eggs and they were delicious 😋 especially with the bread which was quite light. My partner had the granola which was great too. The fresh orange juice and coffee was good too!

reviews.author: V G
reviews.text: This is a nice restaurant in the Kasbah area of Marrakesh, with an indoor space (with no AC or fan so hot and not very big) and an outdoor rooftop area (No fans and in summer also really hot). The decor of the restaurant is nice, staff are friendly wearing touristic t-shirts. In the entrance area there are loads of pamphlets and brochures of the Marrakesh area as this is a touristy restaurant. We ordered the fried chicken burger and Chicken Rfisa. The prices are quite high, but the quantity is good and food is freshly cooked. The burger came with french fries which tasted horrible as they were soggy. It was our first time trying the Chicken Rfisa as it's a local Moroccan delicacy but it was unique and a one time try for us: filled with lentils, bread, and chicken (basically chicken tagine with bread and not served in a local style pot that tagine is famously served in). The Rfisa was also very filling and nice. The staff, when asked, also promptly gave us a takeaway box to take our leftovers with us.

reviews.author: Clement Leung
reviews.text: Great restaurant with good vibes. When we went, we had live music playing which was great. Definitely get the camel burger. It's not for everyone but it's worth the try.
