reviews.author: Sidrah
reviews.text: I booked a tea time experience in February for the experience to take place in April (cost is approximately $170 USD - not cheap). My booking was confirmed by the hotel in an email soon after the booking was made. I received no further communications from the hotel regarding my booking and expected that everything was in order. The day of our tea time booking it rained in Fes, however I received no email or phone call from the hotel concerning our booking, so I assumed that the experience was taking place. You’d expect that a four star hotel providing such an expensive experience/service would communicate appropriately with their guests. We arrived at the hotel and immediately upon arrival the doorman was shocked to hear we had a tea time booking. He escorted us to the two women working at the reception. They were shocked to hear about the booking as well. They advised that the tea time is not going to take place because it rained and they can accommodate us for dinner. I refused as we already had dinner and we booked the experience and I was not going to pay $170 for dinner. The problem isn’t that the tea time was cancelled - the problem is that they were unaware that I had a booking and how shocked everyone was. I was met with hostility by one specific woman working at reception that was very annoyed that I didnt want the dinner and I wanted a refund. I booked for a specific service at a four star hotel and paid a decent amount, the least the hotel can do is coordinate and communicate with their guests and not do a run around when someone walks through the doors. You’d expect such a high end hotel to have it all together but unfortunately they do not. They agreed to refund me and took my credit card to process the refund but not shockingly I still haven’t received the refund and it’s been a week. (This is not normal timeline) I have to dispute this with my credit card company. I do not recommend making any advance booking at this hotel. Their reception also needs proper training to deal with customers and treat them kindly. I was not upset that my tea time was cancelled because I completely understood the reasoning behind it, I was upset that I received no update but they didn’t even know it was booked and never apologized and instead treated me like I was a problem because I wanted a refund for something that was not taking place. Absolutely ridiculous. I have many friends and family that travel to Fes and I will continually put it out there and social media how this specific hotel responds and treats their customers.

reviews.author: Rachel Lyubovitzky
reviews.text: Very negative experience at a restaurant due to poor service. At first they tried to push fixed price menu but as we started to leave they’ve offered a la carte very limited menu. The food took over 1.5 hour to arrive. Wine portions are insanely small - just a little more than what you get when tasting the wine - never seen anything like that. One in our party ordered hot water and lemon - pretty typical thing to order here - and she got half a cup of water and lemon. The waiters forgot to bring half the dishes and some of those we got, were not what we ordered - you can’t make this up. Tea took 30 minutes to arrive. The food was OK tasting but not worth the wait. Nice views - hence a star. A table next to us came 30 min later and got served and left before us. As we were leaving they told us they serve the royal family - must have been saving their strength. Not recommended. The worst experience in Morocco.

reviews.author: KHALID ALAASRI
reviews.text: it was nice place to have drink in roof top nice view but it so warm during the day espacailly one thing i dont like is for people who are going to have only drink they should sit under the sun and the price of drink starts with 60 dh so that is not fair !

reviews.author: Ismail Ett
reviews.text: Review about the terrace (not hotel) - over priced - Chocolat chaud had no chocolate in it. Milk + powder - Coffee doesn’t come with water. You have to order it separately. - Their most expensive smoothie (Smoothie du jour) was a bit of peach, orange and lots of water (tasteless) and that was 100Dh Staff were nice and the view is decent but their drinks are a disaster

reviews.author: Angi Harrison
reviews.text: I had the flying carpet tea booked. Unfortunately due to rain it was canceled which is not anyone's fault however when I arrived at reception I was met with a complete lack of knowledge of my reservations. I was asked if I in fact had a reservation which I of course did. We ended up having dinner that was just honestly ok. We had chicken skewers and the chicken was extremely dry. The service was great! I however wouldn't make a return.

name: Restaurant Dar El Ghalia
address: Restaurant Dar El Ghalia, Fes, Morocco

reviews.author: Ernst Peter Tamminga
reviews.text: Beautifull hotel, but hard to find hoddrn in the medina

reviews.author: Lily Gal
reviews.text: Moroccan palace…magic…I’ve never seen a place like that before!! Everything is great, rooms, breakfast. Many thanks to people who work there. I got sick and they helped me a lot. They treated me like a family member. God bless this hotel and people who work there!!

reviews.author: Dominic Williams
reviews.text: Magical place with amazing food! Like being back in the 1920's!

reviews.author: Fatima Zahrae
reviews.text: Nice place. Nice people. Great Riad.

reviews.author: psychiatricboy
reviews.text: Nice Pigeon !!!

reviews.author: Ruslana Zastavna
reviews.text: I had a wonderful experience at this restaurant! The food was absolutely delicious, and even though the vegetarian options were a bit limited, they were happy to adapt the dishes and prepare something vegetarian. The Moroccan appetizers were especially tasty and full of variety. It really felt like homemade cooking — warm, authentic, and made with love. The owner and her children were incredibly kind and welcoming, making the atmosphere feel very personal and cozy. The restaurant itself is also beautifully decorated. I truly enjoyed everything and highly recommend this place!

reviews.author: Thomas Goldby
reviews.text: A lovely family run place - warm welcome by the lady at the front desk, spoke good English. We requested for a table on the terrace which they set up specially for us, and later we realised that must have been a great deal of effort for the staff to serve just us on the terrace (we didn’t realise it’s just us upstairs when we asked for terrace) Food was delicious, all the small plates were excellent - very homemade. We customised the menu by ordering the mains we wanted as opposed to going by the set menu and they happily complied. A friendly lady looked after us, recommended dishes and quantities, spoke very good English, was always smiling and warm. Definitely recommend the small salad plates, chicken and lamb tagines, we found the pastilla alright. The bill was transparent and clear in the end as we had picked our own dishes and the lady at the front desk explained in detail to us. This was one of our most memorable meal while in Fes.

reviews.author: Haley Sweat
reviews.text: This is a family run restaurant suggested to us by our riad manager. This is the perfect place to go if you are looking for a traditional homemade moroccan meal. It’s also good to note that this restaurant does serve wine! So if you are an international traveler looking for a good half bottle of red wine, this is the place to go. It’s hidden in the medina so if you can call ahead and someone will walk you to the restaurant and then back to your accommodation. We were so glad we did that. Also all the meals are served in 3 courses, not al a carte! I actually prefer this so I can try everything but just as a heads up in case you were just looking for a quick appetizer.

reviews.author: Houcine Bouaa
reviews.text: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Dar Hatim - A True Gem in Fès! From the moment you step into Dar Hatim, you feel the warmth of Moroccan hospitality. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming — perfect for families or friends looking to enjoy authentic Moroccan cuisine. The food is absolutely delicious! Every dish, from the tender tagines to the perfectly spiced couscous, bursts with rich traditional flavors. Their grilled meats and homemade desserts are equally impressive. Service is friendly and attentive, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. Whether you are a local or a visitor, Dar Hatim offers an unforgettable taste of Moroccan culture and cuisine. Highly recommended for anyone wanting a genuine and memorable meal in Fès

reviews.author: ThePink Dore
reviews.text: Really delicious home cooked Morrocon food. The lamb tagine was cooked to perfection and the nutty slightly sweet cous cous was melt in your mouth. The hosts were very warm and welcoming.

reviews.author: Benjamin Hillyard
reviews.text: Exceptional experience staying at Dar Roumana. Staff was eager to support in many ways including arranging transportation, personal walk through of city by map, food preparation, excellent communication for arrival and departure. Rooftop terrace is favorably located for a nearly unobstructed view of the Medina. Conveniently situated within reasonable walking distance to several key highlights of the city. Clean interior, quiet with beautiful adornments. Breakfast was delicious! Fruit, chocolate crepes, fried cakes, bread, jelly, cream cheese, butter, orange juice made fresh. We wish we could have met the owner. Very great experience staying at Dar Roumana.

reviews.author: A. Newland
reviews.text: We only went to the restaurant here and had an amazing experience. Within our two months in Morocco this place was definitely a highlight. The quality of the food was amazing, the host was a gentleman that knew what he was doing, the atmosphere was pure Moroccan beauty ánd we where invited to have a drink before dinner on the roof terrace which was spectaculair. Costs a bit more than the usual in Morocco but you (finally) get good worth for your money. It really made our first night in Fez one to remember.

reviews.author: Arthur Steel
reviews.text: Stayed a few nights in this exceptional Riad. No way near a 2-star hotel, easily a 4! Beautiful courtyard, beautiful rooms, feels like home thanks to the outstanding service! The view from the rooftop is worth the visit in itself! And wait till you find the turtle 😂 Small tweaks would make this place a 5/5 without any hesitation: -The bin in my room was not emptied on my arrival -For Morning breakfast, service is busy in the kitchen so doesn’t notice you get here, so you have to go find someone, easy fix with a camera in the kitchen -There are many flies especially in the morning Overall I highly recommend this place and will be coming back!

reviews.author: Thomas Goldby
reviews.text: We didn’t stay but had a dinner at the restaurant - great looking riad, good service once we ordered, delicious food - we did the two course tasting menu and dessert separately; a good change from the local cuisine. It is on a little on the pricier side but good experience overall. One observation - when we arrived the staff who received us made it look like they were busier than they were, said will look if they have availability, made us review the menu and wait for table - which is typically not an issue but there was only one other table occupied, throughout our dinner we noticed not even half the tables were occupied at any given time, so not sure why he did all that fuss in the beginning when they clearly had not availability issues. Didn’t feel very welcomed.

reviews.author: Andrew Klein
reviews.text: I’m putting this under the hotel but this review is just for the restaurant (which Google, it should have its own listing!) and it is out of this world - by far the best meal we’ve had so far. You walk down a very unassuming alley to get to a small door and once inside you see this incredibly beautiful restaurant - amazing setting. The service is just perfect - not pretentious but always there exactly when you need or want someone. And then there is the food - just spectacular - such great flavors, very creative, portions not too big; bread and olives to start were wonderful; we had a shrimp appetizer in this incredible sauce; followed by the sea bass in a sauce I wish I knew what it was because I’d make it every week. The dessert - a small cream brûlée with chocolate mousse adn pear sorbet (sounds awful) just worked so well together - not sure how they figured that out but it was awesome. They had a porter walk us the 15 minutes to/from our hotel so we would not get lost at night in the Medina - just such a great meal.

reviews.author: Neeraj Moondra
reviews.text: We were in Fes for 3 days. This was our best meal. The owner is very kind and friendly. Food was fresh, tasty and authentic. We sat in a lovely courtyard outside with greenery. Felt like a perfect lunch spot away from hustle and bustle. Peaceful setting with seriously amazing food!

reviews.author: Siddharth
reviews.text: Very nice atmosphere(outside) and very friendly staff. We ordered starter and fresh orange juice. Both were just amazing and very distinct flavours. Starter has aubergine, cauliflower, 3 different types of beans ( please see picture) I would definitely go to this restaurant again.

reviews.author: Tamsin Clement
reviews.text: This is our favorite restaurant in Fes BY FAR!!! The food is absolutely incredible, the best you can find in the city. Only the highest quality ingredients and cooking. I have eaten here almost every day for the whole month I’ve been here and I have never had something on the menu I didn’t like. The courtyard is beautiful and clean and quiet, so it’s also a wonderful place to just drink coffee or tea and relax. The owner is one of the best people I’ve met here and his love shows through his cuisine. Everyone who works here is incredibly welcoming, polite, and generous. I’m so grateful to all the staff for making this feel like a home while I am visiting Fes. 💗

reviews.author: Allie H.
reviews.text: I discovered this by chance after wandering the streets and it offered perfect refuge in a quiet patio with fresh mint and greenery after the energetic, bustling Medina. I was delighted to meet Mourad who was genuinely kind, honest, and shared a lot of his culture, history, and experiences which was a lovely experience beyond just the food. As for the food, it was a fixed menu which has a different special everyday. With fresh ingredients, carefully chosen spices and prepared based on the market, I thought it was well priced for the array of accompaniments - every appetizer was fresh, delicious, and flavourful. I certainly could not finish and they kindly packed everything up individually to enjoy later. What was also helpful is that credit card is accepted but as anywhere else, tip is best in cash.

reviews.author: Théo Nunes
reviews.text: We had an excellent dinner last night. Everything was delicious, the service was perfect. Polite, helpful and very welcoming. We had the chicken tajine and the chicken pastilla, the taste of the food was amazingly good, the fresh orange juice was simply the best I ever had. This family owned business deserves to be found, the chef is a really passionate and you feel the love he puts in its craft at every bite. A MUST TRY !

reviews.author: Abdou Baba
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: 2 A
reviews.text: nan

name: Restaurant La Maison Bleue
address: Restaurant La Maison Bleue, Fes, Morocco

reviews.author: Peter Shamamian
reviews.text: What a wonderful hotel! Stayed here with a group of friends for two nights. The rooms were beautiful and spacious with great amenities (and very clean!), and the hotel itself was in a perfect location just outside of the Fes medina, so it was accessible by car but you could walk to the medina in minutes. The service was unparalleled, we felt so welcomed and taken care of by Khalid at the desk. Our check in was seamless, our bags delivered to the room, we had an amazing Moroccan breakfast every morning, and tea in the evening. I can’t express how kind and welcoming Khalid was! We will be returning to Fes and definitely staying at Maison Bleue!!

reviews.author: Bo Sundius
reviews.text: We stayed here two nights and had dinner. I never write bad reviews. As my grandma says if you don’t have anything nice to say then keep it to yourself. But Fes is so wonderful and folks come a long way to get here so they should have the opportunity to have the best experience. And this place is uniquely bad. The staff is totally checked out. No one wants to be bothered. Fantastically overpaid for a dinner. When asked about the wine waiter said it’s all Moroccan, it’s all good. When asked if he knew anything more or which one he could recommend, he flatly said no. When asked if anyone knows more because I was interested in Moroccan wine he laughed and said he knows the most. Food arrived. It’s mountains of something. A pile of couscous with a tiny bit of veal. A heap of grey/green peas and grey lamb tagine. It’s a single flavor and resembles slop. It’s $50/ person. There is no chef, no love, obviously but there are some cooks back there making sure to feed us, but nothing else. They are robbing you of the opportunity for a decent or maybe even great meal somewhere else. The room is full of tour groups with a guide. The guides get kickbacks. Im sure it looks great on the brochure, but the food is terrible and the service is worse. Mystery wine was $40. Wine was fine. Fes is really not that daunting, trust me you don’t need a guide. Your gps works. Music was great. So that’s was a bonus. When leaving we asked for a taxi. Reception told us to go outside and flag one. A bit exhausted from all the Medina haggling and begging I asked him if he could do it. He said he will just fight with them. Didn’t want to do it. I asked again he begrudgingly found a taxi but was very annoyed. Family got a weeks worth of laundry done. It was $125. Bottom line this place is terrible and you should not stay or eat here. There are much better options in fes which has delightful architecture and wonderful hospitality throughout. But just not here. This place is full of beggars and con artists.

reviews.author: LS SPK
reviews.text: It's should kept for Museum. The most part of Everything looks like old antique that for viewing not for using. I had an experience with Ambivalent sexism toward woman. My partner booked this place under my approved, so if I said "NO" your staff wouldn't have seen us here. The room we booked was with balcony. But there was no bathtub stopper. My partner called to inform them. The Staff running over point at me asked me to show. Later he came again with the stopper that not fit I told my partner to get up open the door and also told him I don't want to pay any attention to this male staff anymore. At the end of the exhausted desert trip we really need a bathtub. So, we got downgraded from the room with balcony to the normal room that cannot open windows that look down to the restaurant. There was no kettle, no slipper, no tea and no coffee machine in the room as stated in room condition on booking.com. The driver can't find the hotel. I had a local sim I had to make a called ask for location. The Batha Café is right next to it. If you come at night. The hotel front in the review looks nothing like it!!! We tired and intended to eat the the restaurant but it was set menu 440 dh per set per person. We are allergic for sesame, nuts, and everything that came out of the river or sea. So, we couldn't eat there. We had to dragged our tired bodies looking for food elsewhere. But at least after the meal we can came back and enjoyed the alcohol beverage in the mini bar fridge. Fez is more conservative than any other cities we had been in Morocco. Most restaurants doesn't serve alcohol. So, if you enjoy food with a glass of wine or beer look at the beverage menu before you decide to eat there. The location was best which can access by car. The petit Taxi here had the same problem as Casablanca meter said 9.87 dh. He want 50 dh. Oh well we had to catch up with the train back to Casablanca no time to fight. We paid it. The steps in the hotel were very steep and many of steps till you arrived the room so be prepared. We paid a lot for 2 nights compared to the 5 stars hotel in Casablanca. We just agreed that think about it, we stayed in an old museum!!!

reviews.author: Art Block
reviews.text: Had a lovely birthday meal here with fantastic gnawa musicians and really delicious Moroccan food.

reviews.author: Amy Lynch
reviews.text: My husband and I fell in love with this hotel! I have never seen a more beautiful room! We felt like royalty with the beautiful four poster bed under the 20ft ceilings, to the beautiful velvet purple couch, and the bathroom that was not only spacious, but beautifully designed. Our sofa table had a fresh bowl of fruit and a plate of cookies. The hotel itself is splendid in it's Moroccan design. The restaurant was also lovely. I took advantage of the spa and had a wonderful, very inexpensive massage after a full day of walking the medina. Top all of this off with a welcoming, personal staff who also treated us like royalty. Very accessible, and on the outer edge, and quieter side of the medina.

reviews.author: Tamara Gray
reviews.text: This place was an absolute gem and our host recommended it. The food was filling and each course was delicious. Our waiter was friendly and took great care of us. There was also live entertainment that we enjoyed with our meal. Would recommend it.

reviews.author: Kevin Adam
reviews.text: Beautiful restaurant in a beautiful part of Fez. Food was certainly plentiful and delicious and service was prompt, friendly, and professional. The show (drummers, dancers, and magician) were all excellent as well (although the drums went a little longer than I expected). We had traditional Moroccan cuisine and all was fresh, prepared well, and not under/over done. Prices for my partner and myself with a bottle of wine including gratuity was 1,000dh which was very reasonable as well. Place was empty when we arrived and packed within short order making the atmosphere fun and lively. Reservations recommended.

reviews.author: Michelle Zilen
reviews.text: Everything was great about our visit. The couscous couscous was so delicious. Can't say enough about our visit, very enjoyable.

reviews.author: Muhsen Albawab
reviews.text: The entrance is a bit shabby looking but it’s in the older part of the city. The food was excellent, and the service was super nice. There was a show that was so much fun but what really stands out is the design of the place. It’s so nice and maximalist

reviews.author: Jon Gittins
reviews.text: We visited this restaurant as a group. The main attraction is the show, which was there at night. The prices are higher because you're paying for a show. The food and drinks were great. The only issue: not every member of our group was hungry but they wanted to charge a cover fee to those that weren't hungry.

reviews.author: Thomas Goldby
reviews.text: We had dinner, didn’t know they had a terrace - were sat on the ground floor. Terrible food, rather banal.Service was atrocious, had to repeatedly ask for things, they forgot my mint tea despite reminding twice, food took forever to arrive, we decided to skip the fruits course and simply leave, leaving behind half the food we ordered. The sweets came with the first course of soup - see the photo, so strange. Asked for the bill thrice, only to be told to go and pay at the counter after waiting for ages. Easily the worst meal and service we had in Fes.

reviews.author: Geetika Nagpal
reviews.text: A beautiful place to dine with great food. Each person gets a set three course menu. The beef tajine and the chicken pastilla were outstanding. We got the creme caramel for dessert. This was one of our favorite meals during our entire trip to Morocco. Note: the place is definitely hard to find and you have to navigate dark alleys! So definitely take a longer route in google maps!

reviews.author: Mano Rajendran
reviews.text: The restaurant was very pretty inside, like a mini palace. You can either dine inside or at the roof top with nice views of the Medina. The service and the people were excellent. You get a soup and a wide assortment of salad before the main course. Everything was tasty. I just reduced 1 star for the meat tagine I ordered where I expected the meat to be a little tender instead it was chewy. Maybe it's how it's supposed to be but not my preference.

reviews.author: Monique Verhoef
reviews.text: The food here is absolutely delicious! Every dish we tried was packed with flavour and well prepared. Highly recommended are the Tajine Kefta and Tajine Chiken & Lemon. You get a complete menu which allows you to try many different dishes. Gorgeous location, super friendly people, in short an ideal Moroccan experience. Only we had ordered a Couscous & Vegetables and got a Couscous Vegetables & chicken, but that was delicious too ;-)

reviews.author: Heddy C
reviews.text: We checked and saw that the restaurant was supposed to be open at 1:15pm, but the door was closed, so we knocked once. A gentleman immediately opened the door, we asked if the restaurant was open, and he showed us in. So if the door is closed- do knock! We were the only customers for our entire meal in that gorgeous Riad. I ordered the 150 MAD vegetarian cous cous, my hubby ordered the 160 MAD lemon chicken tajine, and the waiter came back saying it would take 40 more minutes for my order, but if I wanted the 180 MAD chicken pastilla, it could be served quickly with my hubby’s tajine. I agreed. I’ve never had any type of sweet/savory chicken dish before and my first pastilla was delicious! Sprinkled with powdered sugar and cinnamon, it was savory inside, flavored with warm spices. My husband loved his tajine. For that set price, they start you off with a nice soup, then Moroccan “salad”, and the menu says they will end with seasonal fruits, but they gave us a yummy flan type dessert with caramel sauce instead. Also the fresh squeezed OJ was fab. With such gorgeous decorations surrounding us, (truly beautiful!) we recommend! They also have 9 rooms for rent in their Riad.

reviews.author: Victoria Danan
reviews.text: We had the most wonderful stay at Palais Amani. True to its name, its is a true tucked away palace within the Medina of Fes. The room was splendid and the attention to details showed in every aspect of the hotels from the mosaic to the stained glass windows. The service was excellent, warm, friendly and the staff went above and beyond to make our stay comfortable. I would come back in an instant and can’t recommend enough. Thank you Palais Amani for a wonderful stay exemplary of Moroccan hospitality.

reviews.author: Ankita Gupta
reviews.text: This is a very beautiful Riad turned hotel in the heart of the old Fes Medina. It was a special occasion as one of my friends proposed to his fiance today at the venue. The staff arranged for the occasion. We even booked the tea ceremony tour as well however that was very average! The food too wasn’t that great as there was a set menu and no a la carte menu. The property is beautiful. The views from the rooftop are breathtaking.

reviews.author: Heidy Cemaj
reviews.text: Beautiful riad in the center of the medina. Since we were the only guests, we got a big suite which was amazing! Staff was very friendly and we even experienced the body scrub at the hammam. Breakfast was also very good

reviews.author: Susan Chronister
reviews.text: Our stay was delightful. The service was top notch, the food was excellent. Our room was tidy. Just wish there was more light. I would stay here again.

reviews.author: Marisa Kanemitsu
reviews.text: The staff and service at Palais Amani were amazing- everyone was so kind, gracious, and fun to talk to. The palais itself is beautiful with a peaceful courtyard and a rooftop terrace offering stunning views of the old medina from above. Overall, our stay was thoroughly enjoyable and we would love to come back. Thank you to everyone at Palais Amani!

reviews.author: Oscar Mendez
reviews.text: I was very disappointed with several aspects of our stay. The gym closes at 9 PM, which is far too early for guests who want to work out after dinner. There was a persistent musty smell in the room, which was unpleasant. Despite being listed, there was no hair salon, no spa, and no sauna available. I ordered a drink from the menu, and they didn’t have it. My wife also ordered a wine that was listed, and they didn’t have that either. The WiFi was extremely unreliable — constantly going in and out, which made it difficult to stay connected. This experience did not meet the expectations set by the hotel’s description.

reviews.author: Oana Oana
reviews.text: I asked for a very simple cocktail—an Amaretto Sour—which wasn’t on the menu, but the bartender refused to make it. It’s disappointing, especially since it’s such a basic drink. A better approach would have been to say they run out of stock🤣🤣 rather than simply saying no. In hospitality, you should never turn down a reasonable customer request without a proper explanation. The dishes were nice, except the canoli something was wrong with the cream inside.

reviews.author: SABA BASH
reviews.text: We had a great stay in Morocco, and Fes was beautiful. However, the only bad experience we had was at Faraj Hotel. It felt like a scam for them to present themselves as a 5-star hotel. Let me tell you, it was dirty, and the staff were incredibly rude—I wish I could say something better, but honestly, they were a 0 out of 5. The room was too dark, with no lights or proper lighting, and we felt very uncomfortable. When we asked to change rooms for better lighting, they refused. Worse, they spoke about our issues in their own language right in front of us, which made us feel even more uncomfortable. The bathroom was filthy. While I know the building is old and charming, that’s the only nice thing I can say about it. The breakfast was awful, and even when we asked for tea or coffee, they never served it. There was no lighting in the breakfast area, making it hard to see what we were eating. The breakfast manager, a lady, only asked people speaking the same language if everything was okay, without offering any real assistance. We also had dinner at the hotel, and it was very disappointing—poor quality food and terrible service. This hotel was a nightmare, and I would highly recommend finding a better option.

reviews.author: Robert Freeman
reviews.text: The staff here are some of the most friendly and hospitable people that I've ever met. When we had to leave a nearby Riad before checking in due to the rude and threatening behavior of the staff, we walked here in the pouring rain and they let us stay in the lobby to dry off and figure out what we were going to do. They didn't have a room that would fit our family, but they were so accommodating trying to find an arrangement that would work. Even though we couldn't stay, we did enjoy the restaurant and it was incredible. Probably the best food we had in our entire trip in Morocco. Cannot be more grateful for their hospitality and kindness.

reviews.author: Mana Salem
reviews.text: Staying at Palais Faraj Suites was an experience of contrasts. The hotel’s setting in a restored 19th-century palace is undeniably stunning, with intricate tilework (zellige), carved cedar ceilings, and a serene pool area that feels like a hidden oasis . The staff were warm and attentive, especially during breakfast, which offered a delicious spread of fresh pastries, Moroccan breads, and made-to-order eggs . However, the two-story stair climb to our room became a recurring challenge. While the historic architecture is part of the charm, navigating narrow, steep staircases multiple times a day especially after exploring the medina—was exhausting. We stayed in one of the Trendy Riad Rooms, which, as noted on their website, lack elevator access and require staircase use . This might be manageable for some, but with heavy luggage or limited mobility, it’s a significant drawback. Even simple trips to the pool or restaurant felt like a workout! Other positives included the rooftop terrace with panoramic views of Fes and the traditional hammam, though the spa treatments felt rushed and overpriced . The location is "just" outside the medina, which provided peace but required a 15-minute walk to major attractions—a mixed blessing if you’re not keen on daily hikes . In short: Palais Faraj delivers on Moroccan elegance and hospitality, but the stair-heavy layout and accessibility limitations dampened the experience. If you’re fit and love historic charm, it’s worth considering—just pack light and brace for leg day, every day.

reviews.author: Emma Walker
reviews.text: We stayed there in February 2025 during Ramadan. Everything in the hotel looks way better in person than shown in pictures. Very artistic and casual elegant. Very clean. Impeccable service. After sunset, the staff invited us into the kitchen and shared their feast with us. The food was amazing and the genuine hospitality was one of the highlights of our trip! The court yard is beautiful, the pool is zen, and the rooftop is peaceful and has amazing views of the city. We wish to return for a longer stay and highly recommend this hotel!!

reviews.author: Alex McCauley
reviews.text: Wow this is a gorgeous riad. We stayed in the incredible Green suite and it was one of the most gorgeous hotel rooms we have ever had. 30 ft high ceilings, mosaic floors, gorgeous furnishings and a very comfortable bed. The staff here are wonderful and go out of their way to make your stay incredible. Breakfast on the breathtaking roof terrace is divine - as is dinner at the bistro. The pool is a godsend. The location is unbeatable. And the atmosphere is just so serene.

reviews.author: Katie Flynn
reviews.text: We had the pleasure of staying here during our time in Fes. Wonderful experience! The whole setting felt both authentic and elevated. Comfortable, luxurious feeling large rooms and a central courtyard and beautiful swimming pool that made us feel at home. Every detail was beautiful!

reviews.author: Katherine W
reviews.text: Our two nights at Riad Laaroussa were perfect. We received a warm greeting with mint tea and cookies in their stunning courtyard. Our room was large with a very comfortable bed, large bathroom, and the entire room was well appointed with thoughtful touches and beautiful decor. They offered purified water rather than plastic bottles and were very cognizant of the environmental impact of tourism. We ate our first night in their rooftop restaurant. The lamb chops and lamb shank were excellent, as was the service. Everybody was kind, welcoming, and eager to make our stay the best it could be. Highly recommend to stay here to visit the Medina of Fez!

reviews.author: Bella Jiang
reviews.text: The most stunning riad with excellent and kind staff who made us feel like family. We stayed for two nights at Riad Laaroussa at the Terrace Suite, which we highly recommend to anyone if the room is available- you have two private balconies, and the view itself made it worth it. Thanks to the amazing Zach for brought us breakfast the morning we left for the road. They also helped with our luggage to the next stop. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Andrea Sim
reviews.text: Magnificent Riad in Fes. We spent 2 nights me and my girlfriend and we really enjoyed the real Riad atmosphere. The owners are really nice people, as well the staff working in the Riad. The dinner was superb. The room are spatious and comfortable. Probably the best stay during our Moroccan holidays! I strongly recommend it :)

reviews.author: Sloan Stefanek
reviews.text: My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Riad Le Calife. We regrettably only had one night there as we had a busy itinerary full of different cities, but that one night couldn’t have been better. Upon arrival, Yasmine sat down with us to give us the best instructions and local tips, I don’t know what we would’ve done without her. Also, we were visiting as part of our honeymoon and she really did her part to make it extra special for us. Truly an amazing experience and I would recommend this riad for anyone who visits Fes. Thanks again Yasmine and we hope to return!!

reviews.author: Sidrah
reviews.text: Such a lovely gem in Fes. To be honest their social media and online photos do not do this place justice. I was very surprised to see how beautiful this Riad was and the decor was stunning. What I expected from photos was very different! The Riad is so peaceful, quiet and overall has a beautiful vibe. Yasmine and Alex (owners) are both very kind and help coordinate your stay in the Medina. The food (dinner and breakfast) were amazing! The presentation and quality were that of a high end restaurant. Everyone working throughout the Riad were very kind and attentive. We truly appreciated them all! Overall, the rooms are very comfortable and clean. There is a lot of space in the room and bathroom. The location of the Riad is convenient as well as you cannot use a car to get directly to the Riad but the taxi drop off location is only a few mins away. I highly recommend this Riad and hope to visit again soon!

reviews.author: Atia Noor
reviews.text: Our stay in this riad was so lovely that I was sad to be leaving. The staff were so kind and helpful. They constantly asked us if we were comfortable, needed any help, or wanted more mint tea! The owners of the riad made sure we feel at home and we truly did. The chef Fatima would show us the menu everyday to confirm if we had any allergies with the yummy food she was cooking. Our stay at this riad felt like an authentic Moroccan experience that we will never forget.

reviews.author: Ryan Afromsky
reviews.text: This is a great place to stay when visiting Fes. We had originally booked this hotel back in October 2020 but could not come due to the pandemic but we were happy to return in March 2025 and it did not disappoint. Everyone at the Riad is very nice and welcoming and always made us feel at home. It is situated in a quieter part of town, which is nice, but you can easily get to the Medina in a few minutes. The hotel itself is very charming and the room we had, amethyst, had all the essentials. There was ample space Inside and had a nice view of the inner courtyard. We enjoyed the roof deck every single day we were there around sunset and had a great view of the city. The breakfast was nice and was served on the rooftop as well with that beautiful panorama view of the city. There are a lot of nice touches at this hotel but made it special where the people there. I would highly recommend this Riad and would definitely come back next time and fest.

reviews.author: Tina AH
reviews.text: While the service was fantastic and accommodating and the terrace offered a beautiful view, the overall experience at this hotel fell far short of expectations. The rooms were extremely small, dark, and not well-maintained — cleanliness was a real issue. Despite being advertised as a 5-star property, I would generously rate it as a 3-star at best. The pool, which is prominently featured in photos, is more of a decorative element than a functional swimming pool. It looks nice, but don’t expect to actually use it for swimming. With better upkeep and more honest advertising, this place could improve, but as it stands, I wouldn’t recommend it to travelers expecting luxury or comfort.

reviews.author: AR
reviews.text: I would like to start with a sincere thank you to Hassan, Mohammed, Bader and Abdulelah. They are the staff members that elevated my family’s and I’s experience at this hotel. They are very friendly and accommodating to any needs. They are professional and will go overboard with their service. The riad itself looks amazing and it stuns you at every part you look at. I stayed here for a couple of days, but it was a worthwhile visit.

reviews.author: Victoria S
reviews.text: An incredibly beautiful riad in a very central location. I had some concerns before arriving, but I should not have worried. While the streets leading to the Riad Rcif were small and narrow, there were helpful signposts and we found it easily (and did not feel unsafe, even at night, when I was pleasenty surprised to find the paths well lit). The staff were beyond accomodating, and arraged a last minute hammam for us on arrival and a walking tour for the next day. The walking tour was informative and our guide took us to various places selling local items (this was great for us as we wanted to do some shopping, but perhaps bear in mind that you do feel expected to spend some money). The breakfast on the roof terrace was 10/10. I only wish we we could have stayed longer.

reviews.author: Antony Mompo
reviews.text: A beautiful Riad in the heart of the Medina. The staff is extremely friendly and always ready to accommodate the guests. They helped us book a guided tour of the Medina with local guide Rachid Mouttaki, 5 stars for him as well. An amazing experience !

reviews.author: Samuel Hathaway
reviews.text: You are probably here because you saw how beautiful this riad is. And you'd be correct on that point. It's objectively one of the most beautiful in Fes. Beautiful architecture and a great view on the patio. We were very excited for our stay here, unfortunately we left disappointed - especially for the luxury price we paid. This one felt like a racket from start to finish. Like I was in the medina negotiating for everything. - It did not seem well maintained for a luxury riad. Stuck lock on our room door (struggled to get the key to work). Paint peeling off bathroom ceiling. Shower drain was clogged and the showerhead fixture was broken when we arrived. (When I first told the staff they frowned and said "It wasn't broken before." So...it's my fault? No apology. Took 2 days to repair the showhead. Drain remained clogged but I got tired of asking.) - Anything you need, you'll have to ask multiple times. I asked for hammam prices, guide contact info, and shower repair, had to follow up each time. Felt forgotton as a guest. - Breakfast isn't served until 8:30 - and even then doesn't really get going until 8:45. Would be nice to have an option for earlier, or at least a cup of cofee/tea while you wait. Though the medina does tend to open around 10, so that must be why. - When I asked about room payment, the staff told me to get Euros from an ATM then go find a currency exchange to get MAD (I later learned this was so the riad could avoid paying credit card transaction fees). They did eventually accept my card but I had to ask a few times. - The tour guide provided by the riad seemed like a nice guy, but was a speed walker and never checked that my wife and 1 year old daughter were struggling to keep up. Unfortunately he was also very difficult to understand. - Hotel offered help to carry our bags from the taxi to the hotel, then when we arrived I was ordered directly to pay the porter. I like tipping but don't like being ordered directly. When we were leaving, the porter looked at the money I gave him and said "This is nothing." Unbelievable rudeness. What is the cost of a porter in Morocco? I don't know. If there is an expected price that the riad should tell me.

name: Street Stall - Bab Boujloud
address: Street Stall - Bab Boujloud, Fes, Morocco

reviews.author: Mana Salem
reviews.text: Bab Boujloud (also spelled Bab Boujeloud or Bab Boujloud) is a historic and iconic city gate in Fez (Fès), Morocco, serving as the main entrance to Fes el-Bali, the city’s ancient medina and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Here’s a detailed overview: 1. Historical Background Construction: Built in 1913 during the French colonial administration, it replaced a simpler 12th-century gate. The original gate, designed with defensive angles to hinder invaders, remains visible but closed today. Name Origi: The name "Boujloud" is derived from a corruption of Abu al-Junud ("Father of the Troops"), referencing a nearby military 2. Architectural Features Design: A triple-arched gate in Moorish-Mauresque style, featuring intricate zellij tilework(geometric mosaics). - Exteriorm: Blue tiles, symbolizing Fez’s famed cobalt-blue pottery. - Interior: Green tiles, representing Islam. - Arches: Three horseshoe arches, a hallmark of Islamic architecture, with the central arch accommodating pedestrians and vehicles. 3. Cultural and Practical Significance - Gateway to the Medina: Marks the transition into Fes el-Bali’s labyrinthine streets, souks, and historic landmarks like the Bou Inania Madrasa and Al Quaraouiyine Mosque. - Daily Life Hub: Surrounding cafes and restaurants (e.g., rooftop terraces) offer views of bustling activity—donkeys, vendors, and tourists mingling in the car-free zone. 4. Unique Details - Locking Mechanism: The French-designed gate locks from the outside, a reversal of traditional defensive gates, reflecting colonial control over medina access at night. - Minaret Views: From outside the gate, the arches frame minarets of the Sidi Lazzaz Mosque (topped by stork nests) and the **Bou Inania Madrasa. 5. Visitor Tips - Best Time to Visit: Early morning or late afternoon for photography and avoiding crowds. - Nearby Attractions: Explore the Souk el Attarine (spice market) and Dar Batha Museum for traditional crafts. Bab Boujloud is not just a monument but a living symbol of Fez’s blend of history, artistry, and daily vitality. Its dual-colored tiles and strategic role make it a must-see for travelers entering Morocco’s medieval heart.

reviews.author: Stephen Anyan
reviews.text: This is one of the famous gates in Fes Medina. I notice that tour vans pick tourists from this spot. There’s a generous park directly opposite the gate where you can sit to enjoy the sunshine. The road infront of the gate can be quite chaotic and you need to be extra careful when crossing. Not a disability-friendly location

reviews.author: Mike Gmt
reviews.text: Hectic.The food. The spiced air. The coffee. The people. I am in love.

reviews.author: Mattia Martinelli
reviews.text: Beautiful hate to the old Medina. A must see if you are in Fez.

reviews.author: Elhocine Mayffrs
reviews.text: The first gate that welcomes you to the heart of the Medina. Most people take pictures at the entrance especially during the night when the lights are on around the pillars of the gate. I had the chance to stay there for a week and enjoy the tasty food and the simplicity of the people there. I never felt that I don't belong there. Cons: like everywhere in the world there are bad sides. I didn't like the fact that in some restaurants they add 10 dirhams or even 20 dirhams to the receipt (as a tip) without telling anyone. Which sounds fishy and unprofessional. The server deserves a tip for sure if he treats, welcomes you with a smile and gives you the time you need. But obliging the client to pay a tip he/she isn't even aware of sometimes some sort of a scam. You'll also be annoyed by vendors sometimes if they know you're new or asking about what to eat. Someone will show up out of nowhere to force you to eat in their restaurant and that they're the best out there. I personally experienced racism after simply and respectfully not accepting to eat at their restaurant. Things to keep in mind, but overall the spot is touristic and deserves a visit.

name: Street Stall - Bab Ftouh
address: Street Stall - Bab Ftouh, Fes, Morocco

reviews.author: Shaik Masood
reviews.text: Beautiful Gate just before entering The Royal Palace of Fes. Very neat and clean road walking around which is so peaceful.

reviews.author: i 3
reviews.text: The largest of the old city gates. The location of a huge historical cemetery containing many saints including Al-Hirzihim on the east side and Ad-Dabbagh on the west side. There are several local men in the graveyard who can show you to any specific grave of famous people/saints that you wish to visit, you can give them any amount of money as a donation; usually upto 20dirhams.

reviews.author: YOUNES younis
reviews.text: Good culturally speaking coz it relates Moroccon historical era if power , but in terms of security one should be careful , especially at night.

reviews.author: Lucy Harris
reviews.text: Saw this on a guided walking tour of Fes. Beautiful buildings and markets in the city

reviews.author: ZAKARIAE Lahlou
reviews.text: It was wonderful old and modern powerful people and sepect between them am sure it's very nice place to visit

name: Street Stall - Bab Guissa
address: Street Stall - Bab Guissa, Fes, Morocco

reviews.author: Shaik Masood
reviews.text: One of the old city Gates aka Entrance. A very beautiful and peaceful cemetery just by the side.

reviews.author: lawyer.traveler.dreamer
reviews.text: What we liked about Dar Bab Guissa - the way the place looks like - the value for the money - the welcoming tea and cookies - the breakfast - the friendliness of the personnel You have to take into consideration that this place: - has a problem with the plumbing and the shower drain and sink drain might clog - accepts no card payment

reviews.author: busysuzie in Seoul
reviews.text: After googling the meaning of 'Bab', now I have better understanding. As one of 14 gates to the city of Fes, it was interesting starting point for the visit. We were pretty shocked with the price of dove poop (20 dh per kg), maybe Koreans can export it?:)

reviews.author: Natalia Fernandez
reviews.text: Great view, easy to access by foot from the Medina. Entrance is free.

reviews.author: Dia Deis
reviews.text: Close to RIYAD Atlantic and a lovely mosque too

reviews.author: kaira kaplinsky
reviews.text: The most magical Blue City in the world! Bucket list for all! The best time to explore without crowds is early morning right after sunrise. greeting sunsets at the Spanish mosque is a must, although be prepared for bugs😩😁

reviews.author: Nazim Lala
reviews.text: This is a beautiful town with very hospitable people. There aren't many sellers / hawkers constantly pestering you too but their wares, so you can really enjoy your stroll through town. We went later in the day when it cooled down a bit and there were fewer people in the streets.

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. Chefchaouen is a must-visit for photographers, art lovers, and anyone looking to experience Morocco’s laid-back and artistic side. Whether you’re exploring the picturesque alleys, enjoying a mint tea in a cozy café, or watching the sunset from a hilltop, every moment here feels magical.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: Beautiful city! I love the colors, the people, the food and most importantly the shops on the street😍 If you want to get away to the mountains for some peaceful time away from the city, I highly recommend spending two or three days in Chefchaouen!

reviews.author: Mourad Chafik
reviews.text: Chefchaouen’s medina is truly one of the most beautiful and peaceful places I’ve ever visited. The blue-washed walls, narrow alleys, and stunning doors create a dreamlike atmosphere that feels both relaxing and inspiring. Locals are friendly, the shops offer authentic handmade crafts, and there are plenty of cozy cafes to enjoy traditional Moroccan tea. It's the perfect place to wander without a map, discover hidden gems, and take amazing photos at every corner. Whether you're there for the colors, the culture, or just the peaceful vibe—Chefchaouen is unforgettable

reviews.author: Said Belowahed
reviews.text: Rabat is an amazing city to visit, There is a lot of places to see and enjoy, Hassan tower is an amazing place with the Shrine next to it, and view to river. The Mausoleum of Mohammed V is a mausoleum located on the opposite side of the Hassan Tower, on the Yacoub al-Mansour esplanade in Rabat, Morocco. It contains the tombs of the Moroccan king and his two sons, late King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah. The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah in Rabat, Morocco. It is located at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river opposite Salé. The Chellah or Shalla, is a medieval fortified Muslim necropolis located in the metro area of Rabat, Morocco, on the south side of the Bou Regreg estuary. The Phoenicians established a trading emporium at the site.

reviews.author: Jose Tavares
reviews.text: I really liked this medina, very little touristy and essentially frequented by the inhabitants of Rabat. while walking its streets I learned a lot about local habits. Inside the medina are some good restaurants, so you have to ask them why they are difficult to find. Medina very safe

reviews.author: Monsignore Catweasel
reviews.text: big old medina where you can buy a lot of different things. Mobile phones from all brands. Alot of different brands clothes shoes . Also in the have a nice food to get many meals and spices fom fastfood to cousine . There also many free shops where you buy anything handmade .

reviews.author: Errol Clement Dsouza
reviews.text: Nice place but street food charged me more because I was from a different country

reviews.author: Mohammed Ezzine HADDADY (‫محمد الزين الحدادي‬‎)
reviews.text: Beautiful city , even though it is some times overcrowded but in most of the year it's a pleasant place to visit

reviews.author: Kevin Costello
reviews.text: Beautiful mosque in the medina. Very ornate.

reviews.author: Jonathan Boutsicaris
reviews.text: I did not venture inside, but I checked out the area at different times of day. Very much alive, with children playing soccer and normal life. Defining feature of the skyline in the medina.

reviews.author: Ettaqi Saida
reviews.text: It's a very nice mosque, in which u can do ur prayers

reviews.author: Mo Ahmed
reviews.text: Nice mosque in the old medina

reviews.author: Mohammed Dibi
reviews.text: As always nice places to pray

name: Street Stall - Talaa Kebira
address: Street Stall - Talaa Kebira, Fes, Morocco

reviews.author: Phoebe Dhi
reviews.text: A beautiful spot to enjoy authentic Moroccan cuisine in Fes: The setting is stunning—you dine right in the middle of a lush garden, creating a calm and unique atmosphere. The food was delicious and portions were generous. Prices are slightly higher than other places, but the quality and experience make it worth it. They’re also happy to pack up any leftovers to take away. Just keep in mind that they only accept cash, so come prepared. Highly recommended if you’re looking for a special meal in Fes.

reviews.author: Albena Simeonova
reviews.text: Very beautiful and exotic garden. Definitely a unique place, especially in the old town. They give a compliment in the beginning- a small dip and a bread. It’s a little pricey, but it worth the money. Totally recommend it.

reviews.author: Martin Hills
reviews.text: After the hassle and bustle of the narrow street of the Medina, this was a wonderful find. It's a calm oasis in the ruins, very simply done with lots of greenery. The food is very good and filling. Really chilled out here with a coffee After lunch and some good background music. Good price and the staff were very friendly and accommodating.

reviews.author: Thomas Goldby
reviews.text: We had lunch here right after they open, so wasn’t too busy and managed to get a table instantly. A nice atmosphere, friendly staff and good service, food was quite good (we tried the sardine and chicken tagines) and is at a reasonable price point.

reviews.author: Chaitra Cn
reviews.text: Cute little place with nice garden feels. This place doesn't accept cards. Cash in either MAD or Euros are accepted. We tried soup of the day which was zucchini soup, it was quite good. Besara soup was a bit bitter for our palatte. Moroccan trio salade was quite good. The vegetarian pastilla was very good. The outer layer was light and crispy and the vegetable fillings was quite good. Thanks to the person who took our order, he suggested pastilla instead of the briwat which were planning to order as this one is much bigger if we are sharing. And both the dishes are quite similar from a taste profile. Vegetarian tagine was also good. The deserts were amazing!! Figs and dates cake which was heavenly. Along with dates and figs it had almonds, walnuts and almond flour to bind them. One of the best cakes I have eaten so far. Other cake was chocolate cake with prunes and apricots which was very nice.

reviews.author: Mana Salem
reviews.text: Al Fassia in Marrakech is a culinary gem that deserves every bit of its glowing reputation. Nestled in the Gueliz district, the restaurant offers a refined yet warm atmosphere, blending traditional Moroccan decor with understated elegance. From the moment you step inside, the scent of saffron, cinnamon, and slow-cooked meats sets the tone for an unforgettable meal. The dining area is adorned with intricately carved wood, soft lighting, and crisp linens, creating a welcoming space that feels both luxurious and unpretentious. The menu is a celebration of Moroccan classics executed with precision. Standouts include the tender lamb tagine with prunes and almonds—succulent and richly spiced—and the chicken pastilla, a flaky pastry layered with savory shredded meat, dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar. Each dish arrives beautifully presented, highlighting the care put into both flavor and aesthetics. The couscous, steamed to fluffy perfection and paired with seasonal vegetables, is a must-try. Desserts like orange blossom-infused pastries or mint tea served in silver pots provide a sweet, aromatic finish. What truly sets Al Fassia apart is its all-female staff, a rarity in Morocco’s dining scene. The service is attentive without being overbearing, guided by genuine warmth and expertise. Portions are generous, and while prices lean toward the higher end, the quality justifies the cost. Reservations are advisable, as the restaurant draws both locals and travelers. For an authentic taste of Moroccan hospitality and cuisine, Al Fassia delivers an experience that lingers long after the meal ends.

reviews.author: Jeremias Perez
reviews.text: We had our first dinner in Marrakesh at Al Fassia Gueliz, celebrating my mom’s birthday, and it couldn’t have been a better choice. Every dish was incredibly tasty, showcasing the best of Moroccan cuisine with depth and refinement. The wine we chose was just as impressive, perfectly complementing the meal. Beyond the food, the restaurant’s concept—empowering women in hospitality—adds another layer of appreciation to the experience. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making it an enjoyable place to dine. Given the quality and overall experience, the price is very fair for such a refined dinner. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Wayne Whitwell
reviews.text: If your in Marakesh, this is the place to visit. Booking a table is highly recommended, service is on point and the food is great ( we had the slow cooked shoulder of lamb). The staff only speak French and Arabic, but don't let that put you off, they do have English menus.

reviews.author: Layla Juma
reviews.text: This is one of the best restaurants I've been to in a long time. The food was exceptional, and the service was top-notch, especially from Fatiha, who was delightful and attentive. I highly recommend this place!

reviews.author: michelle barton
reviews.text: Beautiful restaurant, serene ambience, absolutely sublime food, and really attentive and friendly ladies looking after you! Attention to detail fabulous. Best experience of our week in Marrakesh. Special mention to the very lovely Fatiha who made our evening, with her laughter and good humour x

reviews.author: catch_hug
reviews.text: Authentic legendary Juwel Tabuthema spice market. Enjoy the quiet atmosphere on the roof top terrace and enjoy beautiful views. The food is served quickly and it tastes good, seasoned to taste. Best mint tea so far. Try the Nutella crepes and the lamp omelette. Perfect breakfast spot.

reviews.author: Fadoua Atif
reviews.text: I’ve been coming to Café des Épices for years, and it’s still one of my favorite spots in the heart of the Medina. As a local from Marrakech, I always appreciate a place that stays consistent—and this one does. The food is tasty, the drinks are refreshing, and the rooftop view over the bustling souks is just perfect. It’s a great mix of calm and energy, right in the middle of the Medina. Highly recommend whether you’re visiting for the first time or looking for a familiar place to unwind.

reviews.author: S H
reviews.text: Amazing drinks and super convenient location amidst the labyrinth of souks. We went there in afternoon and it was burning hot but after few minutes it felt alright. Service was ok. We sat on the first floor and not many servers were available to look after our table. Food was good but we loved the drinks and ordered 4 different lemonades one after another. Overall good experience and would definitely recommend.

reviews.author: Marta Zaczkowska
reviews.text: I visited this restaurant every day during my stay in Marrakesh, and it quickly became my go-to spot. The food is absolutely delicious, and the service never disappoints—always friendly and attentive. One of my favorite things was sitting outside, soaking up the sun while watching the hustle and bustle of the square. It’s the perfect spot to enjoy a meal and people-watch as locals and tourists go about their day. Whether for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, this place was consistently great, and I can’t recommend it enough!

reviews.author: Heavenlykid 18
reviews.text: Here's the revised and concise review for Laddha Spices: "Laddha Spices was a fantastic breakfast spot with an amazing rooftop view of the Atlas Mountains. The setting, right in the middle of a lively souk, added to the charm. The breakfast was delicious, reasonably priced, and served in generous portions. The service was quick, and the staff were warm and hospitable. Honestly, don’t waste time looking elsewhere—this place is perfect for a great start to your day. Highly recommended, and I’d happily return anytime!"

reviews.author: Chehrazad C
reviews.text: Lovedddd this place! I had such a nice evening here. The lady and gentleman at the front desk greeted me with such warmth upon arrival. The waiters are very attentive and provide excellent arrive. The ambience of the place was sublime, with the candlelight lighting and stunning interior. The food was delicious and I recommend the Jawhara dessert as it was yum! Overall, really enjoyed it and would come again.

reviews.author: Zainab Khan
reviews.text: We just went for tea and desserts. And both did not disappoint. We ordered the jahwara and aubergine crumble with rose Damascus tea and Moroccan mint tea. The aubergine crumble was absolutely delicious!!! It had subtle notes of rose and cinnamon and the texture was great, a bit chewy, a bit sticky, a bit crumbly, and the acidity of the lemon mousse on top was exactly what was needed. The jahwara had pieces of fresh fruit in it, less sweeter and more delicate in taste with pronounced floral notes. Both the teas were great, strong and unsweetened. Classic. The service was kinda slow for ordering just desserts and drinks, however very friendly and accommodating. The art was just horrible, an absolute eyesore but the architecture of the place itself was really beautiful and traditional with some book shelves here n there. All in all, a great find in the heart of Marrakech.

reviews.author: Emilie Gibney
reviews.text: My husband and I came to eat here on a Wednesday (when they normally close early). They told us this and we shared we would order quickly and eat quickly. This wasn’t a problem - the service was impeccable and the food came quickly. It was delicious and a beautiful atmospheric location. Would highly recommend to anyone visiting Marrakech - one of the best restaurants we’ve been to here! (camel tagine is a must as well as an iced tea!)

reviews.author: Benjamin
reviews.text: I had to wait a bit despite my reservation, but honestly, I was on holiday, there to enjoy the moment, and the whole team made me feel very welcome. Special mention to Oussama and his big smile. His kindness set the tone for the night. The setting is absolutely charming, peaceful and intimate — I can imagine it's perfect for a romantic dinner. As for the food, I really appreciated the chance to try traditional Moroccan dishes I had never tasted before: briouates, chicken pastilla, and the jawhara dessert. Even if some of the flavors weren’t exactly my type, I could tell the quality was there, especially in the pastilla. It’s great to discover something new in such a beautiful place. All in all, a special experience with attentive service, a magical setting, and the joy of discovering Moroccan culinary traditions.

reviews.author: Sara Riofrio Garcia
reviews.text: The food was great and I loved the ascetics of the place where I ate. It was a hidden gem restaurant to eat amongst the Medinas of Marrakesh. The video doesn't capture how beautiful the place is and the sunlight that shines into the restaurant. Also when ordering any food, olives and bread are always served before the food arrives.

reviews.author: Aya Louzi
reviews.text: Amazing atmosphere! Amazing music! The dancers were to die for and the food (coming from a Moroccan) was so authentic and delicious! Our waiter Bono, was always there whenever we needed him and even danced with us in the circle! They even dedicated a song to me! 10/10 Would 100% recommend to anyone looking for the most authentic Moroccan restaurant in town.

reviews.author: Nai Tana
reviews.text: We went for dinner with entertainment. It was so fun. The music was loud and the atmosphere was great. The musicians and dancers were so talented. It was well worth the price. The mains were large and they serve mint tea at the end. All the staff, especially our waiter Bono was so friendly and helpful. They definitely made everyone have a wonderful time. We would definitely come back.

reviews.author: Leah Sage
reviews.text: Dar Essalam in Marrakesh is a rooftop gem that delivers on both atmosphere and flavor. The views from the top are absolutely stunning, you get a sweeping look over the city that makes the whole dining experience feel extra special, especially as the sun sets and the lights come on. We went all in on the appetizers, and it was absolutely worth it. Everything was fresh, vibrant, and beautifully plated. From traditional Moroccan bites to more creative twists, each dish had something unique to offer.

reviews.author: said oukhatour
reviews.text: I’ve been familiar with Restone Dar Es Salaam for a long time and used to book there regularly for people visiting the area. It was always a smooth, friendly process, just a quick call or message, and everything was arranged with no problem. But recently, that’s changed completely. Now, bookings must be made only through their website, and you’re required to pay in advance. That might work for some, but it adds unnecessary pressure, especially for guests who prefer flexible arrangements or are booking on short notice. It’s honestly disappointing to see such a rigid policy replace what used to feel like a more welcoming and cooperative approach. I really hope they go back to valuing long-term relationships and make it easier again for people who’ve supported them from the start.

reviews.author: G R
reviews.text: A lovely drink on the rooftop with beautiful views, followed by an A class show of traditional Moroccan music, band and dancing accompanied by a 4 course meal. This was all at the cost of less than £60 for 2 people including wine for the whole evening. Brilliant service by Bono who was class at giving a great service even though it was very busy. The dancers were amazing and the atmosphere outstanding. Best night in Marrakesh for sure!

reviews.author: Ed Westerbeck
reviews.text: We stumbled onto this place as and unplanned dinner. We should have purchased a lottery ticket at the same time! The ambiance is incredible. Made new friends with the clientele. The staff was highly professional. There was engaging and skilled entertainment. The traditional Moroccan food beyond compare. Just go!

reviews.author: Wiby Setya Permana
reviews.text: We had only drunk on the rooftop with 3 glasses of non alcoholic drinks. The waiter gave us a free snack. Was so generous. Rooftop was quite nice but probably only 20% of it has the best view. I went also to the restaurant on the ground floor and i found the interior looked very authentic and interesting

reviews.author: J M
reviews.text: An unexpected gem tucked away. Small menu, sells alcohol. And we were provided with a plate of free tapas on arrival. Pretty rooftop vibes. Not the best spot if looking to catch the sun set.

reviews.author: Sasha Lewis
reviews.text: We visited this tucked away rooftop restaurant/bar a few times during our visit as it was by far the best out of all places we ate at. Ismail looked after us each time we went, recommending local food and wine. He was attentive without being overbearing, giving local recommendations and suggestions. The rooftop is spacious and airy, and the indoor lounge area is comfortable in what used to be a private house. We had a selection of local savoury pastries followed by a lamb dish with lentils and salad. All prepared and seasoned to perfection. The fig pudding is to die for. We truly recommend it.

reviews.author: Binta Onifade
reviews.text: My sister and I really enjoyed the foods here, it was finger licking good and delicious from the starters down to dessert and the staffs were very welcoming and attentive and the restaurant itself was inviting. The tempura prawns and chicken wings is not to be missed 😋

reviews.author: Shelley Kimber-Smith
reviews.text: We were recommended to try this restaurant, and it exceeded all expectations. The food was the best we’ve had on our trip, and the setting was absolutely stunning. The staff, especially Nabil, were incredibly attentive, taking the time to explain each dish in detail. While some have mentioned the pricing, we found it to be excellent value for the quality and service—if anything, it felt slightly underpriced. The Moroccan wine was outstanding and definitely worth trying. We’ll certainly be returning later this year!

reviews.author: Zainab Ayub
reviews.text: Atmosphere was so beautiful and peaceful, staff were so friendly, and helpful as well- they also provided a charger so I could charge my phone! The food was amazing! We ordered the unmissable tangia and it was one of the best dishes I’ve had! The meat was so tender and the vegetables were made perfectly. The portion sizes were so generous as well and I still daydream of this meal! Will definitely go back to Morocco just for that meal again!

reviews.author: Alison Sweetnam
reviews.text: Dashed in for lunch on our last day because the weather was cold and wet. Was a great way to spend a couple of hours - probably the most interesting meal we have had over 5 days - very Moroccan but far more on interesting than most restaurants offer. Excellent value although although not the cheapest . Nabil was an attentive and welcoming head waiter but they were all lovely.

reviews.author: Bill Lang
reviews.text: The ambiance and service were excellent, but having had only a weekend visit , I found that there were other places where I could eat which were considerably less expensive and had an equally good atmosphere and service. I am from Britain and was not very happy that smoking was allowed anywhere in the restaurant. I must confess I am not sure if that is true in the whole of Morocco (because I was there only for a short time) but I am always disinclined to revisit places where smoking is allowed in any places where non-smokers are likely to be located together.

reviews.author: Anouk
reviews.text: The food was really nice. It tasted amazing and there was no problem getting a vegetarian option. It was beautifully made and very authentic. The waiter was amazing and they were really attentive and welcoming. It's a beautiful atmosphere and there even was life music. Nabil was a really nice waiter and he made us feel very special on this evening. Thank you :)
