reviews.author: Malysa Johnson
reviews.text: Wow!!! We were looking for an authentic and beautiful Moroccan dinner experience and that's what we got here. Amazing food (seriously, come hungry, its 5 courses) and the staff was great. He let us take home our pastries because we literally could not eat more (we wanted to!) Also definitely get reservations and let them know about food allergies and preferences ahead of time.

reviews.author: Safae F.
reviews.text: We had a really nice evening at Dar Yacout. The place is beautiful, with amazing traditional decor that gives you a real Moroccan vibe. The staff were super friendly and helpful, and the whole experience felt very welcoming. The food was tasty and there was a lot of it – course after course of Moroccan dishes. We loved the setting, the music, and the atmosphere. A great spot if you want to enjoy a special night out in Marrakech!

reviews.author: KAM
reviews.text: Dar Yacout offers an exceptional journey into Moroccan cuisine and culture. From the moment you step inside, the stunning traditional décor and warm ambiance set the stage for an unforgettable evening. The food is simply outstanding—rich, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every dish, from the aromatic tagines to the perfectly spiced pastilla, was a delight. The service was impeccable, with staff ensuring a seamless and welcoming experience. The rooftop views of Marrakesh add an extra touch of magic, making it not just a meal, but an experience to remember. If you’re looking for authentic Moroccan cuisine in a breathtaking setting, Dar Yacout is a must-visit.

reviews.author: Haneen AlQunaibit
reviews.text: Exceptional experience The true Moroccan Experience The amazing hospitality Amazing Food The High respect to culture and religion We had lamb Shoulder, Couscous with Vegetables Traditional appetizer Amazing service as our server Mr Youssef has been working here for 32 years and he says this is his Family Shows you what an amazing place this is to the community, the people and culture May god bless them

reviews.author: Baert D’hauwers
reviews.text: Fantastic place for those who love authentic Moroccan cuisine and enjoy in an authentic setting. Quality wines could be a little better though, work with some French or Italian references?

reviews.author: Justyna Baker
reviews.text: What an amazing tucked-away beautiful place this is! From the moment we arrived at this charming Moroccan riad, we knew we were in for something special. (Though, I must admit — we did mistakenly walk through the back door at first — silly of us! But honestly, even that little detour couldn’t spoil what was to come.) Once inside, we were blown away by how absolutely stunning the interior is — full of authentic character and elegance. We were warmly welcomed and invited to enjoy drinks up on the roof terrace, which was the perfect way to ease into our evening. The service throughout our visit was outstanding — so attentive, kind, and genuine. It really felt like everyone wanted us to have the best time possible, and their hospitality made all the difference. We decided on the famous Dar Zellij Mechoui, and oh my… the lamb was simply delicious — cooked to perfection, tender, and full of flavor. As the sun set, the whole riad transformed into a romantic paradise, with soft, beautiful lights twinkling all around us. It was a truly unforgettable evening, and I can’t recommend this magical place enough.

reviews.author: Salaman Veerathas
reviews.text: This place supposedly has great reviews so we tried it for our anniversary. To the staffs credit, they were fantastic and very polite and accommodating. They even sang us a happy anniversary song for us without us asking which was really lovely. However, I'm not sure if it was the time we arrived (6:30pm). We were the first customers in an empty and silent restaurant. We thought as per the reviews that there would be live music and other entertainment. Absolutely nothing. Was very awkward. Other customers turned up a little bit later but the atmosphere was still very awkward. The place itself inside is lovely. Food was ok, though for the prices you pay, it is ridiculous! Super expensive for average food with decent presentation.

reviews.author: Dale Harrington
reviews.text: A truly stunning interior to this restaurant. Very authentic and you can feel the history of the building. Staff were very attentive. No alcohol served at lunch. Very generous portion sizes, we couldn’t finish the couscous. Highly recommend. Starters were also delicious. Freshly baked bread too.

reviews.author: Raluca Monac
reviews.text: Really nice tasteful and traditional place in Medina. It is worth trying it for a tasty meal during your visit. We were all pleased with the food and atmosphere as well as the extremely nice and serviceable staff. The beef with plums and peaches was amazing in particular.

reviews.author: YJ
reviews.text: I had a great experience at Dar Zellij! The lamb for 2 was super tasty and melted off the bone. The highlight was our waiter Hisham, that was really attentive and so lovely.

name: La Mamounia - Le Marocain
address: La Mamounia - Le Marocain, Marrakech, Morocco

reviews.author: Hiroko E
reviews.text: A dinner for two costed $400 😵 For that price I could have a way better dining experience in any major cities in the world.. Like others say in their reviews, the place is gorgeous and super photogenic. However the food was pretty average and nothing special - which was disappointing… I should have read more reviews carefully before we came here but we didn’t know anything about the city after we arrived at night, so we went along with our hotel’s recommendation. The service was ok. Our server kept recommending things without much explanation instead of answering our questions, so at the ends we were like « hmm….ok we will get that then. » The wine guy seemed inexperienced as he kept forgetting which glass was clean vs already being used. It was not a bad experience but it was way overpriced, definitely not for 400 USD 🥴

reviews.author: David Prowse
reviews.text: Very beautiful setting within the grounds of La Mamounia. Stylish, excellent food with a wine list and price to match. If you want top shelf you won't be disappointed. Very good service high you'd expect in a hotel of this standing. Warning - we found the portions huge - the lamb shank could have served two people easily, but there didn't appear to be an a la carte option, just the set menu. All the starters and mains were delicious. Wine starts at 900MAD. Dress for the occasion. Long trousers required for men.

reviews.author: Mahe Haroutinian
reviews.text: Reserved for 8:30 PM for our last dinner here in Morocco. We arrived a little early, around 8 PM, and at the reception, we were stopped and had one of our bags taken and held, with the explanation that only closed bags were allowed and it could be picked up at the end of the dinner which was surprising to us. At around 8:10 PM, we sat down at the table and were given an explanation of the menu—everything started off rather well. We received our appetizers, and they were quite good. After that, things went downhill. After waiting 30 minutes for our main courses, nothing arrived. We followed up with the manager, who said it was coming soon. It is now 10 PM and still no food. We’ve followed up with multiple waiters and the manager twice, who just kept saying, “Sorry, sorry, it’s coming.” Overall, we were expecting the best dining experience and ended up having our only terrible food experience in Morocco. Unless they seriously improve their service, it’s a worthless place to be.

reviews.author: Andrew Pang
reviews.text: Atmosphere was lackluster - not much to see as you’re sat in a tight corner with another guest a few feet away from you and a drawn curtain at the other end. Food was alright, nothing amazing save for the fish and lamb (for 2) which were indeed outstanding (also the only reason I’m posting a 3* not 1). Menu was confusingly laid out - all the guests around us found it difficult to decipher (and low lighting did not help). Service was very good - but door staff had a air of arrogance I found a bit odd. Also English isn’t their forte. Presentation of food was off - don’t even bother taking photos. Overall just wanted to clock out asap. Best part was possibly the walk to the restaurant. I would say Mamounia is a stunning hotel - shame it’s Moroccan restaurant can’t live up to the hotel name. Personally I would’ve thought it is almost a bit embarrassing. I definitely won’t be visiting this restaurant should I ever decide to spend the weekend at La Mamounia.

reviews.author: Sridevi B
reviews.text: We had a great time here. We love wine and this was our first time trying Moroccan wine. I honestly did not have many expectations, but it turned out to be really good wine (who knew Morocco is capable of producing such good wine). Food was really delicious, we are vegetarian and everything was customized for our needs. We especially loved the Tagine (still can’t stop thinking about it) and the salad platter. Really good flavors in all dishes and definitely a must try. But like others mentioned service is a little slow. But the staff is friendly and accommodating.

reviews.author: M
reviews.text: Sadly the food here was very disappointing. We ordered spring rolls which were cold and slimey very odd texture. Expected them to be served hot and crispy. Meatballs had an odd taste, unfortunately I just ate round them and had a little amount of the spaghetti. Staff were lovely but it was very slow service and food did take a very long time

reviews.author: Emiliano Sallustri
reviews.text: The food is average. Good Tajin but starters are not at the expected level for the price. Small quantities and poor quality. Atmosphere is nice, and we tried a good Moroccan wine. I wouldn’t go back because of the high price, quality of food and slowness in serving, but the restaurant is ok, definitely not a scam.

reviews.author: Arisa S.
reviews.text: Nice atmosphere. Special recipe of couscous is highly recommended. But what we liked the most is the service of ushering you to find taxi so you don't get lost again finding your way back to hotel.

reviews.author: Franziska Leibrock
reviews.text: Let’s start with the good things: The restaurant has a very cozy atmosphere, mostly lit by candles. It’s a very scenic place and you can sit very comfortably. The place itself is quite modern and clean and both the menu for drinks and food are rather extensive. HOWEVER, We went there for dinner because we heard a lot of good things. Unfortunately, Le Foundouk could not even remotely live up to that. So here’s the negative points from our visit: - as a couple, we ended up paying a substantial amount more than the typical bill that we would have when we go out to eat in Amsterdam, having the same amount of food - it was so cold inside that we had to keep our jackets on - the food itself was rather underwhelming. We had two different starters and two different mains and all of them basically tasted like nothing - even though there is a quite large amount of food on the menu, there’s nothing really special or new - and lastly what made our experience truly unpleasant: when we paid our bill we stayed seated for a while, waiting for the change to arrive. After a few minutes we had to ask for it and then finally received it. When we received it, we got a „friendly“ hint from the waitress that there was no tip included, only taxes. When we then left the waitress almost run to our table to see if we had left some tip after her friendly reminder and when she saw that we didn’t do so, she gave a sign to her coworkers who didn’t even say goodbye to us All in all this could be a very nice place for a romantic dinner, but after our visit, we are not at all surprised that the place was only filled for about 15% despite the peak hour that we went.

reviews.author: Celine La.
reviews.text: We were a group of nine and were very satisfied with the food and impressed by the ambiance. The service was attentive and friendly, and despite our large group, we didn’t have to wait long for our orders. Even during Ramadan, alcoholic beverages were available. For the reservation, a deposit of €20 per person was required, but this was deducted from the final bill. The location of the restaurant strongly reflects the contrast between wealth and poverty in the region. BUT!!! During our visit, one person had their wallet stolen from their bag on the chair—€400 was taken, and the wallet was later found in the restroom. When we asked the staff about it, they simply said, “This happens here often,” but did not offer any further assistance. We cannot say whether it was a staff member or another guest, but we were not sitting in a high-traffic area leading to the restroom. We strongly recommend keeping a close eye on your valuables and carrying them securely.

reviews.author: M
reviews.text: Sadly the food here was very disappointing. We ordered spring rolls which were cold and slimey very odd texture. Expected them to be served hot and crispy. Meatballs had an odd taste, unfortunately I just ate round them and had a little amount of the spaghetti. Staff were lovely but it was very slow service and food did take a very long time

I wouldn’t go back because of the high price, quality of food and slowness in serving, but the restaurant is ok, definitely not a scam.

reviews.author: Kevin Grubi
reviews.text: Le Jardin offers a beautiful setting right in the heart of the Medina—an oasis of calm with a charming atmosphere and a lovely view. The décor and ambiance are definitely highlights, and the staff were extremely friendly and welcoming throughout our visit. As for the food, it was of good quality and tasted great, but leaned heavily toward a Western/European style rather than offering something authentically Moroccan. That in itself isn’t a problem, but it’s important to note if you’re hoping for local flavors. The main issue was the price. While the food was enjoyable, it felt overpriced—comparable to what you’d pay in many parts of Europe, even Switzerland. Considering we’re in Marrakech, where quality food is usually more affordable, it didn’t feel justified. It almost felt like we were paying more for the ambiance than the cuisine. In summary: a lovely place, nice staff, and good food, but the price-to-value ratio just isn’t there. If you’re visiting Marrakech for its authentic and affordable culinary experiences, Le Jardin might not be the best choice. I wouldn’t recommend it overall.

reviews.author: Dave Rascal
reviews.text: We had been recommended to come here as it was close to our Riad. The food was ok, but I expected so much more than just ok to justify the high price. I had Chicken escalope which I enjoyed,but not much in the way of garnish or veg or sauce,I ordered chips which were tasty enough. My wife had Bolognese pasta which should have had cheese or garnish but was just a bowl of adequate pasta with an ok sauce. Hot chocolate was warm and again tasty but not very hot. I left feeling that we paid a premium for an adequate meal. Service was fairly slow,I had to ask the chatting waiters for drinks and desserts rather than them noticing we had finished. Certainly an ok meal with a busy feel, but more cafe than top restaurant.

reviews.author: Heavenlykid 18
reviews.text: Le Jardin is a fantastic restaurant that truly exceeded our expectations. The food was delicious, offering great quality and flavors at a very reasonable price. The hospitality was outstanding—Meenal, the front-end staff member who welcomed us, was particularly warm, accommodating, and went out of her way to ensure we felt comfortable, even without a prior reservation. The ambience of the restaurant is charming, adding to the overall experience. It’s the perfect spot for a delightful meal with excellent service. I highly recommend Le Jardin for its lovely food, great atmosphere, and top-notch hospitality!"

reviews.author: 254 Grace
reviews.text: The food was average. Decor and atmosphere amazing. The waiter who served me was so nice and helpful. Didn’t expect service charge to be added since it wasn’t stated anywhere only noticed it on my bill.

reviews.author: Micah Polston
reviews.text: If you're a foodie, you'll need to stop in. The staff was very courteous, manager and food servers checked on us consistently. The ambiance is comfortable and relaxing. The food is crazy good; even one of my pickier kids tried several things and liked several dishes. Most memorable meal in the Marrakesh Medina. Definitely eat here at least once, twice for a fuller menu sampling.

reviews.author: Dick Cairns
reviews.text: Honestly, underwhelmed. We have had better dining locally - if you look at other reviews, people are essentially happy they serve alcohol. We were seated in the enclosed rooftop, the views were okay, if you ignore the fat dripping from the kitchen chimney outside the window next to our table. The table cloths were dirty and the bowl all cracked or chipped. I wondered if it added charm, but it didn’t really. Half the hanging plants on the ceiling were dead. The view of the sunset was largely obscured by another rooftop crammed with people with their phones out nearby (I didn’t mark them down for their geography). The place looked better after dark. The food was okay, but more expensive than other places we’d eaten. Drinks slightly more expensive too. The meats were well cooked, that was decent. The flat breads were a bit sad. The service was okay, nothing standout and not particularly quick given the amount of people in there but the chaps were nice, spoke good English and got our order correct. On leaving we found our bags wet because the floor was wet due to a spilled drink a fair way from us seemingly running all the way to our table. Overall, I’d just pick somewhere else.

reviews.author: Tamara Gray
reviews.text: Our server Salah was very attentive and took care of us. We arrived right before the kitchen closed and he made sure we had what we needed. We just got starters but they were very tasty. Would highly recommend coming to eat here. Drinks were good here too!

reviews.author: Geoff Perry
reviews.text: Great bar / restaurant for those who prefer to have a drink with their meal. My visit coincided with happy hour (4-6pm), the local bottle beer was very good. The food was predominantly Moroccan and was well prepared and tasty. The level of service was exceptional.

reviews.author: Paul Ciprian
reviews.text: A very nicely decorated restaurant. And they serve alcohol, which is not available in all restaurants in Morocco. The staff is OK. I only had a beer, I didn't stay long, but I would come back anytime.

reviews.author: James M
reviews.text: I came for pizza and beer from suggestion online. There was no pizza here, maybe they stopped a while ago, however the drinks were good. I’ve read reviews saying people say the happy hour is a scam, I’m not sure if I paid full price or it was happy hour but I ordered 2x local flag for 70 from the happy hour menu which is reasonable price. Nice rooftop views and a very nice uptown venue with nice chilled local music

reviews.author: Norb Now
reviews.text: It’s little bit hidden and difficult to find. Definitely requires a reservation. Highly recommended. The staff is so polite and moves like shadows. Food is amazing. It was a great journey through key maroccan dishes. Live music is a good addition.

reviews.author: E C
reviews.text: This is a very nice place for a multi course meal with entertainment. The entertainment was sounded very repetitive. The first course with many small plates of food was very good. It was followed by a tagine and a desert. It was a set price menu that included a bottle of wine. Expect to spend at least a couple of hours or more here. Food was nice prepared and presented.

reviews.author: Filippo Scanzano
reviews.text: Beautiful place! Amazing food, superb service and lovely music - at a fair price

reviews.author: Jessica May
reviews.text: Magical experience. Excellent food and service. The atmosphere was fabulous. We loved everything about it including the door-to-door escort from El Fenn. Highly recommend!!

reviews.author: Jonathan H
reviews.text: This is not an easy place to find, just a discrete brass plaque marks the entrance and you must knock to be let in. But once in you can't fail to be enchanted by the lovely ambience. I was prepared for the extensive fixed menu so didn't eat lunch. The cost is 650MAD per person and for that you get:- Your choice of Aperitif with olives Bottle of wine 8 meze starters (vegetarian) Chicken tagine Lamb tagine Couscous with vegetables 2 x deserts Tea or coffee It is a ridiculous amount of food for 1 person and I couldn't eat it all. I'm sure most people would think less food and less cost? But I understand the restaurant is full most evenings so I guess the owner feels they have a winning formula. Service was excellent and there is live music.

reviews.author: Erwin Abreo
reviews.text: I recently dined here with my wife and had a wonderful experience. We kicked things off with the taster shots, which were perfect for anyone on a detox or looking for a light, refreshing start—each juice was made with natural ingredients. For starters, we ordered the zucchini fritters, and they were absolutely amazing. The portion size was just right, with four fritters that packed in great flavor. For the main course, I opted for the calamari with squid ink rice, which was also delicious—perfectly cooked and flavorful. Overall, the dining experience was excellent, and the customer service was top-notch. The staff made sure we felt well taken care of, especially on the lovely terrace. One thing to note, though, is that the portion sizes are on the smaller side, so if you're a big eater, this might not be the best fit. However, if you're open to trying a variety of dishes, you'll definitely be satisfied. Thanks again to the wonderful team who made our evening memorable!

reviews.author: Connor Greenhalgh
reviews.text: Me and my girlfriend visited this restaurant with high hopes due to the excellent reviews, preparing to pay higher than average prices for an excellent meal. The restaurant itself is absolutely beautiful, with a rooftop area that looks out over Marrakech. The food was pricey, and we started with a portion of zucchini fritters. These were a good size and very fresh but nothing to write home about. We then received our main courses, lamb chops with potato (as they had ran out of the usual accompaniments), and a lentil salad for my girlfriend. The salad was presented well and tasted good, but nothing special. The lamb was the real issue. I ordered it medium, which is supposed to be slightly pink. Two of my lamb chops were perfect, the last however was incredibly undercooked, being closer to rare/blue than medium. By this point I had already pretty much finished but told the waiter anyway as feedback. The waiter then told me I was wrong, and that the chop was in-fact medium. If this was the case then my other two were overcooked. I couldn’t be bothered arguing and we just left the food and got the bill. After bringing the bill, he joked that “I should order it well done next time”. Rest assured I will not, because there will not be a next time. There is much better in Marrakech for much cheaper. I would not recommend this restaurant.

reviews.author: Monika Filonowicz
reviews.text: We went for a late lunch with a reservation we made in advance. Rooftop is beautiful and views are great. However, the food was terrible and much overpriced. Chicken pastilla Looked good but was extremely dry. All of our food came super fast so didn’t seem freshly prepared

reviews.author: Anisa
reviews.text: Really nice rooftop restaurant/bar in the heart of the souk! I had gone here for lunch without reservation, so unfortunately I did not manage to get a seat on the rooftop. But regardless, the food was amazing! I ordered gambas, and it had been one of the best gambas that I have tried in my life.

reviews.author: Rocio Elortegui Pascual
reviews.text: Lovely place. The quality of the food is worth the price, also, the atmosphere is beautiful. Only but is one of the waitresses ignored us all the time, she seemed angry to even look at us. We were three and she left one of the plates on the only empty place and just left without explaining which plate it was. But the rest of the staff was really nice.

reviews.author: Ha W
reviews.text: Great restaurant! Fresh and delicious foods, excellent service with english speaking staff. Serves wine / alcoholic beverages. Upscale atmosphere with beautiful inner courtyard. Prices compared to others in Morocco expensive, expect to pay European prices for food and drinks.

reviews.author: Jayanthi Gupta
reviews.text: The best Italian food I have ever had . The ravioli was so delicious and melting in my mouth. And the ambience is excellent with good music . It's a 5 star place I would rate this

reviews.author: Eleanor Coate
reviews.text: Wow this place is incredible. Wonderful staff and atmosphere. Can’t wait to go back one day. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Paix SurTerre
reviews.text: The exquisite setting, in a spectacular Riad courtyard makes up for the mis-steps in other areas. The food is good - as is the service - But overall in our opinion both are a little heavy-handed, and for the high price both could easily be finessed to become a little more sophisticated. Though regardless this restaurant is well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Martin Hills
reviews.text: After 6 days in Marrakech I was looking for something different for an evening meal and our hotel recommended Pepe Nero which was nearby. This was the best meal by far in Marrakech to date. I've been traveling a lot in South America, Europe and Asia in the last 6 months and this ranks right at the top of the restaurants I've dined in in that period. Every dish we had was great but the lamb especially was delicious. All the staff we engaged with were professional and engaging but Mr Rabie was a delight. The atmosphere of the restaurant was excellent even though we weren't in the main courtyard. We were lucky to get a table without booking and I'd recommend you book in advance as the restaurant filled up after we sat down. The price of the meal was very reasonable for the quality of the food, the setting and the service we received. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: iman salem
reviews.text: a bit overhyped. The view is nice, but the overall experience didn’t match the price. We only had two main dishes, one dessert, and soft drinks—no starters and no alcohol—and still ended up paying quite a lot. The value for money just isn’t there in my opinion. On top of that, the service was incredibly slow. We waited a full hour for our main dishes, and then another 45 minutes for desserts

reviews.author: Kate M
reviews.text: We had a booking for supper and the whole experience was very disappointing. The place is very run down and dirty on the rooftop. Our drinks were pleasant, they have a decent cocktail and wine list, but the food was mediocre at best. The lamb wellington was inedible and sent back (we did get this off the bill and were of course grateful for that). It was such a shame as it has been on our list for ages to visit. Not value for money at all and absolutely will not be recommending to friends!

reviews.author: Joshua Küssner
reviews.text: I don’t usually write reviews that often, but I felt this one needed a bit of balance. The atmosphere of the club is genuinely amazing — beautifully done, great music, really a place you want to love. But the service was extremely disappointing. On my last visit, I had to walk to the bar for every little order or change — it felt like I was being purposely ignored. Some items from the food order were missing, portions were small, and the prices felt unjustified. On top of that, when I gave a tip, the bartender gave me a look like it wasn’t enough — only for me to realize later there was already a nearly 10% service charge included. That made the whole interaction feel awkward and off. At the end, they even asked if the service was great. Honestly, it wasn’t. In short: beautiful venue, but the service really needs work. Maybe I caught them on a bad day — but this was my experience.

reviews.author: Nead “Nead92” El
reviews.text: We had an amazing experience at El Fenn in Marrakech! The food was absolutely delicious — full of flavor, beautifully presented, and clearly made with care. The atmosphere was just perfect: cozy, stylish, and full of good energy. The vibe throughout the evening was relaxed yet lively, making it the ideal spot to enjoy a great meal. A special shoutout to Hicham, who gave us the best service we could’ve asked for. He was friendly, attentive, and made us feel genuinely welcome from start to finish. Everything was truly on point — we couldn’t have asked for more. Highly recommend this place if you’re in Marrakech!✨

reviews.author: Marnie J
reviews.text: Located in the heart of the Medina in Marrakech lies El Fenn. Combining traditional Moroccan style with contemporary chic designs, each area is more Instagram-ready than the next! It comprises 12 interconnected riads, and around each corner, you will find a unique set of character and charm. The attention to detail is bar none, and the boutique hotel setting makes you feel like you are at a quiet, luxury resort while still in the middle of the bustling Medina. The only part we weren't a fan of was, sadly, the rooftop bar. It was very crowded with people who were not hotel guests, making it difficult for us to find seats, get service, and enjoy the view of the Atlas Mountains. It was kind of a scene. However, we enjoyed the quiet of the Colonnade Cafe (only guests are allowed here), where we enjoyed breakfast, lunch, and drinks in the afternoon. The service at the cafe was much more attentive, and the food and drinks were delicious! Overall, it was a wonderful and unique experience in the heart of Marrakech! @marnfluencer

name: Street Stall - Djemaa el-Fna
address: Street Stall - Djemaa el-Fna, Marrakech, Morocco

reviews.author: Albert Babinskas
reviews.text: Heart of the city. Lots of action! Food vendors of various flavors, local craftsmen, acrobats, live music, henna artists, exotic animal trainers, and more. Everything in the main square. Lots of action and lots to look at and just spend time. People watching is excellent here. Lots of tourists from all over the world. At night/evening it gets even better, not so hot.

reviews.author: Noah Von Dauber
reviews.text: This square transforms into an amazing cultural experience at night. As soon as the sun sets, it fills with vendors, story tellers, musical performers, snake charmers, and just about anything else you could ever imagine. The square also serves as a great starting point if you plan on exploring the maze-like medina.

reviews.author: Fares Al-waeel
reviews.text: A lively and vibrant spot to experience a mix of cultures. The different streets each offer their own unique atmosphere, with plenty of street food to enjoy. It’s a crowded and noisy area, but full of energy and character.

reviews.author: Amie Lange
reviews.text: Amazing, if somewhat crazy, experience. The sun will absolutely bake you during the day as there is no shade, but once night falls, it is a most interesting place to pass time. The night market is full of food vendors, buskers, and all kinds of oddities ranging from snake charmers to henna artists. The atmosphere is buzzing with energy, but be wary of anyone putting a monkey, hat, or henna on you - they will demand money.

reviews.author: Pawel Nojmiler
reviews.text: Wild, colorful and intense – a true Marrakech experience The main market (Jemaa el-Fnaa) has everything you’d expect – tons of people, colors, sounds, smells. You’ll find stalls with fresh fruit, local street food, spices, clothes, and souvenirs. It’s chaotic in a good way – but keep your eyes open for scooters weaving through the crowds and the overwhelming number of people. A big downside is the exploitation of animals – monkeys, snakes, and even peacocks used as tourist props. It’s upsetting and hard to ignore. Prices for tourists are usually twice as high as elsewhere, but many stalls now list fixed prices, which is a huge plus. Haggling is still part of the game, though. Be firm with locals – if you’re too polite, they’ll take advantage of it. It’s not unusual to be approached by someone offering hashish or followed for several minutes by someone asking for money. If you’re not assertive, they won’t leave you alone. Still, it’s absolutely worth a visit for anyone wanting the real Marrakech experience – wild, exotic, and unforgettable.

name: Street Stall - Jemaa el-Fnaa
address: Street Stall - Jemaa el-Fnaa, Marrakech, Morocco

reviews.author: Albert Babinskas
reviews.text: Heart of the city. Lots of action! Food vendors of various flavors, local craftsmen, acrobats, live music, henna artists, exotic animal trainers, and more. Everything in the main square. Lots of action and lots to look at and just spend time. People watching is excellent here. Lots of tourists from all over the world. At night/evening it gets even better, not so hot.

reviews.author: Noah Von Dauber
reviews.text: This square transforms into an amazing cultural experience at night. As soon as the sun sets, it fills with vendors, story tellers, musical performers, snake charmers, and just about anything else you could ever imagine. The square also serves as a great starting point if you plan on exploring the maze-like medina.

reviews.author: Fares Al-waeel
reviews.text: A lively and vibrant spot to experience a mix of cultures. The different streets each offer their own unique atmosphere, with plenty of street food to enjoy. It’s a crowded and noisy area, but full of energy and character.

reviews.author: Amie Lange
