reviews.author: Mushed Miah
reviews.text: Beautiful classical Masjid, such a contrast to the modern structures I am used to. SubhanAllah, you can feel the historic nature of it, inside was clean and relatively new. Decent walking distance from the Jma'a Al Fanaa too.

reviews.author: Jennifer E.
reviews.text: Only experienced this Mosque from the outside but either way, great site to see. They were currently reconstructing a few spots due to the earthquake they had about 2 years ago. Great big mosque. Nice huge walking platform to see the mosque from all different angles. Excited I was able to see this place up close and admire it. Walking distance to Souks and hotels around the area.

reviews.author: Kashif Aasi
reviews.text: I loved this place, it’s spacious and beautiful, calm, soul healing place. Must do if you in Marrakesh city. Mosque opens at prayer times so go in at that time for free and do prayer plus appreciate the architecture and simplicity of this marvellous structure. Loved the tall rising minaret.

reviews.author: Suzanne Bedwell- Byatt
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful 😍 the Koutoubia mosque feels so peaceful in the madness of Marrakech. The architecture of the building is amazing. Would definitely advise to go there with a guide as there is some much history and information to learn, it's fascinating. The gardens are very well looked after and perfect compliment to the mosque.

reviews.author: Aayan Toys & Gaming
reviews.text: This mosque is amazing. It shows how much work was put into it and how beautiful it is. It's over 800 years old, and considering that, I think that it must deserve to be a five-star. Another great reason to give it five stars is because the mosque is kept very clean and tidy. You must put your shoes in a bag which helps to keep it clean. Please note that you must be a Muslim to enter.

name: Street Stall - Mechoui Alley
address: Street Stall - Mechoui Alley, Marrakech, Morocco

reviews.author: SP
reviews.text: Came on a Friday afternoon and we were lucky as there was no queue. The restaurant was packed though and seats were so close to one another that there were barely any movement space. Noise level was uncomfortable. It was chaotic. Hygiene was an issue. We were shown a table and they just grabbed used paper liners from another table where customers just finished eating to put onto ours. I could see bits of food and oil blotches on the paper liners. Staff were just lazy and wants to make quick money. Ordered their Mechoui lamb and Tangia Marrakchia. Servings were large as it was a lot of meat - a single portion could be shared by two pax. Taste-wise, the dishes were just average fare. The Mechoui lamb was mostly dry and did not have any gaminess on it. It needed the salt and herb seasoning it came with. Otherwise, it was just dry, tasteless meat. The Tangia was slow cooked and came in a pot. Its content were promptly poured into a plate. It looked good, smelled good but the lamb meat was surprisingly dry. I imagined slow cooking would have made the meat tender, but it was dry. Oh well. The dishes were served with bread as per the norm. What irked me was that when they brought a baslet of bread to my table, one of them just partially tipped onto the used paper liner. It was just another day for the server as he just walked off. Ewww. None of us touched the bread, any of them. I would not return. The hype was a letdown. Hygiene questionable. Prices were on the average-high side for the food quality and poor service.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: If you want to experience authentic moroccan meat, this is the right place. We had mechaoui and tangia that are cooked in an underground oven so the taste was amazing, the meat melts in your mouth. Must try if you love meat, crave local food and if you don't freak a lot about cleanliness😅

reviews.author: Hüseyin Güngör
reviews.text: One of the best meat I have eaten! Highly recommended but you have to come early because when you come in the evening you get the last parts of the lamb.

reviews.author: Amir Sultanbekov
reviews.text: WARNING: larvae in the meat. I got mutton's head and the meat was delicious. However, while eating I found two larvae. The waiter said it's fine though. I finished the meal and didn't get food poisoning. Tea was nice

reviews.author: Yasemin Kaya
reviews.text: This place is MADNESS, but worth it for the lamb. If you want to get service, you’ve got to be super aggressive to get the waiters attention 😅 It’s always busy and deserves to be. Lamb is good and tasty. Although, now we’ve tried mechoui in Agadir, we know this place is not giving you exact measurements and cutting you short. We’ve had 1kg in 2 different places, and the portion here is small compared to other places. So be aware, you’re getting smaller portions but paying same prices.

name: Street Stall - Rahba Kedima
address: Street Stall - Rahba Kedima, Marrakech, Morocco

name: Street Stall - Souk Ableuh
address: Street Stall - Souk Ableuh, Marrakech, Morocco

name: Street Stall - Souk Cherifia
address: Street Stall - Souk Cherifia, Marrakech, Morocco

reviews.author: Rash M
reviews.text: Better to do your shopping here. Most will ask you where you're from then determine the price, always haggle. You'll always pay twice as much as locals but never accept the first offer.

reviews.author: Alena Novik
reviews.text: very nice interior and good coffee

reviews.author: Sophia Jong
reviews.text: We regret that it wasn't the gastronomic experience we expected from reading other reviews. The service was excellent. The Moroccan salad too but the chicken in both dishes was dry, very overcooked. The decor was charming if a bit too eclectic for our tastes though the proportions of the rooms were impressive.

reviews.author: adam Pinson
reviews.text: Great place to escape from the rest of the busy market, much more peaceful, and there is a lovely cafe in the middle where you can sit and rest from all the hustle and bustle

reviews.author: Ayoub EL BOUHAMIDI
reviews.text: The local products are very colourful and very beautiful. The prices are e little bit higher than the markets outside the remparts but the experience is full magnifiscence

name: Street Stall - Souk El Khemis
address: Street Stall - Souk El Khemis, Marrakech, Morocco

reviews.author: Asad Chaudary
reviews.text: This is a very local flea market, and is busiest on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. The outdoor area can get very crowded, but you will find everything here and negotiating prices is a must!!

reviews.author: Olga Gilow
reviews.text: Something like that you will only see here. I just LOVED it. Even though everything looks sordid, it still has its charm.

reviews.author: Shikha Singh Thakur
reviews.text: Definitely worth going. You get little tid bits so much cheaper than the souks

reviews.author: Moe M
reviews.text: Feeling a bit unsafe but not too dangerous, the place has a decent vibe and fun to hang out in, and discover products and clothes, tho the prices went up during covid, but overall a nice place to go to at least once every once in a while.

reviews.author: Andrew Barrett
reviews.text: Not my favorite souk in Marrakesh mostly banded clothing and mass produced souveniers most stalls selling the same stuff. However i like to find unique and strange locally made goods so my review might be a little swayed, its worth checking out

name: Street Stall - Souk Semmarine
address: Street Stall - Souk Semmarine, Marrakech, Morocco

reviews.author: Chehrazad C
reviews.text: Lovedddd this place! I had such a nice evening here. The lady and gentleman at the front desk greeted me with such warmth upon arrival. The waiters are very attentive and provide excellent arrive. The ambience of the place was sublime, with the candlelight lighting and stunning interior. The food was delicious and I recommend the Jawhara dessert as it was yum! Overall, really enjoyed it and would come again.

reviews.author: Zainab Khan
reviews.text: We just went for tea and desserts. And both did not disappoint. We ordered the jahwara and aubergine crumble with rose Damascus tea and Moroccan mint tea. The aubergine crumble was absolutely delicious!!! It had subtle notes of rose and cinnamon and the texture was great, a bit chewy, a bit sticky, a bit crumbly, and the acidity of the lemon mousse on top was exactly what was needed. The jahwara had pieces of fresh fruit in it, less sweeter and more delicate in taste with pronounced floral notes. Both the teas were great, strong and unsweetened. Classic. The service was kinda slow for ordering just desserts and drinks, however very friendly and accommodating. The art was just horrible, an absolute eyesore but the architecture of the place itself was really beautiful and traditional with some book shelves here n there. All in all, a great find in the heart of Marrakech.

reviews.author: Emilie Gibney
reviews.text: My husband and I came to eat here on a Wednesday (when they normally close early). They told us this and we shared we would order quickly and eat quickly. This wasn’t a problem - the service was impeccable and the food came quickly. It was delicious and a beautiful atmospheric location. Would highly recommend to anyone visiting Marrakech - one of the best restaurants we’ve been to here! (camel tagine is a must as well as an iced tea!)

reviews.author: Benjamin
reviews.text: I had to wait a bit despite my reservation, but honestly, I was on holiday, there to enjoy the moment, and the whole team made me feel very welcome. Special mention to Oussama and his big smile. His kindness set the tone for the night. The setting is absolutely charming, peaceful and intimate — I can imagine it's perfect for a romantic dinner. As for the food, I really appreciated the chance to try traditional Moroccan dishes I had never tasted before: briouates, chicken pastilla, and the jawhara dessert. Even if some of the flavors weren’t exactly my type, I could tell the quality was there, especially in the pastilla. It’s great to discover something new in such a beautiful place. All in all, a special experience with attentive service, a magical setting, and the joy of discovering Moroccan culinary traditions.

reviews.author: Sara Riofrio Garcia
reviews.text: The food was great and I loved the ascetics of the place where I ate. It was a hidden gem restaurant to eat amongst the Medinas of Marrakesh. The video doesn't capture how beautiful the place is and the sunlight that shines into the restaurant. Also when ordering any food, olives and bread are always served before the food arrives.

reviews.author: catch_hug
reviews.text: Authentic legendary Juwel Tabuthema spice market. Enjoy the quiet atmosphere on the roof top terrace and enjoy beautiful views. The food is served quickly and it tastes good, seasoned to taste. Best mint tea so far. Try the Nutella crepes and the lamp omelette. Perfect breakfast spot.

reviews.author: Fadoua Atif
reviews.text: I’ve been coming to Café des Épices for years, and it’s still one of my favorite spots in the heart of the Medina. As a local from Marrakech, I always appreciate a place that stays consistent—and this one does. The food is tasty, the drinks are refreshing, and the rooftop view over the bustling souks is just perfect. It’s a great mix of calm and energy, right in the middle of the Medina. Highly recommend whether you’re visiting for the first time or looking for a familiar place to unwind.

reviews.author: S H
reviews.text: Amazing drinks and super convenient location amidst the labyrinth of souks. We went there in afternoon and it was burning hot but after few minutes it felt alright. Service was ok. We sat on the first floor and not many servers were available to look after our table. Food was good but we loved the drinks and ordered 4 different lemonades one after another. Overall good experience and would definitely recommend.

reviews.author: Marta Zaczkowska
reviews.text: I visited this restaurant every day during my stay in Marrakesh, and it quickly became my go-to spot. The food is absolutely delicious, and the service never disappoints—always friendly and attentive. One of my favorite things was sitting outside, soaking up the sun while watching the hustle and bustle of the square. It’s the perfect spot to enjoy a meal and people-watch as locals and tourists go about their day. Whether for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, this place was consistently great, and I can’t recommend it enough!

reviews.author: Heavenlykid 18
reviews.text: Here's the revised and concise review for Laddha Spices: "Laddha Spices was a fantastic breakfast spot with an amazing rooftop view of the Atlas Mountains. The setting, right in the middle of a lively souk, added to the charm. The breakfast was delicious, reasonably priced, and served in generous portions. The service was quick, and the staff were warm and hospitable. Honestly, don’t waste time looking elsewhere—this place is perfect for a great start to your day. Highly recommended, and I’d happily return anytime!"

reviews.author: Kevin Grubi
reviews.text: Le Jardin offers a beautiful setting right in the heart of the Medina—an oasis of calm with a charming atmosphere and a lovely view. The décor and ambiance are definitely highlights, and the staff were extremely friendly and welcoming throughout our visit. As for the food, it was of good quality and tasted great, but leaned heavily toward a Western/European style rather than offering something authentically Moroccan. That in itself isn’t a problem, but it’s important to note if you’re hoping for local flavors. The main issue was the price. While the food was enjoyable, it felt overpriced—comparable to what you’d pay in many parts of Europe, even Switzerland. Considering we’re in Marrakech, where quality food is usually more affordable, it didn’t feel justified. It almost felt like we were paying more for the ambiance than the cuisine. In summary: a lovely place, nice staff, and good food, but the price-to-value ratio just isn’t there. If you’re visiting Marrakech for its authentic and affordable culinary experiences, Le Jardin might not be the best choice. I wouldn’t recommend it overall.

reviews.author: Dave Rascal
reviews.text: We had been recommended to come here as it was close to our Riad. The food was ok, but I expected so much more than just ok to justify the high price. I had Chicken escalope which I enjoyed,but not much in the way of garnish or veg or sauce,I ordered chips which were tasty enough. My wife had Bolognese pasta which should have had cheese or garnish but was just a bowl of adequate pasta with an ok sauce. Hot chocolate was warm and again tasty but not very hot. I left feeling that we paid a premium for an adequate meal. Service was fairly slow,I had to ask the chatting waiters for drinks and desserts rather than them noticing we had finished. Certainly an ok meal with a busy feel, but more cafe than top restaurant.

reviews.author: Heavenlykid 18
reviews.text: Le Jardin is a fantastic restaurant that truly exceeded our expectations. The food was delicious, offering great quality and flavors at a very reasonable price. The hospitality was outstanding—Meenal, the front-end staff member who welcomed us, was particularly warm, accommodating, and went out of her way to ensure we felt comfortable, even without a prior reservation. The ambience of the restaurant is charming, adding to the overall experience. It’s the perfect spot for a delightful meal with excellent service. I highly recommend Le Jardin for its lovely food, great atmosphere, and top-notch hospitality!"

reviews.author: 254 Grace
reviews.text: The food was average. Decor and atmosphere amazing. The waiter who served me was so nice and helpful. Didn’t expect service charge to be added since it wasn’t stated anywhere only noticed it on my bill.

reviews.author: Micah Polston
reviews.text: If you're a foodie, you'll need to stop in. The staff was very courteous, manager and food servers checked on us consistently. The ambiance is comfortable and relaxing. The food is crazy good; even one of my pickier kids tried several things and liked several dishes. Most memorable meal in the Marrakesh Medina. Definitely eat here at least once, twice for a fuller menu sampling.

reviews.author: Ana Romano
reviews.text: Had a great sunset dinner here, amazing view to the main market. Ordered the chicken taco and a margherita pizza. The chicken tacos were very good, lots of sauce! The pizza was very simple, not much taste in the sauce. The service was great, although it was very busy we were still able to get a little table with an amazing view and we didn’t feel forgotten or ignored by the staff at all. We were there for quite a while having drinks prior to dinner and didn’t feel like we were being hurried to leave at all. Will definitely come back on another trip.

reviews.author: Robert Harder
reviews.text: 10pm on a Saturday, many terraces are filled or only seating for dinner but this place had plenty of spots on the balcony, with zero wait, just for coffee. We did end up getting some snacks too but give this place a look. Big menu, reasonable price, and a great view.

reviews.author: Adán García Borja
reviews.text: Seemingly paid for the view. Great place to people watch under shade. Food was pretty mediocre. Service was good. Credit Card accepted.

reviews.author: Tinagirl Travels
reviews.text: We ordered a chicken taco, what you get is a chicken wrap with chicken and fries inside. It’s food. What I don’t understand is why every single restaurant has the exact same menu. We got the same thing in Fez, I was hoping for better in Marrakech.

reviews.author: Adele Ashton
reviews.text: Absolutely wonderful food and service. Delicious drinks and staff were kind and helpful. Highly recommend this lovely place.

reviews.author: Shelley Kimber-Smith
reviews.text: We were recommended to try this restaurant, and it exceeded all expectations. The food was the best we’ve had on our trip, and the setting was absolutely stunning. The staff, especially Nabil, were incredibly attentive, taking the time to explain each dish in detail. While some have mentioned the pricing, we found it to be excellent value for the quality and service—if anything, it felt slightly underpriced. The Moroccan wine was outstanding and definitely worth trying. We’ll certainly be returning later this year!

reviews.author: Zainab Ayub
reviews.text: Atmosphere was so beautiful and peaceful, staff were so friendly, and helpful as well- they also provided a charger so I could charge my phone! The food was amazing! We ordered the unmissable tangia and it was one of the best dishes I’ve had! The meat was so tender and the vegetables were made perfectly. The portion sizes were so generous as well and I still daydream of this meal! Will definitely go back to Morocco just for that meal again!

reviews.author: Alison Sweetnam
reviews.text: Dashed in for lunch on our last day because the weather was cold and wet. Was a great way to spend a couple of hours - probably the most interesting meal we have had over 5 days - very Moroccan but far more on interesting than most restaurants offer. Excellent value although although not the cheapest . Nabil was an attentive and welcoming head waiter but they were all lovely.

reviews.author: Bill Lang
reviews.text: The ambiance and service were excellent, but having had only a weekend visit , I found that there were other places where I could eat which were considerably less expensive and had an equally good atmosphere and service. I am from Britain and was not very happy that smoking was allowed anywhere in the restaurant. I must confess I am not sure if that is true in the whole of Morocco (because I was there only for a short time) but I am always disinclined to revisit places where smoking is allowed in any places where non-smokers are likely to be located together.

reviews.author: Anouk
reviews.text: The food was really nice. It tasted amazing and there was no problem getting a vegetarian option. It was beautifully made and very authentic. The waiter was amazing and they were really attentive and welcoming. It's a beautiful atmosphere and there even was life music. Nabil was a really nice waiter and he made us feel very special on this evening. Thank you :)

reviews.author: Kerry Pealing
reviews.text: I had eggplant parmigiana and panacotta and both were delicious😁Little warm in there but it was 44 degrees outside so not too bad. Service can be improved particularly for 1 person who seemed liked he didn’t want to be there. But great food😁

reviews.author: Dave Rascal
reviews.text: Good quality food tucked away from the hustling streets of Marrakech. Lovely courtyard with plenty of dappled sunshine,can also be covered during a rain shower. Food was good, tagine arrived steaming hot and the anchovy & capers pizza was excellent. Good service too from hard working attentive staff.

reviews.author: Bart Zijderlaan
reviews.text: The place is beautifully decorated, so they have that going for them. But unfortunately the food was not from the same level. For the price you pay and the fancy setting you hope for top notch food, but it was okay at the best. It was nothing special, the pasta was overcooked and definitely not fresh. Go there for the perfect location and the insta shot, but stick with a tea or coffee.

reviews.author: Lukey
reviews.text: Really nice place to have lunch & a few beers. Really cheap, higher quality food. Fish is great. Nice & sheltered from the sun & they have fans to keep you cool. Nice servers

reviews.author: Rob Thomale
reviews.text: I can’t think of a better place to stop for a drink after a tour of Le Jardin Secret than Cafe Arabe. The quiet elegance makes for a welcome retreat from the bustling Souk Mouassine. I was there in the early afternoon and the ambience was delightful. The fine young men running this place are real professionals and it was a pleasure watching them practice their craft. I highly recommend it.

reviews.author: Cindy Cheng
reviews.text: If you want a delicious bowl of Moroccan Harira soup & don't mind eating at a truly local spot, this is the place. A perfectly spiced (but not spicy) soup with chickpeas, lentils, noodles, herbs & spices in a tomato based broth will hit the spot for 3 dhrms. You'll also get a sweet minty tea after you finish the soup. One of the highlights of my Morrocan food adventures 😃😋

reviews.author: charifa zemouri
reviews.text: Best place ever! I came here every morning for moroccan coffee with spices (ask for coffee without sugar). The harrira is absolutely amazing. You can have a coffee and a soup for less than 1 euro!!!

reviews.author: Håvard Anda Estensen
reviews.text: Get a bowl of porridge or soup from this hole-in-the-wall for a couple of dh. Locals hang out here.

reviews.author: Abi Curtis
reviews.text: Very cheap at 30 Dirhams a bowl, we ended up getting a second bowl

reviews.author: Hanane Ben Belaid
reviews.text: I've been coming to this restaurant for lunch a few times, and it’s always such a lovely experience. They used to offer a daily menu with about three options for each course—starters, mains, desserts—plus a few fresh juice choices. Lunch in the garden, with soft music playing and the sound of the fountain in the background, is a real treat. 🎶 Now that it’s summer, they’re open for dinner too, and the vibe is totally different in the best way. The evening breeze, cozy lighting, and relaxed ambiance create such a special atmosphere. ✨🌙 The new à la carte menu has so many tempting options. Last night, we tried the mini pastilla with beef and the chicken liver croquettes—both were absolutely delicious! Highly recommend. 👌🍽️ Service is awesome! Thanks to Chaima, Bouchra, and Hasna

reviews.author: Pawel Nojmiler
reviews.text: The food was absolutely delicious – every dish was full of flavor and beautifully prepared, from the fragrant tagines and classic zaalouk to the mouthwatering desserts like jawhara and mhencha. A true taste of Morocco at its finest! What makes this place even more special is the wonderful idea of supporting hearing-impaired staff – a truly heartwarming initiative that adds soul to the entire experience. We joked among ourselves that only a deaf man could handle working with so many women – the team spirit and positive energy in this restaurant are simply amazing. At the end, they kindly let us take a group photo and even posed with us, which was such a lovely gesture and the perfect way to wrap up the evening. A beautiful place – we highly recommend it to everyone! Come for the food, stay for the kindness and the atmosphere.

reviews.author: Abrar A
reviews.text: A Gastronomic Gem Empowering Women Amal is a truly special place, run exclusively by women, and it offers an experience that goes beyond just great food. Having lunch here was an absolute delight, combining a warm atmosphere with impeccable service. The food is not only delicious but also reasonably priced, making it an excellent value for the quality provided. The menu is thoughtfully curated, showcasing the best of Moroccan flavors with a touch of love and care in every bite. If you’re in the area, Amal is well worth a visit. It’s open only for lunch, so plan accordingly. Just 10 minutes’ drive away from Jama El Fna, this hidden gem is worth the short drive. Supporting Amal means not just enjoying an amazing meal but also contributing to an inspiring initiative empowering women in Marrakesh. Highly recommended for a memorable and meaningful dining experience!

reviews.author: Cathy R
reviews.text: My husband and I ate here 5 out of the 8 days we were in Marrakech in January. Starting from the beautiful patio with trees bulging with oranges to the welcoming staff and tasty menus, we fell in love with Amal. A bonus is its important mission to train women in multiple roles in the food and hospitality industry. We generally ordered one vegetarian tagine plus another of the rotating main dishes. We had several starters over our multiple visits, a few fresh fruit drinks and the fabulous cookies/biscuits that are on display inside. A value meal, not as inexpensive as some restaurants but wellworth the very reasonable prices. On our last day I got hugs from staff who we had gotten to know. Take the time to get to know them!

reviews.author: John McLaren
reviews.text: This is a fab find. Great food, had the Chicken Tagine & the Ground Meat Taco for lunch today. The service and food was outstanding. I love that this is also a training place for ‘disadvantaged women’ who are trained and then they go out and get careers in the catering industry, well worth supporting. It’s cheap too as it is a non-profit organisation. I highly recommend it and I will be going back to try some more of their other dishes. The menu is small but varied and looks like it changes often too and you can also do cookery classes here as well.

reviews.author: Mana Salem
reviews.text: Al Fassia in Marrakech is a culinary gem that deserves every bit of its glowing reputation. Nestled in the Gueliz district, the restaurant offers a refined yet warm atmosphere, blending traditional Moroccan decor with understated elegance. From the moment you step inside, the scent of saffron, cinnamon, and slow-cooked meats sets the tone for an unforgettable meal. The dining area is adorned with intricately carved wood, soft lighting, and crisp linens, creating a welcoming space that feels both luxurious and unpretentious. The menu is a celebration of Moroccan classics executed with precision. Standouts include the tender lamb tagine with prunes and almonds—succulent and richly spiced—and the chicken pastilla, a flaky pastry layered with savory shredded meat, dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar. Each dish arrives beautifully presented, highlighting the care put into both flavor and aesthetics. The couscous, steamed to fluffy perfection and paired with seasonal vegetables, is a must-try. Desserts like orange blossom-infused pastries or mint tea served in silver pots provide a sweet, aromatic finish. What truly sets Al Fassia apart is its all-female staff, a rarity in Morocco’s dining scene. The service is attentive without being overbearing, guided by genuine warmth and expertise. Portions are generous, and while prices lean toward the higher end, the quality justifies the cost. Reservations are advisable, as the restaurant draws both locals and travelers. For an authentic taste of Moroccan hospitality and cuisine, Al Fassia delivers an experience that lingers long after the meal ends.

reviews.author: Jeremias Perez
reviews.text: We had our first dinner in Marrakesh at Al Fassia Gueliz, celebrating my mom’s birthday, and it couldn’t have been a better choice. Every dish was incredibly tasty, showcasing the best of Moroccan cuisine with depth and refinement. The wine we chose was just as impressive, perfectly complementing the meal. Beyond the food, the restaurant’s concept—empowering women in hospitality—adds another layer of appreciation to the experience. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making it an enjoyable place to dine. Given the quality and overall experience, the price is very fair for such a refined dinner. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Wayne Whitwell
reviews.text: If your in Marakesh, this is the place to visit. Booking a table is highly recommended, service is on point and the food is great ( we had the slow cooked shoulder of lamb). The staff only speak French and Arabic, but don't let that put you off, they do have English menus.

reviews.author: Layla Juma
reviews.text: This is one of the best restaurants I've been to in a long time. The food was exceptional, and the service was top-notch, especially from Fatiha, who was delightful and attentive. I highly recommend this place!

reviews.author: michelle barton
reviews.text: Beautiful restaurant, serene ambience, absolutely sublime food, and really attentive and friendly ladies looking after you! Attention to detail fabulous. Best experience of our week in Marrakesh. Special mention to the very lovely Fatiha who made our evening, with her laughter and good humour x

reviews.author: Erwin Abreo
reviews.text: I recently dined here with my wife and had a wonderful experience. We kicked things off with the taster shots, which were perfect for anyone on a detox or looking for a light, refreshing start—each juice was made with natural ingredients. For starters, we ordered the zucchini fritters, and they were absolutely amazing. The portion size was just right, with four fritters that packed in great flavor. For the main course, I opted for the calamari with squid ink rice, which was also delicious—perfectly cooked and flavorful. Overall, the dining experience was excellent, and the customer service was top-notch. The staff made sure we felt well taken care of, especially on the lovely terrace. One thing to note, though, is that the portion sizes are on the smaller side, so if you're a big eater, this might not be the best fit. However, if you're open to trying a variety of dishes, you'll definitely be satisfied. Thanks again to the wonderful team who made our evening memorable!

reviews.author: Connor Greenhalgh
reviews.text: Me and my girlfriend visited this restaurant with high hopes due to the excellent reviews, preparing to pay higher than average prices for an excellent meal. The restaurant itself is absolutely beautiful, with a rooftop area that looks out over Marrakech. The food was pricey, and we started with a portion of zucchini fritters. These were a good size and very fresh but nothing to write home about. We then received our main courses, lamb chops with potato (as they had ran out of the usual accompaniments), and a lentil salad for my girlfriend. The salad was presented well and tasted good, but nothing special. The lamb was the real issue. I ordered it medium, which is supposed to be slightly pink. Two of my lamb chops were perfect, the last however was incredibly undercooked, being closer to rare/blue than medium. By this point I had already pretty much finished but told the waiter anyway as feedback. The waiter then told me I was wrong, and that the chop was in-fact medium. If this was the case then my other two were overcooked. I couldn’t be bothered arguing and we just left the food and got the bill. After bringing the bill, he joked that “I should order it well done next time”. Rest assured I will not, because there will not be a next time. There is much better in Marrakech for much cheaper. I would not recommend this restaurant.

reviews.author: Monika Filonowicz
reviews.text: We went for a late lunch with a reservation we made in advance. Rooftop is beautiful and views are great. However, the food was terrible and much overpriced. Chicken pastilla Looked good but was extremely dry. All of our food came super fast so didn’t seem freshly prepared

reviews.author: Anisa
reviews.text: Really nice rooftop restaurant/bar in the heart of the souk! I had gone here for lunch without reservation, so unfortunately I did not manage to get a seat on the rooftop. But regardless, the food was amazing! I ordered gambas, and it had been one of the best gambas that I have tried in my life.

reviews.author: Rocio Elortegui Pascual
reviews.text: Lovely place. The quality of the food is worth the price, also, the atmosphere is beautiful. Only but is one of the waitresses ignored us all the time, she seemed angry to even look at us. We were three and she left one of the plates on the only empty place and just left without explaining which plate it was. But the rest of the staff was really nice.

reviews.author: Georgia Hurley
reviews.text: By far the nicest place to eat. Myself and my mum went here 3 times on our time away.. for 2 dinners and a lunch. Generous portions. Clean food. It is very small and they do try to pack in as many people as they can within reason. Nice views. And a cool vibe. Tagines are by far the best we had. And the nutella pastilla was incredible... highly recommended 😊

reviews.author: Alison C
reviews.text: Great little place with good food and good views. Staff were lovely and helpful in explaining the menu. Kofta and egg tagine was delicious as were the briwates for the starter (filo pastry parcels, like mini samosas, with a selection of fillings - cheese, spinach, meat and veg). Would definitely recommend it and suggest going up to the terrace for the view!

reviews.author: Caterina Puccio
reviews.text: Definitely worth!! Just the perfect place to have dinner, super central, nice staff, good food for not too expensive prices... Definitely something hard to find in Marrakesh, so absolutely recommended!! The view from the terrace is also lovely and they have a nice system to keep the whole place cool (with some humidity vaporizer) We spent 17euro for one thuna salad, one tajine with prunes and drinks. Both dishes were delicious. Problematic are only the seats, which are not exactly big or super comfortable. So don't expect to be in a restaurant with much room for yourself. This wasnt a problem for us though.

reviews.author: Klarissa
reviews.text: Beautiful restaurant with great local cuisine. I had the lamb tajine with apricots and walnuts - very tender and perfectly seasoned. The coffee is good as well. Went there twice during our 3 days in Marrakesh.

reviews.author: 고지나
reviews.text: Heard a lot of good things about this restaurant so we were pretty excited to try it for lunch today after visiting the Koutoubia Mosque. The service was good but the food was quite disappointing. Restaurant was small and felt very touristy.

reviews.author: M
reviews.text: Sadly the food here was very disappointing. We ordered spring rolls which were cold and slimey very odd texture. Expected them to be served hot and crispy. Meatballs had an odd taste, unfortunately I just ate round them and had a little amount of the spaghetti. Staff were lovely but it was very slow service and food did take a very long time

reviews.author: Emiliano Sallustri
reviews.text: The food is average. Good Tajin but starters are not at the expected level for the price. Small quantities and poor quality. Atmosphere is nice, and we tried a good Moroccan wine. I wouldn’t go back because of the high price, quality of food and slowness in serving, but the restaurant is ok, definitely not a scam.

reviews.author: Arisa S.
reviews.text: Nice atmosphere. Special recipe of couscous is highly recommended. But what we liked the most is the service of ushering you to find taxi so you don't get lost again finding your way back to hotel.

reviews.author: Franziska Leibrock
reviews.text: Let’s start with the good things: The restaurant has a very cozy atmosphere, mostly lit by candles. It’s a very scenic place and you can sit very comfortably. The place itself is quite modern and clean and both the menu for drinks and food are rather extensive. HOWEVER, We went there for dinner because we heard a lot of good things. Unfortunately, Le Foundouk could not even remotely live up to that. So here’s the negative points from our visit: - as a couple, we ended up paying a substantial amount more than the typical bill that we would have when we go out to eat in Amsterdam, having the same amount of food - it was so cold inside that we had to keep our jackets on - the food itself was rather underwhelming. We had two different starters and two different mains and all of them basically tasted like nothing - even though there is a quite large amount of food on the menu, there’s nothing really special or new - and lastly what made our experience truly unpleasant: when we paid our bill we stayed seated for a while, waiting for the change to arrive. After a few minutes we had to ask for it and then finally received it. When we received it, we got a „friendly“ hint from the waitress that there was no tip included, only taxes. When we then left the waitress almost run to our table to see if we had left some tip after her friendly reminder and when she saw that we didn’t do so, she gave a sign to her coworkers who didn’t even say goodbye to us All in all this could be a very nice place for a romantic dinner, but after our visit, we are not at all surprised that the place was only filled for about 15% despite the peak hour that we went.

reviews.author: Celine La.
reviews.text: We were a group of nine and were very satisfied with the food and impressed by the ambiance. The service was attentive and friendly, and despite our large group, we didn’t have to wait long for our orders. Even during Ramadan, alcoholic beverages were available. For the reservation, a deposit of €20 per person was required, but this was deducted from the final bill. The location of the restaurant strongly reflects the contrast between wealth and poverty in the region. BUT!!! During our visit, one person had their wallet stolen from their bag on the chair—€400 was taken, and the wallet was later found in the restroom. When we asked the staff about it, they simply said, “This happens here often,” but did not offer any further assistance. We cannot say whether it was a staff member or another guest, but we were not sitting in a high-traffic area leading to the restroom. We strongly recommend keeping a close eye on your valuables and carrying them securely.

reviews.author: Youssef youssef
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Younes Haouari
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Kha Rh Mu
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Kaoutar Karroubas
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: El khafik Abdelmalk
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Malysa Johnson
reviews.text: Wow!!! We were looking for an authentic and beautiful Moroccan dinner experience and that's what we got here. Amazing food (seriously, come hungry, its 5 courses) and the staff was great. He let us take home our pastries because we literally could not eat more (we wanted to!) Also definitely get reservations and let them know about food allergies and preferences ahead of time.

reviews.author: Safae F.
reviews.text: We had a really nice evening at Dar Yacout. The place is beautiful, with amazing traditional decor that gives you a real Moroccan vibe. The staff were super friendly and helpful, and the whole experience felt very welcoming. The food was tasty and there was a lot of it – course after course of Moroccan dishes. We loved the setting, the music, and the atmosphere. A great spot if you want to enjoy a special night out in Marrakech!

reviews.author: KAM
reviews.text: Dar Yacout offers an exceptional journey into Moroccan cuisine and culture. From the moment you step inside, the stunning traditional décor and warm ambiance set the stage for an unforgettable evening. The food is simply outstanding—rich, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every dish, from the aromatic tagines to the perfectly spiced pastilla, was a delight. The service was impeccable, with staff ensuring a seamless and welcoming experience. The rooftop views of Marrakesh add an extra touch of magic, making it not just a meal, but an experience to remember. If you’re looking for authentic Moroccan cuisine in a breathtaking setting, Dar Yacout is a must-visit.

reviews.author: Haneen AlQunaibit
reviews.text: Exceptional experience The true Moroccan Experience The amazing hospitality Amazing Food The High respect to culture and religion We had lamb Shoulder, Couscous with Vegetables Traditional appetizer Amazing service as our server Mr Youssef has been working here for 32 years and he says this is his Family Shows you what an amazing place this is to the community, the people and culture May god bless them

reviews.author: Baert D’hauwers
reviews.text: Fantastic place for those who love authentic Moroccan cuisine and enjoy in an authentic setting. Quality wines could be a little better though, work with some French or Italian references?

reviews.author: Muhammad Ali
reviews.text: Absolutely stunning. Photos don’t do it justice. It doesn’t really need a review but here are a few things that I hope might help. Entry was 100dh. Take cash. They weren’t accepting card when I went. I saw them turn people away. Go first thing and enjoy it while it’s empty. Weekday is better than weekend. If you see a group going in. Quickly get in front of them because trust me. They will ruin it for you. It will take around an hour or so to explore. Be respectful of people trying to take photos. If you see someone waiting for a shot. Don’t be an idiot and walk in front. Most important. Enjoy!

reviews.author: Rama
reviews.text: I went with my friend on a morning and there was a big queue but it took us less then 5 minutes to buy our tickets and enter. To say the least it was absolutely stunning and highly recommend that you best this historic site . The rooms were absolutely beautiful and jaw dropping. This must be on your bucket list

reviews.author: David Masters
reviews.text: Wonderful from start to finish, buy your tickets online, they are neither dated or timed. Entry was quick and efficient, I would go early, some of the courtyards are suntrap and will quickly get uncomfortable in the strong sunshine. The rooms and spaces are exquisite and beautiful.

reviews.author: A-S-K
reviews.text: We bought tickets on the day and there was a small queue but it was ok, it did get very busy when it got to around 1pm so best to go earlier. The palace was lovely but there is some construction that is still going on. Me and my sisters just wandered around the fascinating palace and took lots of great photos.

reviews.author: Aniik Gupta
reviews.text: Beautiful palace. Really intricate artwork on ceilings, doors and mosaic floors walls etc. Worth a visit. Could easily spend 2-3 hrs here. Not wheelchair accessible or people with mobility issues may struggle

reviews.author: Jeff Zander
reviews.text: The personnel were some of the most pleasant people you can find, loved the atmosphere and the cafe was located within the Medina near the blue gate. Got the camel burger, excellent and got the carrot cake, also excellent. Highly recommended

reviews.author: Stephen Anyan
reviews.text: Had an amazing experience at Café Clock and I can’t recommend it enough! The ambiance is warm and inviting, with a unique blend of cozy corners and an artistic vibe that makes you feel right at home. The facilities are good (by North African standards) The food? Brilliant. The menu is diverse, with plenty of options to suit all tastes, and everything I tried was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. But what really made my visit stand out was the exceptional service. Not only was the staff attentive and friendly, but I also had a small incident where I dropped my wallet in the bathroom. I wasn’t aware it was gone until I was about to leave, but a man who had been playing guitar noticed it and kindly returned it to me. That kind of thoughtful gesture really added a personal touch to the experience. 4.5 stars for me. Not giving 5 stars because it’s not a wheelchair accessible area.

reviews.author: Y S
reviews.text: They have many cozy rooms and beautiful terraces. The food was great as well! We tried their recommendation, the camel burger—it was our first time eating camel meat, and it had a unique and delicious taste. Unfortunately, we couldn’t finish our lemonade and ginger drink because it was a bit too strong for us! 😅

reviews.author: Amy Leese
reviews.text: Gorgeous setting and friendly attentive staff. I was guided to rooftop area with plenty of seating. Super chilled vibe. Relaxing. Attracts tourists. Mostly young singles or young families. I tried the famous camel burger!! 🍔 Well cooked and presented. Never tried camel before!!!

reviews.author: Brendan DS
reviews.text: Legendary Fez cafe which now has branches across Morocco. Housed in a Riad the cafe is spread over four levels with an impressive roof terrace. The service is top notch with waiters friendly and knowledgeable

reviews.author: Guy Manchester
reviews.text: We loved this place. The atmosphere was wonderful with lots of different levels and spaces to sit and the food was great. Especially recommend the (vegan) vegetable pastilla - the coriander dressing was especially inspiring! To cap it off there was some great local musicians playing live upstairs.

reviews.author: James Gomm
reviews.text: Really nice chilled cafe in the south part of the old city, which has a nice friendly atmosphere and colourful artwork on the walls (we ended up visiting twice). They have a roof terrace as well as some indoor seating. They do a few different moroccon dishes - the lamb tagine was particually good (sadly didnt get a photo) and went very well with the mint lemonade. The coffee was pretty decent as well. They also offer cooking classes (we didn't do pne, but saw some people having a lession when we ate upstairs).

reviews.author: Aishah B
reviews.text: Great breakfast, had the Berber eggs and they were delicious 😋 especially with the bread which was quite light. My partner had the granola which was great too. The fresh orange juice and coffee was good too!

reviews.author: V G
reviews.text: This is a nice restaurant in the Kasbah area of Marrakesh, with an indoor space (with no AC or fan so hot and not very big) and an outdoor rooftop area (No fans and in summer also really hot). The decor of the restaurant is nice, staff are friendly wearing touristic t-shirts. In the entrance area there are loads of pamphlets and brochures of the Marrakesh area as this is a touristy restaurant. We ordered the fried chicken burger and Chicken Rfisa. The prices are quite high, but the quantity is good and food is freshly cooked. The burger came with french fries which tasted horrible as they were soggy. It was our first time trying the Chicken Rfisa as it's a local Moroccan delicacy but it was unique and a one time try for us: filled with lentils, bread, and chicken (basically chicken tagine with bread and not served in a local style pot that tagine is famously served in). The Rfisa was also very filling and nice. The staff, when asked, also promptly gave us a takeaway box to take our leftovers with us.

reviews.author: Clement Leung
reviews.text: Great restaurant with good vibes. When we went, we had live music playing which was great. Definitely get the camel burger. It's not for everyone but it's worth the try.

reviews.author: Marc Young
reviews.text: Visited this iconic hotel, renowned as a retreat for the rich and famous. A smart dress code is required to enter, but the experience is worth the effort. The elegant lobby exudes timeless luxury, the service is impeccable, and the surrounding gardens are perfect for a leisurely stroll after coffee or tea.

reviews.author: Anas Najm
reviews.text: Disappointing Experience – Not Worth the Hype or the Price As an American traveler, I had high expectations for La Mamounia given its reputation and the steep nightly rate of around $1,500. While the property itself is undeniably beautiful and well-maintained, the overall experience left a lot to be desired — especially for guests who expect hospitality, not hassle. One of the most frustrating aspects of our stay was the hotel’s strict and frankly discriminatory policy on guests. Despite booking rooms that were clearly designated for two people each, we were constantly harassed by staff when we tried to bring visitors — particularly Moroccan friends — to our room. The hotel’s solution was always to force us to purchase an entirely new room, sometimes quoting up to $1,000 per night, which felt more like a money grab than a legitimate policy. On our last night, they even claimed the hotel was fully booked, yet we found availability online — further evidence that they simply didn’t want to accommodate us. Service, for a hotel of this caliber, was also underwhelming. Several staff members made us uncomfortable by directly asking for tips any time we paid with cash — turning every interaction into an awkward negotiation. For the amount of money we spent, we expected to feel welcomed and relaxed — not micromanaged, bullied, or taken advantage of. Ultimately, while La Mamounia may offer a visually stunning backdrop, the hospitality and treatment of guests — especially Americans traveling with local friends — was disappointing. I do not recommend this hotel to fellow travelers from the U.S. or to anyone who expects fair, transparent service. There are better places in Marrakesh that respect their guests and provide a more inclusive, enjoyable experience.

reviews.author: Alexandre Choves
reviews.text: My visit to La Mamounia was truly unforgettable. From the moment I arrived, I felt immersed in a world of elegance and authentic Moroccan charm. The service was impeccable — every staff member was warm, professional, and made me feel like royalty. The rooms were beautifully designed, the gardens were absolutely enchanting, and the attention to detail throughout the hotel was flawless. I enjoyed a peaceful afternoon tea surrounded by timeless beauty and a serene atmosphere. La Mamounia is not just a hotel — it’s a cultural and artistic experience in the heart of Marrakech. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for something truly special.

reviews.author: E Lei
reviews.text: Iconic hotel and a must visit! Beautiful interior. Even if you don't stay here, come for a nice stroll and grab a bite/drinks in the stunning garden. You'll love it! Beats the touristic attractions like Bahia Palace.

reviews.author: Matthew Guillory
reviews.text: I didn’t stay overnight at La Mamounia, but I had the chance to visit the property — and it absolutely lived up to its legendary reputation. The gardens are stunning, perfectly manicured and peaceful, with hidden corners and orange trees that make you feel like you’ve stepped into another world. The pool area is just as impressive, with elegant design and a luxurious vibe. Even as a visitor, I was treated with genuine warmth. The service was exceptional, and the staff made me feel welcome every step of the way. If you’re in Marrakech, it’s well worth stopping by — whether it’s for tea, a walk through the gardens, or just to soak in the atmosphere of one of the most iconic hotels in the world.

reviews.author: Cindy Cheng
reviews.text: If you want a delicious bowl of Moroccan Harira soup & don't mind eating at a truly local spot, this is the place. A perfectly spiced (but not spicy) soup with chickpeas, lentils, noodles, herbs & spices in a tomato based broth will hit the spot for 3 dhrms. You'll also get a sweet minty tea after you finish the soup. One of the highlights of my Morrocan food adventures 😃😋

reviews.author: charifa zemouri
reviews.text: Best place ever! I came here every morning for moroccan coffee with spices (ask for coffee without sugar). The harrira is absolutely amazing. You can have a coffee and a soup for less than 1 euro!!!

reviews.author: Håvard Anda Estensen
reviews.text: Get a bowl of porridge or soup from this hole-in-the-wall for a couple of dh. Locals hang out here.

reviews.author: Abi Curtis
reviews.text: Very cheap at 30 Dirhams a bowl, we ended up getting a second bowl

reviews.author: Jamie Coxon
reviews.text: Great restaurant with perfect ambience ce and lovely food. The service was second to none. We tried the Manfouk tagine and Marrakchia Tanjia. Lovely wine too and the wine selection was huge. Lovely spacious plot on the roof. It is more high end for those on a budget. Advisable to book a table in advance.

reviews.author: Julia Riera
reviews.text: A peaceful oasis in the Medina, this restaurant offers great quality food in an elegant atmosphere. The rooftop has amazing views of the city. Staff was friendly and helpful. Food is a bit overpriced compared to the average restaurant, but worth paying for the location. Highly recommend the lamb tajine!

reviews.author: Emilie Gibney
reviews.text: Was recommended this restaurant and it did not disappoint. Incredible food and drinks (lamb tagine and chicken tagine were delicious, iced tea was also superb. If you’re interested in wines or beers - a huge menu is available !). The service was slow given how busy they are but not a problem if you’re happy to wait. Brilliant views and atmosphere as a rooftop restaurant in Marrakech

reviews.author: Shiona Luke
reviews.text: We came for dinner and ordered the ceviche to share as a starter, then a burger and the seabream as mains. The ceviche was a standout, delicious and fresh. We also had wine and beer. Overall, the service was good and friendly. 4*s given as price is significantly above other places in the area and we felt it didn't stand out as much given this. The live music and terrace is beautiful though so worth a visit if you want a fancier night out.

reviews.author: Genith Copeland
reviews.text: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Terrasse des Épices totally delivered! What a vibe — beautiful rooftop setting right in the middle of the Medina. Even though it was super hot out, the little mist fans at the booths made all the difference. We were totally comfortable and could actually enjoy the afternoon. The drinks were phenomenal — seriously some of the best we’ve had anywhere. The food was full of flavor, and the desserts? Dangerous. 😄 Everything was on point — great service, great atmosphere, totally worth it. Would go back in a heartbeat.

reviews.author: Mushed Miah
reviews.text: Beautiful classical Masjid, such a contrast to the modern structures I am used to. SubhanAllah, you can feel the historic nature of it, inside was clean and relatively new. Decent walking distance from the Jma'a Al Fanaa too.

reviews.author: Jennifer E.
reviews.text: Only experienced this Mosque from the outside but either way, great site to see. They were currently reconstructing a few spots due to the earthquake they had about 2 years ago. Great big mosque. Nice huge walking platform to see the mosque from all different angles. Excited I was able to see this place up close and admire it. Walking distance to Souks and hotels around the area.

reviews.author: Kashif Aasi
reviews.text: I loved this place, it’s spacious and beautiful, calm, soul healing place. Must do if you in Marrakesh city. Mosque opens at prayer times so go in at that time for free and do prayer plus appreciate the architecture and simplicity of this marvellous structure. Loved the tall rising minaret.

reviews.author: Suzanne Bedwell- Byatt
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful 😍 the Koutoubia mosque feels so peaceful in the madness of Marrakech. The architecture of the building is amazing. Would definitely advise to go there with a guide as there is some much history and information to learn, it's fascinating. The gardens are very well looked after and perfect compliment to the mosque.

reviews.author: Aayan Toys & Gaming
reviews.text: This mosque is amazing. It shows how much work was put into it and how beautiful it is. It's over 800 years old, and considering that, I think that it must deserve to be a five-star. Another great reason to give it five stars is because the mosque is kept very clean and tidy. You must put your shoes in a bag which helps to keep it clean. Please note that you must be a Muslim to enter.

reviews.author: Justyna Baker
reviews.text: What an amazing tucked-away beautiful place this is! From the moment we arrived at this charming Moroccan riad, we knew we were in for something special. (Though, I must admit — we did mistakenly walk through the back door at first — silly of us! But honestly, even that little detour couldn’t spoil what was to come.) Once inside, we were blown away by how absolutely stunning the interior is — full of authentic character and elegance. We were warmly welcomed and invited to enjoy drinks up on the roof terrace, which was the perfect way to ease into our evening. The service throughout our visit was outstanding — so attentive, kind, and genuine. It really felt like everyone wanted us to have the best time possible, and their hospitality made all the difference. We decided on the famous Dar Zellij Mechoui, and oh my… the lamb was simply delicious — cooked to perfection, tender, and full of flavor. As the sun set, the whole riad transformed into a romantic paradise, with soft, beautiful lights twinkling all around us. It was a truly unforgettable evening, and I can’t recommend this magical place enough.

reviews.author: Salaman Veerathas
reviews.text: This place supposedly has great reviews so we tried it for our anniversary. To the staffs credit, they were fantastic and very polite and accommodating. They even sang us a happy anniversary song for us without us asking which was really lovely. However, I'm not sure if it was the time we arrived (6:30pm). We were the first customers in an empty and silent restaurant. We thought as per the reviews that there would be live music and other entertainment. Absolutely nothing. Was very awkward. Other customers turned up a little bit later but the atmosphere was still very awkward. The place itself inside is lovely. Food was ok, though for the prices you pay, it is ridiculous! Super expensive for average food with decent presentation.

reviews.author: Dale Harrington
reviews.text: A truly stunning interior to this restaurant. Very authentic and you can feel the history of the building. Staff were very attentive. No alcohol served at lunch. Very generous portion sizes, we couldn’t finish the couscous. Highly recommend. Starters were also delicious. Freshly baked bread too.

reviews.author: Raluca Monac
reviews.text: Really nice tasteful and traditional place in Medina. It is worth trying it for a tasty meal during your visit. We were all pleased with the food and atmosphere as well as the extremely nice and serviceable staff. The beef with plums and peaches was amazing in particular.

reviews.author: YJ
reviews.text: I had a great experience at Dar Zellij! The lamb for 2 was super tasty and melted off the bone. The highlight was our waiter Hisham, that was really attentive and so lovely.

reviews.author: Israel Oliveira
reviews.text: My family and I liked it a lot! It was an excellent rooftop in Marrakech. Good food, good space very well decorated, friendly staff, a wonderful night!

reviews.author: Berat Onur Ersen
reviews.text: We asked our hostel for a reliable restaurant to eat good food on our first day and they recommended here. We found their food such tasty that came back again to eat other tagine varieties. Lamb tagine is a must try. You can fjnd maybe other tagine elsewhere such as chicken tagine or meatball tagine but that lamb was fantastic. Their service speed is average. Overall ambience at this restaurant and dining around sunset with view was such an authentic experience.

reviews.author: Olivia Schneider
reviews.text: Great rooftop seating with an amazing view! It's a good spot to get a break from the business of the medina. I only ever had drinks but the food looked really good. Wifi works well.

reviews.author: Jay Frankera
reviews.text: After exploring Agafay and getting stuck in the usual Marrakech traffic, we were more than ready for lunch. Bâcha Café, as expected, had a 3-hour wait (yep, three). A quick Google search brought up Atay Café, and we decided to give it a shot. There were five of us, no reservations, so we waited about 30 minutes which wasn’t too bad. Once seated, we ordered a mix of dishes: chicken, kefta, and lamb tagines, chicken skewers, and chicken couscous. The chicken and lamb tagines were the standouts—rich, vibrant, and deeply flavorful. They came with couscous on the side, which soaked up the sauce perfectly. The kefta tagine, unfortunately, wasn’t as flavorful. The chicken couscous was tasty too, but fair warning: it comes with what felt like two full cups of couscous—definitely shareable. We wrapped up with a brownie and an almond tart, but both were just okay. Not worth the extra calories. The rooftop setting is a great spot to take in the views of the bustling alley below. Most of the staff were friendly and accommodating, though the hostess had a bit of an attitude during check-in and again when we were leaving. Not a dealbreaker, but definitely took away from the overall experience. All in all, 4 stars for solid food, good vibes, and rooftop views—but minus one star for that less-than-welcoming first and last impression.

reviews.author: penny Sims
reviews.text: Couldn’t give any more stars , the food was pretty bad , and sadly my friend suffered with a nasty tummy bug after eating fish tagine which we complained about because it was salty and really unpleasant…. Nothing was done about it ! And we left soon after , my chicken with lemons and saffron was very dry.

reviews.author: Norb Now
reviews.text: It’s little bit hidden and difficult to find. Definitely requires a reservation. Highly recommended. The staff is so polite and moves like shadows. Food is amazing. It was a great journey through key maroccan dishes. Live music is a good addition.

reviews.author: E C
reviews.text: This is a very nice place for a multi course meal with entertainment. The entertainment was sounded very repetitive. The first course with many small plates of food was very good. It was followed by a tagine and a desert. It was a set price menu that included a bottle of wine. Expect to spend at least a couple of hours or more here. Food was nice prepared and presented.

reviews.author: Filippo Scanzano
reviews.text: Beautiful place! Amazing food, superb service and lovely music - at a fair price

reviews.author: Jessica May
reviews.text: Magical experience. Excellent food and service. The atmosphere was fabulous. We loved everything about it including the door-to-door escort from El Fenn. Highly recommend!!

reviews.author: Jonathan H
reviews.text: This is not an easy place to find, just a discrete brass plaque marks the entrance and you must knock to be let in. But once in you can't fail to be enchanted by the lovely ambience. I was prepared for the extensive fixed menu so didn't eat lunch. The cost is 650MAD per person and for that you get:- Your choice of Aperitif with olives Bottle of wine 8 meze starters (vegetarian) Chicken tagine Lamb tagine Couscous with vegetables 2 x deserts Tea or coffee It is a ridiculous amount of food for 1 person and I couldn't eat it all. I'm sure most people would think less food and less cost? But I understand the restaurant is full most evenings so I guess the owner feels they have a winning formula. Service was excellent and there is live music.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: The food was so nice! I tasted the seffa madfouna and it was so good. It's a must try if you like experiencing local traditional dishes! The traditional soup and the briouat were also as good.

reviews.author: Bean W
reviews.text: Nice decoration restaurant But if you are a Asian you will not have any service For another nationality I think you can come

reviews.author: Kentaro Wada
reviews.text: Hospitality was great and the view from the table (1st floor) was nice. The vegetables and the bread were very good - chicken skewered were OK so rated 4.0.

reviews.author: Aivar
reviews.text: Simple tasty food for lunch made inside the Tahini are always good. Lamb chops are more tender and juicy compared to chicken. On the terrace there was also lovely locals (turtles)

reviews.author: Papa Faye
reviews.text: We ate there while visiting the nearby Bahia palace. The food if amazing, authentic Moroccan, and the service was excellent. Highly recommended, mashaAllah!

reviews.author: Aya Louzi
reviews.text: Amazing atmosphere! Amazing music! The dancers were to die for and the food (coming from a Moroccan) was so authentic and delicious! Our waiter Bono, was always there whenever we needed him and even danced with us in the circle! They even dedicated a song to me! 10/10 Would 100% recommend to anyone looking for the most authentic Moroccan restaurant in town.

reviews.author: Nai Tana
reviews.text: We went for dinner with entertainment. It was so fun. The music was loud and the atmosphere was great. The musicians and dancers were so talented. It was well worth the price. The mains were large and they serve mint tea at the end. All the staff, especially our waiter Bono was so friendly and helpful. They definitely made everyone have a wonderful time. We would definitely come back.

reviews.author: Leah Sage
reviews.text: Dar Essalam in Marrakesh is a rooftop gem that delivers on both atmosphere and flavor. The views from the top are absolutely stunning, you get a sweeping look over the city that makes the whole dining experience feel extra special, especially as the sun sets and the lights come on. We went all in on the appetizers, and it was absolutely worth it. Everything was fresh, vibrant, and beautifully plated. From traditional Moroccan bites to more creative twists, each dish had something unique to offer.

reviews.author: said oukhatour
reviews.text: I’ve been familiar with Restone Dar Es Salaam for a long time and used to book there regularly for people visiting the area. It was always a smooth, friendly process, just a quick call or message, and everything was arranged with no problem. But recently, that’s changed completely. Now, bookings must be made only through their website, and you’re required to pay in advance. That might work for some, but it adds unnecessary pressure, especially for guests who prefer flexible arrangements or are booking on short notice. It’s honestly disappointing to see such a rigid policy replace what used to feel like a more welcoming and cooperative approach. I really hope they go back to valuing long-term relationships and make it easier again for people who’ve supported them from the start.

reviews.author: G R
reviews.text: A lovely drink on the rooftop with beautiful views, followed by an A class show of traditional Moroccan music, band and dancing accompanied by a 4 course meal. This was all at the cost of less than £60 for 2 people including wine for the whole evening. Brilliant service by Bono who was class at giving a great service even though it was very busy. The dancers were amazing and the atmosphere outstanding. Best night in Marrakesh for sure!

reviews.text: Nice hotel and a short taxi ride to the main square.

reviews.text: Good value for money. Professional service

reviews.author: Hamza Izourane
reviews.text: The large swimming pool is magnificent
