reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Ha W
reviews.text: Great restaurant! Fresh and delicious foods, excellent service with english speaking staff. Serves wine / alcoholic beverages. Upscale atmosphere with beautiful inner courtyard. Prices compared to others in Morocco expensive, expect to pay European prices for food and drinks.

reviews.author: Jayanthi Gupta
reviews.text: The best Italian food I have ever had . The ravioli was so delicious and melting in my mouth. And the ambience is excellent with good music . It's a 5 star place I would rate this

reviews.author: Eleanor Coate
reviews.text: Wow this place is incredible. Wonderful staff and atmosphere. Can’t wait to go back one day. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Paix SurTerre
reviews.text: The exquisite setting, in a spectacular Riad courtyard makes up for the mis-steps in other areas. The food is good - as is the service - But overall in our opinion both are a little heavy-handed, and for the high price both could easily be finessed to become a little more sophisticated. Though regardless this restaurant is well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Martin Hills
reviews.text: After 6 days in Marrakech I was looking for something different for an evening meal and our hotel recommended Pepe Nero which was nearby. This was the best meal by far in Marrakech to date. I've been traveling a lot in South America, Europe and Asia in the last 6 months and this ranks right at the top of the restaurants I've dined in in that period. Every dish we had was great but the lamb especially was delicious. All the staff we engaged with were professional and engaging but Mr Rabie was a delight. The atmosphere of the restaurant was excellent even though we weren't in the main courtyard. We were lucky to get a table without booking and I'd recommend you book in advance as the restaurant filled up after we sat down. The price of the meal was very reasonable for the quality of the food, the setting and the service we received. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Minoukis Places
reviews.text: Closed for non-Muslims, which I can understand but still…

reviews.author: Karim Idrissi
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Brandon Chang
reviews.text: Had an extraordinary experience at this hotel! The decor is immaculate -- truly one of the most beautiful properties I’ve ever encountered. The rooms are both spacious and elegantly appointed. Service is impressively swift; for instance, when I requested a toothbrush, it was delivered in just five minutes. Every staff member I met was exceptionally kind and eager to help. Plus, the hotel boasts some outstanding dining options. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Alexandre Choves
reviews.text: This was my very first stop in Marrakech, and starting my journey at Royal Mansour was nothing short of magical. The entire experience felt like stepping into a story from One Thousand and One Nights—a perfect blend of refined luxury and authentic Moroccan heritage. The service was truly exceptional; every staff member made me feel like a valued guest, paying close attention to every detail with warmth and professionalism. From the stunning riads to the serene gardens and the subtle scents throughout the spaces, everything was thoughtfully curated to create an unforgettable atmosphere.

reviews.author: Salma Aallam
reviews.text: Royal Mansour is undoubtedly a stunning property—everything from the architecture to the tranquil gardens is breathtaking. Our riad was absolutely gorgeous: beautifully designed, spacious, and full of character. The setting is serene and luxurious, offering a truly unique experience. However, the service unfortunately did not meet the high standards one would expect from a hotel of this level. The check-in experience felt underwhelming, lacking the warmth and attention to detail that typically defines a five-star welcome. During our stay, we were asked multiple times a day for our riad number—even when just walking through the gardens—which felt intrusive and disrupted the sense of privacy and relaxation. Room service was another letdown. I ordered a simple dish—chicken pasta with cheese and mushrooms—and instead received a whole chicken, a plain plate of pasta, and a separate cheese platter. It was confusing and disappointing, especially given the expectations of such a refined establishment. Overall, while the hotel itself is spectacular and the setting magical, the service needs serious refinement to truly live up to the Royal Mansour name.

reviews.author: Nicolas Liénart
reviews.text: Where to start… Service, beauty, luxury, personalized attentions, extremely good food, and so much more. A place to stay and go to. I got engaged here, so in addition to Al emotions, I was lucky enough to live this in such a gorgeous hotel. Do not miss this hotel, since it’s worth every single penny.

reviews.author: H Alkabi
reviews.text: From the moment you step into the Royal Mansour, you’re transported to a world of classical luxury and timeless elegance. We celebrated a friend’s birthday with afternoon tea, and it was truly an unforgettable experience. The atmosphere was outstanding — refined, peaceful, and full of charm. The staff were incredibly welcoming and hospitable, making us feel special throughout. The tea, coffee, and cakes were nothing short of heavenly — each bite a perfect blend of flavor and finesse. The gardens were absolutely magical, offering a serene backdrop that made the whole experience feel like a dream. We loved every moment and couldn’t have asked for a more beautiful setting to celebrate. A must-do in Marrakesh!

reviews.author: Cindy Cheng
reviews.text: If you want a delicious bowl of Moroccan Harira soup & don't mind eating at a truly local spot, this is the place. A perfectly spiced (but not spicy) soup with chickpeas, lentils, noodles, herbs & spices in a tomato based broth will hit the spot for 3 dhrms. You'll also get a sweet minty tea after you finish the soup. One of the highlights of my Morrocan food adventures 😃😋

reviews.author: charifa zemouri
reviews.text: Best place ever! I came here every morning for moroccan coffee with spices (ask for coffee without sugar). The harrira is absolutely amazing. You can have a coffee and a soup for less than 1 euro!!!

reviews.author: Håvard Anda Estensen
reviews.text: Get a bowl of porridge or soup from this hole-in-the-wall for a couple of dh. Locals hang out here.

reviews.author: Abi Curtis
reviews.text: Very cheap at 30 Dirhams a bowl, we ended up getting a second bowl

reviews.author: Ed Westerbeck
reviews.text: We stumbled onto this place as and unplanned dinner. We should have purchased a lottery ticket at the same time! The ambiance is incredible. Made new friends with the clientele. The staff was highly professional. There was engaging and skilled entertainment. The traditional Moroccan food beyond compare. Just go!

reviews.author: Wiby Setya Permana
reviews.text: We had only drunk on the rooftop with 3 glasses of non alcoholic drinks. The waiter gave us a free snack. Was so generous. Rooftop was quite nice but probably only 20% of it has the best view. I went also to the restaurant on the ground floor and i found the interior looked very authentic and interesting

reviews.author: J M
reviews.text: An unexpected gem tucked away. Small menu, sells alcohol. And we were provided with a plate of free tapas on arrival. Pretty rooftop vibes. Not the best spot if looking to catch the sun set.

reviews.author: Sasha Lewis
reviews.text: We visited this tucked away rooftop restaurant/bar a few times during our visit as it was by far the best out of all places we ate at. Ismail looked after us each time we went, recommending local food and wine. He was attentive without being overbearing, giving local recommendations and suggestions. The rooftop is spacious and airy, and the indoor lounge area is comfortable in what used to be a private house. We had a selection of local savoury pastries followed by a lamb dish with lentils and salad. All prepared and seasoned to perfection. The fig pudding is to die for. We truly recommend it.

reviews.author: Binta Onifade
reviews.text: My sister and I really enjoyed the foods here, it was finger licking good and delicious from the starters down to dessert and the staffs were very welcoming and attentive and the restaurant itself was inviting. The tempura prawns and chicken wings is not to be missed 😋

reviews.author: maya K
reviews.text: A beautiful architectural structure with an affordable entry fee for foreign tourists (100 MAD per adult). We visited in the morning when it was very quiet, which allowed us to take beautiful photos without crowds. An additional attraction is the majestic storks nesting around the walls.

reviews.author: Matt Moy
reviews.text: Arrived in the morning and there was no wait to enter. Unfortunately, I do not know French nor Arabic so I was unable to appreciate much of the information. There was also some construction ongoing as they seemed to be preparing for an event. This is one tourist attraction I wouldn't mind skipping in Marrakech.

reviews.author: Zach
reviews.text: The entrance is located in the north at the end of Rue de Berrima street. El Badi is a ruined Palace with only a handful of descriptions. It does contain a mini museum but the inscriptions are only in French and Arabic. Still enjoyable to wonder around the massive complex that was modeled after Alhambra in Spain. The only historical site in the city that I felt worth paying the $10 (100DH) to see.

reviews.author: Shaik Masood
reviews.text: Nothing much to see here, but well worth a walk around spending around 2hrs. Entry into the Palace is MAD100.0 which is a loot as there's nothing much to see inside except a pond and a small Museum with just a few artifacts. There is enough to see from the outside itself, save your money and get some good shots from outside itself.

reviews.author: Kamilla Luca Dávid
reviews.text: I would not recommend. Another place where they try to pull off some money of you. This area is under construction and of course you can walk around but it doesn’t worth the time. It was dirty, it was abandoned. In my opinion, you can’t really see any significant sight here. My marrakech experience wouldn’t be less without this part.

reviews.author: Beatriz
reviews.text: DANGER!!!!!!! Ve careful after 15p.m. the people is selling drug and they persecute and harass you and it was very scary. Only go in the morning! The most dangerous thing is to go to the Jewish cemetery and the narrow street that leads to the synagogue salat Alzama.

reviews.author: FarFar Tony
reviews.text: Are the negative comments here part of a scheme to keep this gem of tranquility undiscovered? Spent a week in Riad DarOne. Loved every minute. Walked the little streets. Ate the local food. Had a great time. Old white bloke and wife. Video on YT soon.

reviews.author: Zach
reviews.text: Wouldn’t walk in this area after the sun goes down. Let’s just leave it at that.

reviews.author: Dominik Stříbrný
reviews.text: Almost no tourists. I recommend getting lost in there

reviews.author: Barbara Rabelo
reviews.text: Sadly, felt super unsafe here especially if you’re a woman traveling on your own. I was with my boyfriend and still, it wasn’t a pleasant experience. Lots of scams too.

reviews.author: Ana Rita Correia
reviews.text: I recently stayed at Dar Rhizlane with my partner and we loved every single day! Absolutely stunning hotel, amazing architecture but most importantly, amazing, super friendly staff who made us feel super welcome! Super super polite and attentive to details! They made sure everything was perfect! The room was extremely clean, air conditioning on, an absolute oasis in the desert! The swimming pool is absolutely gorgeous! No words can describe how wonderful our stay was! Definitely recommend anyone who wants to have an amazing Moroccan experience to stay there! We’ll definitely be back! :)

reviews.author: Andrew Judge
reviews.text: We spent a week here and I have to say it is easily one of the best hotel experiences we have ever had. All the staff were so friendly and easy going, couldn't do enough for you. Food was delicious and we also enjoyed the entertainment a few evenings with dinner. Nice relaxed music and signing. Our room was just incredible. We felt like we were at home it was that comfortable. The room was air conditioned and as someone who is strict on cleanliness I can say every day it was immaculate. You are within walking distance to a lot of places but if you want, plenty of taxi's available right outside. I can easily recommend staying here, it is absolutely worth every penny and we will re-visiting in the future.

reviews.author: Michaelle G. Bonaccorso
reviews.text: Not dog friendly ! While all ten guests loved our puppy. Initially we asked prior to arriving. We were told its was ok, when we arrived and entered the restaurant area the manager came and said there are no animals allowed in the hotel.

reviews.author: Huda Zeitouni
reviews.text: We had dinner here and it was’t the best experience. The food wasn’t very good and the service was slow. Also, the meals were pricy with small quantity. However, the place is luxurious and the atmosphere was very elegant and nice!

reviews.author: Nils Buer
reviews.text: I booked the class and it was amazing. Everything was very good prepared. Each participant had his own gas cooking field. The Chef was also very skilled. I can highly recommend it.

reviews.author: Alexandru Dodoiu
reviews.text: Best coffee in the area. Good food and good service. It has tables inside and outside. You can smoke inside to. Great view of the Atlas mountains. Great prices. Loved the place.

reviews.author: Anna Silkina
reviews.text: Great! 5 from 5. We had coffee, fruits salad and tiramisu. 10 euros. The quality is good and the place is quite cozy, the waiter is a very nice guy who speaks English. There’s free WiFi and a lot of sockets to charge your gadgets. Just in front of the train station.

reviews.author: Joana Martinho
reviews.text: Good place for a drink and to enjoy the sun. The food was ok, good natural juices.

reviews.author: C Bnz
reviews.text: We ordered a Croque Monsieur to take away for our travel (3eu), it took them super long to bring it, then in the train we realized it was all burned ...

reviews.author: Asif Zubair
reviews.text: Very nice food. Fresh juices. Excellent environment. Friendly professional staff. Very reasonable prices. Very clean. Tasty fresh food. Beautiful scenic. Beautiful train station and royal theatre in front of you. Prices are comparatively better than the normal street takeaways.

reviews.author: Khalyl Bouzayène
reviews.text: Average

reviews.author: Ridha SAADAOUI
reviews.text: Pretty good overall.

reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Anis TOUMI
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Riadh Bizid
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Valencia McDuffy
reviews.text: Our girls trip to Marrakech was unforgettable! The hotel is beautiful and the food was delicious. I loved relaxing in the cafe & bar which was full of books, beautiful art (and rugs) and a gorgeous fireplace. From the first time we contacted the concierge until we left for our return flight, we received great care and service. Qualid was attentive, flexible, and accommodating. He understood our desire for a mix of relaxation, adventure, and cultural immersion, tailoring our itinerary to perfection. We had such a great time and enjoyed every moment!

reviews.author: Joelle Elkhoury
reviews.text: ✨ Overall Experience This resort is a true gem in Marrakesh. From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed into an atmosphere of calm, authenticity, and beauty. The entire place has a grounded, peaceful energy — it feels like an escape from time. If you’re looking for a space to reset, connect with nature, and enjoy meaningful hospitality, this is it. 🌿 Atmosphere & Nature The surrounding nature and garden are simply stunning — vibrant, serene, and clearly nurtured with love and care. Everything feels alive, fresh, and in harmony. Whether you’re wandering through the garden paths or just sitting quietly under a tree, or by the pools there’s a strong sense of calm that stays with you. 🌱 Sustainability One of the most impressive aspects of this resort is their commitment to sustainability. It’s clear the owners have gone to great lengths to build and maintain a place that respects the environment. From eco-conscious design to mindful daily practices, the sustainability focus adds real depth to the experience. It’s inspiring and rare. 🏡 Cleanliness & Comfort Every corner of the resort is impeccably clean and beautifully maintained. It’s fresh, airy, and comfortable in a way that feels effortless. There’s a genuine authenticity in the design that reflects Moroccan tradition without sacrificing comfort. 💛 Hospitality The owners are incredibly kind, warm, and attentive without ever being overbearing. Their care for the guests and the space is evident in every detail. You feel like a welcomed friend, not just a customer. 🍽️ Food The food was good and nourishing — fresh ingredients and a thoughtful presentation. While it may not have been the standout highlight of the stay for me, it was still enjoyable and in line with the calm, homegrown vibe of the place.

reviews.author: the della kit
reviews.text: Absolutely stunning and magical boutique hotel ! Everything is nourishing and intentional. As soon as we entered we felt so well taken care of. We book the pool and spa lunch. The food was healthy and delicious and from their own garden. The pool is saltwater and heated. The whole place was peaceful and tranquil and the staff were kind and accommodating. The cocktails and desert were amazing too !!! Highly recommend. Can’t say enough good things about this place !

reviews.author: Addi Dunn
reviews.text: I recently stayed at Jnane Tamsna in Marrakech, and it was truly unforgettable. This boutique hotel offers a perfect blend of luxury and tranquility. From the warm welcome to the attentive service, the staff made my stay exceptionally comfortable. The owner Meryanne was a delight and I enjoyed meeting her. The rooms beautifully combine traditional Moroccan decor with modern amenities, creating a cozy atmosphere. The gardens are a peaceful oasis, perfect for relaxation, and the pool area is a lovely spot to unwind. The only thing I didn’t like was there was 1 too many flies by the pool area but there are no mosquitoes which was great. Dining at the on-site restaurant, especially under the stars, was a memorable experience with delicious Moroccan cuisine. My favorite was the lamb chop, so delicious. Jnane Tamsna is a serene escape while still close to the city's vibrancy. I highly recommend it to anyone seeking a relaxing getaway. I can't wait to return!

reviews.author: Gail Robins
reviews.text: Jnane Tamsna is a wonderful boutique hotel about 20-30 minutes taxi ride from central Marrakesh. It’s not the hotel for you if you want 5star glitz but if you want quiet comfort, be surrounded by beautiful art and stylish decor this is the perfect place. Serving an expansive buffet breakfast , three course set lunch and dinner . All organic vegetables are grown on the property. Delicious. Nothing is too much trouble for the staff, always helpful and kind. Oualid the lovely concierge can arrange anything from a taxi to a cup of tea by a WhatsApp text. Overall a memorable stay enhanced by the staff and new friends that I made.

reviews.author: Matthew Guillory
reviews.text: I recently stayed at Riad Dar Anika, and I cannot recommend it enough. From start to finish, the experience was exceptional. The hospitality was top-notch—the staff made me feel right at home and truly went above and beyond. They arranged a fantastic private tour guide who spoke five languages and was clearly a local expert. I appreciated that he wasn’t pushing tourist traps; instead, he introduced me to authentic local shops in the souks just 5–7 minutes’ walk away. The airport pickup and return were seamless—organized directly by the hotel with thoughtful, timely communication. And wow—the breakfast was incredible. A delicious spread of traditional and modern options, and the iced coffee was unmatched. I completely echo other guests who praised the staff’s warmth and attention to detail. From a welcome tea at check-in to complimentary beverages and helpful suggestions, every interaction felt sincere. This is a place I’d confidently return to and recommend to anyone looking to experience true Moroccan hospitality in a beautiful, centrally located riad.

reviews.author: Prasiddha Halder
reviews.text: Had an amazing time at Riad Dar Anika with my husband and couldn’t have asked for a better experience. The hospitality here was amazing, breakfast was delicious with a diverse set of dishes and the location was spectacular. Very close to the main square and many great restaurants. I loved that this location was right outside the Medina which made it easily accessible by car. I want to give a shout out to the entire staff for making our stay amazing. When we checked in at 1 am we were provided tea and snacks while we waited for checkin. When we left we were provided a bagged lunch even though we didn’t ask for it. The room was very clean and whenever we asked they provided beverages on the house. Would highly recommend!

reviews.author: Helen Graves
reviews.text: After much research, we decided on Riad Dar Anika for a party of 5 couples to celebrate my husbands 60th birthday. We were collected from the airport and arrived at the Riad with welcome drink and food and a brief chat about the surrounding areas. Everything about this Riad was superb from the friendly staff who went out of their way to help, nothing was too much trouble, the traditional breakfast of soups, fresh fruit, eggs and pastries and the cleanliness of the whole Riad. Great location for walking around the souks and only a 20 minute ride to the airport. Would highly recommend.

reviews.author: Candi O.O
reviews.text: This was an absolutely amazing and unforgettable experience thanks to YouNes. He was so accommodating and kind providing us with tea pastries and dates upon arrival and even packing my group breakfast to go. I felt so welcomed and taken care of, and the hotel and rooms were absolutely beautiful. I couldn’t recommend YouNes and staying at this property more, I want to go back immediately. Thank you!

reviews.author: Andy Katz
reviews.text: We had a very pleasant stay at Dar Anika. The location is perfect for exploring and the staff couldn’t have been more helpful or friendly. The only comment I’d make is that the picture of the swimming pool is a little misleading - there is a small pool inside and a hot tub on the roof.

reviews.author: Muhammad Ali
reviews.text: Absolutely stunning. Photos don’t do it justice. It doesn’t really need a review but here are a few things that I hope might help. Entry was 100dh. Take cash. They weren’t accepting card when I went. I saw them turn people away. Go first thing and enjoy it while it’s empty. Weekday is better than weekend. If you see a group going in. Quickly get in front of them because trust me. They will ruin it for you. It will take around an hour or so to explore. Be respectful of people trying to take photos. If you see someone waiting for a shot. Don’t be an idiot and walk in front. Most important. Enjoy!

reviews.author: Rama
reviews.text: I went with my friend on a morning and there was a big queue but it took us less then 5 minutes to buy our tickets and enter. To say the least it was absolutely stunning and highly recommend that you best this historic site . The rooms were absolutely beautiful and jaw dropping. This must be on your bucket list

reviews.author: David Masters
reviews.text: Wonderful from start to finish, buy your tickets online, they are neither dated or timed. Entry was quick and efficient, I would go early, some of the courtyards are suntrap and will quickly get uncomfortable in the strong sunshine. The rooms and spaces are exquisite and beautiful.

reviews.author: A-S-K
reviews.text: We bought tickets on the day and there was a small queue but it was ok, it did get very busy when it got to around 1pm so best to go earlier. The palace was lovely but there is some construction that is still going on. Me and my sisters just wandered around the fascinating palace and took lots of great photos.

reviews.author: Aniik Gupta
reviews.text: Beautiful palace. Really intricate artwork on ceilings, doors and mosaic floors walls etc. Worth a visit. Could easily spend 2-3 hrs here. Not wheelchair accessible or people with mobility issues may struggle

reviews.author: Brandon Chang
reviews.text: Had an extraordinary experience at this hotel! The decor is immaculate -- truly one of the most beautiful properties I’ve ever encountered. The rooms are both spacious and elegantly appointed. Service is impressively swift; for instance, when I requested a toothbrush, it was delivered in just five minutes. Every staff member I met was exceptionally kind and eager to help. Plus, the hotel boasts some outstanding dining options. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Alexandre Choves
reviews.text: This was my very first stop in Marrakech, and starting my journey at Royal Mansour was nothing short of magical. The entire experience felt like stepping into a story from One Thousand and One Nights—a perfect blend of refined luxury and authentic Moroccan heritage. The service was truly exceptional; every staff member made me feel like a valued guest, paying close attention to every detail with warmth and professionalism. From the stunning riads to the serene gardens and the subtle scents throughout the spaces, everything was thoughtfully curated to create an unforgettable atmosphere.

reviews.author: Salma Aallam
reviews.text: Royal Mansour is undoubtedly a stunning property—everything from the architecture to the tranquil gardens is breathtaking. Our riad was absolutely gorgeous: beautifully designed, spacious, and full of character. The setting is serene and luxurious, offering a truly unique experience. However, the service unfortunately did not meet the high standards one would expect from a hotel of this level. The check-in experience felt underwhelming, lacking the warmth and attention to detail that typically defines a five-star welcome. During our stay, we were asked multiple times a day for our riad number—even when just walking through the gardens—which felt intrusive and disrupted the sense of privacy and relaxation. Room service was another letdown. I ordered a simple dish—chicken pasta with cheese and mushrooms—and instead received a whole chicken, a plain plate of pasta, and a separate cheese platter. It was confusing and disappointing, especially given the expectations of such a refined establishment. Overall, while the hotel itself is spectacular and the setting magical, the service needs serious refinement to truly live up to the Royal Mansour name.

reviews.author: Nicolas Liénart
reviews.text: Where to start… Service, beauty, luxury, personalized attentions, extremely good food, and so much more. A place to stay and go to. I got engaged here, so in addition to Al emotions, I was lucky enough to live this in such a gorgeous hotel. Do not miss this hotel, since it’s worth every single penny.

reviews.author: H Alkabi
reviews.text: From the moment you step into the Royal Mansour, you’re transported to a world of classical luxury and timeless elegance. We celebrated a friend’s birthday with afternoon tea, and it was truly an unforgettable experience. The atmosphere was outstanding — refined, peaceful, and full of charm. The staff were incredibly welcoming and hospitable, making us feel special throughout. The tea, coffee, and cakes were nothing short of heavenly — each bite a perfect blend of flavor and finesse. The gardens were absolutely magical, offering a serene backdrop that made the whole experience feel like a dream. We loved every moment and couldn’t have asked for a more beautiful setting to celebrate. A must-do in Marrakesh!

reviews.author: Chehrazad C
reviews.text: I went to the spa and it was great. The lady at the front desk was friendly and answered all my questions. I booked a time via email to make sure I could attend. The property is beautiful and the spa itself is very relaxing. The spa treatment was amazing and I’d definitely return. I also had lunch at the restaurant which was delicious. The waiters are very kind and accommodating. Thank you for such a nice afternoon.

reviews.author: May
reviews.text: Absolutely amazing. I have traveled the world and stayed at many well known luxury hotels. This trip I spilt my stay between Mamounia and La Sultana. Totally new experience for me feels like home it is absolutely gorgeous the vibes of the place are just magical feels like I have traveled in a Time Machine and lived in a beautiful mansion the restaurants and rooftop are something else and the food is fantastic. My husband and I had a very hard time leaving the place it was that good. Totally great place to take a vacation and just unplug a modern hectic life. Thank you to all the lovely and amazing staff who have made our stay magical. We can see and feel all the extreme to detail that has been offered in this hotel.

reviews.author: Jagojools
reviews.text: Amazing spa. If you want to experience a hammam treat this is the place! We had no idea what to expect. It was an incredibly relaxing hour long session. So good that we added a massage in too! We came away totally chilled and feeling so clean and refreshed.

reviews.author: Réka Kálló
reviews.text: A real 5 star experience in Marrakech. The quality of all the services, food, rooms, restaurants and pool are very high level, staff is kind and polite, everything is clean, so I can only recommend it. We even got a free upgrade upon arrival.

reviews.author: Anand Vasudevan
reviews.text: Review is for the spa. Went for the full treatment - royal spa and massage package. Wonderful relaxing experience in luxurious surroundings. The hotel interiors looked stunning, a collection of exceptionally luxurious riads.

reviews.author: Cindy Cheng
reviews.text: If you want a delicious bowl of Moroccan Harira soup & don't mind eating at a truly local spot, this is the place. A perfectly spiced (but not spicy) soup with chickpeas, lentils, noodles, herbs & spices in a tomato based broth will hit the spot for 3 dhrms. You'll also get a sweet minty tea after you finish the soup. One of the highlights of my Morrocan food adventures 😃😋

reviews.author: charifa zemouri
reviews.text: Best place ever! I came here every morning for moroccan coffee with spices (ask for coffee without sugar). The harrira is absolutely amazing. You can have a coffee and a soup for less than 1 euro!!!

reviews.author: Håvard Anda Estensen
reviews.text: Get a bowl of porridge or soup from this hole-in-the-wall for a couple of dh. Locals hang out here.

reviews.author: Abi Curtis
reviews.text: Very cheap at 30 Dirhams a bowl, we ended up getting a second bowl

reviews.author: Elisabeth
reviews.text: One of the best accommodations I’ve ever stayed in! It truly feels like stepping back in time — the breathtaking, authentic architecture is paired with discreet, high-quality service that never intrudes on your privacy. The Riad offers every facility you might need, and the food is equally exceptional. Located in the heart of the Medina, it provides an unexpected oasis of calm; once inside, the chaos of the souks simply fades away. I’d return in a heartbeat — and I don’t say that lightly.

reviews.author: Scott Moore
reviews.text: Lovely Riad! Very luxurious, staff very attentive, and just gorgeously decorated. Some very thoughtful touches, and very helpful in organizing things around the city. Breakfast on the roof was lovely, which you can do before the day gets too hot. Some nights had a live musician in the courtyard which was cool. Only thing to be wary of is a few charges adding up - there are no irons or steamers in the building so only option is to pay to send things out for ironing, and they have a sauna but it's US$17 to turn on.

reviews.author: Raiza Arnone
reviews.text: Five Stars – An Oasis of Luxury in the Heart of the Medina I absolutely loved my stay at Riad Kniza in Marrakech. Tucked away in the middle of the Medina—an area that can feel a bit gritty at first—the riad is a hidden gem. The exterior is unassuming, aside from its stunning, ornate wooden door, but the moment you step inside, you’re transported into paradise. The hospitality is truly exceptional—warm, attentive, and genuine. The entire place is impeccably clean and beautifully decorated with authentic period furniture that gives it a rich, elegant charm. Breakfasts were a daily highlight: fresh, flavorful, and served in a peaceful, gorgeous setting. Riad Kniza is a perfect blend of old-world beauty and modern comfort. I can’t wait to return!

reviews.author: Richard Lee
reviews.text: We were pleased to be able to stay at Riad Kniza even if it was just for one night. The hotel is ideally located in the centre of the city. It's a series of interlocking converted traditional Marrakesh houses. They have maintained the traditional architecture so there are some lovely courtyards and water features. Our room was large, extremely comfortable and quiet (and, in a nice touch, strewn with rose petals!) We chose to eat the fixed price dinner at the hotel. The meal was fabulous, although there was way too much food! Wine and beer are available. Breakfast is served, not a buffet, and was lovely although again there was too much to choose from.

reviews.author: Leon Doorn
reviews.text: This place definitely earns its 5-stars for everything. The building is beautiful, the staff is friendly, the rooms are great, the beds are superb and the place itself is a quite oasis amidst the busy streets of Marrakesh. It's a bit on the outer skirts of the Souk, however we found it a fun and nice route to walk to the central square (around 20 minutes). We would surely stay here again.

reviews.author: abdellah Guidir
reviews.text: They have a poor breakfast, I like the design of this place but services doesn't satisfied my needs

reviews.text: Bon service

reviews.text: The best place

reviews.author: niisa s.
reviews.text: Very pretty! But climbing it on the waterfall is too dangerous The restaurants along the waterfall are so pretty!!

reviews.author: amine bennani
reviews.text: Very beautiful landscape of tagines to eat well, carpets and sofas along the watercourse

reviews.author: Syed Ahmed Zaki
reviews.text: I tried there food several times. Food was tasty, specially the Rfissa chicken and Rice with Poulet. I also ordered vegetable and fruit salad. It was nice. Bit warm in the place if the weather is hot outside. They can keep a fan if possible.

reviews.author: Mike Chai
reviews.text: A little hole in the wall place, it is a superb restaurant with superb authentic Moroccan food. We ordered Chicken Pastilla, Beef Tajine, Chicken Rfissa, Beef Couscous, Lamb Rice. The Pastilla is so good, a mix of sweet, salty chicken and almond with a hint of cinnamon. The Chicken Rfissa was so tasty and tender, literally falling off the bones. Rice was very tasty but a bit hard, lamb was super tender. For the beef couscous, again very tasty but the couscous was a bit wet from the juice of the meat. The last dish beef vegetable tagine was tender and overflowing with the juices from the vegetables and beef. The bonus was the bread was soft and fluffy which went really well with the beef tagine soup.

reviews.author: Vladislava Kursheva
reviews.text: Great homemade simple food. Fresh and delicious. All the experience was like I went to a family house for dinner. Thank you for that authenticity.

reviews.author: Sameera Mushini
reviews.text: Hidden gem in Meknes among the tourist traps! Amazing food. Ordered Harira, Rfisaa chicken and mint tea. Everything was tasty. Best harissa and best mint tea so far. Aisha is a very welcoming host. The ambience is so warm and authentic. The washbasin is so pretty too!

reviews.author: Philipp Ziller
reviews.text: The food was so delicious & we came to the conclusion that this was one of the best traditional food we ate on our trip through Morocco!! Highly recommended :)

name: Restaurant Collier de la Colombe
address: Restaurant Collier de la Colombe, Meknes, Morocco

reviews.author: Lu Andy
reviews.text: nice roof bar restaurant with a good view. Food and service both good 👍

reviews.author: Mimi Menze
reviews.text: We was in the Restaurant and was not good. We was waiting long time for the food. There was only 10 guestes in the Restaurant. Orangejuce was not fresh and was very expensive, smal glas 4€. Meet in tagine was dry and we didnt get any excuse for the not good food. Also the smal mixed salad was realy smal

reviews.author: Karola Karlson
reviews.text: Perfect place for wine on the terrace. The bars usually recommended in Meknes were so dirty and dark that we didn't want to go inside. So we found this hotel restaurant with a perfect view that served wine and food with the average prices. If you're looking for a calm place to enjoy the view and have a dinner, you should definitely visit.

reviews.author: Pelú Yuyu
reviews.text: I can not say which dish I enjoyed the most, but for all that I ate, the prices were reasonable, the food was absolutely delicious, too bad we have to move on because I would definitely would go back there tomorrow, excellent experience, thank you so much!!!

reviews.author: BaSsma Meee
reviews.text: I did not like dealing there the place was not clean I hope that dealing with the customer will improve because he wants to be comfortable and the customer's comfort is the priority.

name: Restaurant Mille et Une Nuits
address: Restaurant Mille et Une Nuits, Meknes, Morocco

reviews.author: Vibrant_ Vagabond
reviews.text: A lovely multi-level restaurant with a rooftop terrace. I’m sure this is a drop off spot for tours but a good one. We met the recent new owner who was very appreciative of the positive guest remarks. Friendly & helpful servers. We enjoyed the terrace in the sun on a gorgeous afternoon in March. We enjoyed a lunch feast of Moroccan salad, Moroccan soup- Harira, lamb tagine with vegetables, lamb tagine with prunes, espressos, mint tea & a sweets assortment. Beautifully prepared dishes with excellent quality ingredients & the best lamb quality that we had in the region. Vegetables cooked to tenderness yet not soft mush as other dishes we had previously. Our lunch all together was 365MAD, beyond fair pricing for the quantity & quality we enjoyed. Highly recommend a stop.

reviews.author: Tricia L.
reviews.text: Fell in love with Moroccan hospitality because of this restaurant ♥️ The service was top notch, we were even served sweets on the house. The food was heart warming and scrumptious paired with reasonable pricing! Personally I would go for the pastilla and tajine, so good. The restaurant was accessible and was tidy with great views from the rooftop seating. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Eddie Lam
reviews.text: Tourist Trap! Restaurant to Avoid in Morocco! This restaurant serves 2 different menus, for the tourist one the price is doubled up with only 2 meal sets to choose! After I placed the order, I realised there was another menu. I asked the staff to bring me that menu, he was reluctant to do so and kept telling me that one was more expensive. I need to ask him for the menu again and I could eventually see that ordinary menu. Although the price was relatively high comparing with other local restaurants, that was a full menu with all single food items I can choose. The first one I got that had no choice and expensive! Finally, I decided to leave right away! It’s the shame on Morocco!

reviews.author: Alex Huiculescu
reviews.text: Awful experience: - only two things in the food menu. Both of them were mid - the waiter had no clue about serving - the table was dirty. Ofc the cutlery was placed directly on the already dirty table - they gave us the wrong coffee - from the three pieces of patisserie, one could break your teeth and another one had no taste - at the end, after we went to pay, they asked "xxx dirhams, no more no less?" They asked for a tip when 0 effort was given on their part. The pros were: - the coffee was good - the view was decent, but nothing special

reviews.author: petertje124
reviews.text: We had some crepes with cappuccino. Quality is very good, nice server. You are in a big city, so you pay more. Perfectly normal!

reviews.author: Freek Horsten
reviews.text: I have been here for lunch. I have a gluten allergy. They got me gluten-free bread, which was really friendly of them! The lunch was perfect, and the service is amazing!!!!!

reviews.author: Helma Kölgen
reviews.text: Delicious food, great service

reviews.author: Maxime
reviews.text: Very good food!! Good service!

reviews.author: Richard Houtzager
reviews.text: Nicely decorated (tourist) restaurant. Three-course menu. Food not very tasty/spicy but with the harissa that was served with it still reasonably tasty. Friendly staff.

reviews.author: Niels A
reviews.text: A tourist restaurant. Here you can try delicious Moroccan dishes. When you enter you enter a beautiful Moroccan building. Nicely decorated with different mosaics on the floor and on the walls. We got a 3-course menu. Especially eggplant with lentils and bread and a delicious 'dynamite'. The sambal is very tasty and quite spicy. This made the dish complete. The main course was a tajine with carrot, pumpkin, zucchini, couscous and beef from a broth. The dish had a lot of flavor. The dessert consisted of fresh fruit and a delicious mint tea that was poured in the traditional way.

reviews.author: Claire Furbush
reviews.text: What a wonderful experience! The Riad is absolutely beautiful, as well as a very quiet and restful experience. Fabulous location right in the Medina just minutes walking from the major sites. The breakfast was out of this world. Rashid was very welcoming and kind, and they arranged a fabulous trip to Volubilis and Moulay Idriss for just 500DH with Karim, who was a lovely guide and great driver. Can’t recommend highly enough!

reviews.author: Fem van der Rijst
reviews.text: We had a wonderful stay at Riad Bahia. We so loved our little room 'Sarah' upstairs on the roofterrace! It was hard to leave. Beautiful service and accommodation. We even had a 4 hour long tour through the medina of Meknes from owner Bouchra, which we also very much enjoyed. Don't believe the Lonely Planet when it tells you Meknes pales to Fez. Meknes is a friendly, interesting, safe and rich (non-touristic) city with a beautiful medina and lovely people.

reviews.author: Au H
reviews.text: We booked for yhe riad in the city center but they gave us the rooms in another riad far from the center. The riad was ok comparing with the rest of riads in Morocco. Thd breakfast was very poor and not enough for all the people

reviews.author: Lawrence Goodrich
reviews.text: Talk about a family affair! What a special place to stay. 👍🏻We were taken care of like we were part of the family. Great 1/2 day tour of the Medina 👍🏻and the most unbelievable cooking class we have taken 👍🏻. The location, accommodations were a real Moroccan experience, staying here is a must ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️.

reviews.author: natalie Addi
reviews.text: Very big and beautiful riad, super cozy and beautiful rooftop terrasse. Stayed here for one night. Staff is friendly. Breakfast wasnt the best we had on our trip but still good. Great location, close to all the sights. Clean rooms and great service. Thanks for a wonderful time!

reviews.author: Tom K
reviews.text: I’ve traveled to over 70+ countries and stayed in hundreds of hotels….and this place has got to be in my Top 5 for the best bang for your buck accommodation! The pictures of the rooms online don’t do this place a justice. It’s a stunning property with extremely friendly hosts/staff. Meknes is far better than Fes in my opinion and this Riad is the best!

reviews.author: Edmund
reviews.text: Royal treatment, This magnificent Riad take you back over 325 years , imagine yourself living with rules of Meknes, amazing interiors from walls to celling , clean rooms each suits different than the others , having every morning the tables ready for the guests to start there breakfast same as evenings and if you are large group better to talk to most welcome lady in the house the owner it make you feel at home, I really mean it , food prepared from fresh ingredients and very generous, fresh coffee brewed in front of you , every waiters very genuine and friendly, location close to all the shops I spend 9days as I was attending the expo Siam 2025 very convenient to reach the expo 7 km , very reasonable $ , well recommended,thanks for your warm hospitality, Morocco 🇲🇦 Australia 🇦🇺

reviews.author: Luca Zaninotto
reviews.text: Wonderful Riad in the ancient medina with big rooms, a lovely terrace with a view over the medina and a very nice pool. The house is beautifully decorated and the room where we stayed was very confortable. The breakfast and the dinner were tasty in a typical Maroccan style. The staff is very kind and eager to help you. We had a very lovely time there.

reviews.author: Kelly Fletcher
reviews.text: This was our favorite riad in Morocco. It’s located not too far from a Medina gate so not as much walking with luggage. The building was so fun to explore with little hallways that lead you into beautifully decorated sitting rooms and up stairs to multiple terraces. The staff are very friendly and helped us book a private taxi to Chefchouen. The bed wasn’t as comfortable but we enjoyed the double room overall with the large shower and good water pressure. Big, yummy breakfast!

reviews.author: Mary Judge
reviews.text: The entry is dark and makes you think you made a bad hotel choice. No one seemed in charge. Very nice garden space and dining area in the truly lovely interior, ground floor. The Rhiad is a warren of often narrow and steep stairways that may not be appropriate for those with mobility issues. We had a large quiet room with beautiful ceiling. The pretty bathroom was up 3 stairs, a bit dangerous at night and had a strong odor of the sewer so we kept the door closed. Our beds were left unmade and the room could have been cleaner. Breakfast was all carbs, not great, and the place seemed understaffed, the manager overworked. The Wi-Fi was totally uneven throughout the premises. However it is also a bargain hotel.

reviews.author: Ian Fitzpatrick
reviews.text: A lovely traditional Riad with tiled walls etc. nice room with good hot shower and heater +aircon. Helpful and kind host Hassan took us to have a good harira soup and helped us with directions. Lovely breakfast. All good!

reviews.author: Customer
reviews.text: What a great find. Hassan is so knowledgeable, friendly and helpful. The Riad is easy to find from the car park and has wonderful & authentic rooms, terrace and the breakfast is excellent and filling. The cost is very reasonable for what you get and is in the top 3 riads we have stayed in Morocco and we have stayed in many. Within easy walking distance from the medina and shopping areas and Hassan as soon as you arrive shows you a map to keep with all the locations of interest. Thank you again Hassan for your hospitality.

reviews.author: 單單
reviews.text: best riad we had in morocco! friendly staff with simple city guide. location: great if you’re driving, parking is nearby with very clear guidance, however since the road to riad is narrow and bumpy, suitcases are not recommended. room: we stayed 5 riad in different city in morocco, at this price range it is expected to be: 1. some furniture/equipment might be broken but still usable. 2. sandy floor. 3. breakfast with no protein. however in this riad only got 2 where all equipment works just fine so we’re happy. dining: great breakfast and even better dinner! very reasonable price and great service, if planning to have in-riad dining, do it here!

reviews.author: Stuart Forsyth
reviews.text: Charming Riad, lovely owners, super roof terraces and all in all probably the best Riad we stayed in while visiting Morocco. Wouldn't fault a thing

reviews.author: Jeff N
reviews.text: Fantastic hospitality and food. The hosts Mouna and Simon are wonderful, and readily share their enthusiasm for Meknes. They helped us with tips for seeing the sights, dining and shopping in town.

reviews.author: Ismail Boushabi
reviews.text: Dear reader, I have been visiting this Riad since very long time, it is absolutely magnificent and very beautiful. I also bring my business guests to this Riad everytime I have the chance to drink coffee, eat something and of course to introduce them to the Moorish/Andalusian architecture. Yesterday, while having with me an off duty business delegation, we were denied entry, I was surprised about the fact that we couldn't sit, enjoy a drink and maybe eat something while the whole restaurant empty was, literally nobody was there. It hurts me a lot to give you 1 star, but the way we have been treated yesterday is absolutely not appropriate. I urge the management team to reflect on this, you have always been loyal, so I am I. Kind regards, Ismail

reviews.author: Mark Sneddon (Marcosolotravels)
reviews.text: Fantastic stay for a night in this hotel. The staff were very accommodating and they even upgraded our room. The room was spacious and clean. The breakfast offered was also good.

reviews.author: Mohammed Herzallah
reviews.text: The reception and the building is the only good thing. I was really sad to discover that the water in the toilets doesn't work in a good way. I could not take a shower during my stay and I had to move out of the riad even i had payed one more day. Breakfast is mini and not prepared. It is not five stars. It's ok to have this level in Marocco but please don't claim 5 stars. To mention Younes and the guide is amazing also the lady who work at the reception.

reviews.author: KAREN TAYLOR
reviews.text: We stayed here as part of a small group tour and I will start with the positives. The staff are lovely, the downstairs is beautiful and the roof terrace comfortable. The claiming of a 5 star is however way off. The beds are so so hard and without mattress protection, you are sleeping on the last guest‘s body fluids. The showers are held together with plumbers tape, with showerheads falling off and taps coming undone at the slightest touch. The showerscreen doesn’t reach the floor, so any water you do get sprays out onto the floor. Toiletry offerings are packeted pieces of soap or magazine sachet shampoo. Coming to breakfast the next day, well I sat on a broken chair, so that didn’t help. Very basic breakfast offers for this 5 star. Maintenance and attention to detail is the key here. This could be a very special Riad in the middle of very average 3 star Riads and unfortunately that is what Riad Ritaj currently is.

reviews.author: W NKS
reviews.text: Supposed to be a nice place but that just didn’t add up the valued. Beautiful place with no hospitality in mind, staff practically shouting or rising voice when they talk each other, drying blanket and other rooms utilities at the balcony is just not something you would see in other hotel , unless on my 25 years of traveling experience. Imagining siting having breakfast and the staff dusting or carrying duster without cover with of course full of dust isn’t a pretty sight let alone hygiene On staff service isn’t even better except probably the receptionist the others just as slow as snails can be. Cleaning table for breakfast is just too painful to watch

reviews.author: Less sweet
reviews.text: Not all items on menu are made available. Waited quite long 30min for food (Friday 3pm) but tasty (spicy kafta targine) & nice panoramic rooftop view & welcoming service.

reviews.author: Diane Germann
reviews.text: We had lemonade drinks and ate chicken, tomato salad, and bread on the upper terrace. They even brought us additional veggies and olive for free. The view was spectacular but just a bit cold for dinner. I would recommend it!

reviews.author: StayCentral Business
reviews.text: Ignore the local restaurant ratings on Wanderlog. We stayed in Meknes for two weeks and they placed Selma at 18. Rubbish. It is one of the best for free tapas, the food, location, views, comfort and service. Others listed near the top didn’t deserve to be there because they didn’t serve much tapas or at all, or the ambiance and the food was really ordinary. And we tried lots of them. We ended up eating at Selma’s several times. They do a great job of looking after you.

reviews.author: siham alahyane
reviews.text: I had a wonderful stay at the riad Selma which is in the center of the medina close to everything.i spent only 2 nights (if i could stay more i would definitely do it but it was my last 2 days of vacation)the communication was fluent from the booking until the end.the guy who i met in the reception who manage the riad (called Mohamed)was really friendly and all ears,he gave me the most important information i could need,the breakfast was yummy in a beautiful cosy terrasse.if i could come back to Meknes i would definitely come at this riad Selma.i highly recommend it!!

reviews.author: Brett Adamek
reviews.text: We were recommended this restaurant by a local, and honestly it was a breath of fresh air. Tasty food. Reasonable price...and a great view of Meknes.

reviews.author: MarLies Hofstede
reviews.text: Breakfast is excellent, very nice staff. Public Parking in front to pay in advance 20 drh per day. Compared to dutch prices 🤯 we can live with this just fine. The room 3 stars because there is no door to the toilet/ bathroom. Sometimes tourists get sick 😳 and thank god we didn’t. We had room 6, I think the smallest but ok for us. One point of attention: the waterpressure. Try to shower as the first one in the morning or in the afternoon. Our shower hardly gave cold water so the water was way too hot. One disadvantage of all riads: windows face the open area in the middle so keep windows closed for privacy. The rooftop terras is large and nice but at this moment too hot to be. The little pool is undeep but nice to cool off. Although it was a bit dirty with leaves and insects because of the hard wind. Circulation pomp was off. But very charming and nicely decorated riad on a central location.

reviews.author: Maria Rosario
reviews.text: Big clean comfortable room. Good service. Only thing to point out is that it was a little bit noisy with street noises outside.

reviews.author: Daniel Rodriguez Sanz
reviews.text: Rooms are ok. Be carefoul the parking is not free even if the hotel tell you to park there.

reviews.author: sébastien balzer
reviews.text: Wonderful stay, excellent location, great staff who made everything possible to satisfy ourselves (they even call the pool company to open it again for my son while it was supposed to be closed since 1 week), we were upgraded (senior suite instead of junior suite). Great meals including breakfast. Thanks a lot to the whole team!

reviews.author: SAM AFC (Morocco)
reviews.text: Very nice place, with an extraordinary decorations, the rooms were cosy and the air conditions is just a mess. They should be careful and tell people that there are no AC in the rooms or it's far from the bedroom. Otherwise, the Riad on the photos are totally different from what appears in the photos. The staff is amazing and very friendly.

reviews.author: Robyn Sheather
reviews.text: Excellent tradition Riad, central location within the souks, close to Place Lahdim. Extremely clean, the ladies work very hard. Great quadruple room to fit our family of four. The cool pool is an added bonus and a nice space to relax. Homemade breakfast was delicious and there was ample choice. Staff always had a smile and willing to help with our needs. A special thanks to Said for his hospitality. Would definitely recommend, you won’t be disappointed.

reviews.author: Anouar Hatem
reviews.text: It was an unparallelled experience in Riad in the heart of the old city of Meknes, where they received us in the best way and gave us tea and some local sweets. They were very nice to us from all respects of information and suggestions. I forgot the thing that surprised me about Riad is that it is a museum of wood indirectly. We thank them very much for their hospitality. We hope to visit them soon.

reviews.author: Ioana Mitu
reviews.text: Very clean, traditional design, hot water, good price. A bit cold if you go in winter but they have air conditioner and warm blankets! As well home made products for the breakfast that is usually included in price of room. Plus lovely terrace with view over the city.

reviews.author: Aleksandra Marković
reviews.text: The rooms are very big and clean and were also heated. The position is pretty good, in the old Medina, but right next to the Mosque, so you will hear the singing of muezzin pretty well. Breakfast was nice, the staff spoke terrible English, but did their best to do the communication. All in all, very good deal for the price!

reviews.author: Giusy Musarò
reviews.text: Nice Riad in Meknès, calm and comfortable. We took a four bedroom room with private toilet. Everything was clean and the toilet quite spacious. We enjoyed the breakfast included and the terrasse.

reviews.author: Parin Kothari
reviews.text: The newly refurbished gates are the very best in Morocco. Across from the gates are a line of local eateries that are awesome to sip tea and take in every detail of the gates as time flows

reviews.author: Franjo Janeš
reviews.text: Still under construction, but you can get a good glimpse of its glory. It will be fabulous when finished.

reviews.author: said ait bajja
reviews.text: 5 Stars – An Unforgettable Desert Experience! Staying at Merzouga Paradise Luxury Camp was truly the highlight of our trip to Morocco! From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with warmth and genuine hospitality. The tents were spotless, beautifully decorated, and surprisingly comfortable—with real beds, private bathrooms, and even hot showers! The food was absolutely delicious—freshly cooked Moroccan dishes served under the stars by the campfire. The camel ride at sunset through the golden dunes was magical, and the Berber music around the fire at night created memories we’ll never forget. What really sets this place apart is the team. They treated us like family, always checking if we needed anything and sharing their culture with pride. We felt safe, relaxed, and completely disconnected from the noise of the world. If you’re looking for a peaceful, authentic, and luxurious desert experience—this is the place. Highly recommend it to anyone visiting Merzouga!

reviews.text: The square was empty, nothing was going on. A walked through the souk on the left-hand side of the square and visited the Dar Jamai - National Museun of Music, located at the square's back wall. There was nothing exciting for me, but others may find it fascinating. However, when you turn around, you'll see the Bab El Mansour Lellej - famous gate.

reviews.text: A memorial monument of ismailian city meknes, where various people show off their talents (singers, comedians, musiciens...)

reviews.author: Rasheed TK
reviews.text: Lahdim Square in Meknes is a perfect for soaking in local culture. The square is filled with street vendors, cafes, and shops, offering a variety of goods and local foods. It's a great spot to relax and watch the lively activities around. The architecture and atmosphere provide a charming glimpse into the heart of Meknes.

reviews.author: Hamza Skalli
reviews.text: Very good place i enjoy my time here.

reviews.author: Ana Hi
reviews.text: Meknes Meknes is a lesser-known imperial city with beautiful gates, royal stables, and a more laid-back charm than Marrakech or Fes. It’s perfect for those seeking history without big crowds.

reviews.author: kaira kaplinsky
reviews.text: The most magical Blue City in the world! Bucket list for all! The best time to explore without crowds is early morning right after sunrise. greeting sunsets at the Spanish mosque is a must, although be prepared for bugs😩😁

reviews.author: Nazim Lala
reviews.text: This is a beautiful town with very hospitable people. There aren't many sellers / hawkers constantly pestering you too but their wares, so you can really enjoy your stroll through town. We went later in the day when it cooled down a bit and there were fewer people in the streets.

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. Chefchaouen is a must-visit for photographers, art lovers, and anyone looking to experience Morocco’s laid-back and artistic side. Whether you’re exploring the picturesque alleys, enjoying a mint tea in a cozy café, or watching the sunset from a hilltop, every moment here feels magical.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: Beautiful city! I love the colors, the people, the food and most importantly the shops on the street😍 If you want to get away to the mountains for some peaceful time away from the city, I highly recommend spending two or three days in Chefchaouen!

reviews.author: Mourad Chafik
reviews.text: Chefchaouen’s medina is truly one of the most beautiful and peaceful places I’ve ever visited. The blue-washed walls, narrow alleys, and stunning doors create a dreamlike atmosphere that feels both relaxing and inspiring. Locals are friendly, the shops offer authentic handmade crafts, and there are plenty of cozy cafes to enjoy traditional Moroccan tea. It's the perfect place to wander without a map, discover hidden gems, and take amazing photos at every corner. Whether you're there for the colors, the culture, or just the peaceful vibe—Chefchaouen is unforgettable

reviews.author: Said Belowahed
reviews.text: Rabat is an amazing city to visit, There is a lot of places to see and enjoy, Hassan tower is an amazing place with the Shrine next to it, and view to river. The Mausoleum of Mohammed V is a mausoleum located on the opposite side of the Hassan Tower, on the Yacoub al-Mansour esplanade in Rabat, Morocco. It contains the tombs of the Moroccan king and his two sons, late King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah. The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah in Rabat, Morocco. It is located at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river opposite Salé. The Chellah or Shalla, is a medieval fortified Muslim necropolis located in the metro area of Rabat, Morocco, on the south side of the Bou Regreg estuary. The Phoenicians established a trading emporium at the site.

reviews.author: Jose Tavares
reviews.text: I really liked this medina, very little touristy and essentially frequented by the inhabitants of Rabat. while walking its streets I learned a lot about local habits. Inside the medina are some good restaurants, so you have to ask them why they are difficult to find. Medina very safe

reviews.author: Monsignore Catweasel
reviews.text: big old medina where you can buy a lot of different things. Mobile phones from all brands. Alot of different brands clothes shoes . Also in the have a nice food to get many meals and spices fom fastfood to cousine . There also many free shops where you buy anything handmade .

reviews.author: Ross Daniels
reviews.text: This is an absolutely fantastic place a bit of a labyrinth but so enjoyable with winding streets and multiple marketplaces and plenty of cafes and eating spots. Great atmosphere and one of the streets will take you down to the beach. We spent hours just wandering around and it’s up there with any marketplace in Morocco.

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: This has got to be the best souk in Morocco! I’ve been to many, but Essaouira’s felt so special. I spent about five hours there and still didn’t want to leave. Each shop has its own unique vibe, and the shopkeepers were incredibly kind and helpful. Every time I asked where to find something, they wouldn’t just point me in the direction—they’d actually walk me there and leave without the other shopkeepers noticing. It was such a genuine experience. You’ll find everything from handmade Moroccan teapots and beautiful tea glasses to breathtaking paintings and handmade rugs, linen clothing, genuine leather goods, and the most fragrant spices. If you’re looking for authentic treasures, this is the place!

reviews.author: S.A.A.
reviews.text: It seemed like a decent restaurant. But in the end, there was that disgusting sign on the bathroom door, that shows a man peeking at a woman using the toilet . Apparently, for Moroccan men, this is funny and amusing. But for a woman, such signs are offensive, cause anxiety, and are very upsetting. I sympathize with local women for having to deal with this kind of attitude. I hope you never find yourself in the situation depicted on that sign. And I wish the restaurant to go out of business.Don’t embarrass yourselves—change the bathroom sign.

reviews.author: Anthony Goodwin
reviews.text: Absolutely loved our visit here. Very nice local food options. Amazingly friendly staff that showed us the history of the place. Tagine was excellent. Best the whole trip. Would come back

reviews.author: J Who?
reviews.text: Tourist prices for decent food. Ordered the moussaka and duck confit which were tasty but expensive. Service was ok as it was clear the waiter did not want to be there.

reviews.author: Jonathan H
reviews.text: If you like a glass of wine with your meal then as far as we could ascertain this is the only restaurant in town, outside of the big hotels, that serves alcohol. Service was excellent. Food was in the hearty / comfort style category - a mixture of Greek and Moroccan. Be careful choosing your wine, there are some horrors on the list, but also some nice ones.
