name: La Kasbah des Sables
address: La Kasbah des Sables, Ouarzazate, Morocco

reviews.author: Arabella Poxon
reviews.text: I am so sad that this place doesn’t get any recognition! It is such a gorgeous place, truly a hidden gem. There is a man sat at the door ready to walk you in (may seem like you’re in the wrong place at the beginning due to it being in a low-lit small road) The service is amazing! The waiter is so attentive and cares truly to make the service the best for you. He is by himself, therefore it may be a bit slow, however this isn’t a fast-food restaurant anyway. He made sure we were warm and comfortable the whole time. Super friendly! The food is lovely too. Great portion sizes, gorgeous bowls, great seasoning. Nothing bad to say about it! In regards to the pricing, I think it is very valid for what you get (bare in mind it is higher prices, it isn’t a place for budget meals). The ambiance is top notch. Great music, super relaxing and gorgeous!! Wouldn’t go anywhere else for dinner apart from this restaurant during my stay.

reviews.author: Radia
reviews.text: One of the best restaurants in Ouarzazate city, I highly recommend it ❤️ The atmosphere is amazing, very calm and suitable for couples, family and friends. It’s an amazing place to enjoy a calm dinner or to celebrate a special occasion… It makes my heart warm knowing that I can enjoy my meal in peace, the music playlist is worth to mention as it makes the atmosphere more pleasant ❤️ I can recommend the dishes they have to everyone I know, but I wish there will more options to choose from in the future :) I tried Pasta with chicken and mushrooms 🍄 and it was delicious, I also tried grilled meat with vegies, my opinion about it was medium but definitely not bad ❤️❤️ The cheese cake was my best part ever🤭🤭 I absolutely enjoyed every piece of it 🫠 For the service, the guys I interacted with was very professional and kind ❤️ Thank you for making me enjoy and I will definitely be back every time I’m visiting Morocco 🙏🏼🥰 See you soon,

reviews.author: Emilie Gibney
reviews.text: A hidden gem in Ouarzazate - I recommend parking on the Main Street and then walking down the small streets to get there. Will not disappoint! Brilliant local and “foreign” cuisine. The decoration and style was beautiful and service great - highly recommend to anyone stopping through the area

reviews.author: Martin Hills
reviews.text: We chose this based on some other people's reviews and photographs and were delighted with what we found. The restaurant is at the end of a very nondescript street but as you step inside you're in a beautiful setting which is done just right. The quality of the dishes we ordered were of a high standard and generous. Tables are placed well apart so you can have a discrete conversation and not be bothered by other guests. A good price for the quality of the food we were served.

reviews.author: Naphat Yothataradol
reviews.text: Best meal in Morocco so far. Good food, great service. free parking. Accept credit card.

name: La Rose des Sables
address: La Rose des Sables, Ouarzazate, Morocco

reviews.author: Marina Thaler
reviews.text: Amazing place and food. We ordered vegetable soup, vegetable tagine, a portion of homemade French fries and the best orange juice - everything was super tasty. The owner is very friendly, prices are unbearable. I guess you will never a restaurant here without an amazing cup of tea :)

reviews.author: Sascha Kesseler
reviews.text: FAKE REVIEWS. Unfortunately, we got tricked by the great reviews here. It's impossible that 1000 people rated this restaurant, let alone positively. The food is sub-par. Already after getting the olives we knew it was a mistake to go there. Only positive about this place is the owner who was very sweet.

reviews.author: Petr Weiss
reviews.text: Nice place to visit, opened for lunch even during Ramadan. The staff was nice and understand English. The tajin was ready to eat but we ordered something else, the preparation took about 45mins. Pizza was very tasty, burger and fries nice, the rest very good.

reviews.author: Ryan Norris
reviews.text: Wonderful experience! Beautiful restaurant and friendly staff. The food is obviously magnificent

reviews.author: Andy Brian
reviews.text: Had a burger and fries, which as others have said, was very fresh and didn't try to copy American burgers - it was unique and tasty. Left very full and also thoroughly enjoyed the Moroccan tea I was served.

reviews.author: Nicole Bell-Levy
reviews.text: I have to give this a 4 star rating only because I believe they are overcharging in the bar area, to the point where I wouldn't go back to the bar again. I paid $22 Eros for one drink. The rest of the stay was very good. The rooms are beautiful, very clean and larger than any of the other hotels we stayed in over our 2 weeks in Morocco. The pool was too cold to swim in, but it was beautiful to sit by and read in the sun.

reviews.author: M U
reviews.text: This is truly a 5 stars hotel and we had best time staying there and their food is exceptionally good too . The rooms are well designed and spaced and their staff is most hospitable and very attentive.

reviews.author: Karan Capoor
reviews.text: Our suite itself was quite nice. However, you have to climb up dark, narrow stairs with timer switch. Lobby and other public indoor areas including the lobby and restaurants were drafty and freezing. Speaking of restaurants, the breakfast was exceptionally weak and avoidable - less than 1 star. Stale fruits, white bread, unlabeled dishes, very inattentive or absent service. Only redeeming feature of the breakfast was the lady at the omelet station. Avoid.

reviews.author: S G
reviews.text: We had lunch in the Italian restaurant. The lobby is welcoming, and the garden with pool very beautiful. The food was delicious, we had pizza and pasta. The staff listened to our vegetarian wishes. Couldn't have been better, thank you 🙏🏻

reviews.author: Marla T
reviews.text: The highlight of the room was the enormous bathroom. The lobby is absolutely spectacular with props from movies. There is only one staff member in the spa; so if you want a massage, there will be interruptions. The breakfast buffet was woefully understaffed. Overall, the food at breakfast and at dinner was good, but not great.

name: Le Relais Saint Exupéry
address: Le Relais Saint Exupéry, Ouarzazate, Morocco

reviews.author: Brie Cosma
reviews.text: Fantastic experience!! The owner/chef was so warm and friendly. Very happy to offer vegetarian options for us. The vegetable couscous was the best Ive ever had! So much flavour and love in the cooking. The bread was homemade and again the best Ive ever had in Morocco. The chef even shared his recipe with us. I highly highly recommend this restaurant!

reviews.author: Wojciech Słowik
reviews.text: I really recommend to visit this restaurant. Very nice owner who cook delicious food. We order a camel and goat dish - both were fantastic.

reviews.author: David O'Dwyer
reviews.text: Brahim is kind, patient and very trusting. A gentleman. Food very tasty and good value.

reviews.author: Oliver Mohr
reviews.text: Really great Cook. He does everything himself from cooking to taking orders and cleaning the dishes. Hard working man with great skills. He also told us about saint exupery and his Story. 10/10 would recommend.

reviews.author: Shelley McDonald
reviews.text: Had a wonderful meal at this cozy restaurant.The chef, who was also our server, has a wonderful way of combining great flavours and presenting an elegant meal. We ordered lamb and the serving was quite large-large enough to be comfortably shared between two of us. This restaurant also offers wine. Not to be missed if you find yourself in the area.

reviews.author: Piotr Sosiński
reviews.text: Authentic food, nice view from the terrace and very friendly and attentive service. The Moroccan (goat milk) yoghurt was a tasty surprise!

reviews.author: Kimberley Howarth
reviews.text: We were recommended this restaurant. And it definitely did not disappoint! It is a very attractive restaurant, parking is very easy in the compound nearby. The waiters and staff were all very pleasant, most spoke excellent English. We ordered a Moroccan salad with argan oil, and foie mchermel (marinated liver) as starters. We also ordered a camel tagine, and baby goat tagine as our mains, as recommended on numerous other reviews. Service is quite sleepy as it seems they are a very small crew in a very big space. And when we arrived, it was really quite full. The restaurant seating spans 2 floor, with the kitchen on the ground floor. So they (2 waiters) are actually running up and down 3 floors to serve and attend to everyone! We sat indoors at the rooftop as it was too cold to sit outside on the terrace. It is a very cosy and inviting space. We did have to wait almost 2hrs for our food as the place was just completely packed... I perhaps would not recommend coming here if you are in a hurry. But it was absolutely worth the wait for us. Everything was really special and unique. The foie was really well prepared, buttery and flavourful. Both tagines were delicious with a rich sauce... probably the best tagine I have had my entire trip! And the argan oil in the Moroccan salad was also a very special touch. It was a very enjoyable dinner for us indeed and worth the trip. The prices are also very fair and reasonable. I can totally see why they are so very popular!

reviews.author: Barbara Madar
reviews.text: Went for a sunset dinner as it has a roof top overlooking the main square. Food was good! Very generous portions. Recommend the tagine and the orange cinnamon at the end. Service needs some working as they are either too busy to serve the 3 floor restaurant or it is just a bit too slow. You will need to wait for initial service and after between all courses.. the view compensates tho.

reviews.author: jonathan hammer
reviews.text: Really nice place with attentive waiters. A go to location for tourists. The menu offers specialty items like goat (which was delicious with figs and dates) and camel. The vin Gris was surprisingly tasty. The waiters work hard in several languages. The place really makes an effort. We ate here twice.

reviews.author: Skye L
reviews.text: Incredible experience! Our server Naim was very friendly, welcoming, and attentive. Food was incredibly flavorful, plentiful, and affordable. Best vegetable couscous with caramelized onions we’ve had in Morocco! I also recommend the Berber omelet. Restaurant also has a nice view and good indoor and outdoor seating options. Highly recommend this restaurant!

reviews.author: Arabella Poxon
reviews.text: I am so sad that this place doesn’t get any recognition! It is such a gorgeous place, truly a hidden gem. There is a man sat at the door ready to walk you in (may seem like you’re in the wrong place at the beginning due to it being in a low-lit small road) The service is amazing! The waiter is so attentive and cares truly to make the service the best for you. He is by himself, therefore it may be a bit slow, however this isn’t a fast-food restaurant anyway. He made sure we were warm and comfortable the whole time. Super friendly! The food is lovely too. Great portion sizes, gorgeous bowls, great seasoning. Nothing bad to say about it! In regards to the pricing, I think it is very valid for what you get (bare in mind it is higher prices, it isn’t a place for budget meals). The ambiance is top notch. Great music, super relaxing and gorgeous!! Wouldn’t go anywhere else for dinner apart from this restaurant during my stay.

reviews.author: Radia
reviews.text: One of the best restaurants in Ouarzazate city, I highly recommend it ❤️ The atmosphere is amazing, very calm and suitable for couples, family and friends. It’s an amazing place to enjoy a calm dinner or to celebrate a special occasion… It makes my heart warm knowing that I can enjoy my meal in peace, the music playlist is worth to mention as it makes the atmosphere more pleasant ❤️ I can recommend the dishes they have to everyone I know, but I wish there will more options to choose from in the future :) I tried Pasta with chicken and mushrooms 🍄 and it was delicious, I also tried grilled meat with vegies, my opinion about it was medium but definitely not bad ❤️❤️ The cheese cake was my best part ever🤭🤭 I absolutely enjoyed every piece of it 🫠 For the service, the guys I interacted with was very professional and kind ❤️ Thank you for making me enjoy and I will definitely be back every time I’m visiting Morocco 🙏🏼🥰 See you soon,

reviews.author: Emilie Gibney
reviews.text: A hidden gem in Ouarzazate - I recommend parking on the Main Street and then walking down the small streets to get there. Will not disappoint! Brilliant local and “foreign” cuisine. The decoration and style was beautiful and service great - highly recommend to anyone stopping through the area

reviews.author: Martin Hills
reviews.text: We chose this based on some other people's reviews and photographs and were delighted with what we found. The restaurant is at the end of a very nondescript street but as you step inside you're in a beautiful setting which is done just right. The quality of the dishes we ordered were of a high standard and generous. Tables are placed well apart so you can have a discrete conversation and not be bothered by other guests. A good price for the quality of the food we were served.

reviews.author: Naphat Yothataradol
reviews.text: Best meal in Morocco so far. Good food, great service. free parking. Accept credit card.

reviews.author: Pavan Simone
reviews.text: I need to say that the restaurant view is stunning as you can look over the bay to the Spanish Coast. Food and service are great level and a special thanks to the high professional, caring and kind service of Ms. Hanna. She welcomes guests with high level approach. My favorite place to dine

reviews.author: Mohammad Ashkanani
reviews.text: One of the worst experiences ever. The food taste was not good at all and the selection on the buffet was limited. Service was bad the never cleaned my table and they didn't asked me if I need anything to drink. Even the napkin on the table was used with lipstick marks.

reviews.author: Thuraya Al Harthy
reviews.text: The atmosphere is amazing, you can see all of Tangier from the top. The Morocco food is very delicious but the international food was fine. I really recommend this place as u don't really find good places around

reviews.author: Alan Mackinnon
reviews.text: What I call the mushroom soup was excellent and then I had really fresh vegetable plate and chicken couscous and finished with a chocolate dessert

reviews.author: Ivan Rostotski
reviews.text: We were on tour and stayed at the Hilton. Dinner and breakfast were included. Dinner was a set menu that included a great salad and the main course was a very good orange chicken confet. Service very polite and the servers do speak good English and Spanish. The breakfast was a buffet and I loved that their was Morrocan dishes to try. Service again was very good

reviews.author: Chunk Monk
reviews.text: A great place with a nice vibe, friendly service , great food and drinks. I especially love terras with its big trees and local people. The owner is a friendly person who gives every customer attention. Love this place!

reviews.author: Dobak Robert
reviews.text: La Renaissance offers an unforgettable culinary journey through Morocco. From the moment we walked in, we were welcomed with warm hospitality and an inviting atmosphere filled with the scent of exotic spices. Every dish we tried was bursting with authentic flavor — the tagine was perfectly seasoned, the couscous light and fluffy, and the mint tea was the best we’ve ever had. The décor and music added to the experience, making us feel like we were transported straight to Marrakech. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy delicious Moroccan cuisine in a refined setting. We’ll definitely be back!

reviews.author: Michał Urbanowicz
reviews.text: Awesomeness is the word for today dinner. Great greetings to the Cook 🍳 Great service as well! High recommendation for tagine omelet and chicken, tea also 👌 No beef and lamb at Ramadan.

reviews.author: Optimus Prime transformer
reviews.text: Located on the Main road of ouarzazate. Host very kind, speaks English french Spanish and Arabic. Cosy little place, nice Moroccan atmosphere.

reviews.author: Paulina Gryz
reviews.text: Very tasty tagine, especially kofta. Nice service and atmosphere. Highly recommended:)

name: Restaurant Le Petit Riad
address: Restaurant Le Petit Riad, Ouarzazate, Morocco

reviews.author: Detlef
reviews.text: The best accommodation on our tour of southern Morocco. We extended our stay in Ouarzazate by three more days and we really liked Le Petit Riad. The staff takes great care of the guests. Special requests for food are gladly accommodated. Breakfast and dinner are highly recommended.

reviews.author: Joy Branyon
reviews.text: Small hotel with excellent service. The staff speaks English very well. The rooms are clean, comfortable and check-in/check-out are efficient. The pool area is quite lovely and the interiors are recently updated and well-maintained.

reviews.author: Adam Giesinger
reviews.text: Best hotel in Morocco we have visited. A lot of space, very clean rooms, lovely pool area and all the people are incredibly kind and helpful.

reviews.author: Alexander Jaus
reviews.text: We were warmly welcomed and the room was very comfortable. Our pool was right near by the pool and we were sceptical that it might be loud, also because the hotel is located directly in front of the airport. But this was not the case and we slept soundly without noise disturbance. The bed was huge and has the right hardness and beautifully decorated. The pool area is also very beautiful, although it was too cold already for us to swim. Breakfast was also amazing, with delicious little pancakes were our favorite. Parking is "just" at the street, but they have a guard watching the entrance at night, who also watched the cars, so we felt safe leaving our car there. The service was outstanding, if we have the chance, would definitely come again :)

reviews.author: Catherine Kricorian
reviews.text: Best parts: 1) Decor 2) Service 3) Food This stay was absolutely beautiful! The inside is decorated incredibly and the layout of the hotel is wonderful. This is a very intimate stay with just a few spacious, and comfortable rooms. What really stood out was the wonderful service of the staff. They were so kind and went above and beyond to ensure that we were comfortable, even letting me pick out which room I preferred! Lastly, the food was amazing! Some of the best I had in my entire time in Morocco. It felt very authentic and high end, absolutely loved it!

reviews.author: Jennifer Duff
reviews.text: Google lists it as a 3-star hotel – but in my opinion, it easily feels more like a 4. This riad is absolutely charming – full of character and warmth. The rooms are beautifully styled, spacious, and incredibly comfortable – perfect for unwinding after a day of exploring. Wonderful shower, extra-large bed, and heating made it even more cosy. Dinner was a real highlight – every dish was packed with flavour and clearly prepared with love. What truly set the experience apart was the staff – so friendly, attentive, and always ready to help with anything we needed. A truly memorable stay!

reviews.author: Lil
reviews.text: The Riad is nice, rooms are spacious and comfortable. The location that the Riad is at doesn’t seem to be the best, but I guess Ouarzazate is a safe city. The food at the restaurant was good, and the staff is nice. Very noisy, you can hear what happens in other rooms. Some stairs are slippery (because they have some sort of paint). I slipped and fell, and I was ok (huge dark bruise though), but I would worry for older people. No elevator available.

reviews.author: Denise Worthy
reviews.text: We stayed at this Riad during the last part of our 5-day tour. It was a beautiful Riad, it is situated in a very residential busy neighborhood, but we felt safe. There was no noise from the outside during night fall. Only thing missing in the room was a hair dryer.

reviews.author: Carlos O
reviews.text: Probably not located in the area that you would expect. It is new(ish) so they are working to get things working smoothly, like breakfast. I would give it another opportunity next time. BTW, painted steps in the main staircase are in general a pretty bad idea because they are slippery.

reviews.author: Abdelilah El Bouni
reviews.text: Top Riad on list of Ouarzazate accommodation, was here several times. Nothing to complain about. High quality service, food and location. We'll decorated Quiet and clean is what I appreciated most

reviews.author: nguyet le
reviews.text: Not recommend for anyone first come and first time driving in Morocco.Very dishonesty and not supportive host. Just to be clear. We drove to near the hotel location last night( which is late around 7pm and all the small turn are dark and no light). When the google started failed to show the exactly way. We tried to call that lady 3 times. She said we to drive straight inside the road. But, there is no road to drive. We already tell her this is our first time we are here. And we have to ask her to pick up us because she cannot understand us well. We parked in a very big store in the road. Then she said she cannot find us in the road but she never asked about our car or color of the car. Then when we asked about the color of her clothes. She did not answer and said this is not about where you are, where we are. You have to drive. But there is no road for us to drive. Then she cannot say anything and hang up. And there is no phone call after that as she said. Please show evidence or you are not honest in this hospitality service. —————///We cannot find the road to get inside the hotel, when we called the number the lady is very angry and we asked her if she can come out and take us inside. Because there is only 5minutes of walking from her. After 3 times of phone call, she hang up. And we have to take another hotel -> make this clear and constructive

reviews.author: Mourad AHAMMAM
reviews.text: A very nice Riad in the heart of the city. The owner is always available and ready to assist everyone. The entire Riad has lovely scents of oil and incense, and the breakfast was delicious. We will definitely come back to this Riad.

reviews.author: Michelle Wick
reviews.text: We stayed two nights in the Riad Dar Rita & absolutely loved it. The owner is super kind & helpful & provides you with everything you need. The rooms are clean & the rooftop terrace is also awesome. We definitely recommend!

reviews.author: sam storey
reviews.text: Beautifully well kept rooms. Very clean and incredibly friendly staff. Ideal for people who want to stay in a more authentic part of ouarzazate. Good breakfast too

reviews.author: Dovydas Stancikas
reviews.text: Very friendly host. Made us a nice dinner, the host recommended places to visit, ext.

reviews.author: Leah C
reviews.text: When we first arrived, we were impressed with the beauty of this hotel. They did a really good job decorating… Unfortunately, the aesthetics are the only pleasing thing about this hotel. The dinner was a buffet and it was very crowded with tourism groups, not traditional Moroccan food, and very average tasting. The dining room was freezing as well. The staff are incredibly rude and we never had hot water in our room… We called them up multiple times and they claimed to have fixed it the first night but then the next morning it was cold again. They sent a technician up and allegedly fixed it but at this point, we were late to continue on our journey and did not get to have a hot shower. The room never really got warm & felt damp, which was strange. On top of that, upon check out the front desk girl accused me of stealing their body wash. I let her know I didn’t even get to shower and I did not steal the body wash and offered to walk up there with her to show her that it was still there, but she refused and they fought our travel company on this. They refused to refund Part of our stay due to not having hot water which is unbelievable. Luckily this stay was the only unpleasant part of our journey, the rest of the people in Morocco were very kind and helpful.

reviews.author: Roberto Grimaldi
reviews.text: Very nice riad, authentic decor probably the best option going around. We had one night stop on our way from Fes to Marrakech. The garden and pool very well maintained, surrounded by nature (a little paradise) there is also a gym (pretty rare when travelling in the country). They also do jazz evening. Our room as well was very spacious and comfortable with nice design. Considering the price you pay you expect bathrobe and slippers for better confort and better food variety (no gluten free - limited vegan options), cheap tea and coffee selection at breakfast. Overall a good experience.

reviews.author: Anna Kleene
reviews.text: We stayed at this hotel for two nights. At first impressions the hotel is gorgeous. We arrived late, so we went straight to the restaurant. We only had the choice for the buffet. We went to our table and it was very cold in the restaurant, also there were big groups from travel agencies around us. We didn’t like that, and nobody told us about it. We didn’t really like the food of the buffet. We went to the spa, which was amazing. During the day we chilled by the pool, which was very nice. We also ate some lunch outside, which was very good. We ate somewhere that night. The room we had the first night, was very uncomfortable and next to a small road. We didn’t like that kind room, but luckily we got upgraded to a better one in the hotel. Although the place is gorgeous if you are looking for authenticity and good food I would definitely not recommend to go here.

reviews.author: Ricardo GC
reviews.text: Awful! It is a 2 to 3 stars hotel at the most. Room was so disappointing, for a few reasons: too small, no place to put the suitcases (I had to place my only one, a carry on, on the night stand, wc is open and shower soills and wets the sink, management placed a sign that shampoo and 2 others (not identified) are for sale but missed to inform what they contain. Vicinity is no existant, I walked around...I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL AND AM REPORTING IT TO OPERATOR AND PORTUGAL TRAVEL AGENCY. I would stay at the hotel if it is the only available, but it is not worth as for the daily rate announced

reviews.author: Melinda Miller
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel, beautiful grounds. We really enjoyed our stay. Our room was very large and comfortable.

reviews.author: Cesarina Gretha Bosscher
reviews.text: The hotel itself is beautiful, the staff super friendly and helpful. We loved the bar and the overall atmosphere but I do agree with everyone else that it just needs a few upgrades, tiny upgrades like new pillows on the chairs would make a huge difference. There were hairs from other guests still on the shower, which gave me thrills to use the sanitary. Breakfast was nice but don't go to early since they start baking fresh later on. Overall a pleasant stay but they really need to finish their details to make it a impeccable stay over and the whole hotel could easily be one of the greater ones. Free and safe parking in front of the hotel, just make sure you pay attention since the location is wrong on the map.

reviews.author: James Wittman
reviews.text: The Hotel is beautiful and a peaceful oasis. We really enjoyed our stay .We slept with the windows open to the sound of crickets and the running fountain by the pool. But the breakfast was bad, the staff dont seem to care for quality or presentation, and even though there were 5 employees none seemed to work at making presentable service. We didn't try dinner there because of this experience. It's a shame! Reception was very warm and helpful besides all that.

reviews.author: TheLaurierstreet
reviews.text: Big hotel with a pool and friendly staff. Rooms are clean. Outdated interiors, old towels. Not the best mattresses (matter of preference, for me too hard). They should have designated rooms for smokers. Now most rooms keep this smell. WiFi works not all the time.

reviews.author: Singular Escape
reviews.text: Need some renovations and more motivated staff. Aisha, the manager, is doing a good work. The air conditioner doesn't work, sometimes the water is dirty, the breakfast could be better. The swimming pool is very good. The restaurant make delicious food. The bar inside is a very very strange place.

reviews.author: Marta R
reviews.text: Comfortable place with a pool and a bar! Rooms are very big and comfortable, could have been a little bit better maintained. The staff are very friendly and helpful! Location great also, close to the major Kasbah and a walking distance to the town centre. Coffee, however at a breakfast, was horrible. And there was a not very nice smell in the neighbourhood, perhaps it wasn't the hotel's fault but it was unpleasant enough. Also, if you are looking for authentic marroccan experience it's better to find a quiet road nearby.

reviews.author: Beck Hosemans
reviews.text: This Riad is beautiful and has a good view of the greenery and area from the roof top. The service was amazing. The gardens inside were beautiful. It is a distance from the town centre so if you didn't have your own transport or didn't want to eat there it could be an issue. My sister and I went for a walk and all the local kids came up and said hello they were very cute. The area was very safe. There were a few small local grocery stores nearby but nothing big. My only issue was that dinner for vegetarians was limited, first we had lentil soup which I would have had more of and if I knew the main would be only chopped cucumber and tomato (just plain) with chips - the chips were good though.

reviews.author: Hajar Allam
reviews.text: This place is like a heavenly Oasis. The Host Mostafa provided us with the hospitality and care of a true family. We felt home, we felt welcome and wanted within his premises, he provided us with everything we needed , the rooms were so fancy, beautiful, and clean. And the pool was to die for, whether it was a day or night swim. The food is very healthy, clean, and delicious. I'm recommending this riad experience to everyone visiting or passing by Ourzazate.

reviews.author: Saif Zayn
reviews.text: The best riad ever. We stayed here only one night, but it was the best stay ever So hospitable, so welcoming, so warm, clean, greenry, lovely food and people. I would recommend everyone to book this riad. Mustafa and Hamid were the best hosts ever. It felt like home, like family. We will come here again.

reviews.author: Sam van Haaren
reviews.text: Very friendly staff, good food and a calm atmosphere once you're inside. Wifi was good, pooltable is a nice addition. The location is the only real issue. It's very difficult to find and get to due to rough terrain and a lot of rubble from houses nearby.

reviews.author: Ming Bao
reviews.text: This hotel is located outside the residential area. We saw a few little kids in the front of the building, and we are told they are not beggars but they might follow you for money, so not safe to walk outside. The hotel room is big tiny but layout is odd. The room front door is a clear full size glass door, there are two small curtains to block the outside but we played how to place them and failed to cover all angles. It seems happen to almost all rooms so people can easily see what’s inside your room, especially in evening. The lamp is placed on a small desk, the power cord and outlet is just above the pillow. It seems the room doesn’t have proper sound isolation. While our neighbour comes back, we can clear hear what they talk, what they do, including bath. The hotel stuff was friendly until we shared our feedbacks. They even didn’t bother to serve us any water, tea or drink menu( they do have alcohol menu, we figured when leaving). The main dish is over cooked, and desert tastes like canned fruits wrapped with sugar. Overall, I don’t think I will recommend this hotel to my friends, and I regret I didn’t look at previous reviews before came here.

reviews.text: Many shops without salespeople harassing you to buy

reviews.author: Hanna M
reviews.text: A souk as you'd imagine it. A lot of chatter and little substance. But despite everything, the people are very nice and friendly!

reviews.author: TheYvanbreizh
reviews.text: Souk not interesting.

reviews.author: Gratien pub (gpnam)
reviews.text: Just one place, tourist bus stopped, everything else being closed.

reviews.author: Ross Daniels
reviews.text: This is an absolutely fantastic place a bit of a labyrinth but so enjoyable with winding streets and multiple marketplaces and plenty of cafes and eating spots. Great atmosphere and one of the streets will take you down to the beach. We spent hours just wandering around and it’s up there with any marketplace in Morocco.

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: This has got to be the best souk in Morocco! I’ve been to many, but Essaouira’s felt so special. I spent about five hours there and still didn’t want to leave. Each shop has its own unique vibe, and the shopkeepers were incredibly kind and helpful. Every time I asked where to find something, they wouldn’t just point me in the direction—they’d actually walk me there and leave without the other shopkeepers noticing. It was such a genuine experience. You’ll find everything from handmade Moroccan teapots and beautiful tea glasses to breathtaking paintings and handmade rugs, linen clothing, genuine leather goods, and the most fragrant spices. If you’re looking for authentic treasures, this is the place!

reviews.author: Mohammed nurul Islam
reviews.text: Best place to shop in all city

reviews.author: Federica Preda
reviews.text: Beautiful and quaint! The shops are full of local souvenirs and for all budgets! Exceptional fish and real Argan oil! We will definitely return. A quiet city where you can reach everything on foot.

reviews.author: World Trip
reviews.text: A favorite ❤️ A truly delightful souk in the port city of Essaouira ✅ The climate is pleasant and the people are truly friendly!

reviews.author: Khedira Ghazi
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: ida russo
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Paul Ciprian
reviews.text: An old fortress, quite impressive, as an overall view. Part of it is renovated and looks OK, but there are also sections with cracked walls, which look ready to fall. Unfortunately, even in the renovated section, open to the public, there is nothing to see inside. Just empty rooms. There is a small art gallery (paintings) but nothing that presents anything related to the history of the place.

reviews.author: yassine hadda
reviews.text: Kasbah Taourirt is located in the city of Ouarzazate in southern Morocco and is considered one of the most prominent historical and architectural landmarks in the region. The kasbah is a remarkable example of traditional earthen architecture that characterizes southern Morocco. Its origins date back to the 17th century, but it gained prominence and was significantly expanded in the 19th century when it became the residence of the powerful Pasha Thami El Glaoui, one of the most influential political figures during the French protectorate period. Kasbah Taourirt is known for its unique architectural design, featuring a network of interlocking towers, high decorated walls, and numerous rooms used for residential and administrative purposes. Its walls are adorned with geometric patterns and intricately carved wooden doors, while the winding passages and inner courtyards reflect the traditional lifestyle within Moroccan kasbahs. In addition to its historical significance, the kasbah is a major tourist attraction. A large part of it has been restored and is open to visitors who wish to explore the region’s history and Amazigh (Berber) culture. It has also appeared in several international films shot in Ouarzazate, adding to its cinematic charm.

reviews.author: M E Lesteri
reviews.text: Is it worth the 20 dirhams? For a tourist — yes. It’s something a bit different and offers a unique experience compared to what you might see in other countries. If you’ve already visited other kasbahs, it may feel quite similar, but the Saharan/Berber architectural style is still fascinating to see. There isn’t much to explore inside — many areas were under renovation during our visit, and the open rooms are mostly empty. It’s more about appreciating the structure and how it was built. A guide isn’t essential, but if it’s your first time and you haven’t read up on the history, having someone explain the background can enhance the visit.

reviews.author: Macaquinha Suiza
reviews.text: There are a lot of empty rooms you can partly visit. The rest is under construction or are art galleries. It's nicely renovated, don't get me wrong but it's not really interesting. I have seen much more interesting Kasbahs which a) you don't have to pay for and b) feel more real. For my taste too pushy guides which are getting grumpy when you don't want their service, too commercial and too many art galleries within the premises. Wouldn't go back

reviews.author: Christine Morrison
reviews.text: Really lovely place, you can see the amount of work that has gone into the renovation, good to see them using traditional methods of mud and straw..

reviews.author: Khawla Ch
reviews.text: It was a truly terrible experience. From the moment I arrived, the staff was rude and unwelcoming, making me feel like I was inconveniencing them rather than being a valued guest and there was a huge lack of warmth, hospitality, and professionalism since my simple requests were met with attitude and rudeness. The service was slow and disorganized, and it was clear that guest comfort was not on the list of priorities. Instead of the relaxing, enjoyable experience I was looking forward to, I felt uncomfortable and unwelcome the entire time. I rarely leave bad reviews, but this stay was truly disappointing and terrible and the food was really terrible and expensive even for tourists. I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone looking for good service and a welcoming atmosphere.

reviews.author: Wissal Miller
reviews.text: Very bad service. The staff are so rude and they were not helpful at all when I had questions or requests. I felt completely ignored and unimportant. My stay was incredibly frustrating, and I would not recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable or pleasant experience. There are definitely much better options nearby. The food prices are also very expensive for tourists! I mean what is this scam? The food is not even that good.

reviews.author: ghalia fassi fihri
reviews.text: Amazing Stay at Dar El Kebira This Riad is a beautiful blend of Moroccan charm and modern comfort. The rooms are spotless and tastefully decorated, and the peaceful courtyard is perfect for relaxing. The staff’s hospitality was outstanding, making my stay unforgettable. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Lina RAISS
reviews.text: I had an exceptional stay at Dar El Kebira! Everything was perfect, from the warm and professional service to the friendly and attentive welcome. The rooms were impeccably clean, beautifully decorated, and incredibly comfortable. Every detail was thoughtfully taken care of, making the experience truly unforgettable. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a perfect getaway!

reviews.author: Zhixuan Li
reviews.text: This is a traditional Riad with friendly hotel staff, located in the ancient city of Rabat. I enjoyed greatly the terrace and the breakfast. The hotel room is not as comfortable as a 5-star hotel, but fully facilitated. I enjoy the feeling of immersion in this place. Also, they welcome us with mint tea and snacks!

reviews.author: ha yek
reviews.text: Great authentic food with great atmosphere with live music, right across from Bab El Had Square. Must try if you are in Rabat. It is nicely decorated; Abdelfattah who served me my Tajine could not be more pleasant. Friday special is couscous, and that is my next diner. Overall: Bonne Service, Bonne Manger, Bonne Prix. Give it a try and do not miss out.... Thank you Abdelfattah and also the entire staff, for the great experience. ..Hani

reviews.author: Yvette O'Brien
reviews.text: Recommended by our guide Asmaa. It looks touristy but the food is absolutely delicious, slow cooked vegetable, lamb, beef, chicken and turkey tagines that are bursting with flavour. Decorated in Moroccan style, very comfortable seating and staff dressed traditionally, excellent food, service and spotless bathrooms. Waiter explained menu and translated very well. Lots of locals dining here too. I highly recommend.

reviews.author: Dean Boudrika
reviews.text: I recently visited this restaurant after hearing several good things about it and was genuinely looking forward to trying it out. The service was excellent—staff were friendly, welcoming, and attentive from the moment I arrived. Unfortunately, the food didn’t live up to the expectations at all. It was quite bland, lacking any real flavor or depth. For a place that came so highly recommended, I was honestly disappointed. What bothered me even more was a small detail that reflected a bigger issue. I asked for a few olives on the side, thinking it was a simple, complimentary item like in many Moroccan restaurants. To my surprise, they charged me 12 dirhams for a very small portion. I was shocked. It gave the impression that they’re looking for any small opportunity to add extra charges, even for something as basic as olives. While the ambiance and service were definitely strong points, the overall experience fell flat due to the quality of the food and the pricing practices. Unfortunately, based on this visit, I wouldn’t go back. There are plenty of other places that offer better food for the same or even lower prices, without the sneaky extras.

reviews.author: Karola
reviews.text: Oh my! How good is the food here!?! Let me tell you. Great! I am a sucker for traditional cuisine and here that part of my being was happy. Not only that but as a bonus it was also delicious! Mrozia? I think I have a new favourite dish (who new raisins can actually be edible?). So, personally, I am a big fan, but if you add a warm welcome consisting of a hand washing service, live music and a mint pouring show... it's a must.

reviews.author: Marion Rogers
reviews.text: Der Naji in Rabat is a great restaurant with a beautiful traditional Moroccan atmosphere. The service was friendly, and when you order tea, they serve it in an entertaining way. The food was good overall, and the prices were affordable—we dined as a group of four for just €37. The chèvre tajine was really good, with tender meat and a slightly sweet flavor. The mixed brochettes were flavorful and well-seasoned. The SADA salad was a delicious dish of cooked vegetables, very well seasoned. Unfortunately, the poulet aux citrons was quite dry and disappointing. The reason I’m giving four stars instead of five is that the menu could be more tourist-friendly. Since it’s a popular spot for visitors, having descriptions of the dishes in English or Spanish would be really helpful. Sometimes, you’re not entirely sure what you’re ordering. Overall, it was a lovely experience with great value for money.

reviews.author: Benjamin
reviews.text: Honestly? Just OK. This was one of the most underwhelming meals I had during my trip in Morocco. The chicken tajine with preserved lemon had no real citrus flavor. The starter salads didn’t feel fresh — served at room temperature and lacking in taste. The harira soup was disappointing compared to others I’ve had. Desserts were bland and forgettable. The service was decent and polite, which I appreciated. Maybe the overall quality was affected by the Aïd holiday, but for 295 MAD, I expected much better. I wouldn’t recommend it unless you have no other options.

reviews.author: Rohan Hearn
reviews.text: Restaurant located in a typical Riad (Moroccan style family house) dating back to the 18th century.The original family house has had its original courtyard closed in to form a dining space. Typical Moroccan dishes are available here with several large banquet menus available all of whoch feature a range of starters and salads followed by mains of tajine or couscous accompanied by desserts. The food was delicious and incredibly filling but it was a little more expensive than other options nearby. It was quite special to explore the building itself as it had a nice style with cool old furniture and draping curtains. I found myself wandering around the open spaces and even upstairs to take a few photos of all of the cool things I saw.

reviews.author: Hanna Smith
reviews.text: A Moroccan Riad turned into a restaurant. We went there for lunch in a group of 20. The place was crowded and the air stuffy because there were other tourist groups. We had some appetisers (mailny grated vegetables, olives, and some sauce) and tajines - a sauté made of sheepmeat and vegetables with big prunes. The food was OK. However, they don't serve you any drinks for free, even water. The place looks authentic. The visitors are free to explore the upper floors, where there are more private spaces with sofas and cushions.

reviews.author: Oliver C
reviews.text: Fantastic good, huge portions and you can tell it’s the real authentic version. Love the desserts also!

reviews.author: Andrea Millado
reviews.text: food was delicious.They serve set menu, ordered the rafissa with chicken and it was so good. Some kind of flaky pasta with lentils and chicken. Beef and chicken tagine was also good. Desert was spectacular! A really nice food experience from this restaurant. The place was also cozy and the server speaks english.

reviews.author: Agha Durrani
reviews.text: What a memorable dining experience! We were a group of 4, came to Dinarjat for lunch. I was specifically interested to have salad. Menu listed two salads, 1. Fine salad, 2. Rich salad. Upon asking, we learned that rich salad had liver and brain. We opted for fine salad which was absolutely delicious. We ordered two tajine dishes, 1. Tajine tfaya (lamb), 2. Tajine Jarret de veau (veal). Prior to food served, the hostess brought water & towels to wash hands. We may term this place as high end restaurant (bill to Morocco Darham: 1133) however we are exceptionally satisfied (in fact very happy) with the fine food quality, service and above all ambiance. I highly recommend, if you are on the lookout for a unique and amazing experience.

reviews.author: Hamada A.
reviews.text: You are paying for the atmosphere and service, not the quality of the food. What I ordered was VERY PLAIN, my friend's dishes were better but only marginally. Considering the price point, I would consider it a crime against food an insult to intelligence. There was very nice live music, and location was amazing. I would say go if you are in Rabat but only for drinks, DO NOT order this food at this price point.

reviews.author: Porter McRoberts
reviews.text: We have been here four times. It is always an incredible experience magicians food presentation taste. It really is incomparable and so this is by far my favorite restaurant and all of Morocco the attentive nature of Mr Adelkader the manager makes it all worthwhile. I guarantee you will not be disappointed!

reviews.author: Máximo Klyetsun
reviews.text: It is a wonderful place to go eat if you are in Rabat, Morocco. The food is delicious, the music brings you to a whole other planet while sitting and enjoying the food. The design inside, just wow!!! 10/10

reviews.author: Goutam Datta
reviews.text: Our hotel recommended here for dinner . I guess they receive commission. My chicken was as dry as Sahara desert . May be cooked few days ago and just placed in a bowl of sauce . Terrible food ! My chair was wobbly. Very uncomfortable seating . This is a tourist trap . Don’t believe other reviews they are made up !

reviews.author: Abdessamad Moumen
reviews.text: The service was really good all of them were friendly and paying attention in case you needed anything. The food was really delicious and well cooked (although it's a bit more expensive than other restaurants but worth the price) the drinks are good too. I'd recommend this place for sure

reviews.author: Salem Alsamour
reviews.text: Great food, great atmosphere, and great service ! The quality of the food is exquisite, the ingredients are fresh and it’s super tasty, the menu has plenty of options which is very nice. Now the prices are a bit high for locals I would say. The service is very good, he was always reactive and close to our table, paying attention. The atmosphere was so nice, there was a live Arabic band, it was a special night, normally it’s a jazz spot. Everyone was singing and dancing while eating, it’s super entertaining:) I highly recommend this place

reviews.author: Mountain Squirrel
reviews.text: Fancy without being too expensive (compared to UK prices). The chefs clearly care about every single dish, everything is cooked to perfection. The Sicilian Penne (vegetarian) and the Lamb Knee were both absolutely fantastic. Really high quality food.

reviews.author: Albert Lieuw
reviews.text: We eventually didn't notice the restaurant. Three man security at the entrance of the restaurant made it look like a club. But inside it was a mixture, bar/ club and restaurant. And the food is good!! Nice servicing staff. Good value for your money.

reviews.author: KASHSH MOVIES
reviews.text: A quiet and beautiful place but a little pricey for what they serve.The staff were not attending properly which needs to be looked upon.Ambience is good minus the late service.

reviews.author: Rae Rae
reviews.text: Pleasantly Surprised Le Dhow was better than expected! I had the octopus and tuna starter, which was well-prepared. The place itself is a bit tatty around the edges, but it has charm, and the staff were really pleasant and welcoming. A nice spot for a casual meal with a view.

reviews.author: Анна Николова
reviews.text: The atmosphere and the service are amazing. The staff is friendly, we were helped to and from our table, greeted with smiles and sent with smiles. The food however can use some improvements. The cocktails we ordered were rather watery and didn’t taste like their regular versions and for me the steak, that I ordered was really dry, at least the veggies and the sauce were really tasty. We tried traditional Moroccan salads (would recommend specifically the Taktouka and Zaalouk) and also the duck. The duck was perfectly cooked and tasted delicious. So, in a nutshell, a place with nice view and atmosphere, be choose what you order carefully - might be great, might be hard to swallow.

reviews.author: Dan Doon
reviews.text: Nice place to have drinks and good food. Would definitely recommend the tuna start and the paella. They had live music which was nice and the prices were decent.

reviews.author: CHYAH
reviews.text: Service was so good and oyster taste like fresh beach, fries tasty even after long time, risotto has great flavour

reviews.author: K Lawlor
reviews.text: Spent a few weeks in Rabat, and this ship wasn't far from where I was staying. I came on board mainly to drink the beer (they have beer on tap), but Issy and some of the staff have a unique charisma that encourages you to return. So 10/10 to those guys- charisma is everything, and if you have the patter you can sell anything! Always seems to be a mix of people on board; mainly French tourists with the occasional American and local mixed in. Helped me to improve my schoolboy French for sure. Occasionally the area at the front of the ship is reserved, restricting access to areas. That can be infuriating for a regular punter who wants to go outside and relax only to find the area they want is sealed off! Food prices seem to be on the steep side, but the food looked plentiful and lovely. If I return to Rabat, I'd certainly call in again. Nice ambience, nice staff.

reviews.author: STANSLAUS ALWYN MASINZA
reviews.text: Wonderful seafood recipes and great service. Ideal for discerning fish-terians

reviews.author: Vester Mccloskey
reviews.text: The service was quick without feeling rushed.

reviews.author: Zoé Jammes
reviews.text: My family and I shared a lovely meal at Le Goeland. The food is scrumptious and the restaurant is tastefully decorated. At the end of our meal, the waiter brought us a dessert to share free of charge, which was a thoughtful gesture. However, please beware that SMOKING IS ALLOWED inside of the restaurant. As Canadians, we were shocked by this and it meant that we rushed to finish our plates because of the awful smell.

reviews.author: Sefa A
reviews.text: Perfect place to have dinner with your friends.

reviews.author: Qatar4ever
reviews.text: They bring the paella burned!!! And the bartender was rude about it

reviews.author: Kenji Nagoshi
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Scarlett Pyemont
reviews.text: Had a delicious dinner here yesterday with my family. As soon as we went in we were amazed by how beautiful the restaurant is! The atmosphere was so nice and the servers were attentive and really friendly. We ordered starters and a main course each, all were very fancy and very scrum. There were lit candles everywhere, even in the bathroom! This restaurant is so nice and i highly recommend :)

reviews.author: David Hastead
reviews.text: Fantastic. After a week in morroco the highlight of culinary delight. French Morrocon, live music, enjoyable but not overwhelming.

reviews.author: Michael G
reviews.text: Nice Seafood, Grumpy Service. Beautiful room with candles and live music. The fresh fish was nicely prepared, but not special. The service was poor, once served I never saw the server again. The server brought me the wrong wine and then became very grumpy when I asked to be charge for the one I ordered. They say they take credit cards but when you go to pay the claim the machine is not working, so cash only. There are heaps of restaurants here, most with happy service.

reviews.author: Karaev Ishan
reviews.text: After a long car trip you arrive in an old port area with a chilling wind and a strong smell of the ocean. You choose a riad to stay and get there a recomendation to dinner at Le Patio. When you get there, you take a bottle of white local wine and the fish of the day. Here your perfect evening begins.

reviews.author: vittorio vedove
reviews.text: I think the bad review of this place are not right.. his intimacy is unknown in the city, the dishes were really good with uncommon flavours. The goat cheese and veggies was awesome 10/10 the shirmp cigars good 8/10 main dishes we tried: Lamb shoulder was very tender and the gravy sauce had the right flavours 10/10 , fish tajin with pears a 10/10

reviews.author: Aymen TOUHENT
reviews.text: Live band singing for fun! Not at all happy with the quality of the performance. The music that started was 100 times better.

reviews.author: Emna Masmoudi
reviews.text: Friendly atmosphere Friendly environment Top service

reviews.author: Foued Daly
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Grech Anis
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Karim Ayoubi
reviews.text: Wonderful local Moroccan cuisine friendly service people always there relaxed crowd exploring local dishes. 75 euro approx x2 adults x2 children. loved the live gentle Oud traditional music. Highly recommend ! Merci شكرا على الضيافة

reviews.author: Jamie M. Kneitel
reviews.text: This is down the street from where we are staying. It is an excellent restaurant! The food was delicious with all the complex spices you expect from Moroccan food. We had the lemon chicken tagine and chicken pastille, both great. They had excellent service but the greatest element of this restaurant is the live lute player. He is outstanding with wonderful playing and singing. This really fills the soul, we could have stayed all night for the music!

reviews.author: Lara Lanslots
reviews.text: The food is incredible! We had the veal tajine and it was the best dish we had in Morocco. It's a cosy restaurant with nice background music, really nice ambiance. Can definitely recommend! I would suggest to arrive early, when they open at 19:30. Or make a reservation. There were several guests who walked in around 20:00/20:30 and were told it was full.

reviews.author: Alexandra Craciunoiu
reviews.text: Came here today based on memories from more than 10 years ago, when I had an amazing lamb shoulder. Will definitely return, for both the food and the great atmosphere.

reviews.author: Didi
reviews.text: I ate here a few times eleven years ago. I loved it then, I love it now. The restaurant serves fresh and delicious Moroccan classic dishes like like lamb with eggplant tajine, chicken with seven vegetables couscous, pastilla and briouate. The musician softly plays classical songs with his oud, making the experience even more memorable. The staff is very attentive and hospitable. I was very delighted to have had a chance to visit it again with service and quality still great.

reviews.author: Hibo Warsama
reviews.text: Le Ziryab is a true gem in the heart of Rabat. The atmosphere is elegant, the view from the terrace is beautiful, and the food is exceptional. The lamb tagine was tender and full of rich flavor, and the mint tea was the perfect finish. Thank you to the wonderful staff for making the experience so warm and memorable. I’ll definitely be back.

reviews.author: Brad Lee
reviews.text: Nice experience and good food but rather pricey. I wish the neat portions were bigger. There were 3 of us and we ordered a special, about US$75 each and received just a single chicken breast and a small lamb shank. It was good but for three adults we left wanting more protein. Now the couscous and veg tanjine was nice and the size was huge. Would I go back? Probably not.

reviews.author: Ashley Kessen
reviews.text: We had such a wonderful dinner here! The service was also excellent, and we even had a tour about the history of the Riad, given by the super nice guy named Nawfal. Additionally, we were joined by a super sweet parrot, which made our experience at this restaurant truly amazing. I give everything a 10. Definitely a must-visit!!

reviews.author: Soumaya B.
reviews.text: It was the perfect business lunch, we went on Tuesday, and it felt like the place was reserved for us. Be prepared to eat A LOT the portions are huge. From the entrance you can smell the Oud and Serghina, and you can hear the little birds singing in the Hall. We had lunch on the roof top, and it was sunny and pleasant and very calm. 100% recommend. The servers were really respectful and attentive, and the food was really fresh. Definitely recommend reserving a table beforehand.

reviews.author: Helen C Haugh
reviews.text: Top quality Moroccan food - friendly attentive waiter throughout the meal, he gave us the tour after dinner. Great atmosphere with music and customers dancing at 1am. We just came across it by accident and it turned a very good day into a great day.

name: Riad Dar El Kebira
address: Riad Dar El Kebira, Rabat, Morocco

reviews.author: Khawla Ch
reviews.text: It was a truly terrible experience. From the moment I arrived, the staff was rude and unwelcoming, making me feel like I was inconveniencing them rather than being a valued guest and there was a huge lack of warmth, hospitality, and professionalism since my simple requests were met with attitude and rudeness. The service was slow and disorganized, and it was clear that guest comfort was not on the list of priorities. Instead of the relaxing, enjoyable experience I was looking forward to, I felt uncomfortable and unwelcome the entire time. I rarely leave bad reviews, but this stay was truly disappointing and terrible and the food was really terrible and expensive even for tourists. I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone looking for good service and a welcoming atmosphere.

reviews.author: Wissal Miller
reviews.text: Very bad service. The staff are so rude and they were not helpful at all when I had questions or requests. I felt completely ignored and unimportant. My stay was incredibly frustrating, and I would not recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable or pleasant experience. There are definitely much better options nearby. The food prices are also very expensive for tourists! I mean what is this scam? The food is not even that good.

reviews.author: ghalia fassi fihri
reviews.text: Amazing Stay at Dar El Kebira This Riad is a beautiful blend of Moroccan charm and modern comfort. The rooms are spotless and tastefully decorated, and the peaceful courtyard is perfect for relaxing. The staff’s hospitality was outstanding, making my stay unforgettable. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Lina RAISS
reviews.text: I had an exceptional stay at Dar El Kebira! Everything was perfect, from the warm and professional service to the friendly and attentive welcome. The rooms were impeccably clean, beautifully decorated, and incredibly comfortable. Every detail was thoughtfully taken care of, making the experience truly unforgettable. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a perfect getaway!

reviews.author: Zhixuan Li
reviews.text: This is a traditional Riad with friendly hotel staff, located in the ancient city of Rabat. I enjoyed greatly the terrace and the breakfast. The hotel room is not as comfortable as a 5-star hotel, but fully facilitated. I enjoy the feeling of immersion in this place. Also, they welcome us with mint tea and snacks!

reviews.author: AHAR TALES (AHAR)
reviews.text: Wonderful Riad, in the heart of the old Médina. Fadwa is a wonderful person, she took good care of us from the moment we arrived by serving us a delicious mint tea and Moroccan pastries. The breakfast is also handmade and delicious, even yogurt is homemade!! The rooms are well done and clean, the riad and the terrace are so quiet and peaceful. It is perfectly located in order to visit all of the city's emblematic monuments. Especially the Kasbah of the Udayas and it's beautiful sunset. A great proof of how marvellous is the Moroccan hospitality 🇲🇦 PS: If you are into street food and spicy food, this is the perfect location for you. Definitely coming back. Thank you Fadwa 🙏

reviews.author: Sally Ortiz
reviews.text: Beautiful, very clean and easy to find riad. Fadwa our host was friendly, helpful and always with a smile. The best breakfast I had in Morocco. Amazing choices of bread, fruits, spreads. I got a pitcher of hot milk. I like to come back again.

reviews.author: Ricky Sanders
reviews.text: What a beautiful place and wonderful host. The breakfast each morning was 10/10. Very comfortable and peaceful rooms and went above and beyond when cleaning our room and folding our clothes! Thank you.

reviews.author: Amy Levitt
reviews.text: Fantastic Riad - beautiful, clean, safe, quiet, great location. Incredible staff went above and beyond. They arranged for a driver to pick me up at the airport at midnight & take me to the Riad. This was amazingly kind, because I never would have found the Riad on my own. I became ill for a couple of days. While I was ill, the staff checked on me several times, bringing me tea and water and making sure that I was comfortable and fed. The staff also offered to wash my son's clothes instead of us going to a laundromat. Breakfast everyday was delicious and enormous. Someone was always available in the Riad 24 hours a day and everyone was very helpful and kind. The location was great - easy to walk to most locations, good restaurants, great shopping & a beautiful, friendly, clean mosque very close to the Riad. Our room was beautiful, clean, well appointed and spacious enough for two people. Bed linens, blankets, pillows, towels, soap, shampoo, toilet paper and hair dryer were provided. The room had one double bed and one single bed (both comfortable), good lighting, two arm chairs, one table, one bench, throw rugs, throw pillows, two armoires and an internal, adjustable heating unit. There was plenty of hot water and great water pressure in the bathroom. One of the nicest features was the rooftop deck which had plenty of comfortable seating and great views. There was also a variety of hot tea available in the lounge 24 hours a day. All in all, a fantastic stay. I hope to stay at Riad Dar Soufa again.

reviews.author: Alissa Allan
reviews.text: Book this place! A beautiful riad with only six rooms. I loved how breakfast was included - a delicious daily feast of fresh fruit, local breads, and traditional Moroccan mint tea or coffee. The room (Hadid) was spacious and so clean. Each room has its own ensuite private bathroom. I believe all rooms now have air conditioning. They have a lovely sun terrace and the entire building has stunning architectural details. It’s in the heart of the Medina and we felt very safe walking through it. People didn’t bother us or aggressively sell to us even when we were walking solo. My only tip is to bring your own toiletries (eg soap, shampoo, conditioner, toothpaste, and shower gel). The ones they provided were small quantities. The staff were exceptionally friendly and kind. I’d stay here again in a second!

reviews.author: Faxon Bishop
reviews.text: When we walked into the riad I turned to my cousin and said now we're really in Morocco. It is beautiful and extremely comfortable. The service could have been better particularly from Idahmed Ayoub. We had a marvelous breakfast before we left and would recommend this hotel to anyone.

reviews.author: Shireen Ahmed
reviews.text: This was my favourite Riad (I stayed in three during my 7 day trip). Riad Kalaa was beautiful and quiet and well taken care of. Staff is friendly and accommodating.

reviews.author: julie bishop
reviews.text: Perfect location in the old city. Lovely atmosphere, pool, public rooms. Comfortable room with all modern conveniences. Great breakfast cooked to order Delightful staff especially if IAhmed ayoub!

reviews.author: Neil Broekhuizen
reviews.text: We were each booked into a "Suite Shatienne". These are described as large rooms, some with a large bathroom. We had 2 of the three rooms and the bathrooms were tidy. Advertised as 30m2, this icluded bathroom and wardrobe, actual room is c.16m2 and is tiny. It is also adverised as being on an internal courtyard. This is actually a busy, noisy restaurant, The only windows (which have no glass) open on the this courtyard and you are inches away from dinners - giving no privacy and a very claustrophobic feel. The building and courtyard are very beautifully restored but the rooms on the courtyyard are unacceptable as hottel rooms, let alone "suites" at this price. Too add to all this we came for breakfast at 7.30 (opening time) and had to wait 45 mins for coffee, still no food, We had to leave for the airport and they couldnt find a pproter to guides us out of the complex streets of the marina. This is the first time I have ever written a hotel revue, and I was very disappointed to finish our Moroccon experience here

reviews.author: Natasha Smoljak
reviews.text: Riad Kalaa is a wonderful choice for your stay in Rabat. The riad is elegant with very luxurious feel with very good value. We loved our Oriental Suite!

name: Street Stall - Bab El Had
address: Street Stall - Bab El Had, Rabat, Morocco

reviews.author: Douglas Langrehr
reviews.text: Well worth the visit. This old Kasbah has been turned into private housing but was originally the Fort which protected the entrance to the river. Take in the peaceful gardens and a mint tea at the cafe.

reviews.author: Habib
reviews.text: One of the UNESCO sites in Morocco with old houses and some magnificent huge doors. There are some good souvenirs shops and local artists paintings. Generally, there is nothing much to see and I am really disappointed as I heard a lot about it, but nice for walking at least. Unfortunately no cafés on top of the castle as it would be good for seating and beautiful scenery of the ocean.

reviews.author: Mana Salem
reviews.text: The Kasbah des Oudayas in Rabat is a place where time slows to a whisper. Tucked at the mouth of the Bou Regreg River, this 12th-century fortress feels like a secret the Atlantic Ocean has been keeping. Its walls, painted in shades of white and blue so crisp they mimic the sky, curve around narrow alleys paved with stones worn smooth by centuries of footsteps. Walking through Bab Oudaya, the main gate, is like stepping into a postcard—if postcards could carry the scent of orange blossoms from the Andalusian Gardens or the salty breeze rolling off the water. The kasbah isn’t a museum; it’s alive. Locals lean in doorways, children dart between walls draped in bougainvillea, and stray cats nap in sunlit patches. Climb to the terrace of Café Maure, where mint tea arrives sticky-sweet alongside almond pastries, and the view stretches across the river to Salé’s sand-colored skyline. Below, the river churns where fishermen haul in their catch, and surfers bob in the distance, waiting for waves. The quietest corners hide the most stories. The Museum of Moroccan Arts—a restored 17th-century house—displays faded carpets and daggers, but the real magic is outside. Wander until the sounds of the city fade, and you’ll find yourself at Plateforme du Sémaphore, where the horizon blurs between sea and sky. This isn’t just a historic site—it’s a feeling, one that lingers long after you’ve left.

reviews.author: Bonnie Kwong
reviews.text: A very relaxing place to walk around by the ocean. Be sure to take 15-20mins walk up to the top where you will have a panoramic view of the beach and the ocean.

reviews.author: Dounia Erreqassa
reviews.text: A beautiful and peaceful place full of history and charm. We really enjoyed walking through the narrow streets and taking in the stunning views.

reviews.author: kaira kaplinsky
reviews.text: The most magical Blue City in the world! Bucket list for all! The best time to explore without crowds is early morning right after sunrise. greeting sunsets at the Spanish mosque is a must, although be prepared for bugs😩😁

reviews.author: Nazim Lala
reviews.text: This is a beautiful town with very hospitable people. There aren't many sellers / hawkers constantly pestering you too but their wares, so you can really enjoy your stroll through town. We went later in the day when it cooled down a bit and there were fewer people in the streets.

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. Chefchaouen is a must-visit for photographers, art lovers, and anyone looking to experience Morocco’s laid-back and artistic side. Whether you’re exploring the picturesque alleys, enjoying a mint tea in a cozy café, or watching the sunset from a hilltop, every moment here feels magical.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: Beautiful city! I love the colors, the people, the food and most importantly the shops on the street😍 If you want to get away to the mountains for some peaceful time away from the city, I highly recommend spending two or three days in Chefchaouen!

reviews.author: Mourad Chafik
reviews.text: Chefchaouen’s medina is truly one of the most beautiful and peaceful places I’ve ever visited. The blue-washed walls, narrow alleys, and stunning doors create a dreamlike atmosphere that feels both relaxing and inspiring. Locals are friendly, the shops offer authentic handmade crafts, and there are plenty of cozy cafes to enjoy traditional Moroccan tea. It's the perfect place to wander without a map, discover hidden gems, and take amazing photos at every corner. Whether you're there for the colors, the culture, or just the peaceful vibe—Chefchaouen is unforgettable

reviews.author: Said Belowahed
reviews.text: Rabat is an amazing city to visit, There is a lot of places to see and enjoy, Hassan tower is an amazing place with the Shrine next to it, and view to river. The Mausoleum of Mohammed V is a mausoleum located on the opposite side of the Hassan Tower, on the Yacoub al-Mansour esplanade in Rabat, Morocco. It contains the tombs of the Moroccan king and his two sons, late King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah. The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah in Rabat, Morocco. It is located at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river opposite Salé. The Chellah or Shalla, is a medieval fortified Muslim necropolis located in the metro area of Rabat, Morocco, on the south side of the Bou Regreg estuary. The Phoenicians established a trading emporium at the site.

reviews.author: Jose Tavares
reviews.text: I really liked this medina, very little touristy and essentially frequented by the inhabitants of Rabat. while walking its streets I learned a lot about local habits. Inside the medina are some good restaurants, so you have to ask them why they are difficult to find. Medina very safe

reviews.author: Monsignore Catweasel
reviews.text: big old medina where you can buy a lot of different things. Mobile phones from all brands. Alot of different brands clothes shoes . Also in the have a nice food to get many meals and spices fom fastfood to cousine . There also many free shops where you buy anything handmade .

reviews.text: Nice place but street food charged me more because I was from a different country

reviews.text: Beautiful city , even though it is some times overcrowded but in most of the year it's a pleasant place to visit

reviews.author: Ben_glt 34

reviews.author: Hanna M
reviews.text: A souk as you'd imagine it. A lot of chatter and little substance. But despite everything, the people are very nice and friendly!

reviews.author: TheYvanbreizh
reviews.text: Souk not interesting.

reviews.author: Gratien pub (gpnam)
reviews.text: Just one place, tourist bus stopped, everything else being closed.

reviews.author: Ross Daniels
reviews.text: This is an absolutely fantastic place a bit of a labyrinth but so enjoyable with winding streets and multiple marketplaces and plenty of cafes and eating spots. Great atmosphere and one of the streets will take you down to the beach. We spent hours just wandering around and it’s up there with any marketplace in Morocco.

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: This has got to be the best souk in Morocco! I’ve been to many, but Essaouira’s felt so special. I spent about five hours there and still didn’t want to leave. Each shop has its own unique vibe, and the shopkeepers were incredibly kind and helpful. Every time I asked where to find something, they wouldn’t just point me in the direction—they’d actually walk me there and leave without the other shopkeepers noticing. It was such a genuine experience. You’ll find everything from handmade Moroccan teapots and beautiful tea glasses to breathtaking paintings and handmade rugs, linen clothing, genuine leather goods, and the most fragrant spices. If you’re looking for authentic treasures, this is the place!

reviews.author: Mohammed nurul Islam
reviews.text: Best place to shop in all city

reviews.author: Federica Preda
reviews.text: Beautiful and quaint! The shops are full of local souvenirs and for all budgets! Exceptional fish and real Argan oil! We will definitely return. A quiet city where you can reach everything on foot.

reviews.author: World Trip
reviews.text: A favorite ❤️ A truly delightful souk in the port city of Essaouira ✅ The climate is pleasant and the people are truly friendly!
