name: Street Stall - Casco Viejo
address: Street Stall - Casco Viejo, Bilbao, Spain

reviews.author: William Frankson
reviews.text: Good car park. Great location and easy access. Easy to pay and reasonable rates.

reviews.author: Geh Kah
reviews.text: Very small parking lots, but in the mid of the city

reviews.author: Mari jose Gago Silva
reviews.text: Ok

reviews.author: Iñigo Romon
reviews.text: Unbeatable location. Access and exit changed, you enter and exit from the left, it is strange especially when you are inside. Spaces not very wide but sufficient, with lights above that indicate availability with colors. Payment machines ok. It doesn't take a photo and that's it, you have to insert the ticket when you leave. Infected toilet. Nausea smell, dirt. That's why I give myself a 3 and not a 4.

reviews.author: MisterTSimmer S
reviews.text: The curves going up and down the floor are very narrow and it is sticky hot. But the price seems very correct to me. Regarding the comment that I have read here about "10 minutes is 2 euros", I must say that it is a lie like a cathedral and confuses future clients. I leave a photo of the receipt, so you can see that it is a lie, the car has been parked from 9 in the morning until 16:42 in the afternoon and as you can see it is "11.60 euros". If it were 2 euros for 10 minutes...do the calculation and you will see how stupid it is.

name: Street Stall - Plaza Nueva
address: Street Stall - Plaza Nueva, Bilbao, Spain

name: Street Stall - Plaza Unamuno
address: Street Stall - Plaza Unamuno, Bilbao, Spain

name: Street Stall - Ribera Market
address: Street Stall - Ribera Market, Bilbao, Spain

reviews.author: Jaquelina Sio
reviews.text: Lovely place to have pintxos (tapas) lunch. Food is fresh and delicious at a reasonable price! We went around 1pm wait time was short and we easily found a table to sit at.

reviews.author: samira mirzaei
reviews.text: Very nice market with plenty of tapas choice with really reasonable price (2.5€ per piece ) and I'm not sure if it's low season or whatever but it's not that crowded. If you find a table outdide as well it has a nice view over river and the colorful building next to it and enjoy the sun in the afternoon. It's so close to the old town where there are plenty of shops, restaurants bars and nice atmosphere in the city.

reviews.author: Danielle Thomson
reviews.text: Really cool market, loads of fresh seafood and meat, there’s a hall downstairs where you can get amazing pintox and wine (5 pintox and 2 glasses of wine for €17!)

reviews.author: Bondiamo
reviews.text: The La Ribera Market is one of the largest covered markets in Europe, built in 1929 beside the river. The floors of the vast hall are flooded with light from the large stained-glass windows. Here you will find local residents seeking out their favorite stall for fresh ingredients for meals at home or visiting one of the bars/restaurants for a meal or snack.

reviews.author: Lighthouse Tai Chi
reviews.text: A fascinating and interesting place to visit and walk around. Architecture and stained glass are lovely.

reviews.author: Ivan Top
reviews.text: What an amazing place…tartare,scallops and the fillet were amazing!maybe they should have an english menu!The waitress was super friendly and guide me through the menu!Amazing lunch

reviews.author: PaulS
reviews.text: My partner and I had the best meal here! Amazing salad, steak and wine feast. We highly recommend this restaurant. Thank you Adal for your warm hospitality!

reviews.author: Valentine Lauwers
reviews.text: Quick service and delicious crema catalana

reviews.author: Ave T
reviews.text: A quiet restaurant in the Mesa y Lopez shopping area. It has a bar space on the first floor and the restaurant in the basement. The decor is really great. We had our work Christmas dinner in El Pote and I have to say that the food was amazing. The dishes are a good size. The service is great too and the waiters are really friendly and help out when in doubt. Can't wait to be back!

reviews.author: Silvia Axt
reviews.text: Nice little Restaurant with very good food. Most of the waiters don't speak english but the are very kind and helpful. Thanks for 2 nice evenings.

name: Bar La Buena Vida
address: Bar La Buena Vida, Granada, Spain

reviews.author: Chen Jerry
reviews.text: Had a very nice experience here until tonight. We ordered a set menu for two, which was a bit of a disappointment. The inside of the fried shrimps were still cold. Calamari was overcooked. Other dishes we had days before were great in general.

reviews.author: Alan G
reviews.text: Stopped off for some lunch here. Ordered a beer & a coke zero, which came with a free tapas with each drink. We chose the pate & the meatballs, which were delicious. We also ordered a patatas brava dish & a Spanish tortilla with salad. These were also very good. Nice place to eat & food served quickly.

reviews.author: Clayton Demski
reviews.text: La Buena Vida tapas bar is a wonderful tapas bar in Granada! The staff is young and friendly, and their portions of tapas plates are substantial! So much so that I filled up on just drinks and complementary tapas each time I've visited! Their montaditos (mini sandwiches) are tasty and come with potatoes or chips. The albondigas (meatballs) were delicious and served with bread and potatoes, and the Carne en salsa was hearty chunks of braised meat with potatoes and sauce. The tostada with goat cheese and caramelized onion was also delicious, as are the boquerones (fried anchovies). The drinks are affordable and tasty as well! I will certainly be returning for tapas and drinks!

reviews.author: Mina Tahaei
reviews.text: Extremely cheap with very good food. A super small local place that is great for dining before exploring in the city, and tapas comes free with any drink that you order. The gazpacho and croquettes very very delicious and the cafe itself is very aesthetically pleasing.

reviews.author: clive hewett
reviews.text: Found this venue quite by chance… we were told this was the street to be on for food (Calla Elvira) but weren’t told where to go. It’s now 10pm on a Monday night and it’s rammed! The general premise is order a drink (no cocktails or hot drinks) and receive a free tapa (tapas if you prefer). Very reasonably priced and the food, especially when you begin to go Andalusian, is excellent.

reviews.author: Rémi Ligez
reviews.text: We loved this tapas bar! Every drink came with a free tapas of our choice. The staff was really nice, would recommend 10/10. Make sure to bring cash at they don't take cards! [June 2025]

reviews.author: Khaled Haj Hamed
reviews.text: a great experience! They offer delicious vegetarian and Halal tapas, and their Portuguese salt cod tapas were truly exceptional. The bartender was also incredibly kind and welcoming, which made the visit even more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Dionne Chen
reviews.text: What a special place. Amazing vibes, super cozy, great food, and all around stellar place. Must go if you’re in Granada. It is cash only so keep that in mind. But the sauces and tenderness of the chicken… need to go back!

reviews.author: Geneieve Sarah Teo
reviews.text: Delicious hot food! Love that our food came piping hot in the little ceramic plates. Everything was great but the spicy chicken liver with coriander & spicy piri-piri pork stew were exceptional 👍🏻 it comes with rice and has a kick to it. SUPER YUMS! Plus, every drink order comes with a free tapas too!

reviews.author: Skin Dude
reviews.text: Our favourite type of bar to find in a new town. Full of punters having a great time with a great vibe. No music as it was hard to hear yourselves above the chatter but all the better for that. Great free tapas with every drink you have and you get to choose from a superb little menu. Run by an Englishman and his wife, I think, who certainly work very hard to make this place into a PROPER BAR! FAB!

reviews.author: Cemre Kırım
reviews.text: The tapas on the tabla were delicious, but the homemade croquettes were definitely our favorite! We came here after hearing they serve their own barrel vermouth it was nice, though not drastically different from others I’ve tried. The place was lively and bustling during lunchtime. You can eat standing at the bar or seated at one of the side tables. The complimentary tapa that came with the first drink (I think it was paella) was really tasty. They don’t serve another free tapa if you order food with your second drink. Overall, a fun and enjoyable stop!

reviews.author: Berk İlhan
reviews.text: it’s an old established Granada institute, both locals and tourist enjoy. The space has a soul, and its lively. The staff were kind and attentive. They have a large selection of food and drinks. We savored the food. Fresh and good quality ingredients and well made. When you get drinks they bring some appetizers on the house which is a Granada tapa bar culture. Bueno bueno. It was around €35 for 2 vermouth + 2 beers + 1 hot mixed tapas plate for two.

reviews.author: berkay atici
reviews.text: It was good to eat outside on the street. How ever, I must say that the platter (meat and cheese) was average, and we had much bigger expectations, as this place has a lot of reviews here on google. As drinks, we ordered vermouth and sangria, and sangria was unfortunately bad. I couldn’t finish it. In addition, there were too many scratches in the cutlery & plate, and they did not seem very clean.

reviews.author: Mary Christianson
reviews.text: We had such a great evening here with lovely tapas, sangría, and vermut, and a fantastic waitress. But the next day, we stepped inside to ask if it was possible to get a table, and a waiter walked up and yelled at us angrily; I'm afraid my Spanish is not good enough to understand him quickly, so within 20 seconds we got yelled at again. Apparently there were other entrance(s), and a place to get in line. I wouldn't feel comfortable going there again.

reviews.author: M Briggs
reviews.text: The bar was recommended on a Web page and I'm so glad we looked for it. Was busy as we expected but managed to get a standing table. Free tapas with our drink and we order 3 others. Great food, atomosphere, staff very attentive and prices great. Would definately recommend popping in.

reviews.author: Qing Lei
reviews.text: The food is absolutely delicious. We ordered the black seafood rice , and the flavors of the seafood blended perfectly with the rice, creating a wonderfully harmonious dish. The duck meat is incredibly tender, and when paired with truffle, it creates a rich and delightful flavor combination. All other food is great. Our server Miguel is really great. We had a very good experience.

reviews.author: Fatma Erdogan
reviews.text: After a tiring day exploring the Alhambra, we had a fantastic meal here. We tried the seafood noodles and their amazing soufflé — both were absolutely delicious. Special thanks to our waiters Paco and Miguel for their warm hospitality and great recommendations. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Paul Baumann
reviews.text: Very nice and strategically located. Great terrace. Very friendly and service-oriented. The tuna was great as well as the Poke bowl. Make a stop for lunch or diner when you are in Granada

reviews.author: Leonard Lache
reviews.text: Exceptional restaurant in downtown Granada. Food is absolutely delicious and while not quite cheap, it is staggering in quality and presentation. Love this place. Make sure to try the signature chocolate desert. Muchas gracias to Alex and Kaue for the outstanding service and superb attitude!

reviews.author: Vargosz Bandi
reviews.text: Top class staff, super helpful and nice attitude, tapas is amazing, all food well made and served. My favourite place to go every night for a drink! Say hello to Shanty, top guy!

reviews.author: Luca Arbore
reviews.text: The food was delicious. We took a red wine that was full of flavour. As the mains, we took the risotto with octopus and bolleto mushrooms, it was the best I have ever eaten, the grilled octopus, and the pork with pumpkin puree. I recommend these dishes. The service was friendly and nice. The atmosphere was peaceful, an oasis full of verdure with a fountain in the middle.

reviews.author: Julia Analena Hollmann
reviews.text: LOVED this restaurant! Been to Granada many times, but I must say this is my favourite restaurant. Not too touristy, located in the beautiful and quiet Albayzín, we loved the flavourful and freshly prepared food, the beautiful terrace, the interiors, the music, and the staff were friendly and well-mannered. Our lovely waitress was Sara. Also fantastic that smoking is banned on the terrace, as well. That way you can enjoy a relaxed meal even outside. Thanks for the lovely time❤️

reviews.author: denisa rafalowski
reviews.text: Lovely restaurant with outdoor romantic setting. Fountains and views or patio with garden. The daily specials are great. Nice wine choices. Not mind blowing but solid regional cooking. I actually did not like their bread but the olive oil was stellar. Caesar was tasty mustard ? non traditional dressing. I had blown out my knee that day so I did a few shots with wine so here ate the pics as details went south!

reviews.author: Olenka Elena Gorochko
reviews.text: We had such a great time in this peaceful courtyard, surrounded by beautiful plants and the relaxing sound of fountains—it was a treat for both the taste buds and the soul. The food was amazing! We had the wild boar and grilled octopus, and both were super tasty and well presented. You can really feel the love for cooking that Jesús Pernía got from his mom and grandma. The service was also excellent—friendly, warm, and attentive from start to finish. Coming back to try other dishes tonight. There are three different areas to enjoy your meal: the cozy indoor space, the lush garden courtyard, and the terraza with a beautiful view. If you’d like a table with a view of the terraza, we definitely recommend making a reservation in advance—it’s worth it! Thanks so much for the warm hospitality! Lots of love from Ukraine and Romania.

reviews.author: Emily Edwards
reviews.text: Delicious food in a beautiful setting. Yes, you will pay a bit more, but it’s not just for the view. After stuffing our faces with potatoes, cheese and egg while tapeando, having a carefully thought out meal was a delight. They have several vegetarian options, including a creamy turmeric pasta with tofu.

name: La Tetería del Bañuelo
address: La Tetería del Bañuelo, Granada, Spain

reviews.author: Jamie O'Donnell
reviews.text: Beautiful spaces inside and out on the patio. The patio has lovely views of the Alhambra. The food is delicious. We shared a Crepe with banana and chocolate. Loved the coffee with condensed milk. Amazing selection of teas! Even more delightful is the cat! April 8, 2025 C & J

reviews.author: ياسمين
reviews.text: A wonderful place to enjoy Moroccan tea in a beautiful, relaxing setting with a stunning view of the Alhambra from the terrace. They open at 12:00 PM and offer a variety of teas. We chose the green tea with mint and orange (called Granada Tea), and we loved it! They also serve Arabic desserts. The waiter was very professional, friendly and was extremely helpful. I highly recommend this place and will definitely return to try other types of tea.

reviews.author: HardBurger
reviews.text: It has a very beautiful view and an interesting Arabic atmosphere and tasty tea.

reviews.author: Shiva N
reviews.text: Great tea and dessert with great views! The tea is very strong so I would ask for more hot water at some point. Do not get the Arabic coffee it’s Terrible.

reviews.author: Luca Arbore
reviews.text: Everyone was very nice and welcoming. We took a load of baklava, which was delicious. The view was amazing. One of the workers took us even higher, and we saw an adorable cat. I definitely recommend coming here. Do yourself a favour and order a Moroccon style tea.

reviews.author: DNA K
reviews.text: This place was fantastic!! You must go here when in Granada. We hardly spent money, but left so full. They offer amazing tapes dishes with every drink. We only ordered 2 paid dishes and the large beers which we were worried if they were very expensive beers. It turns out was the cheapest in the world, 2.8 euro!!! The waiters were also great and very quick service. On top of that, they offered a shot at the end for free, of course 😵 The high table is not very comfortable and there is no option for your bags other than keep them on your lap so go there with no shopping or large bags. I would love to return.

reviews.author: J Seeb
reviews.text: Good place to dine! We decided to eat here based on the reviews. We did decide to get there early 7 pm, and it was a good decision because later in the evening many people stayed outside waiting for a table. We ordered a variety of dishes to get a good idea of the quality and taste. All dishes tasted good. But I was disappointed about the consistency of the oxtail in peppers. It was more like a glue/dough in texture very off putting, taste was not bad. But would not order or recommend to eat. Service was nice but inconsistent on how quickly things arrived. Initially fast than we had to wait quite some time for water and other dishes or the bill. Atmosphere is nice and good for people watching, it seems to be a very popular place on the busy shopping street.

reviews.author: C Portillo
reviews.text: Great place. We went to two of their locations and the food was great at both. They have the best salmorejo on the planet! I had to go back and have it one more time. We enjoyed all the other dishes too. Their prices are reasonable. The service was good and the waiters were attentive.

reviews.author: Rashid Al-Saffar
reviews.text: After reading some great reviews, we decided to give this restaurant a shot, and we’re so glad we did! The atmosphere was lovely, the place was spotless, and the staff were super polite and friendly. The food was fantastic, and the presentation was impressive! We tried a variety of dishes, including a famous Spanish dish, and everything was delicious. Overall, it was a wonderful experience that we really enjoyed!

reviews.author: Eric Lin
reviews.text: I stayed in Granada for three days and chose Los Manueles for all three dinners. Overall, my experience was mixed. First, I was pleasantly surprised that I could easily get a table without a reservation and without waiting in line, which was different from many reviews that described the restaurant as crowded. The process was straightforward, and the service was highly efficient—my food arrived in less than 20 minutes. For reference, on the first day, I dined at 9:30 p.m., while on the following two days, it was around 5:00 p.m. Additionally, the Iberian pork I had on the first day was absolutely divine. Although the fries beneath the pork were soaked in oil and completely soggy, which made them a bit unpleasant to eat, I had rarely tasted such delicious pork before. The oxtail and peppers I tried on the second day were also delightful, as was the fried octopus on the third day. However, none of these dishes gave me the same level of amazement as the Iberian pork. Unfortunately, there were also some disappointments. First, the English proficiency of the staff varied greatly, which is understandable. The lady who served me on the first day spoke excellent English, but on the next two days, the staff barely spoke any English, making ordering quite complicated. Of course, a large part of the issue was my lack of Spanish, but given the restaurant's reputation, I had hoped for a higher level of language support. While I also wish to have a sparkling san gria, which is just a minor reccomandation. More importantly, I must criticize the service attitude, especially on the third day. If my first two experiences had made me eager to give Los Manueles a solid five-star rating, the poor service on the third day was the reason I ultimately settled on three stars. To start, while I again got a table easily, I clearly noticed small bugs crawling on my plate along with black stains. When I tried to ask for a replacement, the waiter seemed unable to understand what I was saying, so I had no choice but to swap my plate with one from a nearby empty table. Additionally, for some reason, I did not receive the complimentary cheese and olives that I had enjoyed on the previous two days. While this was just a small extra perk, I noticed that I seemed to be the only table that did not receive them, especially when the restaurant was not particularly busy at the time. The most frustrating part came when I tried to order padrón peppers. I had checked multiple times that the restaurant offered this dish, but I had trouble locating it on the menu. When I asked, the waitress rudely told me that they no longer served it. However, what infuriated me was that, as I was preparing to leave, I clearly saw several other tables being served the padrón peppers I had requested. This left me feeling extremely disappointed.

name: Street Stall - Campo del Príncipe
address: Street Stall - Campo del Príncipe, Granada, Spain

name: Street Stall - Mirador San Nicolás
address: Street Stall - Mirador San Nicolás, Granada, Spain

reviews.author: James Ludwig
reviews.text: This is the best place in Granada for a panoramic view of the Alhambra. It’s spectacular. I arrived in the morning while it was cool and not crowded. About 10:30 the crowds start arriving. The view at night is reputed to be beautiful but it’s very crowded at sunset.

reviews.author: 貝瑞克（Markpigpapa）
reviews.text: It’s a good location to view Alhambra, also very busy at evening, everyone has been told this is the best spot to view Alhambra when the lights are on. It becomes more popular because of the South Korean TV romance drama, you can see a lot of East Asian. It’s not a long walk uphill from the busy street, maybe 15 minutes if you are a walker, but it will be challenging if you walk during the day when it is hot. The view is worthy. And it’s free.

reviews.author: Nikos Tsirakis
reviews.text: Possibly one of the most dramatic scenes I have seen... Full of vibes, colors, people and music. Just imagine an incredible view of Alhambra, in the background the almost all year long mountains of Sierra Nevada and then Granada city as seen from above. Must visit and you will not regret it!

reviews.author: Andrew Duggan
reviews.text: It's a solid twenty minute walk uphill to get to the viewpoint, but you are a rewarded with a wonderful view of the Alhambra and the Sierra Nevada mountains. The view is prettier at sunset, but the crowds are also thicker. Nice to see the sunset and then go down to the river and walk alongside it back into town at night.

reviews.author: Phuc Tran
reviews.text: A simple Muslim church with gentle simplicity, solemnity, and wonder. It makes me calm my heart to have a little peace and a special invisible connection. It's not a simple church but also a real spirit, the testimony of time of history. The ticket is 3£ but you get the gorgeous view on the top of the church ⛪️ I enjoy it very much Highly recommended!

name: Street Stall - Plaza Larga
address: Street Stall - Plaza Larga, Granada, Spain

name: Street Stall - Plaza Nueva
address: Street Stall - Plaza Nueva, Granada, Spain

reviews.author: Faby Fischbein
reviews.text: We planned a stop in Madrid just to visit this restaurant. I made reservations a year in advance, and it was so worth it! The service experience was top-notch from beginning to end. Our main goal was to try the succulent pig, and it didn't disappoint. (Simply delicious) I also recommend the sangria and the garlic shrimp. The calamari was not our favorite. We have had better, but it's just our opinion. Our server, Paco, was amazing. A genuine person! I strongly recommend this restaurant if you ever visit Madrid.

reviews.author: J van der L
reviews.text: We had a great lunch with the family at the oldest restaurant in the world. Read a lot of reviews but can truly say that the somewhat higher prices are definitely worth it. The dishes, including the famous suckling pig, were all very tasty. There are a lot of staff who work all together like an oiled machine. They are quick and friendly and make you feel welcome. I can recommend this place and if you want to have a special dinner/lunch just go for it but make a reservation on time.

reviews.author: Aneesh Vaghadia
reviews.text: Sobrino de Botin, established in 1725, holds the Guinness World Record for oldest restaurant, and they have used that time to make food the right way! It’s very popular, so we could only get an 11:00pm reservation. When we walked in, there was a live band playing Spanish guitar. We were seated in the basement which had a dramatic ambiance. The staircase is steep and not ideal for those with disabilities but the restaurant was made 300 years ago, so you cannot criticize them! The service was excellent. The waiters are all wearing white jackets and serve you with old world elegance. We had the signature suckling pig which was delicious! The skin was crispy and the meat was soft and juicy. We enjoyed it with sangria, mixed grilled vegetables and salad Botin as well. Before you leave, you can view the ancient wine cellar, accessible down another staircase from the basement. There are no lights and it is extremely dusty. I would not recommend touching anything for fear of picking up an ancient bacterial infection. Overall, the restaurant is a piece of Spanish history with a classic dish and excellent service!

reviews.author: Amy Woedl
reviews.text: What is not to love about dining in the oldest restaurant in the world! Reservations a must! The service was impeccable from the doorman to the wait-staff. Fresh bread, delicious salad and the steaks were cooked to perfection. The tunas performers playing through the restaurant were amazing and added to the lively atmosphere and fun. I booked our reservation nearly 10 months in advance, before any of the rest of our trip to Spain was planned, and I am so happy I did! If you are planning a trip to Madrid- book the table!

reviews.author: Laurie Minto
reviews.text: So happy we decided to go to the oldest restaurant in the World, as the experience and food was exceptional. Across our table we had the signature suckling pig, garlic prawns, veal fillet and mixed vegetables, with all dishes being a delight to eat. We also enjoyed their Sangria and finished by sharing the amazing cheesecake, yum! We got in without a booking, however, making a reservation in advance is probably the best way to ensure you get, as it got really busy while we were there. The service was great, with English being spoken by many of the staff. Our waiter was excellent, adding to the dining experience. Eating here is not a gimmick, it’s a quality restaurant well worth the visit!!

reviews.author: Keta Maziashvili
reviews.text: Absolutely loved our experience at Casa Lucio! The food was incredibly delicious, the atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the service was top-notch. I’d especially like to thank Giorgi, a Georgian staff member, who made our visit even more enjoyable with his kind attitude and professionalism. Highly recommended if you’re in Madrid!

reviews.author: Eddy Semaan
reviews.text: I went there on a Saturday evening for dinner. Staff are very welcoming. The owner Marian was very welcoming and nice. She knows how to run this restaurant. The restaurant is beautiful, amazing design and comfortable seats. The food was 10/10. The desert was amazing. I ordered pain perdu with ice cream. Don’t come to Madrid without trying it.

reviews.author: Yizhou Wu
reviews.text: If you're a serious foodie, you might want to consider my opinion The tripe stew (callos a la madrileña) was stellar and a must try. It's not just tripe theres also pig skin and tendons all for a great collagen mess. All were reduced to mad sticky goodness and for someone who loves tripe, this is the stickiest stew I've had. Yes it's on the mild side but it goes w the free olives. Also, because it's so full of collagen it's really quite surfeiting after half a plate and I recommend you share this dish Rice pudding had a nice aroma from orange zest and good crunch from the sugar but otherwise it was average On the other hand, the eggs are really not it for the price. Yes it's good, it's tender and there's a nice aroma from the olive oil but there's no way you should pay 15€ for eggs and chips. That's crazy and the taste wasn't memorable The oxtail stew was also good but not great. They got it to be very tender and fall off the bone, but it's not cooked in a sauce and so it's quite mild. They were super nice to share a slice of jamon w me. It's got good complexity If you come, come for the tripe stew which is a must try, and don't take other risks. Maybe the jamon only if u must

reviews.author: Adam Binder
reviews.text: Great experience! They were very helpful with the food selection and drink selections! We had the Lamb Shin and the Monk fish, both were really good! The lamb was so tender and most! 🤤🤤 The wines were fantastic and as usual, very affordable! Going back for lunch to try the ox tail and other items!

reviews.author: Maria Margarita de Jesus
reviews.text: New Spanish restaurant discovery! Casa Lucio in Centro! There’s many new restaurants now however it’s still nice to just have the basic traditional classics!! Yummy huevos rotos and garlic soup

reviews.author: alex bonick
reviews.text: Well known "modern" or "gastro" restaurant, from a famous chef? Don't believe the hype - or the bad reviews. It is definitely a modern palate or cuisine here. Nothing amazing though, we think it caters to tourists. But if you're in the area, at the Prado or El Retiro, etc - it's worth a stop. We had bacon artichoke hearts (not pictured), a strawberry gazpacho, Spanish cod, and cheesecake.

reviews.author: Zornitsa Valkanova
reviews.text: The first place in Madrid that had poor service and not fresh food. We had to remind them for our order, the waiter did not speak any English and could not explain the dish they had on the menu. The worst was the quality of the pork presa meal - very hard meat (almost impossible to chew), sour mushrooms as if taken out from a jar with pickles and some spongy potatoes inside again not freshly prepared at all. It was served hardly warmed up. And the price was 25 euro for the dish...

reviews.author: Irene Walshe
reviews.text: Nice gastrobar for tapas with a twist and modern presentation. We had a wonderful Salmorejo with strawberries, the Boquerones( I don't like that they serve them on top of lots of chips, but it's ok) the fried squid sandwich (it needed a bit more sauce or a slice of lemmon), and we finished woth the chocolate lava. I recommend this place if you are near the Prado Museum.

reviews.author: Simon Jones
reviews.text: Nice traditional Spanish tortilla with an onion filling. Seven euros and served on a small cast iron frying pan which was nice. Just enough for lunch before a visit to the nearby art museum.

reviews.author: Leigh Jenkins
reviews.text: Delicious food and kind staff! The fruit dessert was so good we returned for it the next evening!

reviews.author: Jin
reviews.text: This is a traditional restaurant with over a century of history, specializing in stewed pot dishes. To be honest, as a foreign traveler, I found the flavors a bit difficult to get used to. However, this is purely a matter of personal taste and has nothing to do with the restaurant itself. Still, I made an effort to finish everything out of respect for the chef and the food. I believe that part of the joy of traveling is experiencing local cuisine at long-established, traditional restaurants.

reviews.author: Nicole Sarmiento
reviews.text: The perfect cocido to have to end the winter season! Superb cocido. It wasn’t too heavy nor too little. Soup was so good too! We also had a vegetable entree to start which was one of the best I’ve had in Madrid. Dessert was an apple tart with turrones ice cream!! Definitely would come here even during the summer because not only was food superb, the service was 100%

reviews.author: Alan Siu Kuen Wong
reviews.text: Strongly recommend. Very good food especially their stew. One portion is good for 2 people. Reservation is a must. Lamb is excellent. A reminder: keep a copy of your reservation email because they missed our reservation at our arrival.

reviews.author: Saul Berrios
reviews.text: Historic place! Very blessed for the opportunity to be able to enjoy lunch there. We just walked in there believing that we could find a table. For our surprise, the person the received us said that was unprovable to sit us, but anyway she consulted with an emerging gentleman that joined the conversation, telling us that the only chance was to wait for about 1.5 to 2 hours. Then; thanks God the last consult was done to our afternoon hero. This senior waitress gave us the best smile on the city along with a service that we will never forget. Yes, he found the way to sit us and in addition was very supportive and gentle, giving us the most charm service during our visit to the city.

reviews.author: Hassan Gonzalez Otero
reviews.text: Delicious cocido madrileño ! Authentic restaurant. Good service. Recommended.

reviews.author: Jin
reviews.text: This is a traditional restaurant with over a century of history, specializing in stewed pot dishes. To be honest, as a foreign traveler, I found the flavors a bit difficult to get used to. However, this is purely a matter of personal taste and has nothing to do with the restaurant itself. Still, I made an effort to finish everything out of respect for the chef and the food. I believe that part of the joy of traveling is experiencing local cuisine at long-established, traditional restaurants.

reviews.author: Nicole Sarmiento
reviews.text: The perfect cocido to have to end the winter season! Superb cocido. It wasn’t too heavy nor too little. Soup was so good too! We also had a vegetable entree to start which was one of the best I’ve had in Madrid. Dessert was an apple tart with turrones ice cream!! Definitely would come here even during the summer because not only was food superb, the service was 100%

reviews.author: Alan Siu Kuen Wong
reviews.text: Strongly recommend. Very good food especially their stew. One portion is good for 2 people. Reservation is a must. Lamb is excellent. A reminder: keep a copy of your reservation email because they missed our reservation at our arrival.

reviews.author: Saul Berrios
reviews.text: Historic place! Very blessed for the opportunity to be able to enjoy lunch there. We just walked in there believing that we could find a table. For our surprise, the person the received us said that was unprovable to sit us, but anyway she consulted with an emerging gentleman that joined the conversation, telling us that the only chance was to wait for about 1.5 to 2 hours. Then; thanks God the last consult was done to our afternoon hero. This senior waitress gave us the best smile on the city along with a service that we will never forget. Yes, he found the way to sit us and in addition was very supportive and gentle, giving us the most charm service during our visit to the city.

reviews.author: Hassan Gonzalez Otero
reviews.text: Delicious cocido madrileño ! Authentic restaurant. Good service. Recommended.

name: Mercado de San Antón
address: Mercado de San Antón, Madrid, Spain

reviews.author: Ricardo Llovet
reviews.text: And old food market place converted into a gourmet food court. There is a good number of small shops serving their specialties, from traditional Spanish tapas and tortillas to Asian stuff and seafood. These little joints cohabitate with a few remaining shops like Octavio, one of the very best charcuteries in Madrid. I had the menu of the day "menu del dia" in the restaurant located in the upper floor. Food was good and the service too. There was ample space between tables which favored mi lively conversation with two old friends. I plan to visit them again in my next trip to Madrid.

reviews.author: Chris Perry
reviews.text: This place is situated in the trendy and gay area of Madrid called Cuenca. Mercado San Anton is much less crowded than Mercado San Miguel and way less touristy. Lots of wonderful food options.

reviews.author: Ori Atias
reviews.text: I arrived at the complex by accident, there are lots of food stalls there at different prices and with quite a large variety. It is very worth going, especially for lunch, there is also a large variety of food from tapas to Japanese food. Excellent!

reviews.author: Dan Messenger
reviews.text: Cool spot to stop a grab a bite to eat and a drink. There’s something for everyone; from tapas, to seafood to bao buns. With beers and aperol spritz you’ll stay refreshed as well. It could do with more toilets, the queue got quite long.

reviews.author: Paolo Kastelec
reviews.text: In the heart of Chueca thus local market with food as well on the top floors . Food like , tapas pinchos , tortillas, calamari’s etc etc . We went on a Monday so it was not too crowded .

name: Street Stall - Gran Vía
address: Street Stall - Gran Vía, Madrid, Spain

reviews.author: Kaushal Bhatt
reviews.text: Lively and fun! Enjoyed visiting this place where you find almost everything from food, clothes and luxury. Recommended to visit

reviews.author: The Master
reviews.text: Amazing place , full of markets and boutiques , many choices of restaurants.. great vibes

reviews.author: Sujay Sreekumar
reviews.text: One of the best streets in Madrid. Amazing architecture all around, top brand outlets, restaurants, casino, all great vibes. A must visit area in Madrid. We came here around 4pm and the place was buzzing and all lively even then. Do visit! I recommend

reviews.author: nino kapanadze
reviews.text: I started exploring Madrid from Gran Via and I really liked it, it adds grandeur and beauty to the city!

reviews.author: Geovanny
reviews.text: Gran Vía's basically Madrid's flashy main street, packed with cool old buildings, tons of shops, and all the best theaters!

name: Street Stall - Mercado San Miguel
address: Street Stall - Mercado San Miguel, Madrid, Spain

reviews.author: Arnab Pal
reviews.text: Prepare for a culinary adventure at this lively tapas market! While it's pricier than a traditional local market, the extensive selection more than compensates. This sought-after experience is perfect for anyone discovering the city, whether it's your inaugural visit or you're a returning explorer. Indulge in an incredible array of offerings, including pristine seafood, seasonal local produce, a vast assortment of meats, exquisite wines, and every other food imaginable. With so many tantalizing choices, one visit simply won't be enough!

reviews.author: Renae Leith-Manos
reviews.text: What a brilliant market in Madrid. One of the worlds best with incredibly fresh tapas inching meats, cheeses, and every tapas you could imagine. Affordable too. Both cocktails and wines were excellent and very cheap. A fantastic atmosphere-bustling with people and laughter

reviews.author: Henry Suzuki
reviews.text: If you are craving for the great food from all over Madrid, this is the perfect location for you. Be hungry! If you are new to area, then seafood canape are great there. You can also get cooked food as well. Oysters are tasty and fresh as it just arrived. Wines are great. You can start from sparkling all the way up to many types of wines there! If you are American Express Card holder, be aware that some places ONLY accept Visa / Master / Cash. Enjoy your time there!

reviews.author: Sharbel Macaron
reviews.text: Amazing food experience. Lots of great options to choose from. We visited this place multiple times during our stay in Madrid. It’s busy but you can easily find a high table or a a corner to eat. The space is air conditioned which keeps it ambient. Highly recommended for foodies.

reviews.author: Karina Adianto
reviews.text: During our stay in Madrid, we went to this Mercado twice. It's because we love it too much! Although the size of the Mercado wasn't too big, there were many choices of food we could try. We could find any seating because it was too crowded. So we ate while standing up. Definitely worth the visit. It's a must go when you're in Madrid!

name: Street Stall - Plaza Mayor
address: Street Stall - Plaza Mayor, Madrid, Spain

reviews.author: Richard Fodor
reviews.text: The food, the service and everything was absolute PERFECTION. We had a group of 12 on Sunday evening (08/06) that we booked ahead of time. The staff was very attentive, friendly and the food was out of this world. The restaurant is very traditional and has a lovely charm to it. I personally felt guilty of not being able to finish my main dish it was that good. If I could give them 10 stars I would! Thank you to everyone who made our evening a very memorable and amazing!

reviews.author: Joseph Balsamo
reviews.text: Delicious food and great service in a traditional setting. The shrimp were incredible! Friendly staff and relaxed pace made for a great experience overall.

reviews.author: Bruce Taylor
reviews.text: We were a group of 7 and had lunch in an attractive small private dining room. We hadn't been here for a long time and were impressed with the quality. We were regular customers in the mid-1970´s when it was run personally by Padre Luis Lezama. His legacy lives on.

reviews.author: lenswork4
reviews.text: This place has been on my radar for years. I stopped in for lunch on a busy Sunday but was a little early. Managed to get a great table just inside past the bar. The classic Spanish dishes here are authentic and delicious. Garlic shrimp and rabo de toro both cooked and presented perfectly! A selection of tapas from the bar makes the meal complete. Also, plenty of wine to choose from. Service is professional. As we were finishing, the place was full, so go early and enjoy.

reviews.author: Dan Naveh
reviews.text: What a gem! On Christmas it was hard to find a place to eat. By chance, we chose this place. And what a pleasant surprise!! This is an establishment with history and it shows. From the moment we stepped in, through the pictures on the walls and the transparent kitchen. The dishes were very tasty, not overpriced and beautiful. We were too full for desserts, but received one, on the house, and it was delicious. We had cured salmon to share as a starter, lamb chops and ox tail as main, water, soda and a glass of red wine. Total 95 euros. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Chris Clement
reviews.text: This is a very pleasant, cosy, historic restaurant, apparently the second oldest in Madrid, with beautiful tiled walls. The service was friendly and helpful. The menu was has a good variety of dishes. I started with the largest slice of tomato I’ve ever seen - it was delicious. My main course was Iberian ham and eggs, also excellent. I finished by indulging in a very good hazelnut ice cream. I recommend all of these dishes, and the rest of the menu also looked great.

reviews.author: Hazal Şenel
reviews.text: We visited as a family on April 9th. These were the best meals we've ever had. Anna was very sweet and helped us a lot with the service, choices, and the history of the tavern. The other waiters were also equally friendly and helpful. If you happen to be around in Madrid, be sure to come and try their food and wines.

reviews.author: Julio C Morejon
reviews.text: We had such a wonderful dining experience at La Taberna Carmencita. The service was wonderful and the menu selection is a mix of traditional taste with a modern presentation. The Tarta Tatin dessert is worth the preparation. Reservations recommended as it is a popular place.

reviews.author: Eylul Sarer
reviews.text: My boyfriend still reminisces about these tomatoes even 7 months later. He describes them as ‘the kind that encapsulate the world within.’ Paired with a glass of vermut, this place offers a nice lunch break. The vibrant, tasteful tiles add an extra layer of charm to the experience. I’m not entirely convinced about the price-performance ratio; it feels a bit overpriced. Additionally, there’s a noticeable language barrier and a hint of an eye-roll attitude toward tourists.

reviews.author: Eleftheria Thravalou
reviews.text: We visited the restaurant as it was recommended from a friend as "the best place to eat paella". The food was mediocre to absolutely horrendous. Pricey and flavourless. The worst paella we've eaten. Runny, mushy, flavourless. A huge tomato for 18 euros. The only flavorful item on the menu was the cheese balls. The veal overly salty. The service at least was good and the decor was very authentic. But overall, food wise it was really bad.

reviews.author: Maria Theresa Cruciol
reviews.text: I had a great experience at Taberna La Daniela Cuchilleros on a Sunday evening. The restaurant wasn’t too full, so I got to enjoy a relaxed atmosphere while sitting at the bar. I ordered callos and croqueta de cocido, and both were absolutely amazing—rich in flavor and perfectly prepared! I also had a beer and vermut, which paired really well with the food. Even though I was by myself, I felt very comfortable and enjoyed the experience. If you’re in Madrid and looking for authentic Spanish flavors, I highly recommend this place!

reviews.author: Andrea Mitrović
reviews.text: My favorite restaurant in Madrid! ❤️ I love everything about it. I come to this place whenever I’m in Madrid and I always order the same dish - Secreto Ibérico.

reviews.author: María Alejandra Jaramillo Giraldo
reviews.text: Service is so bad that it makes the food taste bad. The worse service I have had in a long time. Both of the waiters were super rude. I guess the Callos were “ok” but they didn’t taste good due to the horrible environment inside this place.

reviews.author: Martha Blackmer
reviews.text: The food was delicious but too much for one person. We told the waiter that we were going to share and he said that it was fine, however when the bill arrived they charged for every person, something that truly surprised us! We couldn’t even eat half of the food!!! Very disappointed with the bill

reviews.author: Christoph Sinarak
reviews.text: After a long stroll through La Latina we found this nice restaurant on the way back to the Plaza Mayor. We ordered patata bravas, blood sausage, the chickpea stew and octopus. Everything tasted delicious and the octopus was perfectly executed. Usually I use salt scarcely in my cooking. Especially the octopus was a little bit too salty for me (but still delicious!). But this is not an issue with this place alone. Like I mentioned I use little salt in general and I had the feeling that the local cuisine in madrid uses more salt than other countries (I visited so far). I just wanted to make clear that this is a personal opinion and I'd still visit the Taberna de La Daniela again. I would probably ask for less salt where it can be avoided. But like I said this means every restaurant we went to during our stay in madrid. Our waiter was friendly and understood englisch without issue. I quite like the ambience because of the traditional setting with the colored tiles and so on. I think we paid around 50 euro for our meal incl Sangria. We had a nice evening and can recommend the place.

reviews.author: Ali
reviews.text: Fresh, crispy and delicious! .. this spot serves the best churros in town. The chocolate is creamy, delicious and lip smacking good. Their cappuccino was equally good as well. Fast and friendly service for sure. Plenty of outdoor seating as well. Would highly recommend this spot if you're visiting Malaga.

reviews.author: Ahmed Bu Asali
reviews.text: Casa Aranda serves hands down the best churros con chocolate I’ve ever tried. The churros are perfectly crispy on the outside, soft and fluffy on the inside, and always served fresh and piping hot. The chocolate sauce is more like a rich, liquid hot chocolate – smooth, not too thick – and it pairs beautifully with the churros. The combination is simply addictive! The ambiance of the place is also a highlight. It has a cozy, authentic Málaga-Spanish charm with so much character. I especially loved just sitting there, soaking in the atmosphere and watching people pass by – it’s the kind of spot that invites you to slow down and enjoy the moment. Definitely a must-visit if you’re in Málaga. I’ll be coming back for sure!

reviews.author: frances bahadori
reviews.text: Casa Aranda is one of those places that instantly feels special. The moment you take a bite of their crispy, golden churros—especially when dipped in that thick, rich hot chocolate—you understand why people have been coming here for generations. It’s simple, it’s comforting, and it’s absolutely delicious. Whether you're starting your morning or taking a sweet break in the afternoon, there’s something magical about sitting there, enjoying the moment. If you’re in Málaga, you can’t miss it!

reviews.author: Bhavana P
reviews.text: Went there on my last day of the trip and it was so good I regret not going sooner! Spanish churros are something else. They are airy and light and the chocolate you can order with it complements the churro perfectly without being too heavy. I already miss it! Apart from churros love the wide range of coffee options and the savoury ham sandwhich was good too.

reviews.author: K L
reviews.text: A cozy little spot in Málaga where you can enjoy piping hot churros with thick, delicious chocolate. Perfect for a quick snack or a leisurely break while soaking in the local vibes.

reviews.author: K E
reviews.text: Not a place for me. Crowded. Ordered snails, meatballs, Mediterranean salad, and fried sardines. So much food for two people that it was unappetizing. Did not care for the flavors. We were seated at the entrance barrels. Beautiful foyer but not a place to seat guests since it’s a constant flow of people. Maybe the dining rooms are better. Would not return.

reviews.author: Xin Jia Wang
reviews.text: Been to El Pimpi bar 2-3 times. We usually sit on the terrace as inside is too busy. It’s like mutliple rooms and decors and SO many peoole walking around. Hectic but fun atmosphere. The terrace is in the back and quite big! It has a view of the nearby ruins so pretty nice spot. Found is not the best i have had but pretty fair for the location and vibe. Menu was big enough with all the main generic tapas. I definitely recommend everyone to try this place at least once. You don’t go there only for food, but more for the atmosphere and central location. Could sit and eat for hours chilling under the sun on the terrace. Cocktails seem delicious but we mainly had wine. Service was good.

reviews.author: Syamimi Bakar
reviews.text: We went as soon as it opened - sat at the bar / tapas area. It became very busy soon after! My Spanish passed enough to order us some vermouth and the goat that we wanted to try. The bartender recommended the octopus salad. Safe to we had a great lunch!! Would go back for both dishes 😋

reviews.author: Toh Kaylen
reviews.text: Had lunch at El Pimpi and it was a memorable experience! The ambience was full of charm—bustling, lively, and steeped in Andalusian character. Although it was quite crowded, we were seated surprisingly quickly. The service stood out—absolutely impeccable. The staff were warm, attentive, and professional throughout. As for the food, the black paella was a bit salty. But the pil-pil prawns more than made up for it—easily the highlight of the meal, bursting with flavor and perfectly cooked. Overall, a great spot in Málaga worth visiting for both the atmosphere and hospitality!

reviews.author: S L
reviews.text: This place is really beautiful! I was looking for a tapas place where I can sit down in air con cause the weather is too hot, this place a is a real gem! Not overprice even in the middle of the tourist area. The beautiful Spanish design, the posters, pictures of history…the tapas and drinks are good and reasonable price, I strongly recommended it!

reviews.author: Marius S.
reviews.text: A Quirky and Fun Breakfast Spot! This place is a truly unique breakfast experience! When you walk in, it feels like you’ve stepped into a vintage thrift store—full of charm and character. The breakfast menu is simple yet original: spreads and jams served in paper egg cartons, alongside toast. It’s not your typical meal, but the presentation and creativity are fantastic. The prices are very reasonable, and it’s a solid 10/10 for originality. If you’re looking for something different and memorable, this is the place to go! 🥚🍞✨

reviews.author: Els Westhovens
reviews.text: Very nice place to go and eat and enjoy the great atmosphere in Malaga. The place is very authentic, it is a restaurant that doubles as an antique store. All the rooms are all with lots of old features. The service was great and also the food, sadly there was only one kind of breakfast. Toast wilth lots off different spreads. And you can choose between coffee or orange juice. It would have been nice if there was the ability to also have eggs. I would recommend to go there enjoy the typical spanish atmosphere.

reviews.author: Carol D
reviews.text: What a little gem this place is. I ended up here three mornings for their lovely little toast breakfast and coffee. The large piece of bread comes with an egg carton filled with home-made spreads, both savoury and sweet. Coffee is excellent. Seating is inside an antique shop, so you are surrounded by all things vintage. Such a vibe. There is also outdoor seating in a little alley. Cost of breakfast with coffee is €3. Best spot in the Old Town of Malaga.

reviews.author: Denis Zagorie
reviews.text: La Recova. At first, it’s hard to tell whether it’s a small museum, an antique shop, or a place for a quick and tasty bite. It’s a great spot for a short break while strolling through Málaga. Friendly staff, a great atmosphere, and definitely worth picking up something as a souvenir.

reviews.author: Ian Highland
reviews.text: How we stumbled upon this place I’ll never know but so glad we did. It’s quite a bonkers place in that it’s a restaurant inside what feels like part junk shop, part antique shop, and part ‘Berts’ store (shop in the uk). It’s weird but wonderful, the food is limited, more snack like but jolly cheap and lovely all the same. Definitely worth a visit as it’s so very unique.

name: Street Stall - Atarazanas Market
address: Street Stall - Atarazanas Market, Malaga, Spain

reviews.author: Scott Harm
reviews.text: We were delighted to find it open on Friday as we walked past on Thursday and it looked almost permanently closed. Very well appointed public market with fresh fruits, vegetables, meats of all varieties and the same for fish and seafood. It was not so large that it took less than 45 minutes to casually stroll through the entire space. We heard from several other visitors that the vendors ready to eat food was very good but we were still full from our previous meal. As an Architect I very much liked its design and was really glad, once again, that we could gain entry.

reviews.author: C an
reviews.text: A Must-Visit Market in the Heart of Málaga! The Atarazanas Market is a vibrant and authentic spot full of life, color, and incredible local flavors. From fresh seafood and seasonal produce to cured meats, cheeses, and delicious tapas, it’s a paradise for food lovers. The atmosphere is lively, the vendors are friendly, and the historic setting adds to the charm. A perfect place to experience the local culture and grab a tasty bite!

reviews.author: Chu M
reviews.text: One of the best places to try local dishes. Went 2 yrs ago, I saved all my food photos and drool over them from time to time. Padron peppers - one of my favorites. This market gets very crowded, long lines but worth the wait.

reviews.author: Oliver Havlík
reviews.text: Overall intention and purpose is great, but there is so many people you can't even move. Lot of shops offer same thing so it isn't much different. You can find there raw sea food, fruit and vegetables, meat, cheese, spices, tapas — it sounds like lot but there is like 6-7 shops which offers the exact same products. Paella was great, fruit was also juicy and tasty! If you are in Malaga, don't miss it!

reviews.author: Boris Sousa (QueenBRani)
reviews.text: For food enthusiasts eager to explore a market, this is a must-visit spot in Malaga. I went around lunchtime, and the place was bustling, making it a bit challenging to navigate through the wide aisles due to the crowd. The market stalls are stunning, overflowing with fresh fruits and vegetables. There are also stalls offering freshly squeezed juices; I enjoyed a ginger shot that had a powerful kick. One stall specializes in cooked meats, where I tried the pork with crackling, along with another sandwich. The meat was incredibly tender and juicy, while the crackling was delightfully crispy—exactly what you hope for in crackling.

name: Street Stall - Calle Larios
address: Street Stall - Calle Larios, Malaga, Spain

address: Street Stall - Centro Histórico, Malaga, Spain

address: Street Stall - El Palo, Malaga, Spain

name: Street Stall - Málaga Beach
address: Street Stall - Málaga Beach, Malaga, Spain

reviews.author: Vittorio Mazzia
reviews.text: Amazing beach with many very tasty restaurants all around it. However, if you want to eat at one of those places, a reservation is strongly suggested. Keep in mind that in Spain, people usually eat late. On the other hand, there are a lot of public spots in which you can stay under the sun by the seaside.

reviews.author: Michael Holmes
reviews.text: Love Malaga so much to do and see. Perfect place to get away to

reviews.author: linda dix
reviews.text: Best steak 🥩 I've ever eaten, perfect xxx 🥰

reviews.author: Khalid Yusuf
reviews.text: The best city i have ever visited in spain

reviews.author: Chaya G
reviews.text: very long stretch of beach & great waters to swim

name: Street Stall - Muelle Uno
address: Street Stall - Muelle Uno, Malaga, Spain

reviews.author: Aleksandra Z
reviews.text: It’s a wonderful place whether you want to take a walk or enjoy a meal or a drink. There’s a wide selection of restaurants offering various cuisines and price ranges—from elegant dining spots to affordable fast-food options. The view of the moored yachts adds to the relaxing atmosphere as you sit at the restaurant tables. In this promenade, you’ll also find several clothing and shoe stores, shops for fans of Spanish sports clubs, and souvenir stores. Regularly, various artisan markets are held here, showcasing unique regional products. And just a few steps away, you’ll find yourself at the iconic Malagueta.

reviews.author: David Matthews
reviews.text: Just cruised past onan1 hour scenic cruise with not much to see. Cruise terminal looks closed for redevelopment

reviews.author: Marcel Knuvelder
reviews.text: Amazing little harbour area. If you are visiting then head for restaurants in town as they are much cheaper, in this area you pay a huge premium and the good is average. But the harbour is great, nice boat rides and great views

reviews.author: CD
reviews.text: We parked our car at Muelle Uno, which is close to Malaga's marina area. For our family, this area was a great and convenient location to explore the rest of the city. The Christmas market huts were pretty and well-decorated, selling touristy trinkets and gifts. In my view, this is one of a better planned marinas with integrated shopping and eateries. There are plenty of these around, albeit you would pay a slight premium. We also did our city sightseeing bus and boat tours from this area. Overall, this place isn't an attraction in itself but a pleasant place for a stroll and there will be something for everyone.

reviews.author: Simon Bunting
reviews.text: Nice boat, good staff, great vibes, the route felt abit boring though

name: Street Stall - Paseo del Parque
address: Street Stall - Paseo del Parque, Malaga, Spain

name: Street Stall - Playa Malagueta
address: Street Stall - Playa Malagueta, Malaga, Spain

reviews.author: Ivana B
reviews.text: Good beach for a location. No extraordinary but very nice it is to sit down there and relax after busy day in town. Sand is quite rough but I don’t see that as an issue. Plenty bars and restaurants round there. Showers to wash your feet were not working when we visited (February 2025).

reviews.author: Michal Huštaty
reviews.text: Even in winter months, this place is magical, pretty clean and so close from old town. Grab a coffee to go and enjoy the unexpected sky each day here at this beach.

reviews.author: Adeel Awan
reviews.text: I had a wonderful time here The sand was clean, the water was crystal clear, and the atmosphere was incredibly relaxing. I really appreciated the facilities available, like the showers and restrooms. The beach was well-maintained, and the surrounding scenery made it a perfect spot for a day out. The staff were friendly and helpful, making it even more enjoyable. I would definitely recommend this beach to anyone looking for a peaceful and beautiful place to spend the day

reviews.author: Noel Noel
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches ⛱️ I have seen in my life! Just stunning!

reviews.author: Cameron
reviews.text: The beach was nice and clean, unfortunately the showers and feet wash stations still do not work as of early April 2025 - make sure you bring some extra water to wash off the sand from your feet. The sea was cold but nice to stand in on a hot day, the waves were aggressive and the beech is quite steep so it gets deep quickly.

reviews.author: Lara Smith
reviews.text: Angel was such a fantastic waiter! So friendly, professional and provided incredible recommendations! Thank you so much, he is a credit to your restaurant. The octopus roll and the ribs in lettuce leaves are our favourites (recommended by Angel) and we had some amazing dessert wine too. We will be back!

reviews.author: Boris Sousa (QueenBRani)
reviews.text: This restaurant in the heart of Málaga is exceptional. I was lucky enough to get a table outside around 3 PM, which was perfect for enjoying the sun. My server was very attentive and helped me navigate the menu. Although they had run out of sangria, I tried the summer red—a great alternative. It was fruity and full of bright, summery flavors. The food was on another level. The garlic prawn mini-kebab and the crusty king prawn rolls with soy sauce were the highlights. The kebab was packed with juicy, fresh prawns, while the king prawn rolls—prawns wrapped in filo pastry and fried—were simple yet executed to perfection. I wasn’t the biggest fan of the black toasted noodles with Málaga little squids. I found them lacking in flavor, and there weren’t many squid pieces. However, it was still an interesting dish to try. Overall, this is a fantastic place to eat. It came highly recommended by a friend, and I can see why. I’ve also tried visiting during peak lunch and dinner hours, but they get very busy. If you can, book a table in advance to avoid disappointment.

reviews.author: Rémi Ligez
reviews.text: The food was simply amazing! A lot of choices on the menu that you can try in tapa/snack size. Our waiter Tomás was incredible, giving us many recommandations and being very nice with us! Given more time, we would have come back a second time, would recommend 10/10! [July 2025]

reviews.author: Sander Petit
reviews.text: Despite looking like a tourist place due to its location, this is actually a place I would recommend going. Upscale tapas and larges dishes. The pulpo was terrific and so were the oxtail balls (although the fries were drenched in gravy), squid and brioche. However, vegetable options are limited.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.text: Lovely little place, excellent tapas, friendly service and the waiter spoke good English. We had 5 small tapas and one medium dish. Our favourites included the ham croquettes, the blackened noodles with baby squid and the lamb couscous. For just over £50 including 3 beers and 2 aperol spritz, it was well worth every penny. We went on a Tuesday night in early April, there were people waiting for tables from about 8:30 so it's well worth booking ahead through their website. Local guides also recommend this place.

reviews.author: K E
reviews.text: Not a place for me. Crowded. Ordered snails, meatballs, Mediterranean salad, and fried sardines. So much food for two people that it was unappetizing. Did not care for the flavors. We were seated at the entrance barrels. Beautiful foyer but not a place to seat guests since it’s a constant flow of people. Maybe the dining rooms are better. Would not return.

reviews.author: Xin Jia Wang
reviews.text: Been to El Pimpi bar 2-3 times. We usually sit on the terrace as inside is too busy. It’s like mutliple rooms and decors and SO many peoole walking around. Hectic but fun atmosphere. The terrace is in the back and quite big! It has a view of the nearby ruins so pretty nice spot. Found is not the best i have had but pretty fair for the location and vibe. Menu was big enough with all the main generic tapas. I definitely recommend everyone to try this place at least once. You don’t go there only for food, but more for the atmosphere and central location. Could sit and eat for hours chilling under the sun on the terrace. Cocktails seem delicious but we mainly had wine. Service was good.

reviews.author: Syamimi Bakar
reviews.text: We went as soon as it opened - sat at the bar / tapas area. It became very busy soon after! My Spanish passed enough to order us some vermouth and the goat that we wanted to try. The bartender recommended the octopus salad. Safe to we had a great lunch!! Would go back for both dishes 😋

reviews.author: Toh Kaylen
reviews.text: Had lunch at El Pimpi and it was a memorable experience! The ambience was full of charm—bustling, lively, and steeped in Andalusian character. Although it was quite crowded, we were seated surprisingly quickly. The service stood out—absolutely impeccable. The staff were warm, attentive, and professional throughout. As for the food, the black paella was a bit salty. But the pil-pil prawns more than made up for it—easily the highlight of the meal, bursting with flavor and perfectly cooked. Overall, a great spot in Málaga worth visiting for both the atmosphere and hospitality!

reviews.author: S L
reviews.text: This place is really beautiful! I was looking for a tapas place where I can sit down in air con cause the weather is too hot, this place a is a real gem! Not overprice even in the middle of the tourist area. The beautiful Spanish design, the posters, pictures of history…the tapas and drinks are good and reasonable price, I strongly recommended it!

reviews.author: Pamela Wong
reviews.text: I found an amazing restaurant that provided different kinds of seafood. The food was delicious and higher quality 😋, all of the stuff was really friendly. There was near sea, so we could enjoy the breeze from the sea. One of thought was to blew my mind that their ordered method really interesting because you didn't need to take an order. They would take a different plate of food and show in front of you. If you would like, you only raised your hand, and the stuff would put it on your table that I have never seen.

reviews.author: Amy Brice
reviews.text: What an experience! The waiters walk around with dishes of food and you raise your hand if it’s something you want, very much like an auction. We went at lunch time and it was busy and such a fun place to go. All the seafood was so fresh and super delicious. If you want authentic seafood, this is the place to go! This place is a little bit out of Malaga central, but a direct bus takes you almost to the door.

reviews.author: Steve Holley
reviews.text: One of our greatest food experiences ever. Great food, theatrical delivery and atmosphere that's unbelievable! Unmissable !

reviews.author: Maksym Zhyzhko
reviews.text: Visiting the place out of season (early March) most probably decreases 5 star rating. Despite the place is quite popular and the dishes are really easy cooked but: a) the chairs are not clean (kind of dusty) b) the food is not salted, we had to ask salt and lemon after the dishes were served c) 18 eur grilled squid is full of oil and the portion is like on the picture. The taste is not for this price as well d) we had to order drinks twice because the waiter did not bring them e) finally - the chicken nuggets were delicious but… raw (see the picture). Summing up, during the season this place seems to be really nice. But in March I don’t recommend

reviews.author: Roxanne De Marcy Chelin
reviews.text: Food was delicious. Service is great and fun. Very busy and popular place.

name: Ca’n Joan de s’Aigo
address: Ca’n Joan de s’Aigo, Mallorca, Spain

reviews.author: SEVEN Emmy Temin
reviews.text: Amazing, traditional pastries and home made ice creams. A real treat, had a beautiful, authentic charm with very friendly staff. We enjoyed the homemade ice cream and two ensaimadas, which were both excellent. Highly recommend!!

reviews.author: Matt Blum
reviews.text: Can Joan de s'Aigo: where you come for a pastry and accidentally time-travel to a slower, better version of life. The ensaimada practically floats off the plate, the gato hits you like a warm hug from your grandmother, and the almond sorbet? Cold, earthy, ethereal...That thing could settle international disputes. Old-school charm, sleepy atmosphere, and just enough sugar to make you briefly consider living here forever.

reviews.author: Raquel Robles
reviews.text: Ensaimadas in this place, one of the best desserts I've ever had. We loved them. They have so many flavours, and a big variety of traditional mallorquina food.

reviews.author: Anja W.
reviews.text: Outstanding service - waiters who really like their job and want you to enjoy the experience. We tried some ensaimadas and had coffee and tea. It was all very tasty. In the end they also let us try their home made ice cream. Definitely worth a visit, also for the traditional interior.

reviews.author: W
reviews.text: What a fantastic place to be in Mallorca! They are a small majorcan family which has been producing homemade traditional products typical of the city for more 3 centuries. It's always very welcoming and relaxing, with a wonderfully friendly team. The Ensaïmadas here are the best you'll find in Mallorca – I'm absolutely addicted!

reviews.author: Roy Roosevelt Fattouh
reviews.text: Chef Elena's dishes stood out. She's very humble and down to earth. The food was outstanding and the staff were very friendly. Overall amazing experience. Highly recommended

reviews.author: Carl Wong
reviews.text: The dinner experience at Arzak was the highlight of our trip to San Sebastian. We made the reservation at least 6 months prior to our visit on May 27th 2025. It was such an honor to chat with Chef Elena briefly, what a wonderful warm touch for her to go to each table. The dishes are amazing and very innovative.

reviews.author: Jade Phichitkul
reviews.text: Among one of the best 3 stars restaurants in Spain ( equally as good as Martin ). Arzak gave me a homie relaxing vibe with bold flavors dishes. The 2 most outstanding dishes were the lobster and the pigeon. They were so delicious and tender and all the flavors were so evenly balanced in the dishes. I wished I could order an extra pigeon(it was too good) ! I highly recommend anyone to reserve and have a pleasant dinner there ! 🍻

reviews.author: V Kho
reviews.text: We have been to a few three stars like Claire Smith, Ramsay and have come out disappointed and thought it was a waste of money and time. When I saw the picture of Arzak’s food lab. I have decided to go, this 3 generations restaurant was one of the best dining experience we had recently. If there is a sixth star in Google Reviews, they deserved it, every single dish was cooked to perfection, if anyone is looking for tasting something unusual with classic cooking techniques, it is worth travelling for. The wine list is a booked thick and they have sourced many unusual Spanish and French wine.

reviews.author: Javier Sempere
reviews.text: The house of the grandfather of modern cuisine in Spain is now in the hands of his daughter Elena. She keeps alive the tradition of perfect food creatively presented, great friendly service and a relaxed ambience. Most of the large staff has spent a life working there, and one feels that they are a welcoming Basque family ready to surprise you with a memorable and unique meal. What was once avant-garde is now a great classic. Worth the 3 Michelin stars, worth the visit and worth the 300 € + wine.

reviews.author: Roy Roosevelt Fattouh
reviews.text: Chef Elena's dishes stood out. She's very humble and down to earth. The food was outstanding and the staff were very friendly. Overall amazing experience. Highly recommended

reviews.author: Andy Jackson
reviews.text: Booked here to gently get into the Pinxtos/bar crawl vibe. Rare a place takes bookings but with older relatives was a great way for them to dip their toes into San Sebastián food culture. Really good food and service.

reviews.author: Sergio Hernandez
reviews.text: Busy place but totally worth the wait (or the inconvenience of eating on the steps of the church in front as that seems to be customary!). First night in San Sebastian and we ended up here based on blog recommendations. Place was packed, we tried to make a reservation for the next day but the next available was a week out (so plan accordingly). We started ordering (and eating) at the bar, followed by sitting and eating at the steps of the church, and lastly sitting at a table! Well, after all they are mostly small plates (pintxos) which you finish fairly quick. The grilled octopus (available only in a regular Portion size) was so tender it didn't feel like octupus at all. The Beef Cheeks (Carrillera) were also spectacular, highly recommended, as it was the slowed cooked Pork Belly (Panceta). Despite being busy and crowded at times, this is a high quality place which I'm looking forward to visit again.

reviews.author: Heather Deason
reviews.text: Always a favorite when we visit San Sebastián. The pork belly with hummus is a stand out along with the beef Cheek but honestly, everything on the menu along with the pinxtos are excellent. Fun to sit outside next to the church and watch the tourist chaos.

reviews.author: Karen Tran
reviews.text: So glad I came here!! Service was great and we managed to snag the last table. We ordered quite a bit: tuna anchovies and green peppers, jamon croquettes, beef cheeks with mash potatoes, grilled foie gras with white chocolate, bao bun, cheese ice cream with red fruits, French toast with vanilla ice cream. Must get the beef cheeks! So soft and tender and delicious. The foie gras with white chocolate was mind blowing! Who knew this combo would work? Both desserts are a must! I still dream about the cheese ice cream, it was incredible!! And who doesn’t love a hot French toast with the coldness of vanilla ice cream? Also don’t skip out on the gin and tonic! No joke one of the best I’ve ever had

reviews.author: Lloyd Ng
reviews.text: Very friendly service. Busy place. Slight wait but managed to get a table outside without a reservation (I suggest you do reserve). Amazing food!

reviews.author: D
reviews.text: It’s a really nicely decorated tapas bar with super nice cold beer, twisted tapas that veer very very tasty and nice staff. Worth visiting. The one in the PINXOS list was actually the less tasty but still good one

reviews.author: K FP
reviews.text: The pinchos are awesome! Lots of variety, and they were ready instantly!! As a Canadian I appreciated trying things I don't normally get to try like a pincho with anchovies and a pincho with duck. Nice outdoor seating area too. A good choice in San Sebastian.

reviews.author: Nhi Ngo
reviews.text: Such a fun vibe and great food too! Best tortilla I've ever had anywhere in Spain! It has anchovies and is oozing with amazing olive oil!

reviews.author: 星尾つける
reviews.text: I ate at 15 restaurants in San Sebastian in 3 days. I have visited this restaurant twice. Itxaso I ordered twice. Creamy prawn on the best pie. The staff recommended it. Anchovy Omellete delicious. A little spice is great. The others are delicious too.

reviews.author: Eunju
reviews.text: Lovely staffs and chilled vibe here. Pintxos are great too. Looks like local spots than touristic place but there have lots of Micheline and Repsol guide signs. Highly recommend to get Itxaso. Wine selections are great as well.

reviews.author: Caitlin Niltiac
reviews.text: We lined up at 19h45 and they took a list of names around 20h15 to take "reservations" - the system isn't super clear but it's effective. Earlier you arrive, earlier you eat. We came back around 21h(after a pintos crawl) and ordered the tomatoes, pimentos and steak. Service was superb, gave us drinks whilst we waited in the street everything was tasty and worth the wait. This place is 100% worth the hype!

reviews.author: Emre Parlak
reviews.text: Interesting concept for dining. Had to write our names in the list before they open at 6.50 pm to get the tortilla, it was sold out the day before. The tomatoes tasted incredibly good, the tortilla was creamy, but too salty. The beef was overly expensive for this taste and texture. I would go back only for the tortilla and tomatoes.

reviews.author: Ivana Pranjic
reviews.text: The torta was good! The service was lovely. The food was definitely a tourist trap. Legit someone at the restaurant almost choked on the steak. It was border inedible- perhaps ungraded beef? Had great glass of red wine and a good laugh. Hats off on the marketing! 🙌🏼

reviews.author: Geneieve Sarah Teo
reviews.text: Had the smaller cut of txuleta, tomatoes and peppers. The txuleta was the STAR of the show, perfectly cooked! The tomatoes were slightly too salty for me. But the peppers tasted amazing, it was roasted just right - you won’t find yourself biting on the seeds. Tip: we went during lunch. although the restaurant is open at 1pm they take in person reservations at 12pm on the same day.

reviews.author: Madeleine Garrett
reviews.text: We queued from 11:10am on Saturday, and we ended up missing the tortilla by 1 person (there is only one tortilla, first 12 to order get it!). We still ordered steak and put our names down at 12 o’clock for the 1pm sitting. When we arrived the staff remembered how disappointed we were and managed to slip us a small slice of tortilla so we could taste it - and it is definitely worth queueing for. Hands down the best restaurant in San Sebastián and well worth the queue. The best steak of the trip, the tomato salad is beautifully simple and delicious. The staff are amazing and friendly and really look after you.

reviews.author: Caitlin Niltiac
