reviews.author: Jo J
reviews.text: Good but not the best tapas place we visited. Definitely a strong 4,5 based on creativity. Visually, the best place to "eat with your eyes". The best pintxos was the duck roll with spring onion and hoi sin sauce. Rest looked amazing and tasted O.K. If you're looking for a romantic venue, move along- this place was very busy, played hard metal and hard a strong "white prison light". However, we found the taste of the bob limon to be nothing special.

reviews.author: Andrej Balaz
reviews.text: Easily one of the best pintxo bar around. Inventive, fine cuisine, friendly staff. It's our all-time favorite in all Donostia, I have eaten here over ten times. Eat from the menu to get the hot dishes and definitely try Bob Limón as dessert, it is spectacular. Be ready to accommodate for some waiting time and a little pushing during high season as it is usual in most of the good bars. Or come at opening time. I was able to sit several times, so it's all up to the timing.

reviews.author: Rob O
reviews.text: This has got to be one of the most creative pinxto bar I've ever visited in Spain! But the key is to order from the board rather than taking from the pinxto bar. Make sure you order the smoked cod (2nd from the top of the board menu), the suckling pig, and last but not least, the passionfruit dessert that pops in your mouth!

reviews.author: Andrea Ramirez
reviews.text: important info : it is always super full and you have to fight to get inside and the staff is really stressed so they might not be as friendly but they are actually really polite and if you ask them something they will answer back. The food is incredible, like no other Pintxos around the area, they totally live up their hype. It is really unique and worth going. Honestly, it's not as expensive as other places. Great experience

reviews.author: Nik Getmygrubon
reviews.text: They do things just a little different here. The shop looks more modern and so do the pintxos, just a little different, just a lil fancier. You'll choose your favorites, collect them on your plate and pass them to the gentlemen behind the counter. They grill, cook or prepare them any possible way and you'll get them back in full beauty. Nice change-up to the classics.

reviews.author: Andy Jackson
reviews.text: The green beans was a really fresh and vibrant dish. The wild mushroom pastry was good, if slightly dry. Croquettes were excellent the pinxtos overall were outstanding. The scallop dish in particular a standout, easily good enough to feature on the menu of any restaurant. The foie was under-seared for me but still a delicious, well-balanced plate. Unfortunately, the experience was marred by the manner in which the food was delivered, accompanied by an aggressive tone. Our mistake, apparently, was not informing staff that we had changed tables. In fact, we had done so, after checking with the same server who took our order and told us it was fine. It wasn’t a great way to receive the food. I appreciate they must deal with many tourists who don’t understand the local customs, but in this case, we did, and were treated as if we didn’t. Go for the food but tread on the egg shells lightly!

reviews.author: Danielle Williamson
reviews.text: What an absolutely incredible experience. We went back twice! I can’t possibly rave about this place enough. Every. Single. Dish. Was incredible. Service was friendly and fast. Our waiter spoke Catalan, Spanish, French, English and Japanese. The jamon iberico was the best I’ve ever had. The scallop also possibly the best ever. The beef cheek was ridiculously tender and the accompanying potato purée delicious. Highly recommend their specials. We tried the white asparagus - incredible and a few others. I literally cannot fault this place. I dream about it. Finally, it was exceptional value for money. Dying to return.

reviews.author: Linbo Zhang
reviews.text: First impression it's too busy, but then the food really changed everything, they have Michelin level small dishes, the scallops and artichokes are must-tries. I also believe they have the best Gildas. Bar staff are super friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Antonio Sanchez
reviews.text: We had a memorable dinner at Casa Urola. We dined at the restaurant (they also have a bar on street floor). The service was very friendly, extremely attentive, knowledgeable and accommodating. The food was excellent, delivering on their promise to focus on the produce quality and not to interfere with strong condiments or sauces. The seasonal vegetables were very fresh and flavourful. The rice with clams cooked to the perfect point. And the 1.3kg Dover sole was truly exceptional. Even the bread, side dishes and desserts were of extremely high quality. A must in San Sebastián for traditional Basque cuisine. We will return to try their “chuleta”.

reviews.author: Tadeusz Woszczyński
reviews.text: Well known restaurant with basque kitchen. We had amazing seafood soup, monkfish, huelva shrimps and crab cake. Waiters were kind and professional. Quite expensive place, we paid 300 eur for a dinner including 3 kids. At the beginning we were frustrated as we were waiting 15-20 minutes for a menu and next 10 minutes for a water (it was very hot inside)

reviews.author: Rica
reviews.text: Our experience here was an absolute treat! Every dish we tried was phenomenal, but some stood out as unforgettable—the hen croquette and the puff pastry with Basque sausage. But the true star of the show? The mushrooms with egg yolk—a stunning combination that blew us away. An experience we’d happily relive!

reviews.author: Sun Lee
reviews.text: Cozy basque style bar and restaurant with a unique selection of pintxos in the Parte Vieja neighborhood of San Sebastian. Friendly service and fresh ingredients. Enjoyed a few different pintxos and wonderful wine. Arrived right when they opened in June 2025. Long wait for us, and the line was out the door as we were eating. Definitely recommend.

reviews.author: Roy Ouwerkerk
reviews.text: First of all, the service is very good. Despite the very long line, the waiter took the time to explain things to us and answer our questions. He also brought us our food, and people are only allowed to go inside once a table is free. Super good! The ham was nice, not very special and not worth 19 Euros, but nice. We ordered the following pintxos: Croqueta de jamon, my sister enjoyed it a lot, me less so, but I also don't love croquetas in general. Gamba rebosada, it was very nice, nothing special. Esparrago rebosada, interesting, and nice, but we don't really like esparragos, so not super for us. Hojaldre con txistorra, very delicious sausage. Tartaleta de txangurro, very delicious spider crab. Rape y langostinos, interesting and tasty, nice combination, for me the potato (?) wasn't necessary.

reviews.author: Melissa Frenzel
reviews.text: Cozy basque style bar and restaurant with a unique selection of pintxos in the Parte Vieja neighborhood of San Sebastian. Friendly service and fresh ingredients. Enjoyed a few different pintxos and wonderful wine. Arrived right when they opened in February 2025. Short wait for us, and the line was out the door as we were eating. Definitely recommend.

reviews.author: Rajiv Jadav
reviews.text: there was a bit of a wait to eat pintxos upstairs but we were seated fairly quickly for the dining room downstairs. we were bought out a complimentary starter of battered pawns and mayo a few minutes after ordering, with the croquettes and Russian salad we ordered following soon after. all were super tasty and moreish starters but the highlight was the steak, cooked rare over the grill with a great sear but still very tender. the desserts were also very nice, but the caramelised rind in the orange dessert was a bit too bitter for us.

reviews.author: Feng Qi Chan
reviews.text: Very good steak and well salted but too chewy for me. Would have preferred if they cut the kebab steak into smaller pieces. We also got sea urchin cream and another pintxos, but we’ve had better elsewhere!! still decent though.

reviews.author: Jim Foster
reviews.text: We had dinner here and had a very nice dinner. The scallops were so delicious and the tenderloin was cooked perfectly. The service was a little slow but that seems to be common in Spain everyone seems to want to linger for hours. Once engaged the staff was lovely.

reviews.author: Brandon Ynayan
reviews.text: Really solid pick for txuleta and turbot! Service was excellent. We opted for their dine-in menu. The scallops were tasty and the turbot was cooked perfectly. Service very much steak house like. Just a heads up for dine-in they require you order at least one starter and a main course per person.

reviews.author: Karen Tran
reviews.text: We went to bar sport but unfortunately it was closed so we came here instead to hide from the rain. They were just opening so it was quite fun to watch them load up the pintxos bars with fresh snacks! We got the foie gras and grilled prawn! Can’t go wrong there. We also got beef skewer and sea urchin cream!!!

reviews.author: Rajiv Jadav
reviews.text: Simple but delicious cooking, you can really taste the quality of the ingredients. The scallops starter and the suckling pig leg in particular were the stand out dishes. The deserts were also both tasty and a good end to the meal. What was really surprising is that we were probably the last cover of the evening (around 22.45 on a Tuesday) after a long day of travelling but everything was still just as nice as if it had been the first.

name: La Cuchara de San Telmo
address: La Cuchara de San Telmo, San Sebastián, Spain

reviews.author: Heather Deason
reviews.text: We loved our experience here. We popped in for lunch around 2pm and like most places it’s small so it was packed. The bartenders Juan and Dani were very friendly and the food was excellent! They recommended the black pudding which I have never liked, but we gave it a shot, and I was blown away by the flavors. So flavorful super creamy and was not at all like the black pudding in the UK. The duck ravioli and beef cheek were also excellent. If you can get in, I highly recommend it!

reviews.author: Zheng Tao
reviews.text: Very popular bar here. Recommend the suckling pork 10/10 for me, very flavourful, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. The pig ear and octopus were done extremely well too and service was great!

reviews.author: Thanos Papaspyropoulos
reviews.text: Top dishes, great place to grab pintxos. They do three different portion sizes. The medium one is pretty good for two people to share! Had a great laugh and ate some great delicacies! A must go place in San Sebastian I'd say.

reviews.author: Ben Z
reviews.text: We have generally avoided places you have to queue for but this place was worth it. Incredible food and genuinely friendly multilingual staff. For me the highlight was the cod cheek and the beef was excellent also. Excellent value for money also.

reviews.author: Oliver Löfström
reviews.text: Five star experience!!! This place is amazing. If you want to order pintxos, go inside and order. If you want to order larger dishes and sit at the tables outside, you have to queue. We waited for about 45min before we got a table, but it was soo worth it. When you queue you sip on a beer and talk, so time flies. And the food is amazing. The squid is a must try, and the crispy pig as well. Can’t recommend this place enough!

name: Street Stall - Alderdi Eder
address: Street Stall - Alderdi Eder, San Sebastián, Spain

reviews.author: James Davis
reviews.text: This is a wonderful area overlooking the beach, there seems to be a local artist that draws pictures in the sand. There is lots to see and do from market stalls to children's fair rides.

reviews.author: rien Chan
reviews.text: This is the second time to come here for memorizing the fist moment hanging around here with my mom, dad n sister. The place still nice, more clean, interesting and so good park. I love this place moreover it is in front of the beatiful beach. I am so sure whoever come here will enjoy in every single time. Recommended to come here with family, friends and especially with couple....

reviews.author: Brad
reviews.text: Alderdi Eder parkea is a pleasant urban park and leisure area situated south of Old Town and northeast of La Concha Beach. The park is filled with palm trees, other interesting tree species and nicely landscaped flowerbeds. There are walking paths, park benches, a merry-go-round and other light entertainment for the little ones. You can see the historic City Hall building and walk along the promenade enjoying views of the sea and beach nearby at Alderdi Eder Parkea. Overall, this is a nice spot if you are looking for green space or leisure grounds while in San Sebastian. Note that there is not much shade anywhere in the park so bring a hat and apply sunscreen if you plan to spend much time here.

reviews.author: Joe Catersales
reviews.text: What is there to say, 5 stars and I would have given 6. One of the many tranquil and beautiful gardens in San Sebastian. I am conflicted as this town is one of my favourite places in the world. It has it all, sun, sea, sand, excellent food, history, culture, friendliness. I just hope it does not get spoilt by mass tourism.

reviews.author: Zoe Smith
reviews.text: Such a perfect place for families visiting San Sebastián! Easy to walk to- the views are amazing accross the sea. The playground is eally great our four and two year old enjoyed it on multiple occasions without getting bored.

name: Street Stall - Gros
address: Street Stall - Gros, San Sebastián, Spain

name: Street Stall - Kursaal
address: Street Stall - Kursaal, San Sebastián, Spain

reviews.author: Achino N
reviews.text: Very beautiful conference venue in a great location!

reviews.author: Natalia Banasik-Jemielniak
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful place. A stunning conference venue.

reviews.author: Maja Mańczak
reviews.text: Very beautiful venue for our conference, in an amazing location! But the air conditioning is too cold

reviews.author: M M
reviews.text: The place is beautiful. The sound in the speakers wasn’t very good.

reviews.author: Suzette R
reviews.text: Loved every bit of San Sebastian but saw this building and thought it was awfully ugly from the exterior & shame it’s covering all those lovely old beautiful architecture behind it, should be placed in a corner somewhere else..not at beach front

name: Street Stall - La Bretxa
address: Street Stall - La Bretxa, San Sebastián, Spain

reviews.author: David Erwin
reviews.text: The market is one level below street level, Google will take you to the square, look for the sheltered escalator (btw good fruit marker on the corner at street level). Descend the escalator to find butchers, fish mongers and more. A well stocked grocery is also here, making the market a one stop shop for all your food needs and vacation supplies. Also a good place to grab mixers, like tonic water and there's also beer, wine, and spirits sold here as well

reviews.author: Pierre Marteau Van Wetter
reviews.text: Very big underground food market center where you can find everything. Fish, meat, vegetables, fruits and ther is a LIdl supermarket where you find everything at good prices. Camembert and Brie are delicious but you have to go early because they fly away fast. San Sebastian is one the most beautifull places we have visited...Glamour and great beaches. Friendly people and excellent food. Many, many Michelin stars are here.

reviews.author: Steven Clark
reviews.text: This is an underground market selling meat, fish etc. it also where the Lidi store is located but you won't find much in the way of signage showing you the way but once inside and down the stairs you will see it, this is one of the best / cheapest food shops in the area.

reviews.author: Mike Ivanenko
reviews.text: Beautiful small mall. We've been there before Christmas, it was decorated with thousands light, it was cool

reviews.author: Johannes Petersson
reviews.text: All cities should have a market like this. This is a must visit if you're a foodie like me. There is fresh fish, seafood, meat and cheese and also high quality canned tuna and vegetables and of course a huge selection of Spanish cured ham (jamon serrano) and sausage (chorizo).

name: Street Stall - Parte Vieja
address: Street Stall - Parte Vieja, San Sebastián, Spain

name: Street Stall - Zurriola
address: Street Stall - Zurriola, San Sebastián, Spain

reviews.author: Juanmi Martin
reviews.text: nan

name: A Tafona
address: A Tafona, Santiago de Compostela, Spain

reviews.author: Charlie King
reviews.text: Great attention, delicious treats, and was pleasantly surprised by the prices.

reviews.author: olinda ohara
reviews.text: Lovely pastries. We had an eclair and mini Santiago tarta (our first one) was busy with locals and lots of options. Servers were very kind with our attempts at limited Spanish and the pastries were delicious. Not too sweet at all, which we prefer. Sweet cream but delicate shoux pastry and the tarta also pleasant.

reviews.author: Olesia Golub
reviews.text: Tarta de Santiago is excellent, very tender and not sweet! The rest of bakery is also good.

reviews.author: Ashley CY
reviews.text: delicious and reasonable price, marvelous taste

reviews.author: Martina O'Sullivan
reviews.text: Delicious fresh pastry! We had single profiteroles and they were divine. Highly recommend

name: O Dezaseis
address: O Dezaseis, Santiago de Compostela, Spain

reviews.author: Nick Meyer
reviews.text: Very good menu del dia. Nice covered patio space. Great fish soup, fresh bread, and apple dessert

reviews.author: David Erwin
reviews.text: A very popular and well reviewed restaurant but not to my liking or maybe an off night in the kitchen. The baby calf was chewy, the fish not appealing, every dish was drowned with salt, it was the only flavour you could taste. I probably drink 1.5 liters of water after dinner. The restaurant decor was warm and inviting.

reviews.author: thekilteddrifters
reviews.text: Great decor and atmosphere along with attentive service and fantastic food make this a great choice! The crab Croquetas and the Galician style Pulpo are simply amazing. The Lamb and Secreto perfectly cooked. Portion sizes are on the large side... Not the cheapest restaurant in town but well worth the price, which is very reasonable for the quality of food and service.

reviews.author: Diego Rivera
reviews.text: It used to be a very good restaurant but sadly the food quality and quantity went down. The "fabada" Bean stew was more like a soup, the "lacon con grelos" Boiled gammon with kale was salty and tasteless. For pudding the peach cheesecake wasn't homemade but supermarket quality. Really disappointed.

reviews.author: Ercan S.
reviews.text: Incredibly cozy and loving restaurant. Starting from the ambience of the restaurant, which is very inviting and lovingly decorated, to the staff, which despite lack of Spanish knowledge on my part, fulfilled all my wishes. And finally, the excellent fresh dishes that I can recommend to everyone. I will come again.

reviews.author: Rocio Diaz-Benjumea
reviews.text: Very cute place in the center of Seville. Friendly and fast service and delicious food. Also, the COLDEST beer I have had in Seville in my life in the cutest clay mugs. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Leah V
reviews.text: I wasn’t expecting much from some of the other reviews but was very pleasantly surprised. I like these churros the best compared to others I’ve had in Madrid and Barcelona. The chocolate was the perfect sweetness. It cost 5.5 euros for the takeaway.

reviews.author: Shih Yuin Chew
reviews.text: For Asians that have 油条 in their cultures, this place could be skippable because it tastes almost the same in terms of texture and flavor. It is the fluffy and soft on the inside and slightly crunchy on the outside. But at the same time the oil temperature wasn’t controlled too well, because the five sticks in my plate had inconsistently all different textures despite fresh from the pot. But for people who’s outside such Asian culture, it’s still try-able. As for the chocolate sauce, I liked that it’s thick while not being very sweet. But it also doesn’t have a deep choc flavor. But I appreciate a lot that the waiter let me pay by card when I wanted to do other tapas to make it above 10 euros but they don’t have it yet.

reviews.author: Greg
reviews.text: Very nice place to relax and escape the heat. We tried their recommended churros with chocolate and we weren't disappointed. The chocolate was really chocolatey, not diluted with a ton of milk and everything is very reasonably priced.

reviews.author: tereza špačková
reviews.text: Touristic place to go and felt like they are a bit tired from the hype (fully understandable, but..) Churros were nice very thin, crunchy and oily but different from what I had in Barcelona there was like donut dough. What was def nice was chocolate! Nice experince for once :) (Payments with card are allowed up to 10euro)

reviews.author: Andrew Antolino
reviews.text: Pleasant tapas bar with attentive staff, delicious food and ice (and I mean ice) cold Cruzcampo on tap. Staff were patient to a couple of tourists with very low Spanish skills. Muy rico!!

reviews.author: Vincent Aun
reviews.text: Very close to the Seville Cathedral but not on the main street, hence it was much less crowded and fairly priced. Foods were ok, staff helpful. We specially like the atmosphere.

reviews.author: Todd Mushovic
reviews.text: Tried a couple different tapas in this establishment. Atmosphere and decor are very interesting. Staff were pleasant and helpful.

reviews.author: Colin Hodkinson
reviews.text: Great place for tapas, food was great and a fair price well recommended 👌 went a 2nd time and the pork cheeks are amazing. Best we have eaten and good value for money

reviews.author: Robert Baker
reviews.text: Old school bar with super food. I tried Russian salad, Spinach with chickpeas & the Adobo (itself a triumph) in lovely surroundings

reviews.author: Ana María Pérez Castro
reviews.text: Amazing spanish culinary experience, if you are looking for the real deal, this is it!! Really busy but worth the wait!! Bursting with flavour and charisma! And the service is outstanding, we had Maria, our super efficient and lovely waitress working effortlessly in a highly stressful environment with a huge smile on her face. Made us feel like at home.

reviews.author: Geneieve Sarah Teo
reviews.text: Possibly our best meal in Seville! It’s a no frills, local place with authentic tapas. The prawns in garlic oil and grilled squid are a must order, the sardines on toast too. Everything is seasoned beautifully, nothing too salty. Go there early so that you don’t need to wait! The place fills up quite quickly.

reviews.author: Burak Kayabaşı
reviews.text: It was an amazing experience for us. All the dishes were fantastic and perfect. This place the best one that I have tried in Sevilla. Atmosphere was good, taste of the meals were good and the service was fantastic. Thanks to everyone from the kitchen to bar side. But special thanks 🙏 to Rania and Maria. These woman's were really nice and polite. More appreciate to them. If I will come to Sevilla again, Bodeguita Romera will be the first place that I will visit.

reviews.author: toeytoeyy K
reviews.text: Enjoyed the: -fried sardines w salt flakes -salmorejo (similar to gazpacho) great w iberico -sardine on toast w garlic aioli -beef cheek stew -aubergine w molasse was interesting too Spanish menu, no reservation. If you want a table, get there early when they open, or walk-in to whichever seat that is available at the bar -but be quick or you might end up standing! #wanderliciousx

reviews.author: Lucy Schofield
reviews.text: Absolutely 10/10 from this place! We loved it so much we came back on our third night. Both nights didn’t have a reservation but found a spot at the bar which is a perfect place to watch the staff efficiently do their jobs with pace. The food is fresh and full of flavour. A specials menu changes daily by the looks of it. Maria our waitress chose a couple of dishes for us and didn’t let us down. The pork cheeks were stunning, the clams were massive, we had a shrimp tortilla which was so unique and yummy. Even the potatoes of the day blew up away! Overall I couldn’t recommend this place enough.

reviews.author: Lily Ly
reviews.text: This place did not disappoint! We arrived very late (3:30pm) just before closing time so most of the day's menu was finished, so in the end I asked the waiter what they had left, and everything was perfect! We had oxtail, pork tripe with chickpeas stew, fried cod and a salmon toasty. Such a random combo but definitely left satiated. We ordered everything tapas size, and although they were closing up at 4pm, they told us to enjoy and go slowly (no need to rush). Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Pete Gleadall
reviews.text: Really great tapas place when you can get just a drink, some small tapas snacks or a really good meal. I had a couple of beers and some tapas. What I really liked was that I could have a small plate of ham for example, suitable for 1 person, rather than a massive plate which would be too much for 1. I had some tortilla with whisky sauce, who knew I needed that, and it would work so well! I had meatballs, and a wonderful anchovy on a small piece of toast.

reviews.author: Niklas G.
reviews.text: A must visit ! We came here three times during our stay in Sevilla because the food was so good ! Check it our and try the dishes shown in the fotos (those are the classics and recomondations from the waiters)

reviews.author: Holly G. Shockley
reviews.text: We loved the staff here. Stopped by three times during our stay in Sevilla and felt at home at Casa Morales. The tapas are top notch. Grab a spot and stand at the bar if the seats are full.

reviews.author: Rob Zom
reviews.text: One of the best if not the best tapas we had in Sevilla. I warmly recommend pulpo, chorizo, bacalao and hamburgesas, also their vermouth. The service is very fast and friendly, while they always have a looot of work- I really hope they are remunerated justly

reviews.author: M L
reviews.text: Located at the Alameda de Hércules, this tapa cafe offers no-frill alfresco dining with laidback vibe. We had the zucchini salad with burrata, salmon tartar with crackers, croquettes and squid on black rice to share. The croquettes were well fried and IMHO, the best dish though I had eaten most of the zucchini salad and salmon tartar by then. Unfortunately, shortly after the black rice dish arrived, I developed an acute tummy ache and had to rush to toilet. It was a bad diarrhea likely due to food consumed within hours prior. My hubby didn't suffer such fate as he didn't eat much of the salad or salmon.

reviews.author: Raúl Barrera Barrero
reviews.text: Great place serving tasty tapas in Alameda de Hercules. I enyojed the meal outside in terrace. I tried: - Gazpacho, -Salmon tatar -Squids in its black ink rice All pretty well served, and good price. Recommended :)

reviews.author: U V
reviews.text: We came here in the evening around 7:30 for dinner. They informed us there was also a specials menu each day. We sat outside in the rain by the heater as the inside is very small and already full. Although it was raining the heater kept us very warm. We ordered goats cheese cranberry and crispy onions, salmon and avocados on toast (which also had onions and tomatoes in) and chicken fingers with mayonnaise. They brought over bread and olives and we told them we didn’t want them and they didn’t take them away. I noticed that the olives already had one half eaten and a stone in the bowl. At the end of the meal they put on the bill the olives and bread even tho we hadn’t touched either when I pointed this out they only took off the bread. I think this left a very sour note to the end of a good meal.

reviews.author: Sinthuja Subashkaran
reviews.text: Ate here twice. Underrated. Great specials & very tasty tapas. Would highly recommend. You may have to queue depending on how busy they are but the staff try their best to accommodate you asap. Thanks so much for the lovely meals. I first came here 12 years ago & have fond memories of it even back then!

reviews.author: Rudi Jenkins
reviews.text: Super nice food at a nice square. Waiter was nice, tapas are perfectly sized, modern and varied in taste. Prices are fair. Only complaint is that the outside chairs are not super comfy.

reviews.author: Enobong Eakin
reviews.text: We stumbled upon this restaurant while looking for another restaurant. From the moment we walked in, service was excellent. We were ushered to our table in a nice little spot. Ambience is really nice and gives off a fine dining feel. Our waiter for the evening, Alberto, was helpful and really pleasant. The food here is delicious. We could not have asked for a better dining experience in Seville.

reviews.author: Justin
reviews.text: Pretty awesome little place! Our friends made a reservation here and we definitely enjoyed it. We started at the bar area as it wasnt time for our reservation yet but they sat us the second the other larger party left in the cozy little back area even before our reservation time. We got gazpacho to start for me and my wife and the steak paella for our main meal. Both were excellent! We had a couple other things that were pretty tasty just not our cup of tea food wise, but these two dishes were excellent! Would definitely come again.

reviews.author: Martin Couture
reviews.text: Despite the fact that it is a lovely place with a nice atmosphere, I would not recommend it. We sat at the bar and had mediocre service from Pepe. Tomato tartare had more red onions than tomatoes. The bred was stale like never experienced in Spain. My lamb chops had no meat on them. I could go on.

reviews.author: Doug Noble
reviews.text: Really disappointed with our meal here after reading some great reviews, one of which was in CN Traveller. We had a reservation for 19:45 and when we got to the first floor there were only 2 other couples in the restaurant which didn’t provide much atmosphere. We were told by the waiter that it wasn’t possible to have any paella or rice dishes that they are known for as it would ‘take too long’ as a result of the restaurant being ‘fully booked’ and too busy during Semana Santa (we didn’t see another person arrive in the restaurant for the hour and 15 minutes we were there. The gazpacho was very good as was the pork cheek stew (the daily special), but the chips were a very disappointing portion size for €8 as were the Lamb chops at €4.2 per chop, they were the smallest I’ve ever eaten (see photo). Whilst our waiter was good and attentive, there were a group of waiters and waitresses standing around gossiping and staring at us whilst we ate, right behind our table whilst we were eating in an empty restaurant, void of atmosphere. A frustrating and expensive experience given there are other places in the city serving much better food at half the price.

reviews.author: Derek Xie
reviews.text: Recommended by our hotel staff. Excellent food and service. Our server Ismael was great! Both nights! This is not the cheapest joint around but you get what you pay for. The quality is excellent and the wine list is sufficiently deep. I would recommend the blue label rioja I posted if they still have it. The foie gras and steak are both on the rare side but we didn't get sick. That speaks to the quality of the ingredients. They also brought out a hot plate to heat the aged steak more if you prefer. Excellent experience both nights! Highly recommended if you want something a bit higher class and have it be worth it.

reviews.author: David S
reviews.text: the restaurant is small but the quality is over expected. last year, during a WE trip in Sevilla, the restaurant was full, but they agreed to serve the seven of us at the end of service and even after the delicious tapas and raciones, they did not ask us to leave at all, continuing to pour us very good rums. Food was delicious ( beef and fishes as well) and people were very friendly. We came back just before flying back to Paris, and since then, every time I go back to Sevilla I try to find some available table in this restaurant.

reviews.author: Beatriz Diaz Perez
reviews.text: I loved this site. They have delicious dishes and the waiters are very attentive and friendly. The downside is that good things have to be paid for. I mean, it's quite expensive. But to go once it's worth it.

reviews.author: Alfonso Menéndez Charlo
reviews.text: Very delicious place to go to eat. What a shame it's not bigger. The star dish: Brick bags with cheese, leek and prawns.

reviews.author: Jaime Fdez
reviews.text: The experience..... wow. I really recommend it. 10/10

reviews.author: Carlos Santos
reviews.text: Small restaurant, but of excellent quality.

reviews.author: Michael Lane
reviews.text: When you picture a classic café in Spain, this is the place. People stop at the door just to take a photo. I had been there before for a caña or copa de vino, but today it started to rain, and we stayed at a table just outside for two hours. We enjoyed good wine, beer, and tapas. The food was quite good, as was the service. This is a great place to relax and enjoy life in Spain. One of my favorite places in Sevilla.

reviews.author: David Rincon
reviews.text: We came here for lunch after a day of sight seeing. I highly recommend their stewed Iberian pork jowls, it was so delicious we ended up ordering a full portion after we tried their tapas portion. Also, their sangria was very refreshing and I loved the cinnamon in it.

reviews.author: Dan Poppy
reviews.text: A must visit. Super traditional and great fun. We walked straight in and sat down. The food we had was brilliant and the drinks were good too. Prices are ok. Toilets were a bit chaotic / well used but a minor detail.

reviews.author: Micaëla Boone
reviews.text: Great place! Authentic bar - very relaxed. And with an marvelous interior. Enjoyed it so much!

reviews.author: Bethany Rice
reviews.text: THE best place for ham in the whole of Seville! Very authentic inside and friendly staff. Reasonable prices too! I must visit place in Seville!

reviews.author: M L
reviews.text: This is a large community square / promenade established in 1500s. 2 poignant Roman columns, one crowned with Hercules, considered the legendary father of Seville, and the other Julius Caesar, who closed the city with walls, were set up here. This square is also the football fan gathering place as cafes and pubs mostly are located nearby.

reviews.author: Csaba Biro
reviews.text: Sevilla, Alameda de Hércules, or simply La Alameda, is a garden square or mall in Seville. Built in: 1574, it was originally a promenaded public garden, named after the eight rows of white poplar trees that fill its central part. Four columns were placed to mark off a promenade through the trees. In the beginning it was planned to take four columns from the remains of the Roman temple, believed to be dedicated to Hercules. However, when moving the third column it fell apart, leaving the work temporarily unfinished. Consequently, the two columns at the southern end of the square are from the original Roman temple, whereas the northern columns are modern reproductions.

reviews.author: Dan Leal
reviews.text: Crazy to think that these two pillars are well over 2,000 years old. The left one is of Hercules and the right is off Julius Caesar. I wonder if they had any idea that 2,000 years later they would still be standing. Definitely worth checking out and taking a couple pics or videos

reviews.author: Tony Dani
reviews.text: A nice place to visit and experience local flavor. We went there in the evening. There are many restaurants with various international cuisines and bars on both sides of the large plaza. Most all them have outdoor seating.

reviews.author: Robert Kief
reviews.text: This is a huge rectangular community square. It is lined with restaurants and pubs. In the daytime pretty tame with pop up markets and eateries serving brunch type fares, but as soon as the sun goes down everything comes to life.

name: Street Stall - Plaza de España
address: Street Stall - Plaza de España, Seville, Spain

reviews.author: Travellingaround
reviews.text: Absolutely in love with this mini "plaza". Star Wars (some scenes) got filmed here .and I absolutely love this place . Extremely nice and well taken care of . To go on a boat ride costs 6€ . The whole Plaza feels a little bit like a Venice of the South

reviews.author: Marketa Kimlova
reviews.text: We came early in the morning. Google says that the place opens at 8 but we actually found it open at 7:40 already. It's one of the best squares in the world! The mosaics are beautiful and there is a lot of nature nearby. You can buy some refreshments in the food stalls in the park.

reviews.author: Jake
reviews.text: What an absolute gem. This plaza is breathtaking. There is beauty every angle you look at. We loved the red brick buildings intricately decorated with ceramic tiles. The picturesque bridges covered in tiled as well were gorgeous. There was flamenco dancers in one area showing their talents. There's so many levels to walk on too. Horse and carts nearby waiting for you to show you the rest of the jewels in this city. There's a lovely man made pond/river in the plaza where you can row a boat and a big fountain in the centre. Literally. So much to see. On top of all this There's the stunning parks surrounding the plaza!! Visit here!!

reviews.author: Mahsa Hosseini
reviews.text: Such a beautiful place. I enjoyed walking around for over two hours. The place gets very busy but it is open to public and no tickets needed. It has a beautiful garden and worth walking around. There are some museums, however I didn’t check them.

reviews.author: Nicola Johnson
reviews.text: Plaza de España may be one of Seville’s most iconic sights, but if you’re disabled, don’t expect to be treated as an equal visitor—because you’re not. I was unable to access any of the upper viewing areas. At one end, there’s a lift that requires staff assistance—but no one came, despite repeated attempts to call for help. My son went upstairs to ask in person, only to be met with a shrug and the excuse that the lift was broken. We then struggled across the wide, exposed concourse—where the ramps were steep, awkward, and poorly designed—to try the other side. Again, we rang the bell twice and were ignored. Eventually, a staff member appeared, only to inform us (again, with a shrug) that my mobility scooter wouldn’t fit in the lift—and that was the end of the conversation. No support, no empathy, no effort. Most of the plaza’s key features are only accessible via stairs. The lifts are either broken or completely inadequate. Ramps are few and poorly maintained. Staff seem indifferent at best. If you’re disabled, you’re simply not expected—or wanted—to experience the full site. It’s not just inaccessible. It’s exclusionary. We tried to salvage the visit by going to the gardens, but most of that was off-limits too. A large festival meant closed toilets, no open cafés, and a gigantic stage dominating the centre of the plaza. The famous view? Completely ruined by a giant black structure. Apparently, this goes on for six weeks—something no one warns visitors about in advance. In short: if you’re disabled, don’t bother. If you’re hoping for clear views of the architecture, check ahead carefully. Plaza de España might look good in photos, but for anyone with mobility issues, the reality is disrespectful and discriminatory.

address: Street Stall - Santa Cruz, Seville, Spain

name: Street Stall - Triana Market
address: Street Stall - Triana Market, Seville, Spain

reviews.author: Andrew Giordano
reviews.text: This is such a special restaurant. It’s more than just a meal - it’s an experience. Your meal starts with a history of the restaurant which is given in their incredible wine cellar. You learn about the heritage of Adolfo and can sense the love and passion that comes from Javi, the head chef, who inherited the restaurant from his parents. You are then brought inside and the service is absolutely exceptional (thank you Cecilia!). The multilingual staff (they spoke with us in English) will walk you through the wine selection, ask about any dietary restrictions and help get you on your way to this culinary experience. We opted for the tasting menu and every dish was truly a piece of art. More than just food, these dishes are elegant, refined and relaxed at the same time. Some standouts were the asparagus spears cooked three ways, the artichoke and the fish which has the skin fried separately and delicately laid back on top. We added a cheese course for dessert which was exceptional and their other desserts, including their pomegranate speciality dessert, were so delicious. Please come here for an experience you won’t forget.

reviews.author: Maria Bernstein (MB)
reviews.text: We had one of the most intimate dining experience in Adolfo Restaurante. The experience starts with the tour of their spectacular wine cellar prior to seating us to the beautiful dinning room. The ambiance is quiet, elegant and elevated. Our hostess Cecilia was very warm and welcoming and spoke very good English. The sommelier was also excellent, his choice for wine pairing is perfection. The tasting menu was unbelievable. The presentation is a work of art not to mention delicious! Every course is a delight with anticipation on what’s to come. The timing in between course is also just right, we did not feel rushed and was happy that the evening did not dragged for hours. Having dined in elegant restaurants, Adolfo Restaurante simply meets above our expectations. The chef Javier Muñoz came to the table after the meal to chat and personally thank us for dining at the restaurant. This gave us a chance to personally compliment the chef and the staff. Congratulations to the staff for a job well done. We felt like part of the family by the time we left the restaurant. Thank you for an incredible evening.

reviews.author: Julie Whelan Capell
reviews.text: The most amazing meal I have ever had in my life. Starting with a tour of the restaurant's private wine cellar, in spaces the family discovered when they started knocking out walls underneath a property they purchased many years ago. They began stocking it with exquisite wines and cavas, and now have one of the top wine cellars in the world. We returned to the restaurant and began a seven-course meal with wine pairings. The table was gorgeous, the service was beyond excellent, and each dish was better than the last. Cecilia told us all about each dish and how to eat it in order to taste it the way the chef intended. We finished off with several desserts, including a candy shell shaped like a pomegranate and filled with a frothy yogurt (?) sauce. As instructed, we all picked up spoons and tapped the "pomegranate" shells to break them simultaneously, while wishing for good luck. Finishing off the meal with an exquisite Spanish cava, the evening was deemed a success by all. If you are looking for a once-in-a-lifetime meal experience, you should definitely come to Adolfo's.

reviews.author: ruth burk
reviews.text: Amazing elevated fine dining experience. Beautiful presented unique and innovative plates. Tableware was over the top and changed out for each course. Suckling pig was the best I'll ever have. Predinner tour of 11th century wine cellar was a lovely bonus!

reviews.author: Kellie Erm
reviews.text: What an experience. The afternoon started with a private tour of their extensive wine cellar, which the Collection is not to miss. With the incredible tasting of a 1970 Rioja followed by an exquisite 6 course tasting menu with each dish being explained by the wonderful Cecilia - we came all as friends, left as family. I cannot recommend enough, if you go to Toledo, you have to go. If you don’t believe me - look in their guest book, with comments from Johnny Depp and Gwyneth Paltrow to name a few.

reviews.author: Ricardo Toro
reviews.text: Visiting from NYC with my parents, my two sister’s and husbands (a group of 8), everyone we spoke to who had been to Valencia — plus some local friends — told us we had to try Casa Carmela. I’ll admit, I was a bit skeptical at first, thinking it might be more hype than substance. But I was wrong. We had an amazing experience. We were seated at a round table (which I love for groups of 8+) in the back covered patio area, which was really pleasant. We ordered the arroz negro for five people — absolutely exceptional. Don’t miss it. We also had rodaballo (turbot) carved tableside, which was equally superb. The place was packed for comida (lunch), but somehow it still felt calm, and the service never missed a beat. Midway through the meal, we realized we were going to go over the 2-hour time slot they typically allocate per table. The staff kindly asked if we’d mind having our coffee and after-dinner drinks on the upstairs terrace — which actually turned out to be a perfect way to end the lunch, overlooking the beach. (For the future, definitely try to request one of the large tables on the second floor with ocean views.) As for wine, Casa Carmela has one of the best Spanish wine lists I’ve seen, with a great selection of magnums — we went for two! Anyway, if you’re visiting Valencia, don’t miss the chance to eat here.

reviews.author: Lil
reviews.text: Food is absolutely fantastic, we ordered baked red peppers with cured codfish, garlic and tuna jerky, grilled octopus with parmentier potatoes, brothy rice with shrimp and langoustines and French toast with horchata ice cream and traditional flan. Everything on point, fantastic. The restaurant is nicely decorated and it is great to be able to see how they do the paellas on the wood fire. Músic could be toned down, too loud. And lastly, the service was bad. We waited long for the check, had to ask three times for water. For a restaurant that charges as much as Casa Carmela does, everything should be perfect. Prices are too high in my opinion, about a third more than great rated restaurants in the city center.

reviews.author: Jennifer Drum
reviews.text: Absolutely wonderful wood-fire paella! It is right by the water and has a great atmosphere. My group had some questions and the staff was very helpful when we were deciding what to get. I ended up doing the tasting menu and seafood paella. All of which was extremely fresh and full of flavor. The cheesecake was my favorite between the French toast and that. It was a vanilla bean flavor and had a great crust. The highlights were the oysters and paella of course!

reviews.author: Vanessa Mora
reviews.text: We did the tasting menu and it was wonderful. Some of the cold seafood dishes are just ok but the hot dishes are amazing, with the real star of the show being the traditional paella. Would recommend going when you’re in Valencia!

reviews.author: Matt R
reviews.text: Whenever I visit touristy spots, it feels like a roulette spin - it’s either a big hit or a big miss. This time, I was pleasantly surprised. We started with pan con tomate and a Valencian salad, both fresh and flavorful. But the real highlight was the paella - we had it with lobster, and it was the best I’ve ever had. The rice was perfectly cooked, slightly crispy, and the seafood was incredibly fresh. Great ambience, kind staff - overall, a top experience.

reviews.author: Francis Leung
reviews.text: We didn’t have a reservation, but luck was on our side—we were offered a hidden private room for our group of four! It gave us such a cozy, exclusive dining experience. (A slightly stronger A/C would have made it perfect.) We chose two tasting menus and added a few extras, and every dish that came out—though small in portion—was beautifully crafted and full of flavor. The sheer variety was impressive, and every single item was excellent. The service throughout the evening was warm and attentive, making the whole experience even more enjoyable. We had a truly wonderful evening and left with full hearts and happy taste buds. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Dicle Hames
reviews.text: This place is absolutely amazing! Such a great experience. The interior design is very unique. We sat at the bar and ordered some random tapas and house wine. Everything was so tasty. House wine has a unique taste, one of the best wines i have ever tried. Hope to visit here in the future again ❤️

reviews.author: Bryan
reviews.text: This place was amazing. There is a reason why you will hear about this place when visiting Valencia. I opt for their tasting menu + which included a plate of chorizo and jamon. Every single dish is an art of Spanish gastronomy and history from 1836 tho the portions were abit small but their artisanal bread was sensational and made up for the small portions. The service is absolutely top notch with an amazing sommelier. Even though I ordered by the glasses as a solo diner, he still took me to see their cellar and enthusiastically explained to me how they ended up collecting such delicate wines. Amazing amazing amazing.

reviews.author: Inna Benyukhis
reviews.text: We are visiting Valencia for 3 days and this restaurant was recommended. We didn’t realize it is a Michelin star restaurant. It is so cute! There are only 6 tables and sitting at the bar. All the tapas we selected were exquisite.! Vermouth and Rose wine were perfect! And desert topped out selections! No wonder this restaurant has the Michelin star!

reviews.author: Jasmine W
reviews.text: Hands down the best meal experience I've had to date in Spain. I won't dwell too much on the food and vermut as there's no praise I could give that hasn't already been said ten times over. But it's damn good. Seriously. I'm typically a contrarian, but in this case: believe the hype. Their preparation of simple but fresh ingredients is genius, and I still have the sensation of several of their dishes in the back of my tongue (which is saying something given it's been over 5 months since my visit and I have the memory of a goldfish). Their house vermut was also a wonderful, rich pairing with the dishes I had from the chef's selection menu. Also delighted to report that as of September 2024, they were permitting single diners for their tasting menu -- something I particularly appreciate as a solo diner since many places require a party of at least 2. Last but not least, I'm not usually one to mind too much about service one way or the other, but the staff at Casa Montaña was too outstanding to not give them a shout out. I felt very well taken care of throughout my meal, even as a solo diner at the bar. Every person who served me a dish off the tasting menu was well-versed in the dish, as well as gracious enough to bear my questions in badly-spoken Spanish and (mostly) English. Also worth a mention that reservations are highly recommended. I got lucky lining up on a weekday right at opening, and was one of the last people to get in on a walk-in. Thank you, Casa Montaña, for such an unforgettable dining experience. I hope to return sooner than later.

reviews.text: Amazing traditional vegan paella in a historical restaurant! Yes please. This is a great spot for both gluten free and vegetarian eaters that still want a traditional foodie experience. The staff were accommodating and friendly and the food was great! Such a pretty beach front option. Make a reservation for outdoors if you want to sit on the patio.

reviews.author: Cay
reviews.text: The service was super friendly. Respect to all the staff for working in this weather and still being so friendly. As for the food, we have to say that the paella was the best we’ve had so far after trying four different restaurants. The rest of the menu was just okay.

reviews.author: John McNALLY
reviews.text: A wonderful historic restaurant by the sea. We liked our experience so much that we had an evening meal on 3 occasions. Delicious fish dishes, the best paella and lovely salads. Prices are reasonable too. The waiters are very welcoming, helpful and professional. We would recommend La Pepica very highly.

reviews.author: Paul Prime
reviews.text: Long queue, had to wait for about 1 hour to get my table which was actually promising. I don't mind queuing for great food. It's ok, nothing mind-blowing. I'm sure their produce is fresh. Somehow it was lacking overall punch in the flavors. The sepia was a bit on the chewy side. The mussels were actually plum and juicy just the soup was very peppery. I guess that is their signature taste. I really wanted to like it. Was just not my taste. But for sure it was freshly made and served quickly. The croquettes were creamy and crunchy, golden brown yet lacking flavor. And for sure I couldn't taste the mussels. The olives were great! Overall it's ok. By no means is the food bad. Was it worth waiting for 1 hour? No. Would I eat here for a quick bite? Yes. The waiter was efficient and worked like a machine but I never saw him smile in the 2 hours I've been there .

reviews.author: tiffany chin
reviews.text: Easily top 5 meal in Valencia. We ordered the sepionet (grilled cuttlefish fish with parsley garlic oil), Valencia mussels (in a savory and watery broth), patatas bravas (with a dollop of garlic whip) and a glass of vermouth and tinto de Verano. Everything was delicious. I would recommend this same exact meal.

reviews.author: Michel Blanco
reviews.text: La Pilareta is a charming traditional restaurant in Valencia that beautifully captures the essence of Spanish cuisine through its exceptional tapas offerings. The highlight of the menu is undoubtedly the iconic mussels, which are fresh and flavorful, setting the tone for a delightful dining experience. The grilled cuttlefish is a must-try; it's perfectly cooked, tender, and bursting with flavor. The battered squid, or calamari, is another standout, crispy on the outside while maintaining a succulent interior. To complement the meal, La Pilareta serves a delicious traditional red vermouth, adding a perfect touch to the vibrant atmosphere. Overall, dining here is not just a meal but an immersive experience in Spanish culinary traditions that should not be missed when visiting Valencia.

reviews.author: Nantachit Kitiyakara
reviews.text: La Pilareta in Valencia truly stands out as a gem in the culinary landscape. From the moment you step into this charming eatery, you're enveloped by an authentic Mediterranean vibe that promises a memorable dining experience. The fried calamares here are nothing short of spectacular. They strike the perfect balance between crispy and tender, making each bite a delight. Similarly, the Grilled Cuttlefish is a testament to the kitchen's mastery over seafood, grilled to perfection with just the right char and a smoky flavor that complements the natural sweetness of the cuttlefish. Don't miss out on their potatoes; they're a simple dish done exceptionally well - crispy on the outside, soft and flavorful inside. The mussels are another highlight, fresh, succulent, and served with a preparation that enhances their natural briny taste without overpowering it. The atmosphere at La Pilareta matches the quality of the food. It's unpretentious yet inviting, reflecting the vibrant yet relaxed spirit of Valencia. The service is warm and attentive, adding to the overall experience, making you feel like you're dining with friends. If you're planning a revisit, you're in for another treat as the menu, while rooted in traditional Valencian cuisine, always seems to have something new or a seasonal twist that keeps dining here exciting. La Pilareta isn't just a meal; it's an experience that beckons you to come back for more. Highly recommended for anyone looking to savor the essence of Valencian gastronomy.

reviews.author: Susanna Armentano
reviews.text: Excellent dishes, quality, portions and tastes. We’re so happy about this experience! And great shoutout to Nacho: an amazing waiter with lots of good energy, good tips and great smile! He made our experience even more memorable ❤️🥘🥰

reviews.author: K 2025
reviews.text: A solid 4 from me. We went at opening time with no queue. Excellent, friendly staff, eager to please and swapped one of our cold dishes no questions asked. The tasting menu for €30 was what most people were having. The dishes were decent and imaginative with a few misses. The oyster was lovely, the potato pillow interesting, the squid in white soup fabulous...for me a few were too spicy, the Asian numbers a bit meh (you're never going to win me over with torpedo prawns and a bowl of wasted tartar sauce) and horrifically I left some of the dessert as the white chocolate...not sure what it was, had a rubber like texture reminiscent of tip-ex. Worth coming to and I have no regrets.

reviews.author: Aleks Vladimirov
reviews.text: This was our first dine-in in Valencia. The restaurant was really nice and the waiter recommend us nice dishes to try. Beside the raw fish tapas that my friend had and was not so keen on, everything else was amazing. We love the deserts and my friend 5 year old enjoyed the surprised as well. The staff was very friendly.

reviews.author: Sergio
reviews.text: Amazing place for having lunch. The restaurant itself is really cozy. They offer a wide range of great dishes mixing different flavours, tastes and cultures. It worths trying them. They have a daily menu at a quite affordable price. The staff is nice and effective.

reviews.author: ernest ferreira
reviews.text: BEST. LUNCH. IN. VALENCIA. Wow! Wifey and I had the Menú Bocados today and it blew us away!!!!! 30€ per person. Very delicious and filling. Unique and modern dishes based on traditional tapas menu. The "cold" pizza was a delicious tuna tartare-like dish on a crispy shrimp/rice cake with avocado sauce. Would go back just for this dish alone. Will definitely be back. Maybe for dinner next time.

reviews.author: Chester Lee
reviews.text: The food is special, but we don’t like some of the dishes, but the waiters are very friendly and the atmosphere is really good. You can try once a time.

reviews.author: Daniel Enrique Mamat
reviews.text: Excellent food, service and atmosphere. The attention to detail is as expected from a 2-Star-Michelin cuisine. It was an excellent mix between meats/fish and vegetables. For me the highlight however (apart from the food) was the non-alcoholic/non-wine accompaniment. This mix of drinks of their own produce was an excellent pairing to their food and rounded up this immersive local culinary experience. Kudos to the chef, kitchen and service staff! We had a great experience and are looking forward to our next visit!

reviews.author: S E
reviews.text: Warning 😊 You either will like this place or you won’t! Vegetarian oriented cuisine but will add seafood creations into it. Gets a 5 star for presentation! If you like beef this place most likely will not get you excited. I gave all 5 for creativeness and presentation. As for taste buds satisfaction it gets a much less stars.

reviews.author: Laura Creedon
reviews.text: A perfect experience, thank you to the team. I traveled from Ireland, and was excited for months to visit, and it didn't disappoint in any way! I usually take loads of photos of great meals, but this experience felt too important to have my phone out (I took one photo, with permission from the staff). I did the wine pairing, and my partner got a gorgeous bottle of local Xarel-lo. Both were delicious, but if you love wine, just do the pairing, it was so meticulously considered, and I really enjoyed it. I actually found the pairing very generous. I definitely didn't expect a separate pairing for every single course. We did the full proposal, and I think it's a must if you visit. I'd hate to have missed out on a single plate or pairing that we enjoyed. Beautiful setting, and the front of house staff were absolutely amazing. I felt embarrassed arriving with poor Spanish, but their whole team spoke perfect English, so I didn't miss a single detail of what we were served, and they made me feel so welcome! This was my first 2 star experience, and I was nervous that the service and atmosphere would be stuffy/unfriendly, but the team were all SO sweet and fun in a professional manner. The Sommelier even let us join him briefly in their wine cellar, which I thought was a very kind gesture. Outstanding. The chefs table with the house cured tuna and beautifully umami fermented tomato drink. I could have stayed there forever. Stunning hospitality, I came away feeling like I learned a lot, and we really were treated like royalty. It was my partner's 50th, and the staff made it so special. Thank you to everyone, and sorry for the essay, but so many details were worth mentioning.

reviews.author: Nicolas Carvajal
reviews.text: Lives up to its renown. The food, service, and ambience were all impeccable. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Venkat Balasubramanian
reviews.text: A true farm-to-fork experience! This culinary experience will walk you through how they grow, preserve and cook their food to perfection. After traveling around in Spain for a few days, I come across a place that gives importance to fresh produce and presenting them well in each course. Also one of the few Michelin star restaurants that have a vegetarian tasting menu. Service was excellent and they made sure that we enjoy every bite. The staff was also able to answer all our questions. The sommelier was very knowledgeable and brought us some good selection. We were also taken to a chefs table where the chef was able to talk about using Carob for preserving tuna, etc. The croissant-sourdough hybrid was unbelievable! Some of the dishes were quite adventurous pushing you out of your comfort zone, but isn’t that the point of a chefs tasting menu? It was very fun.

reviews.text: So nice to have a skatepark, nice energy. However the park itself doesn't flow well and sometimes feels intimidating for beginners. There's a public beach near it, small but so nice! reviews.author: Ammar Alnajem
reviews.text: One of the best relaxing 😎 Urban Living Island style place for families. Durrat Al Bahrain is the third largest artificial island in Bahrain. Houses there are private, but the management have future plans for building apartments for rents, hotel and more small shops. All needed facilities are there including restaurants, supermarket, salon 💇, cafes, ice cream shop 🍦 , bicycle and golf carts rental.

reviews.author: Nim Narayanan
reviews.text: A Must-Visit for Adventure Lovers! If you enjoy outdoor activities and hiking, Wadi Shab is an absolute gem. It’s one of the most scenic spots in Oman, offering a mix of rugged beauty, crystal-clear water, and an unforgettable sense of adventure. The hike through the wadi is stunning — with towering cliffs, lush greenery, and serene pools along the way. But this isn’t just a walk in the park. Be prepared! ✅ Tips Before You Go: • Carry water shoes – The rocks are extremely slippery. • Wear a life jacket – Especially if you plan to swim into the famous cave. • Helmet (optional but smart) – Some parts are rocky and can be risky. • Bring your own water and food – You won’t find any shops or services inside. • Be prepared for self-rescue – There are no lifeguards or safety staff; you’re completely on your own. This place is pure adventure — thrilling and beautiful — but not for the unprepared. The effort is 100% worth it if you go ready and cautious.

reviews.author: Hamza Abdul Qadoos
reviews.text: Excellent place for fun. Long walk 50 minutes. Best time to visit early morning 5:30 start from origin. Difficult to take toddler but if you're strong enough you can manage. Amazing place to visit and swimming experience also nice. 10/10 recommended.. 👌🏻💐

reviews.author: Priya Agarwal
reviews.text: Indeed an adventurous experience! Something unforgettable…starting with renting shoes and life jackets, the hike throughout was a bit tiring but the views all along the route was extremely beautiful. The canyons and turquoise waters inculcates a spirit of curiosity for completing the hike. Reaching the water way, it is so soothing to swim, that is when all the hike in the heat pays off. Taking the water route, it is a beautiful experience to reach the famous narrow cave where you squeeze yourself out carefully to enjoy the waterfall there. A great haven for adventure seekers!

reviews.author: Honesty
reviews.text: A lifetime experience. Wadi in Oman is such a natural gem that everybody needs to try/ see at least once ! I had the chance to go and swim there with a guide that was also amazing! Don’t go alone please it’s pretty dangerous ! Specially girls always with a guide a local one of course. The water is so amazing refreshing and clean ! People are welcoming and it’s such actually a healing and peaceful place. Enjoy, but please be safe.

reviews.author: Mahmoud Zaghloul
reviews.text: Le Pirate Monastir is a must-visit dining experience! From the moment we walked in, the staff welcomed us warmly, making us feel right at home. The unique pirate-themed decor truly sets the restaurant apart – it’s like stepping into a ship, with incredible attention to detail that adds so much charm and character to the ambiance. As for the food, the set menu is truly a feast. We started with famous Tunisian harissa, yogurt and olive dishes with bread. Then we were served a legendary seafood soup. Afterwards, an assortment of fresh seafood appetizers, each more flavorful than the last. The shrimp was perfectly cooked, the mussel dish was lightly seasoned and fresh. The octopus was crafted in a mind blowing seasoned tomato sauce.Along side 3 different Tunisian salad dishes. For the main course, the grilled fish was the standout – juicy, flaky, and served with an array of delicious side dishes that complemented it beautifully. The portions were generous, and it was clear that only high-quality ingredients were used. Dessert was the perfect ending to a fantastic meal, with a beautifully presented fruit platter and lemon sorbet that left us completely satisfied. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared and added to the overall experience. If you appreciate fresh, flavorful Mediterranean cuisine in a one-of-a-kind setting, Le Pirate Monastir is a must-try. Highly recommend!

reviews.text: I would give this place a solid 3.5/5 stars. Wish they had an a la carte menu because the quality of dishes of the set menu was all over the place - 2-3 stars for the bread, fish soup, and various appetizers, and 4 stars for the grilled fish and dessert. If I could, I would skip the appetizers and just get the grilled fish, but it all comes together for 55TND. It’s also a lot of food for one person so I feel like I created a lot of food waste. Fish soup - mostly salty, not sure if there was even any fish in it (unless it’s just supposed to have fish flavor, not fish chunks) Appetizers - most of these were unexceptional and tasted like they had been sitting out for a while Grilled fish - this was actually fresh and tasted delicious Dessert - the fruit was so perfectly ripe and juicy. Also enjoyed the citron sorbet. I was stuffed at this point and didn’t get to the plate of cookies that they served alongside mint tea All in all, the food was decent, but the restaurant could definitely use improvements.

reviews.author: Mana Salem
reviews.text: The Kasbah des Oudayas in Rabat is a place where time slows to a whisper. Tucked at the mouth of the Bou Regreg River, this 12th-century fortress feels like a secret the Atlantic Ocean has been keeping. Its walls, painted in shades of white and blue so crisp they mimic the sky, curve around narrow alleys paved with stones worn smooth by centuries of footsteps. Walking through Bab Oudaya, the main gate, is like stepping into a postcard—if postcards could carry the scent of orange blossoms from the Andalusian Gardens or the salty breeze rolling off the water. The kasbah isn’t a museum; it’s alive. Locals lean in doorways, children dart between walls draped in bougainvillea, and stray cats nap in sunlit patches. Climb to the terrace of Café Maure, where mint tea arrives sticky-sweet alongside almond pastries, and the view stretches across the river to Salé’s sand-colored skyline. Below, the river churns where fishermen haul in their catch, and surfers bob in the distance, waiting for waves. The quietest corners hide the most stories. The Museum of Moroccan Arts—a restored 17th-century house—displays faded carpets and daggers, but the real magic is outside. Wander until the sounds of the city fade, and you’ll find yourself at Plateforme du Sémaphore, where the horizon blurs between sea and sky. This isn’t just a historic site—it’s a feeling, one that lingers long after you’ve left.

reviews.text: What a lovely little place! Low-key, quiet, in a beautiful setting, with tasty grilled seafood food, friendly service and a killer (alcohol-free) mojito. If you're in a hurry you're in the wrong place, but that's kind of the point, right? Not cheap by local standards but very reasonable by Western ones. Chairs and umbrellas can be rented by the day for a very reasonable rate.

reviews.author: Andree Ma
reviews.text: The most charming Dar right in the heart of Djerbahood, centre for amazing street mural art. You will be immersed in an intricate labyrinth scented by burgeoning bougainvillea, that leads from private corner to corner, each harbouring a unique chamber decorated in the traditional style, with names like Sheherazade, Prince Jasmin…Breakfast under a huge date palm in an open courtyard, or dine in the luxurious restaurant known for its haute cuisine. Attentive staff are all obliging with every request, from cutting up a watermelon we acquired in the local market and serving it beautifully on a huge silver platter, to indulging our excited 8 year old by the emerald pool just off our room. A must visit to taste the hospitality of Djerba, Island of Dreams! Thank you Dar Dhiafa, hope to see you again before too long!

reviews.author: Seif K
reviews.text: A beautiful hotel setup with elegant and traditional architecture. The food is amazing here and I highly recommend one or two nights here (for couples or adults only). Kids would be bored. If you can’t find a spot, make sure you go for dinner at least. Everything is fresh and tasty here.

reviews.author: Jurgen Coetsiers
reviews.text: This boutique hôtel has a magnificent architecture… the hotel as such is worth a visit. Rooms are simple but very elegant and all have a wonderful architecture. At night the hotel is romantically lit by lots of indirect lights. Staff is really friendly, hotel restaurant serves really good food. Breakfast is very ok. En top it is in a very nice neighbourhood full of wonderful street art and bars/cafes/restaurants. If you do not like the mass tourism feeling like in the Djerba souk… stay here… we stayed 2 nights with a daughter of 10.

reviews.author: Tikhon Levchenko
reviews.text: I’ve used only service of the restaurant. And in general I satisfied. The lamb was cooked nice and was left tender and juicy. Goat cheese which was introduced in the name of the dish I suppose wasn’t from goat milk. I guess it was just a Camembert. Alcohol options are surprisingly impressive if we keep in mind that we are in a Muslim country. A significant drawback is the presence of people smoking in the atrium, causing smoke to infiltrate the restaurant and detracting from the overall enjoyment of the atmosphere, service, and food.

reviews.author: Oana Misha Cancel
reviews.text: We stayed for just one night in the Princess Sherazade suite, because we had booked another place in advance, but then we came back almost daily for dinner, lunch, coffee. The suite is beautifuly decorated, the bed comfortable and the breakfast was pretty balanced from our point of view. We enjoyed most the quiet atmosphere, always smiling & helpful staff and the very nice pools. Also, the lighting in the evening is magnificent. The restaurant serves some traditional dishes, grilled fish and good desserts. We liked in particular the sea bream, shrimps with garlic, creme brulee. Because in the days of our holiday the heat was almost unbearable and it was impossible to do many things outside, we found at Dar Dhiafa an oasis of tranquility and comfort - cold pool, nice people, good food & beverages. Also, the masseuse is very polite and professional.

reviews.author: Teiva Boumah
reviews.text: Great place for people who like mediocre food for a premium price. If you are a foreigner and afraid of real Tunisian cuisine it’s the perfect place for you ! Great atmosphere, sad that the food is made for confused tourists. No the food is not fresh, I ordered a « symphony of the sea », the only thing I can say it’s that nothing was singing in my plate. 8 fries, 50g of fish, 2 frozen calmars, 2 small shrimps and weird vegetables. All of this for almost 20€, this restaurant would be scandal in France and even more of a scam in Tunisia. When I ask the server if he could eventually do something, he told me I can’t do anything « bonne appétit ». In conclusion if you’re white, if you hate the real taste of seafood, and if afraid of poor people. Then it’s the perfect place for you.

reviews.author: Doriana Todorova
reviews.text: Such a beautiful place! Celebrated my partners birthday there.The food was excellent.We had hot and cold starters all amazing.We chose the fish we wanted to have and we also had a massive steak. Service was very attentive and they made a little surprise for the birthday. The best restaurant in hammamet.

reviews.author: Mostafa Hassan
reviews.text: Staff was very friendly and the food was of quality and good portions.

reviews.author: Jack Leader
reviews.text: Amazing experience. Perfect, romantic evening in a fabulous setting. Wissem was our host, very friendly and accommodating. Beautiful restaurant. The lobster was mind blowing, my wife had the catch of the day. Thank you so much, Shukran Jack & Andrea

reviews.author: Siân
reviews.text: Beautiful restaurant. The food was incredible. Best steak and seafood we have had. We went for early dinner about 5pm. Lobster was all gone for the day but the staff showed us the fish they had and tailored a meal for us. He gave us lots of options and it was delicious! Don't forget to try the Tunisian wine.

reviews.author: Mohamed Lotfi Abdelkefi
reviews.text: This place is freaking amazing! The view blew my mind especially the sunset… It was clean and the host was very responsive and attentive, he even suggested places where we can eat etc. The only negative point is the access to the place, if you have a lot of luggage you will suffer for couple of minutes but its totally worth it!!

reviews.author: Omar Nejai
reviews.text: Dar El Bhar, nestled in the historic center of Hammamet, left me with lasting memories of this picturesque coastal town. This guest house offers a delightful blend of tradition and modernity, all while showcasing stunning views of the sea. Dar El Bhar's location is its biggest asset. Situated between the modern allure of Yasmin Hammamet and the timeless charm of Nabeul, it offers the perfect balance for travelers looking to explore both old and new. The proximity to the sea is unbeatable, allowing you to wake up to the sound of waves and enjoy beautiful sunsets. The rooms in this guest house are cozy and comfortable, each with a unique charm. While they may not be overly luxurious, they provide all the essentials for a pleasant stay. The sea-view rooms are a real treat, offering a sense of tranquility that's hard to find elsewhere. The staff at Dar El Bhar are friendly and attentive, always ready to assist with a warm smile. They can help you plan your day, arrange excursions, or provide recommendations for local dining and activities, making you feel like a welcomed guest. While the guest house offers the basics, it lacks some of the modern amenities you might find in larger hotels. However, this is compensated for by the authentic atmosphere and character of the place. The rooftop

reviews.author: Med ali Bellassir
reviews.text: Had a blast staying at Dar el Bhar's place. This treasure is located in the medina of Hammamet, easy access from coffee Sidi Bou Hdid, walkable to attractions and restaurants. The flat was sparkling clean and had all the essentials. Rooms with unique decor and sculptures, kitchen with all items you’d need, the beds were comfy, great shower, the jetted bath was great bonus. There's a gorgeous view of the beach and an amazing rooftop to watch the sunset. Friendly and attentive staff, and the cleaning lady came in the morning and made us a delicious breakfast. It definitely makes the top list of hosts in Hammamet Hilighy!

reviews.text: This is a funky little part-time art gallery which doubles as a guest house in Sidi Bou Said. The staff are friendly, casual and hardworking but the place could do with a bit of sprucing up. Don't come expecting a fancy hotel experience, but I felt that it was clean enough (although a pair of guests from Switzerland left while I was there, claiming it was too dusty). I liked this place for what it was, which is a nice little hangout to get to the amazing beaches at the bottom of the hill. Unsure if I would come again, but ho-hum.
