reviews.author: Sofia Scrans
reviews.text: a dinner worth every dinar la bella marina (hammamet sud, tunisia) nibbles: with our meal we were served complimentary bread and dips. these included cucumber salad, pepper salsa, onion salsa, tomato compote, olives, and butter. this mini platter was a lovely start to our meal. tomato and mozzarella salad: i LOVE tomato and mozzarella, so as soon as i saw this on the menu i knew i was going to get this. i feel like there could have been a little more mozzarella in this salad as it was a little overpowered by the tomato, but you can’t really go wrong with this salad, especially paired with basil. this salad will always receive a thumbs up from me filet mignon: WOW. this dish was incredible. i was served three cuts of streak in the most beautiful creamy mushroom sauce. i asked for my steak to be cooked rare and it came out medium rare(ish) which is still okay for me. it was served with roasted vegetables and chips. the chips were a little underdone for me, but still okay. very, very, very nice dish. lamb shank: the lamb shank was cooked beautifully. it fell away from the bone and tasted delicious. the sauce it was served with could have been a little different in my eyes. it was a gravy made from the lamb so didn’t add much to it. i would have preferred something a little fruity or herby, but it was still okay. this does not take away from how tender and tasty the lamb was. the lamb was served with chips and roasted vegetables, the same as the filet mignon. the service here was great. the staff were so attentive without being overbearing. i ordered wine with the meal, which turned out to be a full bottle! i would love to come back here again and try their seafood - it looks amazing!

reviews.author: Andrew Trickey
reviews.text: We arrived at 7pm so the first diners in the restaurant. My wife had a peppered steak, I had the Bella Marina Steak, which was a surf and turf, with a fillet steak and longustine. For dessert we ordered the delicious dish, which is simply a dessert sharer. The food was delicious and well prepared. A few more fries would have been nice, but thats being picky. The bill came to 223 dt (or £52) and included 4 bottles of beer. We were also collected and returned to our hotel. Would definitely recommend and revisit.

reviews.author: MrTiggersaurus
reviews.text: Fabulous restaurant. We first visited in the 24th October as we were getting bored with the all-inclusive at the hotel. Great food, great service, and great price (we paid 367dt, which is about £90) for both my wife and I, as well as our 10-year-old twins. This included 3 course meals and drinks, with complimentary bread. This sounds expensive, but considering I paid about £71 for 3 bland hot dogs with stale chips and a salad at Luton airport a couple of days beforehand, it's definitely worth it. We enjoyed it so much that we went back there a few days later, and we were not disappointed. I had the Mediterranean Fry for a starter. It was massive, so much so that I struggled to finish eating it - and I can eat! I also had fillet steak with roquefort cheese, which cost about £15, I would have paid at least £35 for a similar dish in the UK. I really did fancy having lobster, but you have to choose which one you want to have. They are still alive, and I couldn't bring myself to decide which one would be killed, but that's a discussion for another day. The desserts are amazing too, I went for the chocolate mousse on both occasions, and it was delicious. Well worth the visit if you are in the area.

reviews.author: Mr S
reviews.text: Great restaurant with good chateau Briand excellent service

reviews.author: Joanne Shaftoe, CWU
reviews.text: Got a free taxi there and back from our hotel and was pleasantly greeted upon arrival. The waiter was very helpful in suggesting a fish dish for me and even brought out the trolley to show that day's catches (including a huge live lobster!) We went with shrimp cocktail and octopus salad for starters; both delicious. Then for mains we had fillet mignon with a mushroom and peppercorn sauce and the recommended fish fillets with a lovely rich, creamy sauce. Both cooked to perfection. We had a bottle of red wine and a lemon sorbet each to finish. Total bill £58. Bargain!

reviews.author: Jeremy Bellefois
reviews.text: Great experience. Top ambience, top service, and good food. ✅️ Variety of food with a beautiful presentation. ✅️ Ambience is amazing at night, with the low light and candles. ✅️ Waiters are professional and polite. ✅️ Wine is served by glass also, if you don't want to go for a full bottle 🚩 Parking in summer is a hustle. 🚩 Prices are expensive if you're on budget 🚩 Too many stairs to reach the top, if you can't walk

reviews.author: Paul White
reviews.text: Delicious food with great portions, friendly staff, and a great view. Very clean and hygienic. Downside is there are quite a few stairs to get to it and the entrance is a little hidden. Highly recommended though.

reviews.text: Amazing place - tasty food, good service and nice atmosphere. We were there in the evening and there was beautiful sunset view

reviews.author: Ghofrane Rabaaoui
reviews.text: I ordered the filet de bœuf. The presentation was nice, but the taste was just average. The atmosphere was medium, and for 84 DT, the portion was small and not worth the price. I expected better

reviews.author: Pier Acerni
reviews.text: Best in town! Great fresh fish really well done and served. Portions are enough and taste is great, not covered by garlic 😝 We had a great time! Highly recommend

reviews.author: Eleftheria Chrys (Ec)
reviews.text: Probably the best dining experience in Tunisia! Great atmosphere! Friendly staff. Located on the beach La Marsa, with great views of water. Serving alcohol!!! Very tasty food, mixed local and international cuisine! I simply loved it!!!

reviews.author: Juliet Choo
reviews.text: Food was excellent. Great view too. Staff are friendly and attentive. Free WIFI provided. Booking is required to avoid disappointment.

reviews.author: Daniel Tam
reviews.text: I was having high expectations but they fell short. The food was mediocre - calamari was soggy! Grilled fish was quite good though.The seat we were given was too dark and even the mobile table lamp was not working. Service was passable.

reviews.author: Saladin Elkadiki
reviews.text: Great Restaurant in Tunis with great sea and beach view. Food and wine selection good for Tunis but there is room to improve. Steak was average, perhaps could be better. The seafood main dishes were a bit dull and not as fresh as we hoped. The calamari was too oily and too much bread batter causing it to be soggy not crisp. Should consider Italian or Greek style of Calamari. The Octopus Carpaccio was tasty and well presented but the Dorade Carpaccio was not fresh tasting and had a bit of bitter taste and the Boutarga was low grade. Some dishes were not available unfortunate but service is great and dessert selection is excellent.

reviews.author: Houssem Eddine Fadhli
reviews.text: Le Golfe is hands down one of my top restaurants. The vibe is super chill, right by the water, and the food never disappoints-especially the seafood, it's always fresh and delicious. Perfect place for a sunset dinner or just to hang out with friends. Service is great too, friendly and professional. If you haven't been yet, you're missing out!

reviews.text: Taxi driver recommended this. What an amazing find. We ordered sea bass and calamari and fresh orange juice. We were given free gazpacho, olives, salads and an amazing basket of bread. Afterwards we had complementary mint tea. The whole meal was less than £20 for 2 and totally delicious.

reviews.author: Wojtek Ziółkowski
reviews.text: Nice place to seat, low prices and very yummy food. Very near to fort and sea, so location is great. Restaurant doesn't look attractive, but it's definitely worth to eat there.

reviews.author: Molka Farhood
reviews.text: Very tasty and for starters. Limited outdoor seating. Annoying cats under the tables while eating. Tasty souris d’agneau. Average stuffed squid. Fries 5/5. No kids menu. Not a restaurant for kids. reviews.text: This restaurant can be consider the best one in Hammamet. When you arrive just enter and ask to see the fish. You can choose what you want to have and how to have it cooked. They bring a fish soup, tunisinian salad and bread complimentary and the service is just stunning as the food. You can decide to eat in one of the room with AC or outside under the little patio. But if you choose the outside, please consider you are near the street and cars are just passing nearby. We tried several dishes during the week, including the cous-cous. Everything was good and I highly recommend to eat here!

reviews.author: Amine Salem
reviews.text: This is the best restaurant in Hammamet. The service is fast and I would like to thank Mr Ramzi for his professionalism and generosity. We order steaks and they cooked them in front of us which made the experience even better. The main dishes and the tea at the end made it even better. Highly recommended

reviews.author: luvfeelin 乐飞翎 (乐飞翎)
reviews.text: Hidden gem at this beautiful place. We were attracted by the reviews and made a decision to try it here. It is a Saturday noon and the restaurant is almost full, luckily we managed to get a few tables for our group. As we have a small appetite, four of us ordered a seafood platter at 100 dinar (for 2 pax) and it comes with side dishes. The seafood is fresh and well cooked. Food served was considered fast under the circumstances of the full house. Staff are being helpful and responsive to us tourist. Truly recommended to those who visit Hamammet and are looking for good food.

reviews.author: T K
reviews.text: Best food in Hammamet! As tourists we’ve tried different food places but within those 4 days this has been the best where we are full and happy with everything. The best orange juice we’ve tried in our life. Definitely recommend and amazing service!

reviews.author: marwa nasri
reviews.text: I highly recommend this place, welcoming staff, cleanliness, mekla bnina and panoramic view of the old port 🥰🥰

reviews.author: Mounir Benamor
reviews.text: Excellent location with a beautiful view of the port. Poor value for money, air conditioning in the middle of summer almost non-existent, cleanliness leaves something to be desired (dirty cutlery). We ordered two breakfast options. As the traditional menu was not available, we took the gourmet menu.

reviews.author: elxas lnz
reviews.text: Great place, good atmosphere Very relaxed Nice waiters

reviews.author: Mahmoud Zaghloul
reviews.text: Le Pirate Monastir is a must-visit dining experience! From the moment we walked in, the staff welcomed us warmly, making us feel right at home. The unique pirate-themed decor truly sets the restaurant apart – it’s like stepping into a ship, with incredible attention to detail that adds so much charm and character to the ambiance. As for the food, the set menu is truly a feast. We started with famous Tunisian harissa, yogurt and olive dishes with bread. Then we were served a legendary seafood soup. Afterwards, an assortment of fresh seafood appetizers, each more flavorful than the last. The shrimp was perfectly cooked, the mussel dish was lightly seasoned and fresh. The octopus was crafted in a mind blowing seasoned tomato sauce.Along side 3 different Tunisian salad dishes. For the main course, the grilled fish was the standout – juicy, flaky, and served with an array of delicious side dishes that complemented it beautifully. The portions were generous, and it was clear that only high-quality ingredients were used. Dessert was the perfect ending to a fantastic meal, with a beautifully presented fruit platter and lemon sorbet that left us completely satisfied. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared and added to the overall experience. If you appreciate fresh, flavorful Mediterranean cuisine in a one-of-a-kind setting, Le Pirate Monastir is a must-try. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Bedoui Jassem
reviews.text: The restaurant is perfectly located within the Monastir port. The food quality is excellent, and the portions are generous. The dessert was wonderful, complemented by live music from a nearby singer. The staff are friendly and empathetic, making the experience even more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Jad Chammas
reviews.text: Great service, food and atmosphere. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Michelle
reviews.text: I would give this place a solid 3.5/5 stars. Wish they had an a la carte menu because the quality of dishes of the set menu was all over the place - 2-3 stars for the bread, fish soup, and various appetizers, and 4 stars for the grilled fish and dessert. If I could, I would skip the appetizers and just get the grilled fish, but it all comes together for 55TND. It’s also a lot of food for one person so I feel like I created a lot of food waste. Fish soup - mostly salty, not sure if there was even any fish in it (unless it’s just supposed to have fish flavor, not fish chunks) Appetizers - most of these were unexceptional and tasted like they had been sitting out for a while Grilled fish - this was actually fresh and tasted delicious Dessert - the fruit was so perfectly ripe and juicy. Also enjoyed the citron sorbet. I was stuffed at this point and didn’t get to the plate of cookies that they served alongside mint tea All in all, the food was decent, but the restaurant could definitely use improvements.

reviews.author: Jan
reviews.text: The food is excellent! I got to this place expecting a menu but I directly got some fish soup and I didn't mind, then I figured out they have the same service for everyone. After the soup I got some delicious appetizers. And after that I got a grilled fish which was very tasty. And we finished with some fruits, Ice cream and dessert. It was a nice experience, which I only can recommend. I will go back gladly :)

reviews.author: Ross Daniels
reviews.text: Lovely place large & nice setting. Staff were courteous & friendly. Food was ok. I think our experience was let down by the very long wait for food. That was a pity because the setting is very pleasant.

reviews.author: Diane Ha
reviews.text: It was nice and quiet during lunchtime on a Monday. Decent sized building with ample seating with different feel; sunny outdoor, partial open roof, indoor casual cafeteria feel, indoor cave wall-like romantic feel. The staff were friendly, helpful and spoke some English. The food was delicious and ingredients were fresh. I got a perfectly grilled sea bream - meat was tender and skin slightly charred, with just a hint of spices where its guts were cleared out from. The fresh salad and grilled vegetables were the perfect amount, variety and balance of flavors. The generous side dish of chickpeas, fresh fennel, olives and bread left me satiated at the end. Looking forward to going back!

reviews.author: Ayesha Seedat
reviews.text: The food was outstanding and the service was impeccable. We had the Citron line fish which was the best meal we had in Tunis !!!!!!

reviews.author: Nayeem Chowdhury
reviews.text: Food was not too great. Ordered their mix of seafood and mixed meat platters and everything on each platter was poor except the tempura prawns. The lamb chops they gave were so small it can be finished after a single bite. The meatballs and merguez tasted like paper mâche and there were no flavour to it. The calimari was hard and too rubbery, it was overcooked. The simplest item to make was the chips and they messed that up too. They were soggy as if they were microwaved. After telling the chef this, they made a fresh batch which also looked microwaved and were just hot and soggy. Don't recommend. Poor place to eat and expensive.

reviews.text: Compared to other hotels i have experienced after this one, i really came to appreciate el fell, it's a decent hotel with all the necessary needs. The staff were all kind and helpful, the food was fairly decent and the place is well located for people who just want to relax and enjoy the Mediterranean. There are enough high end restaurants and cafeterias near by, it's not far from hammamt yasmine but far enough to not be bothered by the loud noises and the crowded roads. The rooms weren't clean but once i told the housekeeper they made a little more effort to clean it. The beach was amazing, well equipped with many activities to do there and many vendors coming and going selling all type of goods. I will without a doubt in mind go back to this hotel as i feel like it's a decent gem that deserves a chance

reviews.author: Julia Kirby Homeopathy
reviews.text: Hugely mixed feelings about Hotel El Fell. On the one hand, they checked me in 3 hours early, offered a late checkout, and upgraded my room. The staff couldn't have been kinder or more helpful. On the other hand, the rooms are a little tatty and there was a full ashtray on the balcony, and several public hairs in the bath and wash basin, and a hole in the bath. The hotel is generally so quiet, that meals are taken in the sister hotel, which I had to hunt down myself, as nobody spoke enough English to help me. I even had to check in with the aid of Google Translate. When I asked where lunch was served, I ended up with a full tour, until he asked what I wanted and I said I was hungry. Turns out he'd misunderstood completely. I still haven't managed to figure out how or where to order a drink, other than the water, that thankfully comes with meals. The staff seem to avoid serving drinks, although I can't help but notice, that the Russians get table service. I've heard complaints about there only being WiFi in the reception, but I had WiFi on the beach, by the pool, and even slow service in my room. The location is perfect, and the beach beautiful, I'm fact the best location of all the hotels my transfer stopped at. With a little tlc, this could be an absolute haven, but for now, come for the location and lovely friendly staff, if you don't mind a Youth Hostel level of accommodation. And if you do come, study the Russians, and follow their lead. 😉

reviews.text: Worst experience ever in Tunisia! I love this country but this place is really awful. We arrived at 1pm so we wanted to take a brunch but according to the waiter, the restaurant policy imposes that if you’re not having lunch you’re not allowed to sit at the first row in the terrace, where there is a good sea view, knowing that the place was not crowded at all at that moment. Also, we received our order 45 minutes after we made it, they served us the hot drinks first so they became cold. I would not recommend at all.

reviews.author: Lena Magda
reviews.text: I stayed at this hotel with a friend at the end of May. Beautiful hotel and great service The resort has three swimming pools: one smaller and quieter, a second one a bit bigger with quite loud music, and a third indoor pool with lovely warm water. The hotel is situated in such a way that there is a kind of old city centre and market with local stalls around it. There are always taxis in front of the hotel; a ride a few kilometres into the city costs about 3 to 4 euros. The beach is only a 5-minute walk away. There you can enjoy a pizza margherita, beer and soft drinks under the all-inclusive concept. In addition, there are many other dishes available for very reasonable prices. Sunbeds are free, beach towels are provided at the hotel (you pay a deposit that you get back when you return the towels). The beach is cleaned regularly by hotel staff. The toilets on the beach are much cleaner than those in Scheveningen! The service in the hotel is of the highest level: the waiters are fantastic, the pool attendant, the reception — really a 12 out of 10! Hygiene in the hotel: the rooms are cleaned daily and the towels are changed daily. Of course, you can always find something to complain about, but let's not forget: Tunisia is and remains Africa. Very often, immediately after a meal, the waiters not only replaced the dishes, but also the white tablecloth for a clean one. The food: the breakfast is simple, but otherwise nothing to complain about. This is the first hotel where I have had really good coffee! Fresh fish and different types of meat every day. Freshly squeezed juices for breakfast. Everyone will find something to their taste here. Most of the guests in the hotel are French. Some people forget or do not know that the bacterial flora in African countries is very different. It is always wise to buy probiotics at the pharmacy and take them on the day of departure. Euros are best exchanged at the hotel reception. Remember that it is forbidden to take Tunisian dinars home from Tunisia. It is also quite difficult to exchange dinars back to euros, so I recommend exchanging small amounts and more often.

reviews.text: This is a beautiful town with very hospitable people. There aren't many sellers / hawkers constantly pestering you too but their wares, so you can really enjoy your stroll through town. We went later in the day when it cooled down a bit and there were fewer people in the streets.

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. Chefchaouen is a must-visit for photographers, art lovers, and anyone looking to experience Morocco’s laid-back and artistic side. Whether you’re exploring the picturesque alleys, enjoying a mint tea in a cozy café, or watching the sunset from a hilltop, every moment here feels magical.

reviews.author: Wanderfly Travel
reviews.text: Beautiful city! I love the colors, the people, the food and most importantly the shops on the street😍 If you want to get away to the mountains for some peaceful time away from the city, I highly recommend spending two or three days in Chefchaouen!

reviews.author: Mourad Chafik
reviews.text: Chefchaouen’s medina is truly one of the most beautiful and peaceful places I’ve ever visited. The blue-washed walls, narrow alleys, and stunning doors create a dreamlike atmosphere that feels both relaxing and inspiring. Locals are friendly, the shops offer authentic handmade crafts, and there are plenty of cozy cafes to enjoy traditional Moroccan tea. It's the perfect place to wander without a map, discover hidden gems, and take amazing photos at every corner. Whether you're there for the colors, the culture, or just the peaceful vibe—Chefchaouen is unforgettable

reviews.author: Said Belowahed
reviews.text: Rabat is an amazing city to visit, There is a lot of places to see and enjoy, Hassan tower is an amazing place with the Shrine next to it, and view to river. The Mausoleum of Mohammed V is a mausoleum located on the opposite side of the Hassan Tower, on the Yacoub al-Mansour esplanade in Rabat, Morocco. It contains the tombs of the Moroccan king and his two sons, late King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah. The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah in Rabat, Morocco. It is located at the mouth of the Bou Regreg river opposite Salé. The Chellah or Shalla, is a medieval fortified Muslim necropolis located in the metro area of Rabat, Morocco, on the south side of the Bou Regreg estuary. The Phoenicians established a trading emporium at the site.

reviews.text: I really liked this medina, very little touristy and essentially frequented by the inhabitants of Rabat. while walking its streets I learned a lot about local habits. Inside the medina are some good restaurants, so you have to ask them why they are difficult to find. Medina very safe

reviews.author: Greg D
reviews.text: A magical and varied island, full of deep historical architecture and rich welcoming culture. The food and wine was excellent, whether we ate simple local food or went high end. I had very little idea how liveable it would feel, as the old town has everything one could need to be comfortable. A slower simpler pace of living is possible here, and we were lucky to have stayed with a wonderful warm family that shared home cooked delights with us. We also found it easy to travel around and go to other islands. The weather is perfect for me as it’s hot yet breezy so I would recommend it to those who also enjoy that kind of feel.

reviews.author: MJ Bold
reviews.text: We visited Old town bazaar clothes shop yesterday, a truly amazing shopping experience; not only did they pay for myself and my families free taxi transport to and from our hotel. The customer service was second to none. The shop has everything you would ever want, the best clothes, footwear, designer bags, and loads more. An enormous range of the latest styles and fashions, at reasonable prices. We were made to feel really welcome by all the staff, and even given free refreshing cooling drinks. Had our every need met, by Mehmet and his excellent very friendly, polite and professional team. There were so many highlights, during our shopping trip, the adorable cats, and the astonishing clothes choices. One of the best things is after we brought lots of clothes, we were able to leave them in the trusted hands of the shop and go off sightseeing, returning later, where the taxi driver Ali who was amazing, one of the most helpful and kind person we've ever met. Delivery them and us back to our hotel. Great value for money, we would definitely comeback again. The old town shop location itself is breathtaking and a stone throw away from the famous historical Roman Hadrian's Gate and the stunning marina.

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: This has got to be the best souk in Morocco! I’ve been to many, but Essaouira’s felt so special. I spent about five hours there and still didn’t want to leave. Each shop has its own unique vibe, and the shopkeepers were incredibly kind and helpful. Every time I asked where to find something, they wouldn’t just point me in the direction—they’d actually walk me there and leave without the other shopkeepers noticing. It was such a genuine experience. You’ll find everything from handmade Moroccan teapots and beautiful tea glasses to breathtaking paintings and handmade rugs, linen clothing, genuine leather goods, and the most fragrant spices. If you’re looking for authentic treasures, this is the place!

reviews.author: Salam Almoghraby
reviews.text: A tour agency booked this hotel for us *** Beautiful property that has seen better days. The caretaker is the highlight of the property and her cooking (extra charge) is the best we had in Kairouan. She went above and beyond and was the highlight for us in an otherwise unfortunate stay. Unfortunately the rest of the property is run down and the upstairs terrace, whilst giving a nice vantage view, is abandoned with dead plants and broken sun ravaged furniture. The room we were given had two double beds on either side of a large room but unfortunately it did not have a bathroom with a shower or hot water... just a toilet and a sink with cold water. Might be refreshing in the summer, but it was miserable when we stayed because it was cold. The room does have access to a shower in the kitchen next door but you do need to walk the internal space to access it. It might not be an issue for most. The other room with an ensuite did have a shower (with a very short curtain so water got everywhere) and hot water, but the beds were singles. Also, the bathroom doors in both rooms did not close. We were offered plenty of clean towels. The bed sheet had a stain but I was told that it is clean but just stained. The heavy blankets had a not so fresh smell to them, but I am one of those people that has a very keen sense of smell. The closets were very dusty when we arrived, so much so that you could not put clothes in them, but a housekeeper was called and when we returned to the room in the evening the shelves were dusted and fabric places on the shelving so we could put our clothes, and the bathroom was cleaned. The room does not have tea making facilities but you can ask for tea and coffee from the caretaker. The house is one of the oldest houses so tourists come to have a look... but it was weird having strangers come into the room I was staying in and I was glad I had cleaned up and locked my suitcase. There is a water pump that turns on every 5 seconds for 7 seconds in the nighttime. I counted. I thankfully had ear plugs...also, I told the caretaker and she just switched it off at night for the rest of the night we were there and it was very silent and serene. We went in Ramadan which is a difficult month to travel and we understand that everyone is tired...but the property needs serious TLC for the price that they are asking. Better properties are available for less. It is hard to write an honest review when someone at the property was so kind and did their best... but I would have wanted a warning to know what i was getting into. The location is amazing and so close to the masjid which was great because we did our early morning prayers there in Ramadan.

reviews.author: Jameela Deen
reviews.text: Perfect place to stay when in Kairouan We spent 2 nights in the Zakia Suite in April 2019 and everything was prefect and even more! The suite was stunning in the old traditional Tunisian style. The bed linens were fresh and clean and everything was there for a good night sleep. The suite was spacious enough and decorated with old style furniture. It was absolutely clean. The rest of the house is worth a visit in itself and spectacular. Breakfast was served on the rooftop terrace and everything was made fresh and delicious (especially the oranges, the best I've ever had). The lady even went to the market each morning to bring back fresh bread, croissants and donuts. There was definitely enough food for everyone and some more that we took for our day's walk around the city. The lady in charge, Madame Feten, is extremely friendly and welcoming and went beyond what we could expect from a guest house host. She even cooked a traditional Tunisian couscous when my kids told her they liked Tunisian food. Added bonus: she can speak English and French as well as Arabic. The location of the house couldn't be better: right in the heart of the old medina, a very short walk from the souk/market and the Great Mosque of Kairouan which you can actually see from the roof. Easy to find, parking space available too. Only one word: PERFECT

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. Chefchaouen is a must-visit for photographers, art lovers, and anyone looking to experience Morocco’s laid-back and artistic side. Whether you’re exploring the picturesque alleys, enjoying a mint tea in a cozy café, or watching the sunset from a hilltop, every moment here feels magical.

Locals are friendly, the shops offer authentic handmade crafts, and there are plenty of cozy cafes to enjoy traditional Moroccan tea. Whether you're there for the colors, the culture, or just the peaceful vibe—Chefchaouen is unforgettable

reviews.author: Mahmoud Zaghloul
reviews.text: Le Pirate Monastir is a must-visit dining experience! From the moment we walked in, the staff welcomed us warmly, making us feel right at home. The unique pirate-themed decor truly sets the restaurant apart – it’s like stepping into a ship, with incredible attention to detail that adds so much charm and character to the ambiance. As for the food, the set menu is truly a feast. We started with famous Tunisian harissa, yogurt and olive dishes with bread. Then we were served a legendary seafood soup. Afterwards, an assortment of fresh seafood appetizers, each more flavorful than the last. The shrimp was perfectly cooked, the mussel dish was lightly seasoned and fresh. The octopus was crafted in a mind blowing seasoned tomato sauce.Along side 3 different Tunisian salad dishes. For the main course, the grilled fish was the standout – juicy, flaky, and served with an array of delicious side dishes that complemented it beautifully. The portions were generous, and it was clear that only high-quality ingredients were used. Dessert was the perfect ending to a fantastic meal, with a beautifully presented fruit platter and lemon sorbet that left us completely satisfied. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared and added to the overall experience. If you appreciate fresh, flavorful Mediterranean cuisine in a one-of-a-kind setting, Le Pirate Monastir is a must-try. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Bedoui Jassem
reviews.text: The restaurant is perfectly located within the Monastir port. The food quality is excellent, and the portions are generous. The dessert was wonderful, complemented by live music from a nearby singer. The staff are friendly and empathetic, making the experience even more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Jad Chammas

reviews.author: Michelle
reviews.text: I would give this place a solid 3.5/5 stars. Wish they had an a la carte menu because the quality of dishes of the set menu was all over the place - 2-3 stars for the bread, fish soup, and various appetizers, and 4 stars for the grilled fish and dessert. If I could, I would skip the appetizers and just get the grilled fish, but it all comes together for 55TND. It’s also a lot of food for one person so I feel like I created a lot of food waste. Fish soup - mostly salty, not sure if there was even any fish in it (unless it’s just supposed to have fish flavor, not fish chunks) Appetizers - most of these were unexceptional and tasted like they had been sitting out for a while Grilled fish - this was actually fresh and tasted delicious Dessert - the fruit was so perfectly ripe and juicy. Also enjoyed the citron sorbet. I was stuffed at this point and didn’t get to the plate of cookies that they served alongside mint tea All in all, the food was decent, but the restaurant could definitely use improvements.

reviews.text: The food is excellent! I got to this place expecting a menu but I directly got some fish soup and I didn't mind, then I figured out they have the same service for everyone. It was a nice experience, which I only can recommend. I will go back gladly :)

reviews.author: Diane Ha
reviews.text: It was nice and quiet during lunchtime on a Monday. Decent sized building with ample seating with different feel; sunny outdoor, partial open roof, indoor casual cafeteria feel, indoor cave wall-like romantic feel. The staff were friendly, helpful and spoke some English. The food was delicious and ingredients were fresh. I got a perfectly grilled sea bream - meat was tender and skin slightly charred, with just a hint of spices where its guts were cleared out from. The fresh salad and grilled vegetables were the perfect amount, variety and balance of flavors. The generous side dish of chickpeas, fresh fennel, olives and bread left me satiated at the end. Looking forward to going back!

The calimari was hard and too rubbery, it was overcooked. The simplest item to make was the chips and they messed that up too. They were soggy as if they were microwaved. After telling the chef this, they made a fresh batch which also looked microwaved and were just hot and soggy. Don't recommend. Poor place to eat and expensive.

reviews.text: This was by far the best place I stayed in Tunisia! Salma was so lovely, I felt instantly like a member of her family. My friend and I had booked a room with two beds, but she gave us each our own room to make us more comfortable. She helped us with anything we needed, from suggestions on the best way to get around, to finding a guide (for Carthage when we returned to Tunis!), to booking ferry tickets to the Kerkennah Islands, to doing laundry. Her cooking was also fantastic. In addition to the generous and delicious breakfasts, we had dinner with her twice and it was the best food I ate in Tunisia. She also brought us tea and cake when we got back in the afternoons. The rooms were very comfortable and the house is very spacious. We had a car, which made staying there more convenient, and she gave us a key fob for the gate so we could come and go as we pleased. I'm so glad I stayed at Dar Salma!

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: This has got to be the best souk in Morocco! I’ve been to many, but Essaouira’s felt so special. I spent about five hours there and still didn’t want to leave. Each shop has its own unique vibe, and the shopkeepers were incredibly kind and helpful. Every time I asked where to find something, they wouldn’t just point me in the direction—they’d actually walk me there and leave without the other shopkeepers noticing. It was such a genuine experience. You’ll find everything from handmade Moroccan teapots and beautiful tea glasses to breathtaking paintings and handmade rugs, linen clothing, genuine leather goods, and the most fragrant spices. reviews.author: Mahmoud Zaghloul
reviews.text: Le Pirate Monastir is a must-visit dining experience! From the moment we walked in, the staff welcomed us warmly, making us feel right at home. The unique pirate-themed decor truly sets the restaurant apart – it’s like stepping into a ship, with incredible attention to detail that adds so much charm and character to the ambiance. As for the food, the set menu is truly a feast. We started with famous Tunisian harissa, yogurt and olive dishes with bread. Then we were served a legendary seafood soup. Afterwards, an assortment of fresh seafood appetizers, each more flavorful than the last. The shrimp was perfectly cooked, the mussel dish was lightly seasoned and fresh. The octopus was crafted in a mind blowing seasoned tomato sauce.Along side 3 different Tunisian salad dishes. For the main course, the grilled fish was the standout – juicy, flaky, and served with an array of delicious side dishes that complemented it beautifully. The portions were generous, and it was clear that only high-quality ingredients were used. Dessert was the perfect ending to a fantastic meal, with a beautifully presented fruit platter and lemon sorbet that left us completely satisfied. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared and added to the overall experience. If you appreciate fresh, flavorful Mediterranean cuisine in a one-of-a-kind setting, Le Pirate Monastir is a must-try. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Bedoui Jassem
reviews.text: The restaurant is perfectly located within the Monastir port. The food quality is excellent, and the portions are generous. The dessert was wonderful, complemented by live music from a nearby singer. The staff are friendly and empathetic, making the experience even more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Michelle
reviews.text: I would give this place a solid 3.5/5 stars. Wish they had an a la carte menu because the quality of dishes of the set menu was all over the place - 2-3 stars for the bread, fish soup, and various appetizers, and 4 stars for the grilled fish and dessert. If I could, I would skip the appetizers and just get the grilled fish, but it all comes together for 55TND. It’s also a lot of food for one person so I feel like I created a lot of food waste. Fish soup - mostly salty, not sure if there was even any fish in it (unless it’s just supposed to have fish flavor, not fish chunks) Appetizers - most of these were unexceptional and tasted like they had been sitting out for a while Grilled fish - this was actually fresh and tasted delicious Dessert - the fruit was so perfectly ripe and juicy. Also enjoyed the citron sorbet. I was stuffed at this point and didn’t get to the plate of cookies that they served alongside mint tea All in all, the food was decent, but the restaurant could definitely use improvements.

I got a perfectly grilled sea bream - meat was tender and skin slightly charred, with just a hint of spices where its guts were cleared out from. The fresh salad and grilled vegetables were the perfect amount, variety and balance of flavors. The generous side dish of chickpeas, fresh fennel, olives and bread left me satiated at the end. Looking forward to going back!

reviews.author: Lena Magda
reviews.text: I stayed at this hotel with a friend at the end of May. Beautiful hotel and great service The resort has three swimming pools: one smaller and quieter, a second one a bit bigger with quite loud music, and a third indoor pool with lovely warm water. The hotel is situated in such a way that there is a kind of old city centre and market with local stalls around it. There are always taxis in front of the hotel; a ride a few kilometres into the city costs about 3 to 4 euros. The beach is only a 5-minute walk away. There you can enjoy a pizza margherita, beer and soft drinks under the all-inclusive concept. In addition, there are many other dishes available for very reasonable prices. Sunbeds are free, beach towels are provided at the hotel (you pay a deposit that you get back when you return the towels). The beach is cleaned regularly by hotel staff. The toilets on the beach are much cleaner than those in Scheveningen! The service in the hotel is of the highest level: the waiters are fantastic, the pool attendant, the reception — really a 12 out of 10! Hygiene in the hotel: the rooms are cleaned daily and the towels are changed daily. Of course, you can always find something to complain about, but let's not forget: Tunisia is and remains Africa. Very often, immediately after a meal, the waiters not only replaced the dishes, but also the white tablecloth for a clean one. The food: the breakfast is simple, but otherwise nothing to complain about. This is the first hotel where I have had really good coffee! Fresh fish and different types of meat every day. Freshly squeezed juices for breakfast. Everyone will find something to their taste here. Most of the guests in the hotel are French. Some people forget or do not know that the bacterial flora in African countries is very different. It is always wise to buy probiotics at the pharmacy and take them on the day of departure. Euros are best exchanged at the hotel reception. Remember that it is forbidden to take Tunisian dinars home from Tunisia. It is also quite difficult to exchange dinars back to euros, so I recommend exchanging small amounts and more often.

reviews.text: This is a beautiful town with very hospitable people. There aren't many sellers / hawkers constantly pestering you too but their wares, so you can really enjoy your stroll through town. We went later in the day when it cooled down a bit and there were fewer people in the streets.

reviews.author: Alfred Ng
reviews.text: A Dreamy Blue Gem in Morocco - Chefchaouen Chefchaouen, the Blue Pearl of Morocco, is an absolutely enchanting destination. Walking through its maze of narrow, blue-washed streets feels like stepping into a fairytale. The calming shades of blue everywhere create a unique, peaceful ambiance. The town is filled with charming shops offering handmade crafts, colorful textiles, and local treats. Exploring the bustling Medina is a visual delight, while the nearby hills offer panoramic views of the entire blue village. The locals are welcoming and proud to share stories of their town's history and traditions. Don’t miss visiting the Kasbah Museum and the beautiful Ras El Maa waterfall just outside the medina. reviews.author: Florence Carruthers
reviews.text: Highly worth a visit to the History of Tunis exhibition, you will never be sure what's around the corner. Will be one of our most memorable museum experiences, in a funny crazy way.

reviews.author: Ross Daniels
reviews.text: Very large and diverse museum in three sections. Not sure about the various religious exhibits as they are a bit simplistic but it’s a bit of fun if you suspend belief. But the first part on evolution would be great for kids as it has everything to trigger imagination. Worth a look especially for kids.

reviews.author: Ines FILALI
reviews.text: Belle aventure, great experience ! 😍 If you are there, you have to discover it

reviews.author: Basit Bhat
reviews.text: Exploring the enchanting Dar Cherait Museum, where history and art tell the stories of a vibrant past. ✨🏛️

reviews.author: Oussama Hafaiedh
reviews.text: Loved the service. I was taken care of from beginning to end. Shown the spaces and explained how to navigate the museum. All while giving me enough space to tour it in peace. Some areas need to me maintained and updated, mainly the evolution of life on earth area, the floor wash unsafe and then arrived at an area with Tunisian history were the light were still off it was so scary and funny at same time. Luckily, a cleaning lady was like you can go it’s fine, I was like I don’t think so it so dark. She turned on the lights for me as I was responding. Overall it’s a cute space, and love to support museums.

address: Dar El Jeld Tozeur, Tozeur, Tunisia

reviews.author: Christina Sairoglou
reviews.text: We were 6 people and we had an amazing stay at Dar el Medina, they got us from the airport, we had great breakfast and the staff was really friendly! The rooms, the service,the hotel and the view were really amazing. They organised for us a private driver to take us to the places we wanted through Tunisia even if requested it the last minute! I completely recommend this hotel for your stay in Tunisia! Thank you for everything guys!

reviews.author: rosa ibarra
reviews.text: We booked this accommodation in advance and were so excited. However a few days before the flight, we had an urgent medical emergency and could not physically go there. We reached out to them explaining the situation and asking for a refund or a change of dates, however they did not respond. The lack of human consideration for their guests and lack of flexibility, lets me know that we made the right choice not going. In the future when things get better in our health and we are able to go to Tuinisia, we will not be staying here.

reviews.author: Yosr chebbi (Rosy)
reviews.text: a beautifully preserved gem in the heart of the Medina. The architecture is stunning. The central courtyard is a peaceful retreat, and the rooftop terrace offers breathtaking views of the historic city. Every corner of this place showcases Tunisia’s rich heritage. Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates history and authentic design!

reviews.author: Mary Gordon
reviews.text: My dad and I had an amazing stay at Dar El Medina. Upon arrival our room wasn’t ready yet, and Mohamed offered us a quick tour of the hotel and brought us tea and some sweets while we waited. All interaction with the staff was very pleasant. They were very helpful when our flight to Djerba was moved up by one day and we had to quickly scramble for a cab to the airport. The included breakfast was plentiful and delicious. We ate dinner one night which was also very good. The building is very historic and charming. The location is also great as it’s within the medina. I would absolutely recommend staying here!

reviews.author: Cafer
reviews.text: The restaurant had nice view and food was delicious. The waiter and waitress were so kind. They need to put more signs for the toilet otherwise you may think that you are in a gift shop you are not wrong but also wrong because the toilet is on the right door 😅

reviews.author: Sophie Reaville
reviews.text: A beautiful hotel in the heart of the médina! We very much enjoyed our stay here, and made the most of the two pools, the beautiful gardens, the great food, and spa! The service was second to none, and the staff were so welcoming! Definitely one of the most beautiful hotel stays I have ever had.Would absolutely recommend 😌❤️

reviews.author: Paula
reviews.text: Had the best time in Dar Tozeur! The location is perfect and you have the option to park in a private parking lot for a small fee or leave it in a popular free parking spot. We left our rented car on the street and had no issues. The hotel is gorgeous, very well decorated. The rooms are big and we had a few restful nights. Super quiet, specially considering it’s inside the Medina. They also have 2 amazing pools (one heated), but it was unfortunately too cold to take a dip. But the highlight of our stay was the staff. Massive thanks to Donia and Ada. Always so helpful and kind, they truly made our days at Dar Tozeur extra special. 3aychek! Highly recommend this place if you’re in the area.

reviews.author: Alexandre T.
reviews.text: Second time at Dar Tozeur Team very nice and helpful. Location amazing, especially the hot pool for relaxing after a trek... Feels like home.

reviews.author: Katarzyna Iwańska
reviews.text: The most beautiful cosy hotel we stayed in during our entire trip through Tunisia. The room was big and splendid, a swim in the palm-surrounded pool divine and the dinner was absolutely lovely. Thank you Bilel for your hospitality!

reviews.author: Glenn'Philip Operations Manager
reviews.text: US$200 a night very romantic Two beautiful pools Very unique establish rooms Several relaxing places Downside, they don’t allow kids if you don’t have kids, it’s a plus ~> If you like my review please press follow on my google profile. If you are the owner and you’re responding to my review and saying thank you please thank me by following me on Google. Thanks Bali Sky

reviews.text: Rope course and Ziplines for 25 TND each. The staff were helpful and spoke good English. A nice distraction for kids from the mosques and medinas. A small reasonably-priced restaurant.

reviews.text: Lovely space, nice sitting area. We did not eat anything, but we played all the games that they had. It was amazing, but they have to make a referbushment for the adventures game as the nets are old.

reviews.author: Ross Daniels
reviews.text: This is an absolutely fantastic place a bit of a labyrinth but so enjoyable with winding streets and multiple marketplaces and plenty of cafes and eating spots. Great atmosphere and one of the streets will take you down to the beach. We spent hours just wandering around and it’s up there with any marketplace in Morocco.

reviews.author: mmm a
reviews.text: This has got to be the best souk in Morocco! I’ve been to many, but Essaouira’s felt so special. I spent about five hours there and still didn’t want to leave. Each shop has its own unique vibe, and the shopkeepers were incredibly kind and helpful. Every time I asked where to find something, they wouldn’t just point me in the direction—they’d actually walk me there and leave without the other shopkeepers noticing. It was such a genuine experience. You’ll find everything from handmade Moroccan teapots and beautiful tea glasses to breathtaking paintings and handmade rugs, linen clothing, genuine leather goods, and the most fragrant spices. If you’re looking for authentic treasures, this is the place!

reviews.author: Mohammed nurul Islam
reviews.text: Best place to shop in all city

reviews.author: Federica Preda
reviews.text: Beautiful and quaint! The shops are full of local souvenirs and for all budgets! Exceptional fish and real Argan oil! We will definitely return. A quiet city where you can reach everything on foot.

reviews.author: World Trip
reviews.text: A favorite ❤️ A truly delightful souk in the port city of Essaouira ✅ The climate is pleasant and the people are truly friendly!

reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Enes Yarli
reviews.text: I’m furious at myself for even stepping foot in this disgraceful café. This place has **ZERO respect** for customers – they treat you like dirt! We ordered **two pizzas at night** – they arrived **uncut, tasteless (no salt!), and ice-cold**. Absolutely disgusting! To make it worse, we got a **lemonade and a strawberry drink**, each for **18 dinars**, and the **pizzas were 30 dinars each** (total: **96 dinars**). **A complete rip-off** for the pathetic quality! When we paid with **100 dinars**, the staff didn’t even bother giving us change! We had to **argue just to get our money back**, and they acted like *we* were the problem. Unbelievable! **The waiter who served us was rude, unprofessional, and shameless.** I hope he gets treated the same way someday. **To the authorities:** This kind of scam is **bad for Tunisian tourism**. Tourists deserve better than being robbed and disrespected. **Final verdict:** **AVOID THIS PLACE!** If you enjoy **being ripped off, eating garbage, and dealing with arrogant staff**, go ahead. Otherwise, save your money and dignity!

reviews.author: BackpackingAndy
reviews.text: This place is for a quick view only and nothing else. It is extremely overpriced for Tunisia. As others have commented the staff will intentionally serve you foods that you do not order and then charge you for it. For example, they gave us a plate of ‘homemade cookies’ but we didn’t touch them then he tried to add it to the bill. I had to call him out on it. He was frustrated and was really rude after that. Honestly if you just want a view you can stand at the top of the stairs for a minute and take a look. The servers will come up the stairs and try to get you to sit down - at that point you can leave.

reviews.author: Hernan Ramirez
reviews.text: Be careful. They will serve food that you didn't order. Then, they will charge you. The food looks good but had no flavor. Have cash, or will you have to go downhill for a 15-minute walk to get cash to pay the bill. Everything they will try to get you, even with a picture from your own phone. All that in the restaurant. The only thing that I enjoyed was the view. It was great. There is too much stress even to order. Food overpriced.

reviews.author: manisankar kalaiselvan
reviews.text: Most beautiful locations. Yes the food & drinks are pricey, but you pay for the perfect seating with great views. Staff are kind and not pushy at all, mini Santorini town

reviews.text: I've been here many times. I love the view and i enjoy it when its not busy. But the tourist traps are seriously getting out of control... to the point it becomes stressful and annoying.

reviews.text: Visit: 03/01/25 1 person, for lunch. PROS: - Very nice place! - good and fast service - it comes A LOT of food. It can be easily shared buy 2 people. Even 3 people if you ask for the full menu (starter + main + dessert) - considering the amount of food, the price is really fair CONS: - the food is good, but not great. I was expecting more. It was not very tasteful as I wish General: this is as very nice place, just in the middle of the Medina and a few steps from the mosque. It’s like an Oasis on the middle of the crowed Medina. The ambiance is calm, elegant and very silent. There are also few booths with local artesian pieces. It’s a good place to rest and breath, but do not expect the best food on earth. It’s just normal.

reviews.author: Nick Vaes
reviews.text: Its a nice and renovated place. It has alot of light because of the roof, tough they added a glass roofing to stay dry even when it rains. Its a nice but busy place to go for eating as it is a bit famous. Would still recommend going there and taking the daily menu for a good deal.

reviews.author: Farah Amouri
reviews.text: The place itself is wonderfully beautiful. The menu for Romdhan is really good, expectedly pricey tho. The soupes were both good, brik well done, desert and tea were good, the main plate was also good except for the rice with calamar. I would just say it’s missing spice overall. All in all, a good experience.

reviews.author: Mira Mora
reviews.text: As a tunisian I brought my foreign husband to enjoy a tunisian dish !!! I found it horrible ,I asked a menu a didn't get it ,the food was really different ! Hold on that's not our traditional food !why cheating tourist by making very simple staff and old chicken !! Even i found a hair in my plate I called someone to bring the senior he took the plate and run ! I didn't ask him to take it ! Im informing any tourist want to visit there that's not the real tunisian taste they making a different food with a cheap price to make look wow good price and fish more client , a place only for taking pictures .couscous with chakchouka lol

reviews.author: Darrow Carson
reviews.text: What a huge mistake. We should have known better. We do know better but we arrived around 3pm and because everyone recommended it, we figured we would just stay. If you find yourself in the same position, leave. It’s a tourist restaurant, it’s all tourists and no locals. The food is substandard. We had the “chicken ravioli” dish which was a really dry piece of chicken and small pieces of square pasta with almost no sauce. We had chicken at a roadside stand the day before which was so much better. The service was terrible. We were told to wait in a side room. They forgot about us until I went to remind them we were still there. We were finally seated and shown the fixed menu which included dessert. When it was time to order dessert, they were all out. They then wanted to charge us full prices for the appetizers and main dishes instead of the cheaper fixed menu price because we didn’t get dessert. This place is a factory. I’d much rather eat in a place where locals eat with good food.

reviews.author: hamza Jabri
reviews.text: If you’re looking for an authentic Tunisian experience, El Mrabet is a must-visit! Located in the heart of the medina of Tunis, it’s the oldest restaurant in Africa, and you can truly feel the history and tradition in every detail. The ambiance is charming and authentic, perfect for relaxing with a tea, a coffee, or a delicious Tunisian meal. One of the highlights is the rooftop, which offers a beautiful view overlooking the iconic Zaitouna Mosque. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to discover the real soul of the Medina

reviews.author: amine mizouni
reviews.text: Never been disappointed there , I was always impressed with the quality of the service and food delivered. An amazing staff with the authentic ingredients. The atmosphere is amazing merging the charm of the old town and the magic of its nice people . 👌👌❤️❤️

Otherwise, save your money and dignity!

reviews.author: BackpackingAndy
reviews.text: This place is for a quick view only and nothing else. It is extremely overpriced for Tunisia. As others have commented the staff will intentionally serve you foods that you do not order and then charge you for it. For example, they gave us a plate of ‘homemade cookies’ but we didn’t touch them then he tried to add it to the bill. I had to call him out on it. He was frustrated and was really rude after that. Honestly if you just want a view you can stand at the top of the stairs for a minute and take a look. The servers will come up the stairs and try to get you to sit down - at that point you can leave.

reviews.author: Hernan Ramirez
reviews.text: Be careful. They will serve food that you didn't order. Then, they will charge you. The food looks good but had no flavor. Have cash, or will you have to go downhill for a 15-minute walk to get cash to pay the bill. Everything they will try to get you, even with a picture from your own phone. All that in the restaurant. The only thing that I enjoyed was the view. It was great. There is too much stress even to order. Food overpriced.

reviews.author: manisankar kalaiselvan
reviews.text: Most beautiful locations. Yes the food & drinks are pricey, but you pay for the perfect seating with great views. Staff are kind and not pushy at all, mini Santorini town

reviews.author: Hatem
reviews.text: I've been here many times. I love the view and i enjoy it when its not busy. But the tourist traps are seriously getting out of control... to the point it becomes stressful and annoying.

reviews.author: Erfaneh Masrour
reviews.text: Absolutely loved this place! The food was fresh, full of flavor, and beautifully presented. The staff was friendly and the owner was also very Kind. Cozy atmosphere and reasonable prices. A must-visit if you’re in the area!

reviews.author: Tim Harders
reviews.text: They have a menu which seems to be just a rough guideline of available dishes. All the dishes we liked were not available and eventually they showed us the fresh fish they actually have. That is fine, but - if always like that - maybe it makes sense to have a daily menu. Food was nice but service not too attentive. Anyway definitely a recommendation for sea food lovers.

reviews.author: Francisco Magalhães Santos
reviews.text: I thoroughly enjoyed this restaurant. It reminds me of excellent restaurants back home, with outstanding service, a simple yet high-quality menu, and a short but well-chosen wine list in a cozy setting. While the prices are a bit higher than average, they reflect the superior quality of both the food and service.

reviews.author: Phuong Tran
reviews.text: High quality seafood and potato. People are friendly and attentive

reviews.author: Wendy Oui
reviews.text: Tunisia's hidden restaurant! It's hard to find, but the service, atmosphere, and grilled seafood are extraordinary. The main dish is delicious, but the fries are really crispy!!

reviews.author: Zied Bargaoui
reviews.text: There is no strong reason not to give this place a 5 stars. it's just a full immersion into the history of the Medina through a very beautiful vintage house with stunning decoration and through a wide variety of Tunisian traditional food. The quantity of the food is more than enough for most of the people. Make sure to have an empty stomach before. It was possible to just go there without any reservation. The daily menu (entrance, main dish and desert, drinks excluded) costs 60 dinars (20€)

reviews.author: Hanna Kaade
reviews.text: Authentic Place with impressive decoration and designs! Very delicious traditional tunisian cuisine! Live arabic music! We loved the experience and it was definitely one of the highlights of our trip to Tunis! Highly recommended

reviews.author: Michele Formica
reviews.text: Food is extremely average for the price, and I was tricked into having a non alcoholic beer, which was sold to me as local... the blind gentleman playing music in the corner was by far the (and possibly only) highlight of the evening.

reviews.author: Safe Cave
reviews.text: I recently had the pleasure of dining at this restaurant, and it was an experience worth sharing. From the moment I walked in, the authentic tunisian ambiance set the tone for an enjoyable meal. The decor with the 17th century tunisian prints, with warm touches that make you feel right at the Beys era. Food: 4.5/5 The menu offers a tiny selection of dishes, and I was thoroughly impressed by the attention to detail in every plate. I ordered cooked lamb meat with vegetables, and it was cooked to perfection, melting tenderness. The flavors were fresh, and the portions were generous. My companion had the traditional fish (local Grouper fish) couscous , which was rich, full of fresh fish flavor. The couscous dish was accompanied by well-paired sauce (not hot) that enhanced the overall taste without overwhelming it. Service: 4.5/5 The staff was attentive and courteous throughout our meal. They were knowledgeable about the menu and offered great recommendations. The team was friendly and professional, and gave us a tour in the place so we can take pictures. Ambiance: 5/5 The lighting and tunisian traditional old music created a relaxed, upscale vibe, making it a great spot for a date night or a gathering with friends. I especially loved the large windows that brought in natural light during the day and created a cozy atmosphere in the evening. We learned from the waiter that starting from 9pm (local hour) there is tours every hour in the medina with the restaurant transport, and also they have artists that play music (I think basically the Qanûn instrument) Value: 4/5 While on the pricier side, the quality of the food, ambiance, and service make it worth the splurge. It's not a place for a quick bite, but if you're looking for an experience to indulge into tunisian culture. Overall, the place is a must-visit for anyone looking for a memorable dining experience with excellent food and a chic atmosphere. I will definitely be returning

reviews.author: umar
reviews.text: To preface this, we didn’t have the food. The waiter we had was rude and asked us where we were from, probably to figure out what type of clientele we were. We weren’t hungry so we ordered a starter and a main instead of 2 mains but the waiter condescendingly told us that it was a 1 main per person policy. When we went to leave, he told us that their place is “classy” and that we should go to a fast food place…which we did.

reviews.author: Hannah Stoddard
reviews.text: We had a wonderful stay at Dar Ben Gacem earlier this spring. The Dar is beautifully decorated and located in the heart of the medina with easy access to several sites and delicious breakfast served daily. The team was so friendly and helpful and made sure our visit was special. A particular highlight was doing a cooking class with Chef Youssef! The class began with a visit to the market to pick out fresh ingredients. Then we returned to the Dar and learned how to cook three delicious dishes - mechouia salad, brik, and Tunisian couscous with fish. We learned so much and had a great time chatting with Chef Youssef and the team - I definitely recommend and hope we can return soon.

reviews.author: Zara Kind
reviews.text: Very central hotel in the Medina of Tunis. All central locations are at walking distance so perfect for those who want to explore. The rooms are vintage, charming, traditional. Breakfast was varied and included also omelette. Here I had one of the best ricottas of my life! Giving 4 instead of 5 because at parity, other properties stood out more.

reviews.author: K L
reviews.text: Booking this Dar because of good reviews. But regret as alll heaters in the room was not working. It was really cold and couldn't sleep. Informed receptionists few times, but they didn't take it seriously. After following up few times, then in the late night only, the answer was sorry, technician only available the next day to repair it, all rooms were full.

reviews.author: Nesam Ha
reviews.text: The location is very central to main sightseeing parts, close to the souks and cafes. The service was very polite. The room could be equipped a little better and be more cleaner. Especially in the shower. Breakfast was decent but not always fresh bakery. The interior riad was beautiful.

reviews.author: Despo Potamou
reviews.text: The location is great, in the medina, and it is easy to go around for sightseeing. Staff is friendly and helpful, special shout out to Josef for all his valuable help and all the information shared. We are really grateful for meeting him as he even came to help us during his free time to do some personal shopping. The room was spacious and beautifully decorated. We were given a free upgrade as first-time visitors from Cyprus. Breakfast was delicious, too.

reviews.author: Konstantin Bozhilov
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Abdulhadi W. Ayyad
reviews.text: This is a funky little part-time art gallery which doubles as a guest house in Sidi Bou Said. The staff are friendly, casual and hardworking but the place could do with a bit of sprucing up. Don't come expecting a fancy hotel experience, but I felt that it was clean enough (although a pair of guests from Switzerland left while I was there, claiming it was too dusty). I liked this place for what it was, which is a nice little hangout to get to the amazing beaches at the bottom of the hill. Unsure if I would come again, but ho-hum.

reviews.author: Hichem Hanafi
reviews.text: 5 stars because they are very very friendly and because they do their best to help. 2 pretty ladies are always present to serve you. Nice breakfast, nice rooms decorated with love and wonderful paintings, they have a wonderful terrace where you can enjoy your own drinks and the nice wiew of Sidi Bousaid. Due to its central location at night it is a litle bit laud Please don't visit the Cafe des Delices in Sidi Bousaid because its unfriendly waiters will still your money and make you unhappy.

reviews.author: samar harrathi
reviews.text: We booked 2 nights there. The sheets, bed and pillows were not clean and used . It was very disappointing

reviews.author: Said Al Rawas
reviews.text: Nice place ...

reviews.author: Hussain R
reviews.text: It was bucket list..soo thankful

reviews.author: Woodley Jean MICHEL TV
reviews.text: Dad Al Jaziri, in the heart of la Medina in Tunis, is was said that the act of independence was written there followed by political by politic persecutions. Now, Beautiful house of poetry.

reviews.author: Nabil Ayachi
reviews.text: Dar El Jaziri [currently the House of Poetry]. Rue du Tribunal. Medina of Tunis. [currently the House of Poetry] 🇹🇳 ✔💯 This house is Bit El Châar, Dar El Jaziri

reviews.author: Bensaou Mohammed
reviews.text: nan

reviews.author: Mahya Hemmat
reviews.text: We had lunch here after walking in the souk in a super hot day. There were plenty of tables available and live music going on. They were very polite and the food was super good (the best we’ve had on Tunisian food). The lamb tasted very delicious and tender, the fish dish that the waiter recommended was perfectly cooked. We also tried Tunisian white wine and it was very smooth. My only suggestion for them would be to add high chair support for kids although this is a high end restaurant, our toddler had to sit on our lap and was very difficult to eat with him.

reviews.author: Kianmehr Ehtiatkar
reviews.text: Amazing food, location, and vibes! It’s definitely very expensive by Tunisian standards, but if you can afford it, it’s worth paying the price. I found the food somewhat unique compared to other nice restaurants, and the live instrumental music was a nice surprise! Places like these are among the rarer places that offer alcohol, and I was pleased to try Tunisian wine which was very delicious!

reviews.author: Uncle Za
reviews.text: I am profoundly perplexed by the high mark this restaurant receives. Apart from the amazing dining room in an old converted palace, everything else is decidedly ordinary. Yes they do welcome you on arrival and make you sit in the front lounge but do not have the finesse to offer you the menu to ponder over whilst waiting, let alone a small nibble to whet your appetite. Once you are sat at the table and given the menu, a miserable looking older man comes around to take your orders with not a sliver of a smile or acknowledgment. Shockingly, the menu is very limited and reminiscent of a fixed priced pre-theatre tourist menu hence you can forget indulging yourself in any kind of feasting. And if that failed to disappoint you, you can then rest assure that the food will taste no different from any other Tunisian restaurants charging half the price. This was our sixth Tunisian restaurant at this point. In fact my fish soup was so tasteless and so was the fish couscous, I had never been so happy to see a salt cruet. Even the wine list fails to include any non-Tunisian wines which is almost a crime for a supposedly upmarket restaurant. All in all, this is a very bog standard Tunisian restaurant that happened to be in a nice room. More hype than substance. You will not eat any better here just because they have pretty mosaics and lamps. Not recommended unless you really don’t know what to do with your money.

reviews.author: Nate Bettini
reviews.text: Beautiful historic hotel in the Medina, immaculately renovated. Rooftop terrace is lovely on a sunny afternoon. Highly recommend to stay. If you’re staying elsewhere in Tunis recommend the a stop at the terrace when visiting the Medina. The bartenders are quite skilled. I particular recommend for couples.

reviews.author: Aymen
reviews.text: Absolutely amazing! Zero fault! Best place to stay near the Medina and top 3 places to stay in all of Tunis, period. You must book a dinner in the downstairs restaurant. The rooftop restaurant is very nice too! Service is top Notch! The room, perfect! The Spa is also very nice. I am typically very critical of places I review but this Hotel is just an absolute Gem! Note: Call when you're on your way there so they can meet you on the street side and help you with your luggage if you have a lot.

reviews.author: Christina Sairoglou
reviews.text: We were 6 people and we had an amazing stay at Dar el Medina, they got us from the airport, we had great breakfast and the staff was really friendly! The rooms, the service,the hotel and the view were really amazing. They organised for us a private driver to take us to the places we wanted through Tunisia even if requested it the last minute! I completely recommend this hotel for your stay in Tunisia! Thank you for everything guys!

reviews.author: rosa ibarra
reviews.text: We booked this accommodation in advance and were so excited. However a few days before the flight, we had an urgent medical emergency and could not physically go there. We reached out to them explaining the situation and asking for a refund or a change of dates, however they did not respond. The lack of human consideration for their guests and lack of flexibility, lets me know that we made the right choice not going. In the future when things get better in our health and we are able to go to Tuinisia, we will not be staying here.

reviews.author: Yosr chebbi (Rosy)
reviews.text: a beautifully preserved gem in the heart of the Medina. The architecture is stunning. The central courtyard is a peaceful retreat, and the rooftop terrace offers breathtaking views of the historic city. Every corner of this place showcases Tunisia’s rich heritage. Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates history and authentic design!

reviews.author: Mary Gordon
reviews.text: My dad and I had an amazing stay at Dar El Medina. Upon arrival our room wasn’t ready yet, and Mohamed offered us a quick tour of the hotel and brought us tea and some sweets while we waited. All interaction with the staff was very pleasant. They were very helpful when our flight to Djerba was moved up by one day and we had to quickly scramble for a cab to the airport. The included breakfast was plentiful and delicious. We ate dinner one night which was also very good. The building is very historic and charming. The location is also great as it’s within the medina. I would absolutely recommend staying here!

reviews.author: Cafer
reviews.text: The restaurant had nice view and food was delicious. The waiter and waitress were so kind. They need to put more signs for the toilet otherwise you may think that you are in a gift shop you are not wrong but also wrong because the toilet is on the right door 😅

reviews.author: Slaheddine Saadallah
reviews.text: Beautiful at dawn

reviews.author: Mira Seo
reviews.text: We were very fortunate to get a spot for iftar during Ramadan— the restaurant was busy and lively with a special holiday menu! The owner is so welcoming with a true passion for Tunisian regional cuisine history. All the servers are so kind and attentive, and every dish was excellent. We loved the distinctive plats du jour: veal braised with olives stuffed with ground veal meatballs, and an oven braised lamb on the bone with potatoes, dried figs, and dates. The generous starters and unusual dessert (zgougou: black pine nut pudding with almond cream and toasted almonds) were stunning! We felt so welcomed by the whole family on our first night in Tunis. The owner speaks very sophisticated English— it was a pleasure to meet him and his lovely family!

reviews.author: Deepali Desai
reviews.text: The food here was absolutely amazing, and the service was incomparable. The portions were very large, and they were accommodating to all of our dietary restrictions. The owner of Dar Slah was the kindest person we met in Tunis. I would love to come back here again, and would highly recommend Dar Slah to anyone looking to have a wonderful traditional Tunisian meal.

reviews.author: Andres Capurro
reviews.text: Food Quality: food was nice. Nothing too special that would stand out, but has a good local touch and experience. Very authentic. Portions: quite good portions. The menus offered have a good representation of different local dishes. Drinks: limited variety Price: $$ good price Service: very friendly and patient to explain the options available. Atmosphere: felt a bit weird, a mix of sensations. Highlights: authentic food Payment Method: cash

reviews.author: mzitun
reviews.text: Very nice experience overall. The couscous was delicious and flavorful (a bit dry though). Excellent friendly service.

reviews.author: Pete

reviews.text: If you’re looking for an authentic Tunisian experience, El Mrabet is a must-visit! Located in the heart of the medina of Tunis, it’s the oldest restaurant in Africa, and you can truly feel the history and tradition in every detail. The ambiance is charming and authentic, perfect for relaxing with a tea, a coffee, or a delicious Tunisian meal. One of the highlights is the rooftop, which offers a beautiful view overlooking the iconic Zaitouna Mosque. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to discover the real soul of the Medina

The atmosphere is amazing merging the charm of the old town and the magic of its nice people . 👌👌❤️❤️

reviews.text: Visit: 03/01/25 1 person, for lunch. PROS: - Very nice place! - good and fast service - it comes A LOT of food. It can be easily shared buy 2 people. Even 3 people if you ask for the full menu (starter + main + dessert) - considering the amount of food, the price is really fair CONS: - the food is good, but not great. I was expecting more. It was not very tasteful as I wish General: this is as very nice place, just in the middle of the Medina and a few steps from the mosque. It’s like an Oasis on the middle of the crowed Medina. The ambiance is calm, elegant and very silent. There are also few booths with local artesian pieces. It’s a good place to rest and breath, but do not expect the best food on earth. It’s just normal.
