address: Seven Spices, Dubai, United Arab Emirates

reviews.author: JayDob Yoo
reviews.text: Sloweeeest service, ordered from talabat it took 2 Hours to deliver. Probably faster for me to travel to india and get the food

reviews.author: Khushboo Raina
reviews.text: rubbish food, will neve order or even suggest anyone, may be my enemies yes

reviews.author: Smriti Grover
reviews.text: Nothing great

name: Sheikh Mohammed Centre Cafe
address: Sheikh Mohammed Centre Cafe, Dubai, United Arab Emirates

reviews.author: huda Salem
reviews.text: Amazing Amazing amazing. Unique experience, and I advise everyone to try it. It took us to the old days in UAE and made us feel the life style during our grandparents timing. Lovely arrangement and very nice knowledgeable staff. Very special service and I will love to go back. They have so many programs you can select based on your needs.

reviews.author: Gabe Me
reviews.text: We've been around for a couple decades and wanted to go for many years. Definitely the best iftar experience we had in the UAE in 20 years. The small group was very mixed from all over the world, people only on a stop-over, on holiday, new expats to many years residents. The local Emirati guide from SHA made us totally comfy, packed the evening full of so much info and was open to answer the most personal questions. The experience was amazing.

reviews.author: Vikas Singh
reviews.text: Just on opposite side of the Al Khayma restaurant they have a exact copy of a traditional Bedouin tent. A traditional Bedouin tent, also known as a khaima or bayt, is a portable structure primarily made of woven goat or camel hair. These tents are supported by poles and ropes, and often include sections for separate sleeping, dining, and guest areas. They are designed to provide shelter from the harsh desert environment and are easily erected and dismantled.

reviews.author: Karen Siebel
reviews.text: Stumbled on this centre while exploring the Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood and it was a pleasant surprise. Small but evocative home museum transporting visitors to a picturesque and rich past. Worth a visit. We noticed there were guided groups and a banquet to be set out, but unfortunately we were not booked on them. Perhaps on another visit.

reviews.author: Jacqueline Stephen
reviews.text: I've participated in many of their cultural events and often bring guests along who are first-time visitors to the UAE. I always learn something new! The staff is welcoming and informative, and the programs are well-organized.

name: Shish Shawerma
address: Shish Shawerma, Dubai, United Arab Emirates

reviews.author: Mohamed Elaarag
reviews.text: Very tasty shawerma served in a freshly baked bread for each sandwich! Best in town!

reviews.author: mark keserwany
reviews.text: Used to be great, but just became like any other shawerma place lately, not worth it

reviews.author: E. Sharaf
reviews.text: Use to be the best shawarma place in dubai until the owner sold it!

reviews.author: Bashir Mraish
reviews.text: it was a great experience very nice food good service

reviews.author: James Babu
reviews.text: very good shawerma crepe

reviews.author: Marion Bourson
reviews.text: I recently hosted a dinner for a group of 35 people at Siraj Restaurant and I must say it was an unforgettable experience! From the moment we arrived, the staff went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. The ambience of the restaurant is stunning, blending traditional Emirati elements with modern elegance. The food was absolutely delicious. Every dish was beautifully presented and bursting with authentic flavors. The service was impeccable even with a large group. The team was very attentive. I highly recommend Siraj Restaurant to anyone looking for an authentic Emirati dining experience. They have privatized the entire bridge to host our dinner. Thank you to the entire team for making our evening so special!

reviews.author: Leyla Almaskyzy
reviews.text: I had an unforgettable dining experience at this Lebanese restaurant in Dubai. The cuisine was absolutely outstanding – every bite was bursting with authentic Middle Eastern flavors. From the freshly baked warm bread to the perfectly grilled meats and vibrant mezze selection, everything was cooked to perfection and served with care. The quality of the ingredients and the attention to detail truly set this place apart. The ambiance was cozy yet elegant, making it a perfect spot for both casual dinners and special occasions. The staff were incredibly attentive and friendly, making us feel welcome from the moment we walked in. If you’re looking for exceptional Lebanese food in Dubai, this place is a must-visit. I will definitely be coming back!

reviews.author: Divya Mishra
reviews.text: Siraj in Souk Al Bahar has beautiful indoor and outdoor seating. We sat inside because the weather was hot. The location is excellent, being on the other side of the famous Dubai Mall. The staff were courteous. We enjoyed our dinner with our family.

reviews.author: sara alaoui
reviews.text: Siraj delivers a unique blend of Lebanese and Emirati flavors in a beautifully designed setting. The ambiance is elegant yet welcoming, making it a great spot for both casual dining and special occasions. The menu offers a variety of flavorful dishes, from creamy hummus and fresh mezze to perfectly grilled meats and seafood. Each dish is prepared with care and beautifully presented, reflecting the restaurant’s high standards. What made the experience truly exceptional was the outstanding service. Yasser, our waiter, was incredibly attentive and ensured everything was perfect, while Elie, the manager, went above and beyond to make us feel welcome. Their professionalism and hospitality added a special touch to the evening. If you’re looking for great Lebanese cuisine with top-notch service, Siraj is definitely worth a visit!

reviews.author: Hanadi Hamdan
reviews.text: Siraj is a charming Emirati restaurant that offers a delightful culinary experience. Located in a beautiful setting, it combines traditional Emirati flavors with a modern twist. The ambiance is warm and inviting, with elegant decor that reflects the rich cultural heritage of the UAE. The menu features a variety of authentic dishes, from aromatic biryanis to flavorful grills, all prepared with fresh ingredients. The staff is friendly and attentive, ensuring a pleasant dining experience. Overall, Siraj is a great place to enjoy a taste of Emirati cuisine in a sophisticated atmosphere.

reviews.author: Nour Saad
reviews.text: We were a bigger group and Sunday did a great job with the service, quick and accurate. He recommended the half-grilled chicken and it was delicious. One of the better locations in terms of service, but their menu has always been unecessarily too long in my opinion.

reviews.author: Local Advisor
reviews.text: I have ordered half grilled chicken, but unfortunately received quarter Burned chicken served with handful Frozen fries!!! despite the fact of receiving it after more than 1 hour, Very bad quality and will never order again

reviews.author: Viju Vijay
reviews.text: Lebanese Shawarma, Grills, Sandwich available. Restaurant decor is good. Good to friends meet and get together, with marina vibe.

reviews.author: Gagandeep Arora
reviews.text: Absolute delight from start to finish. Ambiance warm and inviting. Amazing quality of ingredients which shows in their food

reviews.author: Hadi Amini
reviews.text: Despite of poor view and looks; the food is good and tasty, and definitely traditional Everything here inspire the origin of place which is Syria, from cheap old cutlery to hard chairs and wooden tables Staff are super friendly and I enjoyed a lot of food and service Really recommend, if you are looking for traditional good food 👌🏻👌🏻👌🏻👌🏻

name: Al Bidya Mosque Cafe
address: Al Bidya Mosque Cafe, Fujairah, United Arab Emirates

reviews.author: Engr. Faisal.
reviews.text: A true gem of the UAE! Al Bidya Mosque is the oldest mosque in the country, yet beautifully preserved and still in use. The architecture is simple yet captivating, with four small domes and thick stone walls. The surrounding area is peaceful with scenic mountain views and historic watchtowers nearby. A great spot for history lovers and those looking for a quiet, spiritual experience. Dress modestly, and don’t forget to climb the hill for amazing photos!

reviews.author: 아흐마드무함마드
reviews.text: 🚨 Main Hall Is closed And Have No Update When it will Open again 🚨No need To Buy ticket There is Free Entry 🚨Should Wear Well Clothes 🚨Tombs Are Also Closed it But U Can Go to Mountain For Best Ocean And Mountain view ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Hidden Gem of History & Peace! 🕌✨** Visiting **Al Bidya Mosque** was an unforgettable experience! 🇦🇪 This ancient beauty, with its unique mud-brick architecture and serene vibes, took me back in time. 🕰️ The oldest mosque in the UAE, yet so well-preserved!

reviews.author: Aida Akhmetova Demir
reviews.text: To be honest İ was really amazed with the mosque, it quit picturesque and cozy inside. Mosque considered as the most oldest in UAE. You can also walk behind the mosque, there is a small fort and nice view on the sea. If you will pass by, definitely have a look!

reviews.author: Nouman Yousaf
reviews.text: Great alhamdolillah visited the masjid recently as we heard that this is the old masjid a history of UAE. And we heard that this is the masjid of sahaba ikram time so visited and we saw its nice and amazing creation pure natural made by hands its great to see. If any one is visiting Fujairah should visit this masjid and see from your eyes.

reviews.author: Rebel Ms
reviews.text: The moment you step into Al Bidya Mosque, it feels like entering an entirely different world. As the oldest mosque in the UAE, it takes you back to the 1440s the atmosphere, the spiritual energy, and the sense of peace are simply beyond words. A special thanks to the UAE Government, and especially to His Highness Sheikh Hamad bin Mohammed Al Sharqi, the Ruler of Fujairah, for their dedication to preserving this historical treasure through careful restoration and rehabilitation. Out of respect for my faith, I chose not to take any photos inside the mosque. But I truly encourage you to visit and experience the feeling for yourself. It’s absolutely worth it.

name: Al Meshwar
address: Al Meshwar, Fujairah, United Arab Emirates

reviews.author: David Muller
reviews.text: Was the second time to this awesome restaurant that stands out from the rest of buildings in the area. It is well decorated and creates a beautiful ambiance and a feeling of importance to dine in. The food was excellent and good portions, the freshness and the aroma makes you eat more than what you consume normally. This is a very nice restaurant with great people. reviews.author: Mohammed Aamir Mitha
reviews.text: We had such a wonderful time at Al Bait Al Qadeem, definitely one of the highlights of our trip to Dubai. The ambience was stunning, set in a beautifully preserved historical building with traditional seating that made the whole experience feel special and authentic. A huge shoutout to our host, Linet, who made the evening even better with her exceptional service and deep knowledge of the menu. She took the time to explain the dishes and recommended the Emirati platter, dips and salad platter, and the freshly baked local bread, all of which were absolutely delicious. For dessert, we had the luqaimat with a cup of local Gahwa, which was the perfect way to end the meal. We left with big smiles and full bellies, exactly what you want from a great dining experience. We’ll definitely be back next time we’re in town. Thanks again, Linet and the team, for such a memorable evening!

A bit on the pricy side, but well worth it for the experience. And our lovely Egyptian server lady, was a treasure, so sweet and offered recommendations which turned out great!

reviews.author: Amy Khan
reviews.text: Shababeek Restaurant, Sharjah is a haven for lovers of authentic Lebanese cuisine. Nestled in the charming Al Qasba area, this restaurant offers stunning views of the canal and an ambiance that blends traditional Lebanese aesthetics with modern elegance. During my visit, I was impressed by their commitment to quality and detail. The menu highlights include the creamy Hummus Beiruti, crispy Falafel, and flavorful Tabbouleh salad. I also tried the popular Fatayer Spinach, which was fresh and delicious. The main courses are equally impressive. The Mixed Grill Platter is a must-have, featuring perfectly grilled Shish Tawook, Kafta, and tender Lamb Chops. The Sayadieh (spiced rice with fish) was another standout dish, showcasing a delicate balance of flavors. For dessert, the Kunafa stole the show with its gooey cheese and crispy topping, paired beautifully with a cup of Arabic Coffee. Shababeek Sharjah is not just about food; it’s an experience. The stunning canal views, impeccable service, and authentic Lebanese dishes make it a dining destination worth visiting. Shababeek Restaurant in Sharjah offers a diverse menu of authentic Lebanese cuisine, with prices reflecting the quality and ambiance of the dining experience. On average, a meal for two people costs around AED 220. Here are some popular dishes along with their approximate prices: Crumbed Baked Potato with Kashkaval Cheese Pot: AED 34 Shish Barak with Vermicelli Rice: AED 55 Kabab Halabi: AED 61 Shish Tawook: AED 58 Grilled Lamb Chops: AED 94 Mixed Grills for 1 Person: AED 65 Umm Ali (Dessert): AED 37 Fresh Orange Juice: AED 26 For those seeking value, Shababeek offers a 2-course business lunch on weekdays from 12 pm to 3 pm, priced at AED 55 per person. Additionally, they have a dessert and coffee combo available for AED 25.

reviews.author: Vicky Bo
reviews.text: What can I say? This is just my favorite restaurant! I became a regular in here 😋 The staff is kind and polite. Likewise, the food they serve is incredibly tasty! Any dish you try here is delicious! I definitely recommend to come 😊

reviews.author: Sium Islam
reviews.text: Sharjah Beach is a beautiful and peaceful destination along the coastline of the UAE. It offers a more relaxed and family-friendly alternative compared to the busier beaches of Dubai. Here’s a review based on different aspects: Scenic Beauty & Atmosphere Sharjah Beach features a long stretch of soft golden sand and clear blue waters. Unlike commercialized beaches, it has a more natural and serene ambiance, making it perfect for relaxation. The sunsets here are stunning, providing excellent photo opportunities. Facilities & Amenities • Walking & Cycling Tracks: The well-maintained tracks along the beach make it a great spot for jogging, walking, or cycling. • Shaded Seating Areas: There are plenty of shaded spots and benches where visitors can relax and enjoy the view. • Play Areas for Kids: Some sections of the beach include small play areas, making it family-friendly. • Clean & Well-Maintained: The authorities ensure that the beach remains clean and organized, with regular maintenance. Activities • Swimming: The water is generally calm, making it a good spot for swimming. However, lifeguards may not always be present, so caution is advised. • Picnicking: Many visitors enjoy picnicking with family and friends. BBQs may not be allowed in some areas, so checking local rules is recommended. • Water Sports: While not as commercialized as Dubai’s beaches, some areas may offer kayaking or jet skiing. Accessibility & Location Sharjah Beach is easily accessible by car and has ample parking space. It’s also well-connected to other parts of the UAE, making it a convenient getaway for residents and tourists. Final Verdict Sharjah Beach is a great spot for families, couples, and anyone looking for a peaceful beach experience. It’s not as crowded or commercialized as Dubai’s beaches, making it ideal for relaxation. If you prefer a quiet, scenic spot with basic amenities, it’s definitely worth visiting.

reviews.author: Tahir Mohammed
reviews.text: Umm Al Quwain Fort is a historical landmark located in the emirate of Umm Al Quwain, United Arab Emirates. It is a well-preserved fort that was built in the 17th century. The fort is made of mudbrick and has four towers. It is located on a hill overlooking the city of Umm Al Quwain. The fort is now a museum that houses a collection of artifacts from the history of Umm Al Quwain. The artifacts include weapons, pottery, jewelry, and household items. There are also exhibits on the history of the fort and the emirate. The Umm Al Quwain Fort is a popular tourist destination. It is a good place to learn about the history of the emirate and to see a well-preserved example of traditional Arabian architecture. Here are some pros and cons of visiting Umm Al Quwain Fort: Pros: Well-preserved fort Interesting exhibits on the history of Umm Al Quwain Beautiful views of the city Good place to learn about traditional Arabian architecture Not too crowded Cons: The museum is small Some of the exhibits are in Arabic only Some of the fort is not air-conditioned, so it can be hot inside during the summer in some areas Overall, I would recommend visiting Umm Al Quwain Fort if you are interested in learning about the history of the emirate. It is a small but well-preserved fort that is worth a visit. Here are some tips for visiting Umm Al Quwain Fort: The fort is open from 8am to 8pm, from Saturday to Thursday. It is closed on Fridays. The entrance fee is 5 AED for adults and 2.5 AED for children. There is a parking lot near the fort. The fort is not wheelchair accessible. I hope this helps!

Considering we were a family of four – my wife, two children, and myself – I asked if we could pay only for myself and my wife. Upon returning later, I found a same staff member at the counter. I attempted to pay and requested payment for only two people, as other hotels had accommodated. Initially, the staff member refused and called the manager. Despite my insistence, the manager declined. Undeterred, I requested to speak directly with the manager. After a conversation with the manager, they finally agreed to accept payment for two people. However, to my surprise, the price had escalated to 590 SAR for just two individuals. This unexpected increase left me in a difficult situation, especially considering my children's presence and their inquiries about the escalating cost. Even though the hotel is great and fabulous, I dream to have an opportunity to spend 10 days there all-inclusive, Inchallah, experiencing every luxury and amenity it has to offer.

reviews.author: Fahmi Abbas
reviews.text: Yemen’s Dar al-Hajar – or ‘stone house’ is a rock column behold one of the world’s most spectacular constructions. The former royal residence grows out of the rock pinnacle upon which it’s perched. The Dar al-Hajar or “Rock Palace” is located in Wadi Dhar, around 15 km (9 miles) from the capital city of Sana, Yemen. It seems to grow out of the rocks on which it is constructed and it has the characteristic painting of its windows and edges. Yemen’s architecture Dar al-Hajar palace, built atop a tall natural rock spire is nevertheless fantastical. The five-storey building looks incredible from every angle. So, it won’t be surprised to see Dar al-Hajar on a Yemeni currency note (the 500 rials one). In the 1920’s Islamic spiritual leader named Yahya Muhammad Hamiddin (ruler of Yemen from 1904 to 1948) stayed here as a summer residence. This place didn’t leave good memories for Imam Muhammad Yahya as his grandson assassinated him during a coup in Yemen in 1948. Nevertheless, the palace did remain in the ownership of the Yemeni royal family until the Yemen 1962. However, Islamic scholar Imam Mansoor Ali Bin Mehdi Abbas constructed atop the structure on the rock column. This beautiful building has multiple facilities of kitchen, storage area, guest rooms, and sedate courtyard leading through the five-story structure. The main feature of this building is to look like a fortress with shooting emplacements to defend the place from attackers. Therefore, it’s indeed easy on the eye, though designed to withstand attack and its own water supply from deep below the rock’, meaning it could ‘easily have withstood a siege’. Now it’s a popular example of Yemeni architecture for tourists, who can see the rooms and explore the labyrinth of staircases. Now Dar al-Hajar has a museum, and tourists who paid a visit to the palace have sung its praises on the internet. It’s a fantastic place and one of the best things you will see in Yemen. You will have a wonderful experience to see this old Yemeni palace and understand more about the local life and culture.’ It is nothing like you have ever seen before to pay a must-visit and relish the exquisite view. The majestic five floors offer enough to relish, but walking around at its base is equally impressive and heightens your admiration.

reviews.author: Abdullah Faiz Saleh
reviews.text: The Middle-Eastern-styled palace as it stands today was actually built relatively recently, in the 1930s by an Islamic spiritual leader named Yahya Muhammad Hamiddin, but it seems that he was building atop a preexisting structure that was built in the 1700s by an Islamic scholar. The tall castle was intended to be the leader’s summer home, and featured a number of facilities including appointment rooms for his highly appointed guests and separate spaces for cooling water in earthen jars. The rooms are built up the side of a tall rock spire, culminating in a grand tower at its pinnacle. The Imam Yahya was assassinated in 1948, but his iconic palace still stands and it has become a popular example of Yemeni architecture. While it is no longer used as a royal residence, the palace has been refitted as a museum and can be toured for a fee. Visitors can range about through the kitchens, storage rooms, and appointment rooms connected by a small labyrinth of stairways leading through the five-story structure. But as impressive as it is to explore inside, it is the view from the exterior that really makes the palace one of a kind. Combined with the natural rock on which it is built, it truly looks like a monumental work straight out of a fantasy novel.

reviews.author: Hisham Mohamed
reviews.text: House of stone in the valley of noon. Dar Al-Hajar is one of the historical buildings in Yemen. It is located in Sana'a - Wadi Dhahr. It was built during the 18th century by Ali bin Saleh Al-Ammari and was named after the granite rock on which this house was built. The palace dates back to the late 18th century when the king of Yemen, Imam Al-Mansur Ali bin Abbas, and his minister, Ali bin Saleh al-Amari (1736-1798), who was famous for architecture, astronomy, poetry and literature, ordered him to build a palace in Wadi Zahr to be his summer palace. Historians say that it was built on the ruins of an ancient palace known as the fortress of the sedan built by the donkeys in 3000 BC. The fortress was destroyed by the Turks four hundred years ago, and was restored at the beginning of the twentieth century by the Imam Yahya Hamid religion after being inherited by a number of kings Yemenis. He is currently a tourist destination for thousands of people around the world. [2] The construction was in its primary way for years, until Imam Yahya bin Humaiduddin added the upper floor (the freed). [1] The stories associated with the beginning of the foundation and the construction of Dar Al-Hajar vary, and some stories indicate that the house was demolished dozens of times but was once again rebuilt. It is said that the Turks in the first invasion of Yemen preferred to live in this house for its unique architecture and the valley which, together with the rest of the sites and views surrounding it as a garden and orchard for the inhabitants and visitors of this historic palace due to the characteristic of these beautiful places of evergreen vegetation, Squash and squash, as well as giant dum trees, which have begun to fade as a result of the expansion of qat cultivation. It is also said that the country during the reign of the Turks saw heavy rains led to the demolition of the house and did not have any impact, then came to the region Imam Abdullah al-Mansur, who reconstructed the three roles with a black stone Habash, which is currently, and then settled and after the death of Imam Abdul Allah al-Mansur Imam al-Nasser It is said that during his reign, some wars and disagreements between him and the people of Hamdan, who killed him sleeping on his bed and took him and buried him and the guard that was with him in an area south of the valley of noon and say the people of the region that his grave is still known to everyone. After the death of Imam al-Nasser, the imams were afraid of the residence of this house until Imam Yahya built some other palaces in the valley but soon changed his mind after a period and renovated the house of stone and building some additional roles of the material of the Iagor and added some other facilities such as the porter, People. The Imam also built a mosque adjacent to the house and wrote on his door "built to God Almtawakil God" is still present.

reviews.author: A J Bashha
reviews.text: The Dragon's Blood Tree (Dracaena cinnabari) is a remarkable species endemic to Socotra Island, Yemen, where it grows in large densities of woodland. Its distinctive umbrella-like mushroom shape is entirely natural. These trees can live up to 600 years and reach a height of 10 meters. The tree's deep red resin, resembling blood, has been highly valued since the Roman era for its uses in dye, violin varnish, medicine, makeup, and rituals. Socotra, located in the Indian Ocean near the coasts of Yemen and Somalia, is politically part of Yemen, though it has historical and cultural connections to Somalia. The island features spectacular scenery and is home to numerous endemic species of plants, birds, and other fauna, such as the Dragon's Blood Tree. Its unique landscape includes rugged mountains, canyons, wadis, caves, and picturesque beaches. The calm, shallow sea and the warm climate make it an attractive destination for nature lovers, scientists, and adventurers. Tourists often engage in snorkeling, fishing, hiking, and sightseeing, making the most of the island's natural beauty. However, Socotra lacks proper tourist infrastructure, such as hotels or guesthouses, and camping remains the only accommodation option. Transportation and facilities are underdeveloped, which preserves its untouched appeal.
